column5: Wife of Eliphaz and mother of Teman.
column7: Wife or concubine of Eliphaz, was the mother of Teman, Omar, Zepho, Gatam, and Kenaz.

column5: Wife of Ezekiel - Died as a sign to Israel
column7: Ezekiel's wife died suddenly, and God used her death as a sign to the people of Israel.

column5: Mother of Jerahmeel, Ram, and Caleb
column7: An unnamed wife of Hezron who bore him Jerahmeel, Ram, and Caleb.

column5: Wife of Jerahmeel; mother of Ram
column7: An unnamed wife of Jerahmeel who bore him Bunah, Ram, Oren, Ozem, and Ahijah.

column5: A wife of Josiah; mother of Shallum
column7: One of King Josiah's wives was the mother of his son Shallum.

column5: Wife of Lot, daughter-in-law of Terah
column7: An unnamed wife of Lot, who was Terah's daughter-in-law.

column5: Wife of Peter, whose mother Jesus healed
column7: Peter's unnamed wife, whose mother Jesus healed of a fever.

column5: Wife of Simeon, the son of Jacob.
column7: An unnamed wife of Simeon, the son of Jacob, is mentioned in the genealogy of Simeon's descendants.

column5: Daughter of Abinadab, one of Solomon's wives.
column7: One of Solomon's wives was the daughter of Abinadab, who was placed in charge of the district of Dor.

column5: Moses' brother, first high priest of Israel
column6: a teacher; lofty; mountain of strength
column7: The eldest son of Amram and Jochebed, a daughter of Levi ([[@2006020|Ex. 6:20]]). Some explain the name as meaning mountaineer, others mountain of strength, illuminator. He was born in Egypt three years before his brother Moses, and a number of years after his sister Miriam (2:1, 4; 7:7). He married Elisheba, the daughter of Amminadab of the house of Judah (6:23; [[@13002010|1 Chr. 2:10]]), by whom he had four sons, Nadab and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar.

column5: One of King Ahasuerus' seven eunuchs
column7: One of the seven eunuchs in Ahasuerus’s court ([[@17001010|Esther 1:10]]; [[@17002021|Esther 2:21]]).

column5: A river of Damascus, preferred by Naaman over the Jordan.
column7: Stony (Heb. marg. “Amanah,” perennial), the chief river of Damascus ([[@12005012|2 Kings 5:12]]). Its modern name is Barada, the Chrysorrhoas, or “golden stream,” of the Greeks.

This Syriac or Chaldee word is found three times in the New Testament ([[@41014036|Mark 14:36]]; [[@45008015|Rom. 8:15]]; [[@48004006|Gal. 4:6]]), and in each case is followed by its Greek equivalent, which is translated “father.” It is a term expressing warm affection and filial confidence. It has no perfect equivalent in our language.

column5: Father of Adoram, who was over forced labor
column7: The father of Adoniram, whom Solomon set over the tribute ([[@11004006|1 Kings 4:6]]); i.e., the forced labour (R.V., “levy”).

column5: Father of Shelemiah, an official under King Jehoiakim
column6: a vapor; a cloud of God
column7: Servant of God, ([[@24036026|Jer. 36:26]]), the father of Shelemiah.

column5: A Levite, ancestor of Ethan the musician
column7: Abdi, a Levite, was an ancestor of Ethan, one of the musicians appointed by David to serve in the temple.

column5: A Levite during Hezekiah's reign
column7: Abdi, a Levite, was the father of Kish and served during the reign of King Hezekiah.

column5: An Israelite who married a foreign wife
column7: Abdi, one of the descendants of Elam, was among those who agreed to put away their foreign wives during Ezra's time.

column5: A Gadite leader
column7: Servant of God, ([[@13005015|1 Chr. 5:15]]), a Gadite chief.

column5: A Levitical city in the territory of Asher.
column7: One of the “sons” of Shashak ([[@13008023|1 Chr. 8:23]]). This is the name also of a Levitical town of the Gershonites, in the tribe of Asher ([[@6021030|Josh. 21:30]]; [[@13006074|1 Chr. 6:74]]).

column5: A minor judge of Israel from Ephraim
column7: The son of Hillel, a Pirathonite, the tenth judge of Israel ([[@7012013-7012015|Judg. 12:13-15]]).

column5: A Benjamite, son of Shashak
column7: One of the “sons” of Shashak ([[@13008023|1 Chr. 8:23]]). This is the name also of a Levitical town of the Gershonites, in the tribe of Asher ([[@6021030|Josh. 21:30]]; [[@13006074|1 Chr. 6:74]]).

column5: Son of Abiel (or 'Jeiel') from Gibeon
column7: The first-born of Gibeon of the tribe of Benjamin ([[@13008030|1 Chr. 8:30]]; [[@13009036|1 Chr. 9:36]]).

column5: Adam and Eve's second son, killed by Cain
column7: (Heb. Hebhel), a breath, or vanity, the second son of Adam and Eve. He was put to death by his brother Cain ([[@1004001-1004016|Gen. 4:1-16]]). Guided by the instruction of their father, the two brothers were trained in the duty of worshipping God. “And in process of time” (marg. “at the end of days”, i.e., on the Sabbath) each of them offered up to God of the first-fruits of his labours.

column5: A large stone in the field of Joshua of Beth-shemesh.
column7: (Heb. Hebhel), a breath, or vanity, the second son of Adam and Eve. He was put to death by his brother Cain ([[@1004001-1004016|Gen. 4:1-16]]). Guided by the instruction of their father, the two brothers were trained in the duty of worshipping God. “And in process of time” (marg. “at the end of days”, i.e., on the Sabbath) each of them offered up to God of the first-fruits of his labours.

column5: A city in northern Israel, also called Abel-maim.
column7: (Heb. Hebhel), a breath, or vanity, the second son of Adam and Eve. He was put to death by his brother Cain ([[@1004001-1004016|Gen. 4:1-16]]). Guided by the instruction of their father, the two brothers were trained in the duty of worshipping God. “And in process of time” (marg. “at the end of days”, i.e., on the Sabbath) each of them offered up to God of the first-fruits of his labours.

column5: A place near Ammon, attacked by Jephthah.
column7: Abel-keramim, a town near Ammon, destroyed by Jephthah during his battles against the Ammonites.

column5: A town in Israel, home of Elisha.
column7: Meadow of dancing, or the dancing-meadow, the birth-place and residence of the prophet Elisha, not far from Beth-shean ([[@11004012|1 Kings 4:12]]), in the tribe of Issachar, near where the Wady el-Maleh emerges into the valley of the Jordan, “the rich meadow-land which extends about 4 miles south of Beth-shean; moist and luxuriant.” Here Elisha was found at his plough by Elijah on his return up the Jordan valley from Horeb ([[@11019016|1 Kings 19:16]]).

column5: Mother of King Hezekiah of Judah
column7: The daughter of Zechariah ([[@14029001|2 Chr. 29:1]]; comp. [[@23008002|Isa. 8:2]]), and afterwards the wife of Ahaz.

column5: One of David's mighty men, an Arbathite
column7: Father of strength; i.e., “valiant”, one of David’s body-guard of thirty mighty men ([[@10023031|2 Sam. 23:31]]); called also Abiel ([[@13011032|1 Chr. 11:32]]).

column5: Wife of Hezron, who gave birth after he died
column7: Abiah was the wife of Hezron who bore Ashhur after her husband's death.

column5: High priest during the reigns of David and Solomon
column6: excellent father; father of the remnant
column7: Father of abundance, or my father excels, the son of Ahimelech the high priest. He was the tenth high priest, and the fourth in descent from Eli. When his father was slain with the priests of Nob, he escaped, and bearing with him the ephod, he joined David, who was then in the cave of Adullam ([[@9022020-9022023|1 Sam. 22:20-23]]; [[@9023006|1 Sam. 23:6]]). He remained with David, and became priest of the party of which he was the leader ([[@9030007|1 Sam. 30:7]]).

column5: Son of Midian, grandson of Abraham
column7: Or Abi’dah, father of knowledge; knowing, one of the five sons of Midian, who was the son of Abraham by Keturah ([[@13001033|1 Chr. 1:33]]), and apparently the chief of an Arab tribe.

column5: Leader of the tribe of Benjamin during the Exodus
column7: Father of judgment; judge, head of the tribe of Benjamin at the Exodus ([[@4001011|Num. 1:11]]; [[@4002022|Num 2:22]]).

column5: Father of Kish and grandfather of King Saul
column7: The son of Zeror and father of Ner, who was the grandfather of Saul ([[@9014051|1 Sam. 14:51]]; [[@13008033|1 Chr. 8:33]]; [[@13009039|1 Chr. 9:39]]).

column5: Clan of Manasseh, home of Gideon
column7: Father of help, a descendant of Abiezer ([[@7006011|Judg. 6:11]], [[@7006024|Judg. 6:24]]; 8:32).

column5: One of David's mighty men, from Anathoth
column7: Abiezer the Anathothite was one of David's mighty men and served as a commander in his army.

column5: Son of Hammolecheth, from the tribe of Manasseh
column7: Abiezer, son of Hammolecheth, was a descendant of Manasseh and is mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe.

column5: Wife of Nabal, later married David
column7: The wife of the churlish Nabal, who dwelt in the district of Carmel ([[@9025003|1 Sam. 25:3]]). She showed great prudence and delicate management at a critical period of her husband’s life. She was “a woman of good understanding, and of a beautiful countenance.” After Nabal’s death she became the wife of David ([[@9025014-9025042|1 Sam. 25:14-42]]), and was his companion in all his future fortunes ([[@9027003|1 Sam. 27:3]]; [[@9030005|1 Sam. 30:5]]; [[@10002002|2 Sam. 2:2]]).

column5: Sister of David; mother of Amasa
column7: The sister of David, and wife of Jether an Ishmaelite ([[@13002016|1 Chr. 2:16]], [[@13002017|1 Chr. 2:17]]).

column5: Father of Zuriel, a Levite leader
column7: Abihail was the father of Zuriel, who was the leader of the Merarite clan of the Levites during the wilderness wanderings.

column5: Wife of Abishur; mother of Ahban and Molid
column7: Abihail was the wife of Abishur and the mother of Ahban and Molid, as mentioned in the genealogy of Judah.

column5: A Gadite leader from Gilead
column7: Abihail, a descendant of Guni, was a leader of the tribe of Gad who lived in Gilead.

column5: Mother of Rehoboam's wife Mahalath
column7: The second wife of King Rehoboam ([[@14011018|2 Chr. 11:18]]), a descendant of Eliab, David’s eldest brother.

column5: Father of Esther (Hadassah)
column7: The father of Esther and uncle of Mordecai ([[@17002015|Esther 2:15]]).

column5: Son of Aaron
column7: Father of Him; i.e., “worshipper of God”, the second of the sons of Aaron ([[@2006023|Ex. 6:23]]; [[@4003002|Num. 3:2]]; [[@4026060|Num 26:60]]; [[@13006003|1 Chr. 6:3]]). Along with his three brothers he was consecrated to the priest’s office ([[@2028001|Ex. 28:1]]). With his father and elder brother he accompanied the seventy elders part of the way up the mount with Moses ([[@2024001|Ex. 24:1]], [[@2024009|Ex 24:9]]).

column5: Son of Bela, a Benjaminite
column7: One of the sons of Bela, the son of Benjamin ([[@13008003|1 Chr. 8:3]]); called also Ahihud (ver. 7).

column5: Son of Samuel, a corrupt judge
column7: Abijah was one of Samuel's sons who served as a judge in Israel but did not follow his father's righteous ways.

column5: Son of Jeroboam I, died in childhood
column7: A son of Jeroboam, the first king of Israel. On account of his severe illness when a youth, his father sent his wife to consult the prophet Ahijah regarding his recovery. The prophet, though blind with old age, knew the wife of Jeroboam as soon as she approached, and under a divine impulse he announced to her that inasmuch as in Abijah alone of all the house of Jeroboam there was found “some good thing toward the Lord,” he only would come to his grave in peace.

column5: King of Judah, son of Rehoboam
column7: The son of Rehoboam, whom he succeeded on the throne of Judah ([[@13003010|1 Chr. 3:10]]). He is also called Abijam ([[@11014031|1 Kings 14:31]]; [[@11015001-11015008|1 Kings 15:1-8]]). He began his three years’ reign ([[@14012016|2 Chr. 12:16]]; [[@14013001|2 Chr. 13:1]], [[@14013002|2 Chr. 13:2]]) with a strenuous but unsuccessful effort to bring back the ten tribes to their allegiance. His address to “Jeroboam and all Israel,” before encountering them in battle, is worthy of being specially noticed ([[@14013005-14013012|2 Chr. 13:5-12]]).

column5: Son of Becher, a Benjaminite
column7: Abijah was a son of Becher and a descendant of Benjamin mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe.

column5: Head of a priestly division during David's reign
column7: A descendant of Eleazar, the son of Aaron, a chief of one of the twenty-four orders into which the priesthood was divided by David ([[@13024010|1 Chr. 24:10]]).

column5: Priest who sealed Nehemiah's covenant
column7: Abijah was one of the priests who sealed the covenant during Nehemiah's time and was also listed among the priests who returned from the Babylonian exile.

column5: A region ruled by Lysanias when John began preaching.
column7: A plain, a district lying on the east slope of the Anti-Lebanon range; so called from its chief town, Abila ([[@42003001|Luke 3:1]]), which stood in the Suk Wady Barada, between Heliopolis (Baalbec) and Damascus, 38 miles from the former and 18 from the latter.

column5: Descendant of Shem, son of Joktan
column7: Father of Mael, one of the sons or descendants of Joktan, in Northern Arabia ([[@1010028|Gen. 10:28]]; [[@13001022|1 Chr. 1:22]]).

column5: Philistine king who interacted with Abraham and Isaac
column7: A king of Gerar in the time of Isaac, probably the son of the preceeding ([[@1026001-1026022|Gen. 26:1-22]]). Isaac sought refuge in his territory during a famine, and there he acted a part with reference to his wife Rebekah similar to that of his father Abraham with reference to Sarah. Abimelech rebuked him for the deception, which he accidentally discovered. Isaac settled for a while here, and prospered.

column5: Son of Gideon, self-proclaimed king of Shechem
column7: A son of Gideon ([[@7009001|Judg. 9:1]]), who was proclaimed king after the death of his father ([[@7008033-7009006|Judg. 8:33-9:6]]). One of his first acts was to murder his brothers, seventy in number, “on one stone,” at Ophrah. Only one named Jotham escaped. He was an unprincipled, ambitious ruler, often engaged in war with his own subjects.

column5: Kept the ark of God in his house
column6: father of a vow, or of willingness
column7: A Levite of Kirjath-jearim, in whose house the ark of the covenant was deposited after having been brought back from the land of the Philistines ([[@9007001|1 Sam. 7:1]]).

column5: Son of King Saul, killed in battle
column6: father of a vow, or of willingness
column7: One of Saul’s sons, who peristed with his father in the battle of Gilboa ([[@9031002|1 Sam. 31:2]]; [[@13010002|1 Chr. 10:2]]).

column5: Son of Jesse, brother of David
column6: father of a vow, or of willingness
column7: The second of the eight sons of Jesse ([[@9016008|1 Sam. 16:8]]).

column5: Solomon's son-in-law, an official in his government
column6: father of a vow, or of willingness
column7: One of Solomon’s officers, who “provided victuals for the king and his household.”

column5: Father of Barak, the Israelite commander
column7: Father of kindness, the father of Barak ([[@7004006|Judg. 4:6]]; [[@7005001|Judg 5:1]]).

column5: Reubenite who rebelled against Moses and Aaron
column7: One of the sons of Eliab, who joined Korah in the conspiracy against Moses and Aaron.

column5: Firstborn son of Hiel the Bethelite
column7: The eldest son of Hiel the Bethelite, who perished prematurely in consequence of his father’s undertaking to rebuild Jericho ([[@11016034|1 Kings 16:34]]), according to the words of Joshua (6:26).

column5: Beautiful Shunammite who served King David
column7: Father of (i.e., “given to”) error, a young woman of Shunem, distinguished for her beauty. She was chosen to minister to David in his old age. She became his wife ([[@11001003|1 Kings 1:3]], [[@11001004|1 Kings 1:4]], [[@11001015|1 Kings 1:15]]). After David’s death Adonijah persuaded Bathsheba, Solomon’s mother, to entreat the king to permit him to marry Abishag.

column5: David's nephew, one of his mighty men and commanders
column7: Father of (i.e., “desirous of”) a gift, the eldest son of Zeruiah, David’s sister. He was the brother of Joab and Asahel ([[@10002018|2 Sam. 2:18]]; [[@13002016|1 Chr. 2:16]]). Abishai was the only one who accompanied David when he went to the camp of Saul and took the spear and the cruse of water from Saul’s bolster ([[@9026005-9026012|1 Sam. 26:5-12]]). He had the command of one of the three divisions of David’s army at the battle with Absalom ([[@10018002|2 Sam. 18:2]], [[@10018005|2 Sam. 18:5]], [[@10018012|2 Sam. 18:12]]).

column5: Son of Phinehas, grandson of Eleazar the high priest
Descendant of Benjamin, son of Bela
column7: Abishua was a descendant of Benjamin and one of the sons of Bela mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin.

column5: Son of Shammai, from the tribe of Judah
column6: father of the wall; father of uprightness
column7: Father of the wall; i.e., “mason”, one of the two sons of Shammai of the tribe of Judah ([[@13002028|1 Chr. 2:28]], [[@13002029|1 Chr. 2:29]]).

column5: One of David's wives; mother of Shephatiah
column6: the father of the dew; or of the shadow
column7: Father of dew; i.e., “fresh”, David’s fifth wife ([[@10003004|2 Sam. 3:4]]).

column5: Son of Shaharaim, a Benjaminite
column7: Father of goodness, a Benjamite ([[@13008011|1 Chr. 8:11]]).

column5: Saul's cousin and commander of his army
column7: Father of light; i.e., “enlightening”, the son of Ner and uncle of Saul. He was commander-in-chief of Saul’s army ([[@9014050|1 Sam. 14:50]]; [[@9017055|1 Sam. 17:55]]; [[@9020025|1 Sam. 20:25]]). He first introduced David to the court of Saul after the victory over Goliath ([[@9017057|1 Sam. 17:57]]). After the death of Saul, David was made king over Judah, and reigned in Hebron.

column5: Patriarch, chosen by God to father His people
column7: Father of a multitude, son of Terah, named ([[@1011027|Gen. 11:27]]) before his older brothers Nahor and Haran, because he was the heir of the promises. Till the age of seventy, Abram sojourned among his kindred in his native country of Chaldea. He then, with his father and his family and household, quitted the city of Ur, in which he had hitherto dwelt, and went some 300 miles north to Haran, where he abode fifteen years. The cause of his migration was a call from God ([[@44007002-44007004|Acts 7:2-4]]).

column5: A desert campsite during Israel's wilderness wanderings.
column7: R.V., one of Israel’s halting-places in the desert ([[@4033034|Num. 33:34]], [[@4033035|Num 33:35]]), just before Ezion-gaber.

column5: David's rebellious son who tried to usurp the throne.
column7: Father of peace; i.e., “peaceful” David’s son by Maacah ([[@10003003|2 Sam. 3:3]]; comp. [[@11001006|1 Kings 1:6]]). He was noted for his personal beauty and for the extra-ordinary profusion of the hair of his head ([[@10014025|2 Sam. 14:25]],[[@10014026|2 Sam. 14:26]]). The first public act of his life was the blood-revenge he executed against Amnon, David’s eldest son, who had basely wronged Absalom’s sister Tamar. This revenge was executed at the time of the festivities connected with a great sheep-shearing at Baal-hazor.

column5: An ancient city in Nimrod's kingdom, probably Akkad.
column7: The high land or mountains, a city in the land of Shinar. It has been identified with the mounds of Akker Kuf, some 50 miles to the north of Babylon; but this is doubtful. It was one of the cities of Nimrod’s kingdom ([[@1010010|Ge 10:10]]). It stood close to the Euphrates, opposite Sippara.

column5: A seaport in Asher, also called Ptolemais.
column7: Sultry or sandy, a town and harbour of Phoenicia, in the tribe of Asher, but never acquired by them ([[@7001031|Judg. 1:31]]). It was known to the ancient Greeks and Romans by the name of Ptolemais, from Ptolemy the king of Egypt, who rebuilt it about B.C. 100. Here Paul landed on his last journey to Jerusalem ([[@44021007|Acts 21:7]]).

column5: A Roman province in southern Greece, including Corinth.
column7: The name originally of a narrow strip of territory in Greece, on the north-west of the Peloponnesus. Subsequently it was applied by the Romans to the whole Peloponnesus, now called the Morea, and the south of Greece. It was then one of the two provinces (Macedonia being the other) into which they divided the country when it fell under their dominion. It is in this latter enlarged meaning that the name is always used in the New Testament ([[@44018012|Acts 18:12]], [[@44018027|Acts 18:27]]; [[@44019021|Acts 19:21]]; Rom. 15: 26; 16:5, etc.).

column5: A Corinthian Christian who visited Paul.
column6: a native of Achaia; sorrowing; sad
column7: Achaicus, along with Stephanas and Fortunatus, visited Paul from Corinth.

column5: An Israelite who stole devoted things, causing Israel's defeat.
column7: Called also Achar, i.e., one who troubles ([[@13002007|1 Chr. 2:7]]), in commemoration of his crime, which brought upon him an awful destruction ([[@6007001|Josh. 7:1]]). On the occasion of the fall of Jericho, he seized, contrary to the divine command, an ingot of gold, a quantity of silver, and a costly Babylonish garment, which he hid in his tent. Joshua was convinced that the defeat which the Israelites afterwards sustained before Ai was a proof of the divine displeasure on account of some crime, and he at once adopted means by the use of the lot for discovering the criminal.

column5: Edomite king, son of Baal-hanan
column7: Achbor was an Edomite king, the son of Baal-hanan, who reigned before the establishment of the Israelite monarchy.

column5: Official during the reign of King Josiah
column7: One of Josiah’s officers sent to the prophetess Huldah to inquire regarding the newly-discovered book of the law ([[@12022012|2 Kings 22:12]], [[@12022014|2 Kings 22:14]]).

column5: Philistine king of Gath, gave refuge to David
column6: thus it is; how is this
column7: The king with whom David sought refuge when he fled from Saul ([[@9021010-9021015|1 Sam. 21:10-15]]). He is called Abimelech in the superscription of Ps. 34. It was probably this same king to whom David a second time repaired at the head of a band of 600 warriors, and who assigned him Ziklag, whence he carried on war against the surrounding tribes ([[@9027005-9027012|1 Sam. 27:5-12]]).

column5: A valley near Jericho, where Achan was stoned.
column7: The Valley of Achor, where Achan was punished for his sin.

column5: Daughter of Caleb; wife of Othniel
column7: Anklet, Caleb’s only daughter ([[@13002049|1 Chr. 2:49]]). She was offered in marriage to the man who would lead an attack on the city of Debir, or Kirjath-sepher.

column5: Daughter of Caleb, the son of Hur
column7: Anklet, Caleb’s only daughter ([[@13002049|1 Chr. 2:49]]). She was offered in marriage to the man who would lead an attack on the city of Debir, or Kirjath-sepher.

column5: A Canaanite city-state conquered by Joshua.
column7: Fascination, a royal city of the Canaanites, in the north of Palestine ([[@6011001|Josh. 11:1]]; [[@6012020|Josh 12:20]]; [[@6019025|Josh 19:25]]).

column5: A town in Judah, birthplace of Shelah.
column7: A town in the Shephelah, or plain country of Judah ([[@6015044|Josh. 15:44]]); probably the same as Chezib of [[@1038005|Gen. 38:5]] = Ain Kezbeh.

column5: A coastal town allotted to Asher.
column7: A Phoenician city (the Gr. Ecdippa), always retained in their possession though assigned to the tribe of Asher ([[@6019029|Josh. 19:29]]; [[@7001031|Judg. 1:31]]).

column5: A town in the Negev region of Judah.
column7: Adadah, a town in the southernmost part of Judah.

column5: Wife of Lamech; mother of Jabal and Jubal
column7: The first of Lamech’s two wives, and the mother of Jabal and Jubal ([[@1004019|Gen. 4:19]], [[@1004020|Gen. 4:20]], [[@1004023|Gen. 4:23]]).

column5: Hittite wife of Esau; mother of Eliphaz
column7: The first of Esau’s three wives, the daughter of Elon the Hittite ([[@1036002|Gen. 36:2]], [[@1036004|Gen. 36:4]]), called also Bashemath (26:34).

column5: Father of Jedidah who was mother of King Josiah of Judah
column7: Adaiah of Bozkath's daughter Jedidah was the mother of King Josiah, who reigned over Judah and initiated significant religious reforms.

column5: A descendant of Benjamin
column7: Adaiah, a descendant of Benjamin, is mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin.

column5: Priest, descendant of Malchijah, during the post-exilic period
column7: Adaiah, a priest and descendant of Malchijah, served in the house of God during the post-exilic period in Jerusalem.

column5: Father of Maaseiah, during the reign of Joash
column7: Adaiah was the father of Maaseiah, one of the captains who supported Jehoiada the priest in overthrowing Athaliah and installing Joash as king of Judah.

column5: A leader who married a foreign wife
column7: Adaiah, one of the descendants of Bani, was among the men who had married foreign women during the time of Ezra.

column5: A priest who married a foreign wife
column7: Adaiah, one of the descendants of Harim, was a priest who had married a foreign woman during the time of Ezra.

column5: An ancestor of Maaseiah, a resident of Jerusalem
column7: Adaiah was an ancestor of Maaseiah, a leader who resided in Jerusalem during the time of Nehemiah.

column5: Son of Haman, enemy of the Jews
column7: Adalia was one of the ten sons of Haman, the enemy of the Jews, who was killed along with his brothers.

column5: The first man, created by God
column7: Red, a Babylonian word, the generic name for man, having the same meaning in the Hebrew and the Assyrian languages. It was the name given to the first man, whose creation, fall, and subsequent history and that of his descendants are detailed in the first book of Moses ([[@1001027|Gen. 1:27]]-ch. 5). “God created man [Heb., Adam] in his own image, in the image of God created he him; male and female created he them.” Adam was absolutely the first man whom God created.

column5: A city near the Jordan River.
column7: Red, a Babylonian word, the generic name for man, having the same meaning in the Hebrew and the Assyrian languages. It was the name given to the first man, whose creation, fall, and subsequent history and that of his descendants are detailed in the first book of Moses ([[@1001027|Gen. 1:27]]-ch. 5). “God created man [Heb., Adam] in his own image, in the image of God created he him; male and female created he them.” Adam was absolutely the first man whom God created.

column5: A fortified city allotted to Naphtali.
column7: Red earth, a fortified city of Naphtali, probably the modern Damieh, on the west side of the sea of Tiberias ([[@6019033|Josh. 19:33]], [[@6019036|Josh 19:36]]).

column5: A boundary marker for the territory of Naphtali.
column7: Adami-nekeb, a place marking the border of Naphtali's territory.

column5: Son of Ishmael, grandson of Abraham
column7: Miracle of God, the third of the twelve sons of Ishmael, and head of an Arabian tribe ([[@1025013|Gen. 25:13]]; [[@13001029|1 Chr. 1:29]]).

column5: A place from which some returned exiles came.
column7: Low, one of the persons named in [[@16007061|Neh. 7:61]] who could not “shew their father’s house” on the return from captivity.

column5: A boundary marker for the territory of Judah.
column7: Ample, splendid, son of Bela ([[@13008003|1 Chr. 8:3]]); called also “Ard” ([[@1046021|Gen. 46:21]])

column5: Son of Bela, a Benjaminite
column7: Ample, splendid, son of Bela ([[@13008003|1 Chr. 8:3]]); called also “Ard” ([[@1046021|Gen. 46:21]])

column5: An ancestor of Jesus Christ
column7: Ornament, ([[@42003028|Luke 3:28]]), the son of Cosam, and father of Melchi, one of the progenitors of Christ.

column5: Simeonite leader during the reign of Hezekiah
column7: A family head of the tribe of Simeon ([[@13004036|1 Chr. 4:36]]).

column5: A priest in Jerusalem during Nehemiah's time
column7: Adiel (also called Azarel) was a priest who served in Jerusalem during the time of Nehemiah.

column5: Overseer of King David's treasuries
column7: The father of Azmaveth, who was treasurer under David and Solomon ([[@13027025|1 Chr. 27:25]]).

column5: Jewish exile who returned to Jerusalem with Zerubbabel
column7: Adin was one of the Jewish exiles who returned to Jerusalem with Zerubbabel after the Babylonian captivity, as recorded in the lists of returnees in Ezra and Nehemiah.

column5: Jewish leader who signed Nehemiah's covenant
column7: Adin was one of the leaders of the people who signed the covenant of faithfulness to God during the time of Nehemiah.

column5: One of David's mighty men, a Reubenite leader
column7: Slender, one of David’s warriors ([[@13011042|1 Chr. 11:42]]), a Reubenite.

column5: Alternate name or description of Josheb-Basshebeth
column7: The Eznite, one of David’s mighty men ([[@10023008|2 Sam. 23:8]]).

column5: A town in the Shephelah region of Judah.
column7: Adithaim, a town allotted to Judah in the Shephelah.

column5: Overseer of King David's herds in the valleys
column7: Adlai was responsible for overseeing King David's herds that were pastured in the valleys.

column5: One of the cities destroyed with Sodom and Gomorrah.
column7: Earth, one of the five cities of the vale of Siddim ([[@1010019|Gen. 10:19]]). It was destroyed along with Sodom and Gomorrah (19:24; [[@5029023|Deut. 29:23]]). It is supposed by some to be the same as the Adam of [[@6003016|Josh. 3:16]], the name of which still lingers in Damieh, the ford of Jordan.

column5: One of the seven princes of Persia and Media
column6: a cloud of death; a mortal vapor
column7: Admatha was one of the seven princes of Persia and Media who had access to King Ahasuerus's presence and held the highest positions in the kingdom.

column5: Israelite who married a foreign woman during the exile
column7: Adna was one of the Israelites who had married foreign women during the Babylonian exile and pledged to put away his foreign wife as part of Ezra's reforms.

column5: Priest during the high priesthood of Joiakim
column7: Adna was a priest who served during the time of Joiakim, the son of Jeshua, the high priest who returned from the Babylonian exile.

column5: Manassite leader who joined David at Ziklag
column7: A chief of the tribe of Manasseh who joined David at Ziklag ([[@13012020|1 Chr. 12:20]]).

column5: Commander of 300,000 troops under King Jehoshaphat
column7: A general under Jehoshaphat, chief over 300,000 men ([[@14017014|2 Chr. 17:14]]).

column5: Canaanite king captured and mutilated by Judah
column6: the lightning of the Lord; the Lord of lightning
column7: Adoni-bezek was a Canaanite king who was defeated by the men of Judah, and had his thumbs and big toes cut off as he had done to seventy other kings.

column5: King of Jerusalem who fought against Joshua
column6: justice of the Lord; lord of justice
column7: Adoni-zedek, the king of Jerusalem, formed an alliance with other Amorite kings to fight against Joshua and the Israelites but was defeated and killed.

column5: Son of David who attempted to seize the throne
column7: The fourth son of David ([[@10003004|2 Sam. 3:4]]). After the death of his elder brothers, Amnon and Absalom, he became heir-apparent to the throne. But Solomon, a younger brother, was preferred to him. Adonijah, however, when his father was dying, caused himself to be proclaimed king. But Nathan and Bathsheba induced David to give orders that Solomon should at once be proclaimed and admitted to the throne.

column5: Levite sent by Jehoshaphat to teach the Law
column7: A Levite sent with the princes to teach the book of the law to the inhabitants of Judah ([[@14017008|2 Chr. 17:8]]).

column5: Levite who sealed the covenant with Nehemiah
column7: One of the “chiefs of the people” after the Captivity ([[@16010016|Neh. 10:16]]).

column5: Jewish exile whose descendants returned to Jerusalem
column7: Whom the Lord sets up, one of those “which came with Zerubbabel” ([[@15002013|Ezra 2:13]]).

column5: A fortified city built by Rehoboam in Judah.
column7: Adoraim, one of the cities fortified by King Rehoboam in Judah.

column5: Official in charge of forced labor under David and Solomon
column7: Adoram, also known as Adoniram or Hadoram, was an official in charge of forced labor during the reigns of David, Solomon, and Rehoboam.

column5: Assyrian god worshipped by Sepharvites in Samaria
column6: the cloak, glory, grandeur or power of the king
column7: An idol; a form of the sun-god worshipped by the inhabitants of Sepharvaim ([[@12017031|2 Kings 17:31]]), and brought by the Sepharvite colonists into Samaria.

column5: Son of Sennacherib who murdered his father
column6: the cloak, glory, grandeur or power of the king
column7: A son of Sennacherib, king of Assyria ([[@12019037|2 Kings 19:37]]; [[@23037038|Isa. 37:38]]).

column5: A seaport in Asia Minor, visited by Paul.
column7: A city of Asia Minor on the coast of Mysia, which in early times was called AEolis. The ship in which Paul embarked at Caesarea belonged to this city ([[@44027002|Acts 27:2]]). He was conveyed in it only to Myra, in Lycia, whence he sailed in an Alexandrian ship to Italy. It was a rare thing for a ship to sail from any port of Palestine direct for Italy.

column5: The sea where Paul's ship drifted during a storm.
column7: ([[@44027027|Acts 27:27]]; R.V., “the sea of Adria”), the Adriatic Sea, including in Paul’s time the whole of the Mediterranean lying between Crete and Sicily.

column5: Saul's son-in-law; husband of Merab
column7: Flock of God, the son of Barzillai, the Meholathite, to whom Saul gave in marriage his daughter Merab ([[@9018019|1 Sam. 18:19]]). The five sons that sprang from this union were put to death by the Gibeonites ([[@10021008|2 Sam. 21:8]], [[@10021009|2 Sam. 21:9]].

column5: A Canaanite city, later fortified by Judah.
column6: their testimony; their prey; their ornament
column7: One of the royal cities of the Canaanites, now ‘Aid-el-ma ([[@6012015|Josh. 12:15]]; [[@6015035|Josh 15:35]]). It stood on the old Roman road in the valley of Elah (q.v.), which was the scene of David’s memorable victory over Goliath ([[@9017002|1 Sam. 17:2]]), and not far from Gath. It was one of the towns which Rehoboam fortified against Egypt ([[@14011007|2 Chr. 11:7]]). It was called “the glory of Israel” ([[@33001015|Micah 1:15]]).

column5: A pass on the border between Judah and Benjamin.
column7: The red ones, a place apparently on the road between Jericho and Jerusalem, “on the south side of the torrent” Wady Kelt, looking toward Gilgal, mentioned [[@6015007|Josh. 15:7]]; [[@6018017|Josh 18:17]]. It was nearly half-way between Jerusalem and Jericho, and now bears the name of Tal-at-ed-Dumm. It is supposed to have been the place referred to in the parable of the Good Samaritan ([[@42010030-42010037|Luke 10:30-37]]).

column5: Paralyzed man in Lydda healed by Peter
column7: Aeneas, paralyzed for eight years, was healed by Peter in Lydda.

column5: A place near Salim where John the Baptist baptized.
column7: Springs, a place near Salim where John baptized ([[@43003023|John 3:23]]). It was probably near the upper source of the Wady Far’ah, an open valley extending from Mount Ebal to the Jordan. It is full of springs.

column5: Prophet who predicted famine and Paul's arrest
column6: a locust; the father's joy or feast
column7: A “prophet,” probably one of the seventy disciples of Christ. He prophesied at Antioch of an approaching famine ([[@44011027|Acts 11:27]], [[@44011028|Acts 11:28]]).

column5: King mentioned in Balaam's oracle about Israel
column7: A king of the Amalekites referred to by Balaam ([[@4024007|Num. 24:7]]).

column5: Amalekite king captured and killed by Samuel
column7: Another king of the Amalekites whom Saul spared unlawfully, but whom Samuel on his arrival in the camp of Saul ordered, in retributive justice (Judg. 1), to be brought out and cut in pieces ([[@9015008-9015033|1 Sam. 15:8-33]].

column5: Father of Shammah, one of David's mighty men
column7: Fugitive, the father of Shammah, who was one of David’s mighty men ([[@10023011|2 Sam. 23:11]])

column5: Tetrarch who heard Paul's defense in Caesarea
column6: one who causes great pain at his birth
column7: Tetrarch Agrippa heard Paul's defense and found no grounds for his imprisonment.

column5: Author of Proverbs 30, son of Jakeh
column7: Gatherer; the collector, mentioned as author of the sayings in Prov. 30.

column5: Wicked king of Israel; husband of Jezebel
column7: The son of Omri, whom he succeeded as the seventh king of Israel. His history is recorded in 1 Kings 16-22. His wife was Jezebel (q.v.), who exercised a very evil influence over him. To the calf-worship introduced by Jeroboam he added the worship of Baal. He was severely admonished by Elijah (q.v.) for his wickedness.

column5: False prophet during the Babylonian exile
column7: A false prophet referred to by Jeremiah ([[@24029021|Jer. 29:21]]), of whom nothing further is known.

column5: Son of Harum, from the tribe of Judah
column6: another host; the last sorrow; a brother's sheep
column7: Aharhel was a son of Harum, a descendant of Judah.

column5: Father of Eliphelet, one of David's mighty men
column6: trusting in me; a grown-up brother
column7: Ahasbai the Maachathite was the father of Eliphelet, one of David's mighty men.

column5: Persian Emperor (probably Xerxes I); husband of Esther
column7: The father of Darius the Mede, mentioned in [[@27009001|Dan. 9:1]].

column5: A place where Ezra assembled the returning exiles.
column7: Water, the river ([[@15008021|Ezra 8:21]]) by the banks of which the Jewish exiles assembled under Ezra when about to return to Jerusalem from Babylon. In all probability this was one of the streams of Mesopotamia which flowed into the Euphrates somewhere in the north-west of Babylonia.

column5: King of Judah, son of Jotham
column7: The son and successor of Jotham, king of Judah (2 Kings 16; Isa. 7-9; 2 Chr. 28). He gave himself up to a life of wickedness and idolatry. Notwithstanding the remonstrances and warnings of Isaiah, Hosea, and Micah, he appealed for help against Rezin, king of Damascus, and Pekah, king of Israel, who threatened Jerusalem, to Tiglath-pileser, the king of Assyria, to the great injury of his kingdom and his own humilating subjection to the Assyrians ([[@12016007|2 Kings 16:7]], [[@12016009|2 Kings 16:9]]; 15:29).

column5: Descendant of Saul and Jonathan
column7: Ahaz was a descendant of Saul and Jonathan, from the tribe of Benjamin.

column5: King of Israel, son of Ahab
column7: The son and successor of Ahab. He followed the counsels of his mother Jezebel, and imitated in wickedness the ways of his father. In his reign the Moabites revolted from under his authority ([[@12003005-12003007|2 Kings 3:5-7]]). He united with Jehoshaphat in an attempt to revive maritime trade by the Red Sea, which proved a failure ([[@14020035-14020037|2 Chr. 20:35-37]]).

column5: King of Judah, son of Jehoram and Athaliah
column7: The son of Joram, or Jehoram, and sixth king of Judah. Called Jehoahaz ([[@14021017|2 Chr. 21:17]]; [[@14025023|2 Chr. 25:23]]), and Azariah ([[@14022006|2 Chr. 22:6]]). Guided by his idolatrous mother Athaliah, his reign was disastrous ([[@12008024-12008029|2 Kings 8:24-29]]; [[@12009029|2 Kings 9:29]]). He joined his uncle Jehoram, king of Israel, in an expedition against Hazael, king of Damascus; but was wounded at the pass of Gur when attempting to escape, and had strength only to reach Megiddo, where he died ([[@12009022-12009028|2 Kings 9:22-28]]).

column5: Son of Abishur, from the tribe of Judah
column7: Ahban was the son of Abishur, a descendant of Judah.

column5: Son of Shemer, from the tribe of Asher
column7: Aher was a son of Shemer, a descendant of Asher.

column5: Son of Abdiel, a Gadite chief
column7: Ahi, son of Abdiel, was a chief of the Gadites.

column5: Son of Shomer, from the tribe of Asher
column7: Ahi (or "brother") was a son of Shomer (or 'Shamer'), a descendant of Asher.

column5: Priest who sealed the covenant with Nehemiah
column7: Ahiah was a priest who sealed the covenant during Nehemiah's time.

column5: One of David's mighty men, son of Sharar
column6: mother's brother; brother of a nation
column7: Mother’s brother, one of David’s thirty heroes ([[@10023033|2 Sam. 23:33]]; [[@13011035|1 Chr. 11:35]]).

column5: Son of Shemidah, from the tribe of Manasseh
column7: Ahian was a son of Shemidah, a descendant of Manasseh.

column5: Leader from the tribe of Dan during the Exodus
column7: The chief of the tribe of Dan at the time of the Exodus ([[@4001012|Num. 1:12]]; [[@4002025|Num 2:25]]; [[@4010025|Num 10:25]]).

column5: Benjamite warrior who joined David at Ziklag
column7: The chief of the Benjamite slingers that repaired to David at Ziklag ([[@13012003|1 Chr. 12:3]]).

column5: Leader from the tribe of Asher for land allocation
column6: brother of vanity, or of darkness, or of joy, or of praise;  witty brother
column7: Name different in Hebrew, meaning brother of Judah.

column5: Son of Ehud, from the tribe of Benjamin
column6: brother of vanity, or of darkness, or of joy, or of praise;  witty brother
column7: A son of Bela, the son of Benjamin ([[@13008007|1 Chr. 8:7]]).

column5: Son of Seraiah (or 'Shisha'), a scribe during Solomon's reign
column7: Ahijah, son of Seraiah (or 'Shisha'), served as a scribe during King Solomon's reign.

column5: Prophet from Shiloh who prophesied to Jeroboam
column7: A prophet of Shiloh ([[@11011029|1 Kings 11:29]]; [[@11014002|1 Kings 14:2]]), called the “Shilonite,” in the days of Rehoboam. We have on record two of his remarkable prophecies, [[@11011031-11011039|1 Kings 11:31-39]], announcing the rending of the ten tribes from Solomon; and [[@11014006-11014016|1 Kings 14:6-16]], delivered to Jeroboam’s wife, foretelling the death of Abijah the king’s son, the destruction of Jeroboam’s house, and the captivity of Israel “beyond the river.”

column5: Father of Baasha, king of Israel
column7: Ahijah was the father of Baasha, who became king of Israel and ruled for 24 years.

column5: Son of Jerahmeel, from the tribe of Judah
column7: One of the five sons of Jerahmeel, who was great-grandson of Judah ([[@13002025|1 Chr. 2:25]]).

column5: Son of Ehud, from the tribe of Benjamin
column7: One of the sons of Bela ([[@13008007|1 Chr. 8:7]], R.V.).

column5: One of David's mighty men, the Pelonite
column7: A Pelonite, one of David’s heroes ([[@13011036|1 Chr. 11:36]]); called also Eliam ([[@10023034|2 Sam. 23:34]]).

column5: Levite in charge of the treasuries of the temple
column7: A Levite having charge of the sacred treasury in the temple ([[@13026020|1 Chr. 26:20]]).

column5: Son of Shaphan, protected Jeremiah from death
column6: a brother who raises up or avenges
column7: Brother of support = helper, one of the five whom Josiah sent to consult the prophetess Huldah in connection with the discovery of the book of the law ([[@12022012-12022014|2 Kings 22:12-14]]; [[@14034020|2 Chr. 34:20]]). He was the son of Shaphan, the royal secretary, and the father of Gedaliah, governor of Judea after the destruction of Jerusalem by the Babylonians ([[@12025022|2 Kings 25:22]]; [[@24040005-24040016|Jer. 40:5-16]]; [[@24043006|Jer 43:6]]). On one occasion he protected Jeremiah against the fury of Jehoiakim ([[@24026024|Jer. 26:24]]).

column5: Father of Jehoshaphat and Baana, officials under David and Solomon
column7: Ahilud was the father of Jehoshaphat, David's recorder, and Baana, one of Solomon's twelve district governors.

column5: Father of Saul's wife Ahinoam
column7: The father Ahinoam, the wife of Saul ([[@9014050|1 Sam. 14:50]]).

column5: Son of Zadok the priest, a messenger for David
column7: The son and successor of Zadok in the office of high priest ([[@13006008|1 Chr. 6:8]], [[@13006053|1 Chr. 6:53]]). On the occasion of the revolt of Absalom he remained faithful to David, and was of service to him in conveying to him tidings of the proceedings of Absalom in Jerusalem ([[@10015024-10015037|2 Sam. 15:24-37]]; [[@10017015-10017021|2 Sam. 17:15-21]]).

column5: Solomon's son-in-law, governor of Naphtali
column7: Ahimaaz, who was married to Solomon's daughter Basemath, served as the governor of Naphtali during Solomon's reign.

column5: One of the giant descendants of Anak in Hebron
column7: One of the three giant Anakim brothers whom Caleb and the spies saw in Mount Hebron ([[@4013022|Num. 13:22]]) when they went in to explore the land.

column5: Levite gatekeeper during David's reign
column7: One of the guardians of the temple after the Exile ([[@13009017|1 Chr. 9:17]]).

column5: High Priest at Nob who helped David, killed by Saul
column6: my brother is a king; my king's brother
column7: Brother of the king, the son of Ahitub and father of Abiathar ([[@9022020-9022023|1 Sam. 22:20-23]]). He descended from Eli in the line of Ithamar. In [[@13018016|1 Chr. 18:16]] he is called Abimelech, and is probably the same as Ahiah ([[@9014003|1 Sam. 14:3]], [[@9014018|1 Sam. 14:18]]). He was the twelfth high priest, and officiated at Nob, where he was visited by David (to whom and his companions he gave five loaves of the showbread) when he fled from Saul ([[@9021001-9021009|1 Sam. 21:1-9]]).

column5: Son of Ahitub, a Hittite warrior who joined David
column6: my brother is a king; my king's brother
column7: Brother of the king, the son of Ahitub and father of Abiathar ([[@9022020-9022023|1 Sam. 22:20-23]]). He descended from Eli in the line of Ithamar. In [[@13018016|1 Chr. 18:16]] he is called Abimelech, and is probably the same as Ahiah ([[@9014003|1 Sam. 14:3]], [[@9014018|1 Sam. 14:18]]). He was the twelfth high priest, and officiated at Nob, where he was visited by David (to whom and his companions he gave five loaves of the showbread) when he fled from Saul ([[@9021001-9021009|1 Sam. 21:1-9]]).

column5: Son of Abiathar, a priest during David's reign
column6: my brother is a king; my king's brother
column7: Brother of the king, the son of Ahitub and father of Abiathar ([[@9022020-9022023|1 Sam. 22:20-23]]). He descended from Eli in the line of Ithamar. In [[@13018016|1 Chr. 18:16]] he is called Abimelech, and is probably the same as Ahiah ([[@9014003|1 Sam. 14:3]], [[@9014018|1 Sam. 14:18]]). He was the twelfth high priest, and officiated at Nob, where he was visited by David (to whom and his companions he gave five loaves of the showbread) when he fled from Saul ([[@9021001-9021009|1 Sam. 21:1-9]]).

column5: Levite descendant of Kohath, son of Elkanah
column7: A Kohathite Levite, father of Elkanah ([[@13006035|1 Chr. 6:35]]).

column5: Son of Iddo, a governor under Solomon
column6: a willing brother; brother of a vow
column7: Brother of liberality = liberal, one of the twelve commissariat officers appointed by Solomon in so many districts of his kingdom to raise supplies by monthly rotation for his household.

column5: Wife of King Saul, daughter of Ahimaaz
column6: beauty of the brother; brother of motion
column7: The daughter of Ahimaaz, and wife of Saul ([[@9014050|1 Sam. 14:50]]).

column5: Wife of David, from Jezreel; mother of Amnon
column6: beauty of the brother; brother of motion
column7: A Jezreelitess, the first wife of David ([[@9025043|1 Sam. 25:43]]; [[@9027003|1 Sam. 27:3]]). She was the mother of Amnon ([[@10003002|2 Sam. 3:2]]).

column5: Son of Abinadab, accompanied the ark from Kiriath-jearim
column7: One of the sons of Abinadab the Levite.

column5: Son of Beriah, a Benjamite
column7: Ahio was a son of Elpaal and a descendant of Benjamin.

column5: Son of Abiel (or 'Jeiel'), a Benjamite
column7: One of the sons of Jehiel the Gibeonite ([[@13008031|1 Chr. 8:31]]; [[@13009037|1 Chr. 9:37]]).

column5: Leader of the tribe of Naphtali during the Exodus
column6: brother of iniquity; brother of the shepherd
column7: Brother of evil = unlucky, or my brother is friend, chief of the tribe of Naphtali at the Exodus ([[@4001015|Num. 1:15]]; [[@4002029|Num 2:29]]).

column5: Son of Benjamin, founder of the Ahiramite clan
column6: brother of craft, or of protection
column7: Ahiram, also known as Aharah or Ehi, was a son of Benjamin and the founder of the Ahiramite clan.

column5: Father of Oholiab, a skilled artisan for the tabernacle
column7: Ahisamach, from the tribe of Dan, was the father of Oholiab, a skilled artisan who helped construct the tabernacle.

column5: Son of Bilhan, a Benjamite
column7: Ahishahar was a son of Bilhan and a descendant of Benjamin.

column5: In charge of Solomon's palace
column6: brother of a prince; brother of a song
column7: Brother of song = singer, the officer who was “over the household” of Solomon ([[@11004006|1 Kings 4:6]]).

column5: David's counselor who joined Absalom's rebellion, later committed suicide
column7: Brother of insipidity or impiety, a man greatly renowned for his sagacity among the Jews. At the time of Absalom’s revolt he deserted David ([[@19041009|Ps. 41:9]]; [[@19055012-19055014|Ps 55:12-14]]) and espoused the cause of Absalom ([[@10015012|2 Sam. 15:12]]). David sent his old friend Hushai back to Absalom, in order that he might counteract the counsel of Ahithophel ([[@10015031-10015037|2 Sam. 15:31-37]]).

column5: Father of Ahimelech, High Priest at Nob killed by Saul
column7: Ahitub was the father of Ahimelech, the High Priest at Nob who was killed by Saul for aiding David.

column5: Father of Zadok the priest during David's reign
column7: The father of Zadok, who was made high priest by Saul after the extermination of the family of Ahimelech ([[@13006007|1 Chr. 6:7]], [[@13006008|1 Chr. 6:8]]; [[@10008017|2 Sam. 8:17]]).

column5: Ancestor of Ezra the scribe, in the priestly line
column7: Ahitub, son of Amariah and father of Zadok, was an ancestor of Ezra the scribe in the priestly line.

column5: A Canaanite city allotted to Asher.
column6: made of milk, or of fat; brother of the heart
column7: Fatness, a town of Asher lying within the unconquered Phoenician border ([[@7001031|Judg. 1:31]]), north-west of the Sea of Galilee; commonly identified with Giscala, now el-Jish.

column5: Daughter of Sheshan, a Jerahmeelite
column7: Ahlai was the daughter of Sheshan, a descendant of Jerahmeel, from the tribe of Judah.

column5: Father of Zabad, one of David's mighty men
column7: Ahlai was the father of Zabad, who was one of David's mighty men.

column5: Descendant of Benjamin, clan of David's mighty men
column6: a live brother; my thorn or thistle
column7: Brotherly, one of the sons of Bela, the son of Benjamin ([[@13008004|1 Chr. 8:4]]). He is also called Ahiah (ver. 7) and Iri ([[@13007007|1 Chr. 7:7]]).

column5: Descendant of Judah through Reaiah
column6: a meadow of waters; a brother of waters
column7: Ahumai was a descendant of Judah through his grandson Reaiah.

column5: Son of Ashhur and Naarah, a Judahite
column7: Ahuzzam was the son of Ashhur and his wife Naarah, from the tribe of Judah.

column5: Friend and advisor of Abimelech, Philistine king of Gerar
column7: Ahuzzath was a friend and advisor of Abimelech, the Philistine king of Gerar, who accompanied him when making a treaty with Isaac.

column5: A Canaanite city conquered by Joshua after initial defeat.
column7: One of the royal cities of the Canaanites ([[@6010001|Josh. 10:1]]; [[@1012008|Gen. 12:8]]; [[@1013003|Gen 13:3]]). It was the scene of Joshua’s defeat, and afterwards of his victory. It was the second Canaanite city taken by Israel ([[@6007002-6007005|Josh. 7:2-5]]; [[@6008001-6008029|Josh 8:1-29]]). It lay rebuilt and inhibited by the Benjamites ([[@15002028|Ezra 2:28]]; [[@16007032|Neh. 7:32]]; [[@16011031|Neh 11:31]]).

column5: An Ammonite city, to be destroyed by Babylon.
column7: A city in the Ammonite territory ([[@24049003|Jer. 49:3]]).

column5: Son of Zibeon the Hivite, brother of Anah
column6: vulture, raven; an isle; alas, where is it?
column7: Aiah was the son of Zibeon the Hivite and the brother of Anah, who was a descendant of Esau.

column5: Father of Rizpah, Saul's concubine
column6: vulture, raven; an isle; alas, where is it?
column7: Aiah was the father of Rizpah, who was a concubine of King Saul.

column5: A Levitical city in Dan, site of Joshua's miracle.
column7: A town and valley originally assigned to the tribe of Dan, from which, however, they could not drive the Amorites ([[@7001035|Judg. 1:35]]). It was one of the Levitical cities given to the Kohathites ([[@13006069|1 Chr. 6:69]]). It was not far from Beth-shemesh ([[@14028018|2 Chr. 28:18]]). It was the boundary between the kingdoms of Judah and Israel, and is frequently mentioned in Jewish history ([[@14011010|2 Chr. 11:10]]; [[@9014031|1 Sam. 14:31]]; [[@13008013|1 Chr. 8:13]]).

column5: A place on the eastern boundary of the Promised Land.
column7: Ain or Rimmon, a location marking the eastern border of Israel's territory.

column5: A city in Judah, allotted to the Levites.
column7: Ain or En-rimmon, a city in Judah's Negev region, given to the Levites.

column5: Son of Ezer, a Horite chief in Seir
column7: Akan was the son of Ezer, a Horite chief who lived in the land of Seir.

column5: Field purchased with Judas' betrayal money; burial place for strangers
column7: The name which the Jews gave in their proper tongue, i.e., in Aramaic, to the field which was purchased with the money which had been given to the betrayer of our Lord. The word means “field of blood.” It was previously called “the potter’s field” ([[@40027007|Matt. 27:7]], [[@40027008|Matt. 27:8]]; [[@44001019|Acts 1:19]]), and was appropriated as the burial-place for strangers. It lies on a narrow level terrace on the south face of the valley of Hinnom.

column5: Descendant of King Jehoiachin of Judah
column7: Akkub was a descendant of King Jehoiachin of Judah, listed in the genealogy of the royal line.

column5: Levite gatekeeper during the post-exilic period
column7: A Levite who kept the gate of the temple after the return from Babylon ([[@13009017|1 Chr. 9:17]]; [[@15002042|Ezra 2:42]]; [[@16007045|Neh. 7:45]]).

column5: Family head of Temple servants who returned from exile
column7: The head of one of the families of Nethinim ([[@15002045|Ezra 2:45]]).

column5: Levite who helped explain the Law to the people
column7: Akkub was a Levite who assisted Ezra in explaining the Law to the people during the public reading.

column5: A pass marking the southern border of Judah
column7: Scorpions, probably the general name given to the ridge containing the pass between the south of the Dead Sea and Zin, es-Sufah, by which there is an ascent to the level of the land of Palestine. Scorpions are said to abound in this whole district, and hence the name ([[@4034004|Num. 34:4]]).

column5: A Levitical city in Benjamin
column6: hiding; youth; worlds; upon the dead
column7: A sacerdotal city of Benjamin ([[@13006060|1 Chr. 6:60]]), called also Almon ([[@6021018|Josh. 21:18]]), now Almit, a mile north-east of the ancient Anathoth.

column5: Son of Becher, a Benjamite
column6: hiding; youth; worlds; upon the dead
column7: One of the nine sons of Becher, the son of Benjamin ([[@13007008|1 Chr. 7:8]]).

column5: Son of Jehoaddah, a Benjamite from Gibeon
column6: hiding; youth; worlds; upon the dead
column7: One of the sons of Jehoadah, or Jarah, son of Ahaz ([[@13008036|1 Chr. 8:36]]).

column5: Son of Simon who carried the cross
column7: A man whose father, Simon the Cyrenian, bore the cross of Christ ([[@41015021|Mark 15:21]]).

column5: Member of the high-priestly family in Jerusalem
column7: A relative of Annas the high priest, present when Peter and John were examined before the Sanhedrim ([[@44004006|Acts 4:6]]).

column5: Opponent of Paul, along with Hymenaeus
column7: A coppersmith who, with Hymenaeus and others, promulgated certain heresies regarding the resurrection ([[@54001019|1 Tim. 1:19]]; [[@55004014|2 Tim. 4:14]]), and made shipwreck of faith and of a good conscience.

column5: A major city in Egypt
column7: The ancient metropolis of Lower Egypt, so called from its founder, Alexander the Great (about B.C. 333). It was for a long period the greatest of existing cities, for both Nineveh and Babylon had been destroyed, and Rome had not yet risen to greatness. It was the residence of the kings of Egypt for 200 years. It is not mentioned in the Old Testament, and only incidentally in the New.

column5: A town allotted to Asher
column7: Allammelech, a town allotted to the tribe of Asher.

column5: A boundary marker for the territory of Naphtali.
column7: The expression in the Authorized Version of [[@6019033|Josh. 19:33]], “from Allon to Zaanannim,” is more correctly rendered in the Revised Version, “from the oak in Zaanannim.”

column5: Son of Jedaiah, a Simeonite
column7: The son of Jedaiah, of the family of the Simeonites, who expelled the Hamites from the valley of Gedor ([[@13004037|1 Chr. 4:37]]).

column5: The burial place of Deborah, Rebekah's nurse.
column7: Oak of weeping, a tree near Bethel, at the spot where Deborah, Rebekah’s nurse, was buried ([[@1035008|Gen. 35:8]]). Large trees, from their rarity in the plains of Palestine, were frequently designated as landmarks.

column5: Son of Joktan, descendant of Shem
column7: Immeasurable, the first named of the sons of Joktan ([[@1010026|Gen. 10:26]]), the founder of an Arabian tribe.

column5: Father of apostles James and Matthew (Levi)
column7: The father of James the Less, the apostle and writer of the epistle ([[@40010003|Matt. 10:3]]; [[@41003018|Mark 3:18]]; [[@42006015|Luke 6:15]]; [[@44001013|Acts 1:13]]), and the husband of Mary ([[@43019025|John 19:25]]).

The altar of burnt offering ([[@2030028|Ex. 30:28]]), called also the “brasen altar” ([[@2039039|Ex. 39:39]]) and “the table of the Lord” ([[@39001007|Mal. 1:7]]). This altar, as erected in the tabernacle, is described in [[@2027001-2027008|Ex. 27:1-8]]. It was a hollow square, 5 cubits in length and in breadth, and 3 cubits in height. It was made of shittim wood, and was overlaid with plates of brass.

column5: A campsite during Israel's wilderness journey.
column7: One of the places, the last before Rephidim, at which the Hebrews rested on their way to Sinai ([[@4033013|Num. 33:13]], [[@4033014|Num. 33:14]]).

column5: Edomite chief, descendant of Esau
column7: Alvah was an Edomite chief, a descendant of Esau through his son Eliphaz.

column5: Horite chief, descendant of Seir
column7: Alvan was a Horite chief, a descendant of Seir, who lived in the land of Edom before Esau's descendants.

column5: A border town in the territory of Asher.
column7: Amad, a town on the boundary of Asher's territory.

column5: Son of Helem, an Asherite
column7: Amal was a son of Helem, a descendant of Asher, and is listed in the genealogy of the tribe of Asher.

column5: A nomadic people, descendants of Esau, enemies of Israel.
column7: Dweller in a valley, the son of Eliphaz and grandson of Esau ([[@1036012|Gen. 36:12]]; [[@13001036|1 Chr. 1:36]]); the chief of an Idumean tribe ([[@1036016|Gen. 36:16]]).

column5: Grandson of Esau, ancestor of the Amalekites
column7: Dweller in a valley, the son of Eliphaz and grandson of Esau ([[@1036012|Gen. 36:12]]; [[@13001036|1 Chr. 1:36]]); the chief of an Idumean tribe ([[@1036016|Gen. 36:16]]).

column5: A town allotted to the tribe of Judah.
column7: Amam, a town in the Negev region of Judah.

column5: A mountain range mentioned in the Song of Solomon.
column7: A mountain ([[@22004008|Cant. 4:8]]), probably the southern summit of Anti-Libanus, at the base of which are the sources of the Abana.

column5: Ancestor of Zadok the priest, in Aaron's line
column6: the Lord says; the integrity of the Lord
column7: One of the descendants of Aaron by Eleazar ([[@13006007|1 Chr. 6:7]], [[@13006052|1 Chr. 6:52]]).

column5: Levite, descendant of Hebron, during David's reign
column6: the Lord says; the integrity of the Lord
column7: A Levite, son of Hebron, of the lineage of Moses ([[@13023019|1 Chr. 23:19]]; [[@13024023|1 Chr. 24:23]]).

column5: Chief priest under King Jehoshaphat of Judah
column6: the Lord says; the integrity of the Lord
column7: A “chief priest” who took an active part in the reformation under Jehoshaphat ([[@14019011|2 Chr. 19:11]]); probably the same as mentioned in [[@13006009|1 Chr. 6:9]].

column5: Levite during the reign of King Hezekiah
column6: the Lord says; the integrity of the Lord
column7: One of the high priests in the time of Hezekiah ([[@14031015|2 Chr. 31:15]]).

column5: High priest, ancestor of Ezra the scribe
column6: the Lord says; the integrity of the Lord
column7: Amariah was a high priest during the reign of Jehoshaphat and an ancestor of Ezra the scribe.

column5: Israelite who agreed to put away his foreign wife
column6: the Lord says; the integrity of the Lord
column7: Amariah was one of the Israelites who had married a foreign woman and agreed to put her away during Ezra's reforms.

column5: Priest who sealed Nehemiah's covenant and served as chief priest
column6: the Lord says; the integrity of the Lord
column7: Amariah was a priest who sealed Nehemiah's covenant and later served as a chief priest during the high priesthood of Joiakim.

column5: Judahite who resettled in Jerusalem
column6: the Lord says; the integrity of the Lord
column7: Amariah, a descendant of Judah through Perez, was among those chosen to resettle in Jerusalem during Nehemiah's time.

column5: Ancestor of Zephaniah the prophet
column6: the Lord says; the integrity of the Lord
column7: Amariah was an ancestor of Zephaniah the prophet, who prophesied during the reign of King Josiah of Judah.

column5: Military commander, son of Abigail (David's sister), killed by Joab
column7: The son of Abigail, a sister of king David ([[@13002017|1 Chr. 2:17]]; [[@10017025|2 Sam. 17:25]]).

column5: Ephraimite leader who opposed enslaving Judahite captives
column7: A son of Hadlai, and chief of Ephraim ([[@14028012|2 Chr. 28:12]]) in the reign of Ahaz.

column5: Levite descendant of Kohath
column7: A Levite, son of Elkanah, of the ancestry of Samuel ([[@13006025|1 Chr. 6:25]], [[@13006035|1 Chr. 6:35]]).

column5: Chief of thirty who joined David
column7: The leader of a body of men who joined David in the “stronghold,” probably of Adullam ([[@13012018|1 Chr. 12:18]]).

column5: Priest who blew the trumpet
column7: One of the priests appointed to precede the ark with blowing of trumpets on its removal from the house of Obed-edom ([[@13015024|1 Chr. 15:24]]).

column5: Levite who helped purify the temple
column7: The father of a Levite, one of the two Kohathites who took a prominent part at the instance of Hezekiah in the cleansing of the temple ([[@14029012|2 Chr. 29:12]]).

column5: Commander who volunteered for God's service
column7: Burden of (i.e., “sustained by”) Jehovah, the “son of Zichri, who willingly offered himself unto the Lord,” a captain over thousands under Jehoshaphat ([[@14017016|2 Chr. 17:16]]; comp. [[@7005009|Judg. 5:9]]).

column5: A place near the Euphrates River, associated with Balaam.
column7: Amaw, a place near the Euphrates, where Balaam son of Beor lived.

column5: King of Judah, son of Joash
column7: The son and successor of Joash, and eighth king of the separate kingdom of Judah ([[@12014001-12014004|2 Kings 14:1-4]]). He began his reign by punishing the murderers of his father (5-7; [[@14025003-14025005|2 Chr. 25:3-5]]). He was the first to employ a mercenary army of 100,000 Israelite soldiers, which he did in his attempt to bring the Edomites again under the yoke of Judah ([[@14025005|2 Chr. 25:5]], [[@14025006|2 Chr. 25:6]]).

column5: Simeonite, son of Joshah
column7: The father of Joshah, one of the Simeonite chiefs in the time of Hezekiah ([[@13004034|1 Chr. 4:34]]).

column5: Levite, son of Hilkiah
column7: A Levite, son of Hilkiah, of the descendants of Ethan the Merarite ([[@13006045|1 Chr. 6:45]]).

column5: Priest of Bethel during Amos' ministry
column7: A priest of the golden calves at Bethel ([[@30007010-30007017|Amos 7:10-17]]).

This Hebrew word means firm, and hence also faithful ([[@66003014|Rev. 3:14]]). In [[@23065016|Isa. 65:16]], the Authorized Version has “the God of truth,” which in Hebrew is “the God of Amen.” It is frequently used by our Saviour to give emphasis to his words, where it is translated “verily.” Sometimes, only, however, in John’s Gospel, it is repeated, “Verily, verily.”

column5: Family of Solomon's servants
column7: The descendants of Ami (or Amon) were among the returned exiles who were servants of Solomon.

column5: Father of the prophet Jonah
column7: True, the father of Jonah the prophet, a native of Gath-hepher ([[@12014025|2 Kings 14:25]]; [[@32001001|Jonah 1:1]]).

column5: A hill near Gibeon, where Joab pursued Abner.
column7: A cubit, the name of a hill which Joab and Abishai reached as the sun went down, when they were in pursuit of Abner ([[@10002024|2 Sam. 2:24]]).

column5: Spy from the tribe of Dan
column7: One of the twelve spies sent by Moses to search the land of Canaan ([[@4013012|Num. 13:12]]).

column5: Father of Machir, David's ally
column7: The father of Machir of Lo-debar, in whose house Mephibosheth resided ([[@10009004|2 Sam. 9:4]], [[@10009005|2 Sam. 9:5]]; 17:27).

column5: Levite gatekeeper during David's reign
column7: One of the sons of Obed-edom the Levite ([[@13026005|1 Chr. 26:5]]).

column5: Father of Elishama, leader of Ephraim
column7: The father of the Ephraimite chief Elishama, at the time of the Exodus ([[@4001010|Num. 1:10]]; [[@4002018|Num 2:18]]; [[@4007048|Num 7:48]], [[@4007053|Num 7:53]]).

column5: Father of Shemuel, leader from Simeon
column7: Ammihud was the father of Shemuel, the leader from the tribe of Simeon appointed to help divide the land of Canaan.

column5: Father of Pedahel, leader from Naphtali
column7: Ammihud was the father of Pedahel, the leader from the tribe of Naphtali appointed to help divide the land of Canaan.

column5: Father of Talmai, king of Geshur
column7: The father of Talmai, king of Geshur, to whom Absalom fled after the murder of Amnon ([[@10013037|2 Sam. 13:37]]).

column5: Descendant of Judah living in Jerusalem
column7: The son of Omri, and the father of Uthai ([[@13009004|1 Chr. 9:4]]).

column5: Father-in-law of Aaron, ancestor of David
Levite leader during the Ark's transfer
column7: Chief of the 112 descendants of Uzziel the Levite ([[@13015010|1 Chr. 15:10]], [[@13015011|1 Chr. 15:11]]).

column5: Noble mentioned in a love song
column7: A person mentioned in [[@22006012|Cant. 6:12]], whose chariots were famed for their swiftness.

column5: Father of Ahiezer, leader of Dan
column6: the people of the Almighty; the Almighty is with me
column7: People of the Almighty, the father of Ahiezer, who was chief of the Danites at the time of the Exodus ([[@4001012|Num. 1:12]]; [[@4002025|Num 2:25]]).

column5: Son of Benaiah, one of David's mighty men
column7: People of the giver, the son of Benaiah, who was the third and chief captain of the host under David ([[@13027006|1 Chr. 27:6]]).

column5: An ancient nation and its capital city, enemies of Israel.
column6: a people; the son of my people
column7: Another form of the name Ben-ammi, the son of Lot ([[@1019038|Gen. 19:38]]).

column5: David's firstborn son, killed by Absalom
column7: The eldest son of David, by Ahinoam of Jezreel ([[@13003001|1 Chr. 3:1]]; [[@10003002|2 Sam. 3:2]]).

column5: Son of Shimon, descendant of Judah
column7: One of the sons of Shammai, of the children of Ezra ([[@13004020|1 Chr. 4:20]]; comp. 17).

column5: Priest who returned from Babylonian exile
column7: Amok was a priest who returned from the Babylonian exile and signed the covenant under Nehemiah.

column5: Governor of Samaria during Ahab's reign
column7: The governor of Samaria in the time of Ahab.

column5: King of Judah, son of Manasseh
column7: The son of Manasseh, and fourteenth king of Judah. He restored idolatry, and set up the images which his father had cast down. Zephaniah (1:4; 3:4, 11) refers to the moral depravity prevailing in this king’s reign.

column5: Canaanite people group, enemies of Israel
column7: Highlanders, or hillmen, the name given to the descendants of one of the sons of Canaan ([[@1014007|Gen. 14:7]]), called Amurra or Amurri in the Assyrian and Egyptian inscriptions. On the early Babylonian monuments all Syria, including Palestine, is known as “the land of the Amorites.” The southern slopes of the mountains of Judea are called the “mount of the Amorites” ([[@5001007|Deut. 1:7]], [[@5001019|Deut 1:19]], [[@5001020|Deut 1:20]]). They seem to have originally occupied the land stretching from the heights west of the Dead Sea ([[@1014007|Gen. 14:7]]) to Hebron (13.

column5: Prophet from Tekoa who prophesied to Israel
column7: Amos, a shepherd from Tekoa, called by God as a prophet to Israel.

column5: Son of Naum in Jesus' genealogy
column7: Amos, an ancestor of Jesus, son of Naum.

column5: Father of the prophet Isaiah
column7: Strong, the father of the prophet Isaiah ([[@12019002|2 Kings 19:2]], [[@12019020|2 Kings 19:20]]; 20:1; [[@23001001|Isa. 1:1]]; [[@23002001|Isa 2:1]]). As to his personal history little is positively known.

column5: A city visited by Paul on his missionary journey.
column7: City on both sides, a Macedonian city, a great Roman military station, through which Paul and Silas passed on their way from Philippi to Thessalonica, a distance of 33 Roman miles from Philippi ([[@44017001|Acts 17:1]]).

column5: Believer greeted by Paul in Rome
column7: A Roman Christian saluted by Paul ([[@45016008|Rom. 16:8]]).

column5: Father of Moses, Aaron, and Miriam
column6: an exalted people; their sheaves; handfuls of corn
column7: The son of Kohath, the son of Levi. He married Jochebed, “his father’s sister,” and was the father of Aaron, Miriam, and Moses ([[@2006018|Ex. 6:18]], [[@2006020|Ex 6:20]]; [[@4003019|Num. 3:19]]). He died in Egypt at the age of 137 years ([[@2006020|Ex. 6:20]]).

column5: Israelite who married a foreign wife
column6: an exalted people; their sheaves; handfuls of corn
column7: Amram was one of the Israelites who had married a foreign woman during the Exile and agreed to put her away.

column5: King of Shinar, ally of Chedorlaomer
column7: King of Shinar, southern Chaldea, one of the confederates of Chedorlaomer, king of Elam, in a war against Sodom and cities of the plain ([[@1014001|Gen. 14:1]], [[@1014004|Gen. 14:4]]). It is now found that Amraphel (or Ammirapaltu) is the Khammu-rabi whose name appears on recently-discovered monuments. (See CHEDORLAOMER).

column5: Levite musician, descendant of Merari
column7: Amzi, a descendant of Merari, was a Levite who served as a musician in the temple.

column5: Priest in Jerusalem after the Exile
column7: Amzi was a priest who lived in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile.

column5: A city in the hill country of Judah.
column7: Grape-town, one of the cities in the mountains of Judah, from which Joshua expelled the Anakim ([[@6011021|Josh. 11:21]]; [[@6015050|Josh 15:50]]). It still retains its ancient name.

column5: Horite, father of Oholibamah, Esau's wife
column7: One of the sons of Seir, and head of an Idumean tribe, called a Horite, as in course of time all the branches of this tribe were called from their dwelling in caves in Mount Seir ([[@1036020|Gen. 36:20]], [[@1036029|Gen. 36:29]]; [[@13001038|1 Chr. 1:38]]).

column5: A border town in the territory of Issachar.
column7: Anaharath, a town on the border of Issachar's territory.

column5: Stood beside Ezra during the reading of the Law
column7: Anaiah was one of the men who stood beside Ezra when he read the Book of the Law to the people.

column5: Priest who sealed the covenant
column7: Anaiah was a priest who signed the covenant of faithfulness to God during Nehemiah's time.

column5: Ancestor of giant people in Canaan
column7: Long-necked, the son of Arba, father of the Anakim ([[@6015013|Josh. 15:13]]; [[@6021011|Josh 21:11]], Heb. Anok ).

column5: Descendants of Mizraim, son of Ham
column7: The name of an Egyptian tribe descended from Mizraim ([[@1010013|Gen. 10:13]]; [[@13001011|1 Chr. 1:11]]).

column5: Assyrian deity worshiped by Sepharvites
column7: One of the gods worshipped by the people of Sepharvaim, who colonized Samaria ([[@12017031|2 Kings 17:31]]). The name means “Anu is king.”

column5: Signer of the covenant during Nehemiah's time
column7: Cloud, one of the Israelites who sealed the covenant after the return from Babylon ([[@16010026|Neh. 10:26]]).

column5: Descendant of King David
column7: Anani was a descendant of King David, mentioned in the genealogy recorded in 1 Chronicles.

column5: Repairer of the wall in Jerusalem
column7: Protected by Jehovah, the name of a town in the tribe of Benjamin between Nob and Hazor ([[@16011032|Neh. 11:32]]).

column5: A town inhabited by Benjamites after the Babylonian exile.
column7: Protected by Jehovah, the name of a town in the tribe of Benjamin between Nob and Hazor ([[@16011032|Neh. 11:32]]).

column5: Husband of Sapphira, lied about offering proceeds
column6: or Ananiah, the cloud of the Lord
column7: One of the members of the church at Jerusalem, who conspired with his wife Sapphira to deceive the brethren, and who fell down and immediately expired after he had uttered the falsehood ([[@44005005|Acts 5:5]]). By common agreement the members of the early Christian community devoted their property to the work of furthering the gospel and of assisting the poor and needy. The proceeds of the possessions they sold were placed at the disposal of the apostles ([[@44004036|Acts 4:36]], [[@44004037|Acts 4:37]]).

column5: Disciple in Damascus, baptized Saul (Paul)
column6: or Ananiah, the cloud of the Lord
column7: Ananias, a disciple in Damascus, was sent by God to heal and baptize Saul (later known as Paul) after his conversion on the road to Damascus.

column5: High priest during Paul's trial
column6: or Ananiah, the cloud of the Lord
column7: The high priest before whom Paul was brought in the procuratorship of Felix ([[@44023002|Acts 23:2]], [[@44023005|Acts 23:5]], [[@44023024|Acts 23:24]]). He was so enraged at Paul’s noble declaration, “I have lived in all good conscience before God until this day,” that he commanded one of his attendants to smite him on the mouth. Smarting under this unprovoked insult, Paul quickly replied, “God shall smite thee, thou whited wall.”

column5: Father of Shamgar, a judge of Israel
column7: An answer; i.e., to “prayer”, the father of Shamgar, who was one of the judges of Israel ([[@7003031|Judg. 3:31]]).

column5: A Levitical city in Benjamin, home of the prophet Jeremiah.
column7: The name of one of the cities of refuge, in the tribe of Benjamin ([[@6021018|Josh. 21:18]]). The Jews, as a rule, did not change the names of the towns they found in Palestine; hence this town may be regarded as deriving its name from the goddess Anat. It was the native place of Abiezer, one of David’s “thirty” ([[@10023027|2 Sam. 23:27]]), and of Jehu, another of his mighty men ([[@13012003|1 Chr. 12:3]]).

column5: Son of Becher, descendant of Benjamin
column7: The name of one of the cities of refuge, in the tribe of Benjamin ([[@6021018|Josh. 21:18]]). The Jews, as a rule, did not change the names of the towns they found in Palestine; hence this town may be regarded as deriving its name from the goddess Anat. It was the native place of Abiezer, one of David’s “thirty” ([[@10023027|2 Sam. 23:27]]), and of Jehu, another of his mighty men ([[@13012003|1 Chr. 12:3]]).

column5: Signer of the covenant during Nehemiah's time
column7: The name of one of the cities of refuge, in the tribe of Benjamin ([[@6021018|Josh. 21:18]]). The Jews, as a rule, did not change the names of the towns they found in Palestine; hence this town may be regarded as deriving its name from the goddess Anat. It was the native place of Abiezer, one of David’s “thirty” ([[@10023027|2 Sam. 23:27]]), and of Jehu, another of his mighty men ([[@13012003|1 Chr. 12:3]]).

column5: Apostle, brother of Simon Peter
column7: Manliness, a Greek name; one of the apostles of our Lord. He was of Bethsaida in Galilee ([[@43001044|John 1:44]]), and was the brother of Simon Peter ([[@40004018|Matt. 4:18]]; [[@40010002|Matt 10:2]]). On one occasion John the Baptist, whose disciple he then was, pointing to Jesus, said, “Behold the Lamb of God” ([[@43001040|John 1:40]]); and Andrew, hearing him, immediately became a follower of Jesus, the first of his disciples. After he had been led to recognize Jesus as the Messiah, his first care was to bring also his brother Simon to Jesus.

column5: Fellow prisoner with Paul, outstanding among the apostles
column7: Man-conquering, a Jewish Christian, the kinsman and fellowprisoner of Paul ([[@45016007|Rom. 16:7]]); “of note among the apostles.”

column5: Amorite ally of Abram
column7: A Canaanitish chief who joined his forces with those of Abraham in pursuit of Chedorlaomer ([[@1014013|Gen. 14:13]], [[@1014024|Gen. 14:24]]).

Their functions are manifold. (a) In the widest sense they are agents of God’s providence ([[@2012023|Ex. 12:23]]; [[@19104004|Ps. 104:4]]; [[@58011028|Heb. 11:28]]; [[@46010010|1 Cor. 10:10]]; [[@10024016|2 Sam. 24:16]]; [[@13021016|1 Chr. 21:16]]; [[@12019035|2 Kings 19:35]]; [[@44012023|Acts 12:23]]). (b) They are specially God’s agents in carrying on his great work of redemption. There is no notice of angelic appearances to man till after the call of Abraham.

column5: A tower built by King Uzziah in Jerusalem.
column7: The Angle, a fortified tower constructed by Uzziah in Jerusalem.

column5: Son of Shemida, descendant of Manasseh
column6: a people; the strength or sorrow of people
column7: Aniam was a son of Shemida and a descendant of Manasseh, mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Manasseh.

column5: A city in the hill country of Judah.
column7: Fountains, a city in the mountains of Judah ([[@6015050|Josh. 15:50]]), now el-Ghuwein, near Eshtemoh, about 10 miles south-west of Hebron.

column5: Prophetess who witnessed Jesus' dedication in the temple
column7: Grace, an aged widow, the daughter of Phanuel. She was a “prophetess,” like Miriam, Deborah, and Huldah ([[@14034022|2 Chr. 34:22]]). After seven years of married life her husband died, and during her long widowhood she daily attended the temple services.

column5: High priest during Jesus' ministry and trial
column7: Was high priest A.D. 7-14. In A.D. 25 Caiaphas, who had married the daughter of Annas ([[@43018013|John 18:13]]), was raised to that office, and probably Annas was now made president of the Sanhedrim, or deputy or coadjutor of the high priest, and thus was also called high priest along with Caiaphas ([[@42003002|Luke 3:2]]). By the Mosaic law the high-priesthood was held for life ([[@4003010|Num. 3:10]]); and although Annas had been deposed by the Roman procurator, the Jews may still have regarded him as legally the high priest.

The act of anointing was significant of consecration to a holy or sacred use; hence the anointing of the high priest ([[@2029029|Ex. 29:29]]; [[@3004003|Lev. 4:3]]) and of the sacred vessels ([[@2030026|Ex. 30:26]]). The high priest and the king are thus called “the anointed” ([[@3004003|Lev. 4:3]], [[@3004005|Lev. 4:5]], [[@3004016|Lev. 4:16]]; 6:20; [[@19132010|Ps. 132:10]]). Anointing a king was equivalent to crowning him ([[@9016013|1 Sam. 16:13]]; [[@10002004|2 Sam. 2:4]], etc.).

column5: Son of Shashak, descendant of Benjamin
column6: answers or songs of the Lord; afflictions
column7: Anthothijah was a descendant of Benjamin, mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin.

column5: A major city where the gospel spread to Gentiles.
column7: In Syria, on the river Orontes, about 16 miles from the Mediterranean, and some 300 miles north of Jerusalem. It was the metropolis of Syria, and afterwards became the capital of the Roman province in Asia. It ranked third, after Rome and Alexandria, in point of importance, of the cities of the Roman empire. It was called the “first city of the East.”

column5: A city in Pisidia where Paul preached the gospel.
