column7: In the extreme north of Pisidia; was visited by Paul and Barnabas on the first missionary journey ([[@44013014|Acts 13:14]]). Here they found a synagogue and many proselytes. They met with great success in preaching the gospel, but the Jews stirred up a violent opposition against them, and they were obliged to leave the place. On his return, Paul again visited Antioch for the purpose of confirming the disciples ([[@44014021|Acts 14:21]]).

column5: Faithful martyr in Pergamum
column7: A “faithful martyr” ([[@66002013|Rev. 2:13]]), of whom nothing more is certainly known.

column5: A city where Paul was taken during his transfer to Caesarea.
column7: A city built by Herod the Great, and called by this name in honour of his father, Antipater. It lay between Caesarea and Lydda, two miles inland, on the great Roman road from Caesarea to Jerusalem. To this place Paul was brought by night ([[@44023031|Acts 23:31]]) on his way to Caesarea, from which it was distant 28 miles.

column5: Son of Coz, descendant of Judah
column7: Anub was a descendant of Judah, mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah.

column5: Approved in Christ, greeted by Paul
column7: A Christian at Rome whom Paul salutes ([[@45016010|Rom. 16:10]]), and styles “approved in Christ.”

column5: A city in the Shephelah, site of Philistine battles.
column6: Aphekah, Aphik, strength; a rapid torrent
column7: Aphek or Aphekah, a city in the Shephelah, known for Philistine conflicts with Israel.

column5: A city in the territory of Asher.
column6: Aphekah, Aphik, strength; a rapid torrent
column7: Aphek, a city allotted to the tribe of Asher.

column5: A city in the north, site of Aramean battles.
column6: Aphekah, Aphik, strength; a rapid torrent
column7: Aphek, a city in the north, where the Arameans fought against Israel.

column5: Ancestor of King Saul, a Benjamite
column7: Aphiah, a Benjamite, was an ancestor of King Saul, the first king of Israel.

column5: A city in Macedonia visited by Paul.
column7: A city of Macedonia between Amphipolis and Thessalonica, from which it was distant about 36 miles.

column5: Eloquent Jewish Christian from Alexandria, co-worker with Paul
column7: A Jew “born at Alexandria,” a man well versed in the Scriptures and eloquent ([[@44018024|Acts 18:24]]; R.V., “learned”). He came to Ephesus (about A.D. 49), where he spake “boldly” in the synagogue (18:26), although he did not know as yet that Jesus of Nazareth was the Messiah. Aquila and Priscilla instructed him more perfectly in “the way of God”, i.e., in the knowledge of Christ. He then proceeded to Corinth, where he met Paul ([[@44018027|Acts 18:27]]; [[@44019001|Acts 19:1]]).

Another qualification was the power of working miracles ([[@41016020|Mark 16:20]]; [[@44002043|Acts 2:43]]; [[@46012008-46012011|1 Cor. 12:8-11]]). The apostles therefore could have had no successors. They are the only authoritative teachers of the Christian doctrines. The office of an apostle ceased with its first holders.

column5: Son of Nadab, descendant of Judah
column7: Appaim was a descendant of Judah, mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah.

column5: Recipient of Paul's letter to Philemon
column7: Increasing, a female Christian at Colosse ([[@57001001|Philemon 1]]:2), supposed by some to have been the wife of Philemon.

column5: Jewish Christian tentmaker, co-worker with Paul
column7: Eagle, a native of Pontus, by occupation a tent-maker, whom Paul met on his first visit to Corinth ([[@44018002|Acts 18:2]]). Along with his wife Priscilla he had fled from Rome in consequence of a decree (A.D. 50) by Claudius commanding all Jews to leave the city. Paul sojourned with him at Corinth, and they wrought together at their common trade, making Cilician hair-cloth for tents. On Paul’s departure from Corinth after eighteen months, Aquila and his wife accompanied him to Ephesus, where they remained, while he proceeded to Syria ([[@44018018|Acts 18:18]], [[@44018026|Acts 18:26]]).

column5: The capital city of Moab.
column7: Ar, the capital of Moab, mentioned in the context of Israel's journey and prophecies.

column5: Son of Jether, descendant of Asher
column7: Ara was a descendant of Asher, mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Asher.

column5: A city allotted to the tribe of Judah.
column6: multiplying; sowing sedition; a window; a locust
column7: Ambush, a city in the mountains of Judah ([[@6015052|Josh. 15:52]]), now Er-Rabiyeh.

column5: A desert region in the Jordan Valley and southward.
column7: Plain, in the Revised Version of [[@12014025|2 Kings 14:25]]; [[@6003016|Josh. 3:16]]; [[@6008014|Josh 8:14]]; [[@10002029|2 Sam. 2:29]]; [[@10004007|2 Sam. 4:7]] (in all these passages the A.V. has “plain”); [[@30006014|Amos 6:14]] (A.V. “wilderness”). This word is found in the Authorized Version only in [[@6018018|Josh. 18:18]]. It denotes the hollow depression through which the Jordan flows from the Lake of Galilee to the Dead Sea. It is now called by the Arabs el-Ghor.

column5: A region and its inhabitants, mentioned in various contexts.
column7: Arabia Petraea, i.e., the Rocky Arabia, so called from its rocky mountains and stony plains. It comprehended all the north-west portion of the country, and is much better known to travellers than any other portion.

column5: Arad, Canaanite city, attacked Israel, later inhabited by Kenites
column7: Now Tell Arad, a Canaanite city, about 20 miles south of Hebron. The king of Arad “fought against Israel and took of them prisoners” when they were retreating from the confines of Edom ([[@4021001|Num. 21:1]]; [[@4033040|Num 33:40]]; [[@7001016|Judg. 1:16]]).

column5: A Benjamite, son of Beriah.
column7: Arad was a Benjamite, one of the sons of Beriah.

column5: Son of Shual, an Asherite
column7: Arah, the son of Shual ('Ulla'), was a descendant of Asher.

column5: Father-in-law of Tobiah the Ammonite
column7: Arah, whose daughter was married to Shechaniah, was the father-in-law of Tobiah the Ammonite.

column5: A Jewish leader whose daughter married Tobiah's son.
column7: Arah's daughter was married to the son of Tobiah the Ammonite.

column5: Son of Shem, ancestor of the Arameans
column6: highness, magnificence, one that deceives; curse
column7: The son of Shem ([[@1010022|Gen. 10:22]]); according to [[@1022021|Gen. 22:21]], a grandson of Nahor. In [[@40001003|Matt. 1:3]], [[@40001004|Matt. 1:4]], and [[@42003033|Luke 3:33]], this word is the Greek form of Ram, the father of Amminadab ([[@13002010|1 Chr. 2:10]]). The word means high, or highlands, and as the name of a country denotes that elevated region extending from the northeast of Palestine to the Euphrates. It corresponded generally with the Syria and Mesopotamia of the Greeks and Romans.

column5: Son of Kemuel, nephew of Abraham
column6: highness, magnificence, one that deceives; curse
column7: The son of Shem ([[@1010022|Gen. 10:22]]); according to [[@1022021|Gen. 22:21]], a grandson of Nahor. In [[@40001003|Matt. 1:3]], [[@40001004|Matt. 1:4]], and [[@42003033|Luke 3:33]], this word is the Greek form of Ram, the father of Amminadab ([[@13002010|1 Chr. 2:10]]). The word means high, or highlands, and as the name of a country denotes that elevated region extending from the northeast of Palestine to the Euphrates. It corresponded generally with the Syria and Mesopotamia of the Greeks and Romans.

column5: Son of Shemer, descendant of Asher
column6: highness, magnificence, one that deceives; curse
column7: The son of Shem ([[@1010022|Gen. 10:22]]); according to [[@1022021|Gen. 22:21]], a grandson of Nahor. In [[@40001003|Matt. 1:3]], [[@40001004|Matt. 1:4]], and [[@42003033|Luke 3:33]], this word is the Greek form of Ram, the father of Amminadab ([[@13002010|1 Chr. 2:10]]). The word means high, or highlands, and as the name of a country denotes that elevated region extending from the northeast of Palestine to the Euphrates. It corresponded generally with the Syria and Mesopotamia of the Greeks and Romans.

column5: Kingdom that fought against David
column7: Aram-maacah was an Aramean kingdom that allied with the Ammonites against David.

column5: A region mentioned in the title of Psalm 60.
column7: Aram of the two rivers, is Mesopotamia (as it is rendered in [[@1024010|Gen. 24:10]]), the country enclosed between the Tigris on the east and the Euphrates on the west (Ps. 60, title); called also the “field of Aram” ([[@28012012|Hos. 12:12]], R.V.) i.e., the open country of Aram; in the Authorized Version, “country of Syria.”

column5: A region mentioned in the title of Psalm 60.
column7: (Ps. 60, title), probably the region between the Euphrates and the Orontes.

column5: Concubine of Manasseh; mother of Asriel
column7: An Aramitess, who was a concubine of Manasseh, gave birth to Machir and Asriel..

column5: Son of Dishan, descendant of Seir the Horite
column7: Wild goat, a descendant of Seir the Horite ([[@1036028|Gen. 36:28]]).

column5: A mountain range where Noah's ark rested after the flood.
column7: Sacred land or high land, the name of a country on one of the mountains of which the ark rested after the Flood subsided ([[@1008004|Gen. 8:4]]). The “mountains” mentioned were probably the Kurdish range of South Armenia. In [[@12019037|2 Kings 19:37]], [[@23037038|Isa. 37:38]], the word is rendered “Armenia” in the Authorized Version, but in the Revised Version, “Land of Ararat.” In [[@24051027|Jer. 51:27]], the name denotes the central or southern portion of Armenia.

column5: Father of Anak, former name of Hebron
column7: Four, a giant, father of Anak. From him the city of Hebron derived its name of Kirjath-arba, i.e., the city of Araba ([[@6014015|Josh. 14:15]]; [[@6015013|Josh 15:13]]; [[@6021011|Josh 21:11]]; [[@1013018|Gen. 13:18]]; [[@1023002|Gen 23:2]]).

column5: Son of Herod the Great, Ethnarch of Judea
column7: Ruler of the people, son of Herod the Great, by Malthace, a Samaritan woman. He was educated along with his brother Antipas at Rome. He inherited from his father a third part of his kingdom viz., Idumea, Judea, and Samaria, and hence is called “king” ([[@40002022|Matt. 2:22]]). It was for fear of him that Joseph and Mary turned aside on their way back from Egypt.

column5: Fellow soldier and minister in Colossae
column7: Master of the horse, a “fellow-soldier” of Paul’s ([[@57001001|Philemon 1]]:2), whom he exhorts to renewed activity ([[@51004017|Col. 4:17]]).

column5: Inhabitants of a region near Bethel
column7: A city on the boundary of Ephraim and Benjamin ([[@6016002|Josh. 16:2]]), between Bethel and Beth-horon the nether.

column5: Son of Benjamin, brother of Bela
column6: one that commands; he that descends
column7: Descent, a grandson of Benjamin ([[@4026038-4026040|Num. 26:38-40]]). In [[@13008003|1 Chr. 8:3]] he is called Addar.

column5: Grandson of Benjamin, son of Bela
column6: one that commands; he that descends
column7: Descent, a grandson of Benjamin ([[@4026038-4026040|Num. 26:38-40]]). In [[@13008003|1 Chr. 8:3]] he is called Addar.

column5: Son of Caleb, brother of Jether and Mered
column7: Descendant, the last of the three sons of Caleb by his first wife Azubah ([[@13002018|1 Chr. 2:18]]).

column5: Son of Gad, grandson of Jacob
column6: the light or vision of God
column7: Areli, a son of Gad, is mentioned in the genealogy of Jacob and the census of the Israelites in the wilderness.

column5: A hill in Athens where Paul preached the gospel.
column7: The Latin form of the Greek word rendered “Mars’ hill.” But it denotes also the council or court of justice which met in the open air on the hill. It was a rocky height to the west of the Acropolis at Athens, on the south-east summit of which the council was held which was constituted by Solon, and consisted of nine archons or chief magistrates who were then in office, and the ex-archons of blameless life.

column5: King of the Nabataeans in Damascus
column7: The father-in-law of Herod Antipas, and king of Arabia Petraea. His daughter returned to him on the occasion of her husband’s entering into an adulterous alliance with Herodias, the wife of Herod-Philip, his half-brother ([[@42003019|Luke 3:19]], [[@42003020|Luke 3:20]]; [[@41006017|Mark 6:17]]; [[@40014003|Matt. 14:3]]). This led to a war between Aretas and Herod Antipas. Herod’s army was wholly destroyed (A.D. 36).

column5: A region in Bashan, known for its fortified cities.
column7: Stony heap, an “island,” as it has been called, of rock about 30 miles by 20, rising 20 or 30 feet above the table-land of Bashan; a region of crags and chasms wild and rugged in the extreme. On this “island” stood sixty walled cities, ruled over by Og. It is called Trachonitis (“the rugged region”) in the New Testament ([[@42003001|Luke 3:1]]). These cities were conquered by the Israelites ([[@5003004|Deut. 3:4]]; [[@11004013|1 Kings 4:13]]).

column5: Officer of King Pekahiah of Israel
column7: Stony heap, an “island,” as it has been called, of rock about 30 miles by 20, rising 20 or 30 feet above the table-land of Bashan; a region of crags and chasms wild and rugged in the extreme. On this “island” stood sixty walled cities, ruled over by Og. It is called Trachonitis (“the rugged region”) in the New Testament ([[@42003001|Luke 3:1]]). These cities were conquered by the Israelites ([[@5003004|Deut. 3:4]]; [[@11004013|1 Kings 4:13]]).

column5: Son of Haman, enemy of the Jews
column7: Aridai was one of the ten sons of Haman, who were killed and hanged after their father's downfall.

column5: Son of Haman, enemy of the Jews
column7: Aridatha was one of the ten sons of Haman, who were killed and hanged after their father's downfall.

column5: Officer of King Pekahiah of Israel
column7: The lion, the name of one of the body-guard slain with Pekahiah at Samaria ([[@12015025|2 Kings 15:25]]) by the conspirator Pekah.

column5: Two lion-like men of Moab killed by Benaiah
column6: altar; light or lion of God
column7: Ariel refers to two lion-like men of Moab who were killed by Benaiah, one of David's mighty warriors.

column5: One of the leaders summoned by Ezra
column6: altar; light or lion of God
column7: One of the chief men sent by Ezra to procure Levites for the sanctuary ([[@15008016|Ezra 8:16]]).

column5: King of Ellasar, ally of Chedorlaomer
column7: A king of Ellasar who was confederate with Chedorlamer ([[@1014001|Gen. 14:1]], [[@1014009|Gen. 14:9]]). The tablets recently discovered by Mr. Pinches (see CHALDEA) show the true reading is Eri-Aku of Larsa.

column5: Captain of Nebuchadnezzar's guard
column7: Arioch, the captain of King Nebuchadnezzar's guard, was commanded to execute the wise men of Babylon but brought Daniel before the king to interpret his dream.

column5: Son of Haman, enemy of the Jews
column7: Arisai was one of the ten sons of Haman, who were killed and hanged after their father's downfall.

column5: Macedonian companion of Paul, fellow prisoner
column7: Best ruler, native of Thessalonica ([[@44020004|Acts 20:4]]), a companion of Paul ([[@44019029|Acts 19:29]]; [[@44027002|Acts 27:2]]).

column5: Believer in Rome, greeted by Paul
column7: A Roman mentioned in Paul’s Epistle to the Romans (16:10), whose “household” is saluated.

The sacred ark is designated by a different Hebrew word, ’aron’ , which is the common name for a chest or coffer used for any purpose ([[@1050026|Gen. 50:26]]; [[@12012009|2 Kings 12:9]], [[@12012010|2 Kings 12:10]]). It is distinguished from all others by such titles as the “ark of God” ([[@9003003|1 Sam. 3:3]]), “ark of the covenant” ([[@6003006|Josh. 3:6]]; [[@58009004|Heb. 9:4]]), “ark of the testimony” ([[@2025022|Ex. 25:22]]). It was made of acacia or shittim wood, a cubit and a half broad and high and two cubits long, and covered all over with the purest gold.

column5: Canaanite people group descended from Canaan
column7: ([[@1010017|Gen. 10:17]]; [[@13001015|1 Chr. 1:15]]), a designation of certain descendants from the Phoenicians or Sidonians, the inhabitants of Arka, 12 miles north of Tripoli, opposite the northern extremity of Lebanon.

column5: Son of Saul by Rizpah, killed by Gibeonites
column7: Inhabitant of a fortress, the first-named of the two sons of Saul and Rizpah.

column5: Descendant of David's son Solomon
column7: Arnan was a descendant of David's son Solomon (<ref="1Ch.3.21">1Ch.3.21</ref>).

column5: A river and valley, serving as a boundary for Israel.
column7: Swift, the southern boundary of the territory of Israel beyond Jordan, separating it from the land of Moab ([[@5003008|Deut. 3:8]], [[@5003016|Deut. 3:16]]). This river (referred to twenty-four times in the Bible) rises in the mountains of Gilead, and after a circuitous course of about 80 miles through a deep ravine it falls into the Dead Sea nearly opposite Engedi. The stream is almost dry in summer. It is now called el-Mujeb.

column5: Son of Gad and founder of the Arodite clan
column7: Arod, son of Gad, was the founder of the Arodite clan (<ref="Gen.46.16; Num.26.17">Gen.46.16; Num.26.17</ref>).

column5: A city in Gad, built by the Gadites.
column7: One of the towns built by the tribe of Gad ([[@4032034|Num. 32:34]]) “before Rabbah” ([[@6013025|Josh. 13:25]]), the Ammonite capital. It was famous in the history of Jephthah ([[@7011033|Judg. 11:33]]) and of David ([[@10024005|2 Sam. 24:5]]).

column5: A city on the edge of the Arnon Valley.
column7: A town on the north bank of the Arnon ([[@5004048|Deut. 4:48]]; [[@7011026|Judg. 11:26]]; [[@12010033|2 Kings 10:33]]), the southern boundary of the kingdom of Sihon ([[@6012002|Josh. 12:2]]).

column5: A city in Judah, receiving spoils from David.
column7: A city in the south of Judah, 12 miles south-east of Beersheba, to which David sent presents after recovering the spoil from the Amalekites at Ziklag ([[@9030026|1 Sam. 30:26]], [[@9030028|1 Sam. 30:28]]). It was the native city of two of David’s warriors ([[@13011044|1 Chr. 11:44]]).

column5: Son of Shem, ancestor of Abraham
column7: Son of Shem, born the year after the Deluge. He died at the age of 438 years ([[@1011010-1011013|Gen. 11:10-13]]; [[@13001017|1 Chr. 1:17]], [[@13001018|1 Chr. 1:18]]; [[@42003036|Luke 3:36]]). He dwelt in Mesopotamia, and became, according to the Jewish historian Josephus, the progenitor of the Chaldeans. The tendency is to recognize in the word the name of the country nearest the ancient domain of the Chaldeans.

column5: City conquered by Assyria
column7: ([[@23010009|Isa. 10:9]]; [[@23036019|Isa 36:19]]; [[@23037013|Isa 37:13]]), also Arphad, support, a Syrian city near Hamath, along with which it is invariably mentioned ([[@12019013|2 Kings 19:13]]; [[@12018034|2 Kings 18:34]]; [[@23010009|Isa. 10:9]]), and Damascus ([[@24049023|Jer. 49:23]]). After a siege of three years it fell (B.C. 742) before the Assyrian king Tiglath-pileser II.

column5: Persian king during Ezra and Nehemiah's time
column6: the silence of light; fervent to spoil
column7: The king mentioned in [[@15007001|Ezra 7:1]], in the seventh year (B.C. 458) of whose reign Ezra led a second colony of Jews back to Jerusalem, was probably Longimanus, who reigned for forty years (B.C. 464-425); the grandson of Darius, who, fourteen years later, permitted Nehemiah to return and rebuild Jerusalem.

column5: Companion of Paul, potential replacement for Titus
column7: Artemas was a companion of Paul who could potentially replace Titus in Crete (<ref="Titus 3:12">Titus 3:12</ref>).

column5: A district in Israel under Solomon's rule.
column7: Arubboth, a district governed by one of Solomon's twelve officers.

column5: A city associated with Abimelech and King Jehoiakim's mother.
column7: Elevation, probably the same as Arumah ([[@7009041|Judg. 9:41]]; [[@12023036|2 Kings 23:36]]), near Shechem.

column5: An island city, known for its skilled mariners and soldiers.
column7: Wandering, ([[@26027008|Ezek. 27:8]]), a small island and city on the coast of Syria, mentioned as furnishing mariners and soldiers for Tyre. The inhabitants were called Arvadites.

column5: Canaanite descendants of Canaan, son of Ham
column7: The Arvadites were a Canaanite People from Canaan, son of Ham (<ref="Gen.10.18; 1Ch.1.16">Gen.10.18; 1Ch.1.16</ref>).

column5: Steward of King Elah's household in Tirzah
column7: Arza was the steward of King Elah's household in Tirzah (<ref="1Ki.16.9">1Ki.16.9</ref>).

column5: King of Judah, son of Abijah; father of Jehoshaphat
column7: Physician, son of Abijah and grandson of Rehoboam, was the third king of Judah. He was zealous in maintaining the true worship of God, and in rooting all idolatry, with its accompanying immoralities, out of the land ([[@11015008-11015014|1 Kings 15:8-14]]). The Lord gave him and his land rest and prosperity. It is recorded of him, however, that in his old age, when afflicted, he “sought not to the Lord, but to the physicians” (comp. [[@24017005|Jer. 17:5]]).

column5: Levite gatekeeper who resettled in Jerusalem
column7: Physician, son of Abijah and grandson of Rehoboam, was the third king of Judah. He was zealous in maintaining the true worship of God, and in rooting all idolatry, with its accompanying immoralities, out of the land ([[@11015008-11015014|1 Kings 15:8-14]]). The Lord gave him and his land rest and prosperity. It is recorded of him, however, that in his old age, when afflicted, he “sought not to the Lord, but to the physicians” (comp. [[@24017005|Jer. 17:5]]).

column5: Son of Zeruiah, brother of Joab, killed by Abner
column7: Made by God, the youngest son of Zeruiah, David’s sister. He was celebrated for his swiftness of foot. When fighting against Ish-bosheth at Gibeon, in the army of his brother Joab, he was put to death by Abner, whom he pursued from the field of battle ([[@10002018|2 Sam. 2:18]], [[@10002019|2 Sam. 2:19]]). He is mentioned among David’s thirty mighty men ([[@10023024|2 Sam. 23:24]]; [[@13011026|1 Chr. 11:26]]).

column5: Levite sent by Jehoshaphat to teach the Law
column7: Made by God, the youngest son of Zeruiah, David’s sister. He was celebrated for his swiftness of foot. When fighting against Ish-bosheth at Gibeon, in the army of his brother Joab, he was put to death by Abner, whom he pursued from the field of battle ([[@10002018|2 Sam. 2:18]], [[@10002019|2 Sam. 2:19]]). He is mentioned among David’s thirty mighty men ([[@10023024|2 Sam. 23:24]]; [[@13011026|1 Chr. 11:26]]).

column5: Levite in charge of tithes under Hezekiah
column7: Made by God, the youngest son of Zeruiah, David’s sister. He was celebrated for his swiftness of foot. When fighting against Ish-bosheth at Gibeon, in the army of his brother Joab, he was put to death by Abner, whom he pursued from the field of battle ([[@10002018|2 Sam. 2:18]], [[@10002019|2 Sam. 2:19]]). He is mentioned among David’s thirty mighty men ([[@10023024|2 Sam. 23:24]]; [[@13011026|1 Chr. 11:26]]).

column5: Opposed Ezra's dissolution of mixed marriages
column7: Made by God, the youngest son of Zeruiah, David’s sister. He was celebrated for his swiftness of foot. When fighting against Ish-bosheth at Gibeon, in the army of his brother Joab, he was put to death by Abner, whom he pursued from the field of battle ([[@10002018|2 Sam. 2:18]], [[@10002019|2 Sam. 2:19]]). He is mentioned among David’s thirty mighty men ([[@10023024|2 Sam. 23:24]]; [[@13011026|1 Chr. 11:26]]).

column5: Servant of King Josiah during Book of Law discovery
column7: Asaiah was a servant of King Josiah sent to consult the prophetess Huldah about the Book of the Law (<ref="2Ki.22.12, 14; 2Ch.34.20">2Ki.22.12, 14; 2Ch.34.20</ref>).

column5: Simeonite leader during Hezekiah's reign
column7: Asaiah was a Simeonite leader during the reign of King Hezekiah (<ref="1Ch.4.36">1Ch.4.36</ref>).

column5: Merarite Levite, ancestor of Ethan the singer
column7: Asaiah was a Merarite Levite, an ancestor of Ethan the singer (<ref="1Ch.6.30">1Ch.6.30</ref>).

column5: Descendant of Judah living in Jerusalem
column7: Asaiah, a descendant of Judah, lived in Jerusalem (<ref="1Ch.9.5">1Ch.9.5</ref>).

column5: Levite leader who helped bring the ark to Jerusalem
column7: Asaiah was a Levite leader who assisted in bringing the ark of the covenant to Jerusalem during David's reign (<ref="1Ch.15.6, 11">1Ch.15.6, 11</ref>).

column5: Recorder during King Hezekiah's reign
column7: The “recorder” in the time of Hezekiah ([[@12018018|2 Kings 18:18]], [[@12018037|2 Kings 18:37]]).

column5: Levite descendant who resettled in Jerusalem
column7: Asaph was a Levite descendant who resettled in Jerusalem after the exile (<ref="1Ch.9.15; Neh.11.17">1Ch.9.15; Neh.11.17</ref>).

column5: Levite musician, psalmist, and ancestor of temple singers
column7: A Levite; one of the leaders of David’s choir ([[@13006039|1 Chr. 6:39]]). Psalms 50 and 73-83 inclusive are attributed to him. He is mentioned along with David as skilled in music, and a “seer” ([[@14029030|2 Chr. 29:30]]).

column5: Keeper of the king's forest during Nehemiah's time
column7: The “keeper of the king’s forest,” to whom Nehemiah requested from Artaxerxes a “letter” that he might give him timber for the temple at Jerusalem ([[@16002008|Neh. 2:8]]).

column5: Son of Jehallelel, from the tribe of Judah
column7: Asarel was a son of Jehallelel, a descendant of Judah (<ref="1Ch.4.16">1Ch.4.16</ref>).

column5: Egyptian wife of Joseph; mother of Manasseh and Ephraim
column7: An Egyptian name, meaning “gift of the sun-god”, daughter of Potipherah, priest of On or Heliopolis, wife of Joseph ([[@1041045|Gen. 41:45]]).

column5: A city allotted to Judah and Simeon.
column7: Ashan, a city assigned to the tribes of Judah and Simeon, later given to the Levites.

column5: Levite musician appointed by David to prophesy with lyres
column7: Upright towards God, the head of the seventh division of Levitical musicians ([[@13025014|1 Chr. 25:14]]).

column5: Son of Benjamin, founder of the Ashbelite clan
column7: Ashbel was a son of Benjamin and the founder of the Ashbelite clan (<ref="Gen.46.21; Num.26.38; 1Ch.8.1">Gen.46.21; Num.26.38; 1Ch.8.1</ref>).

column5: A major Philistine city, known for Dagon worship.
column7: Stronghold, a Philistine city ([[@6015047|Josh. 15:47]]), about midway between Gaza and Joppa, and 3 miles from the Mediterranean. It was one of the chief seats of the worship of Dagon ([[@9005005|1 Sam. 5:5]]). It belonged to the tribe of Judah ([[@6015047|Josh. 15:47]]), but it never came into their actual possession. It was an important city, as it stood on the highroad from Egypt to Palestine, and hence was strongly fortified ([[@14026006|2 Chr. 26:6]]; [[@23020001|Isa. 20:1]]).

column5: Son of Jacob and Zilpah, founder of the tribe of Asher
column7: Happy, Jacob’s eigth son; his mother was Zilpah, Leah’s handmaid ([[@1030013|Gen. 30:13]]). Of the tribe founded by him nothing is recorded beyond its holding a place in the list of the tribes (35:26; 46:17; [[@2001004|Ex. 1:4]], etc.) It increased in numbers twenty-nine percent, during the thirty-eight years’ wanderings. The place of this tribe during the march through the desert was between Dan and Naphtali ([[@4002027|Num. 2:27]]).

The ashes of a red heifer burned entire ([[@4019005|Num. 19:5]]) when sprinkled on the unclean made them ceremonially clean ([[@58009013|Heb. 9:13]]). To cover the head with ashes was a token of self-abhorrence and humiliation ([[@10013019|2 Sam. 13:19]]; [[@17004003|Esther 4:3]]; [[@24006026|Jer. 6:26]], etc.). To feed on ashes ([[@23044020|Isa. 44:20]]), means to seek that which will prove to be vain and unsatisfactory, and hence it denotes the unsatisfactory nature of idol-worship.

column5: Descendant of Judah through Hezron
column6: who is happy; or walks; or looks
column7: Ashhur, a descendant of Judah through Hezron, was the  father (ie founder) of Tekoa (<ref="1Ch.2.24; 4:5">1Ch.2.24; 4:5</ref>).

column5: A major Philistine city, often a target of prophecy.
column7: =Askelon=Ascalon, was one of the five cities of the Philistines ([[@6013003|Josh. 13:3]]; [[@9006017|1 Sam. 6:17]]). It stood on the shore of the Mediterranean, 12 miles north of Gaza. It is mentioned on an inscription at Karnak in Egypt as having been taken by king Rameses II., the oppressor of the Hebrews. In the time of the judges ([[@7001018|Judg. 1:18]]) it fell into the possession of the tribe of Judah; but it was soon after retaken by the Philistines ([[@10001020|2 Sam. 1:20]]), who were not finally dispossessed till the time of Alexander the Great.

column5: Grandson of Japheth, son of Gomer
column7: One of the three sons of Gomer ([[@1010003|Gen. 10:3]]), and founder of one of the tribes of the Japhetic race.

column5: A kingdom summoned to battle against Babylon.
column7: One of the three sons of Gomer ([[@1010003|Gen. 10:3]]), and founder of one of the tribes of the Japhetic race.

column5: Two cities in the Shephelah region of Judah.
column7: Ashnah, two cities in the lowlands of Judah, mentioned in the tribal allotment.

column5: Chief official in Nebuchadnezzar's court
column7: The master of the eunuchs of Nebuchadnezzar ([[@27001003|Dan. 1:3]]), the “Rabsaris” of the court.

column5: A city of Og, king of Bashan.
column7: A city of Bashan, in the kingdom of Og ([[@5001004|Deut. 1:4]]; [[@6012004|Josh. 12:4]]; [[@6013012|Josh 13:12]]; [[@6009010|Josh 9:10]]). It was in the half-tribe of Manasseh ([[@6013012|Josh. 13:12]]), and as a Levitical city was given to the Gershonites ([[@13006071|1 Chr. 6:71]]). Uzzia, one of David’s valiant men ([[@13011044|1 Chr. 11:44]]), is named as of this city. It is identified with Tell Ashterah, in the Hauran, and is noticed on monuments B.C. 1700-1500.

column5: Ancient city defeated by Chedorlaomer
column7: Ashteroth of the two horns, the abode of the Rephaim ([[@1014005|Gen. 14:5]]). It may be identified with Ashtaroth preceding; called “Karnaim”, i.e., the “two-horned” (the crescent moon).

column5: Son of Japhlet, descendant of Asher
column7: Ashvath was a son of Japhlet and a descendant of Asher (<ref="1Ch.7.33">1Ch.7.33</ref>).

column5: A Roman province in western Asia Minor.
column7: Is used to denote Proconsular Asia, a Roman province which embraced the western parts of Asia Minor, and of which Ephesus was the capital, in [[@44002009|Acts 2:9]]; [[@44006009|Acts 6:9]]; [[@44016006|Acts 16:6]]; [[@44019010|Acts 19:10]], [[@44019022|Acts 19:22]]; [[@44020004|Acts 20:4]], [[@44020016|Acts 20:16]], [[@44020018|Acts 20:18]], etc., and probably Asia Minor in [[@44019026|Acts 19:26]], [[@44019027|Acts 19:27]]; 21:27; 24:18; 27:2. Proconsular Asia contained the seven churches of the Apocalypse ([[@66001011|Rev. 1:11]]).

column5: Descendant of Simeon
column7: Asiel was a descendant of Simeon mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe (<ref="1Ch.4.35">1Ch.4.35</ref>).

column5: Head of a family of temple servants who returned from exile
column7: Asnah was the head of a family of temple servants (Nethinim) who returned to Jerusalem from Babylonian exile (<ref="Ezra 2:50">Ezra 2:50</ref>).

column5: One of the ten sons of Haman
column7: Aspatha was one of the ten sons of Haman, who were executed after their father's downfall (<ref="Est.9.7">Est.9.7</ref>).

column5: Son of Manasseh, founder of the Asrielite clan
column7: Asriel was a son of Manasseh and the founder of the Asrielite clan (<ref="Num.26.31; Josh 17:2">Num.26.31; Josh 17:2</ref>).

column5: Son of Gilead, descendant of Manasseh
column7: Asriel was a son of Gilead and a descendant of Manasseh (<ref="1Ch.7.14">1Ch.7.14</ref>).

column5: Son of Shem; father of the Assyrians
column6: who is happy; or walks; or looks
column7: Second son of Shem ([[@1010022|Gen. 10:22]]; [[@13001017|1 Chr. 1:17]]). He went from the land of Shinar and built Nineveh, etc. ([[@1010011|Gen. 10:11]], [[@1010012|Gen. 10:12]]). He probably gave his name to Assyria, which is the usual translation of the word, although the form Asshur is sometimes retained ([[@4024022|Num. 24:22]], [[@4024024|Num. 24:24]]; [[@26027023|Ezek. 27:23]], etc.). In [[@1002014|Gen. 2:14]] “Assyria” ought to be “Asshur,” which was the original capital of Assyria, a city represented by the mounds of Kalah Sherghat, on the west bank of the Tigris.

column5: Descendant of Abraham through Dedan
column7: Asshurim was a descendant of Abraham through his son Jokshan and grandson Dedan (<ref="Gen.25.3">Gen.25.3</ref>).

column5: Son of Korah who is grandson of Kohath
column7: Assir was a son of Korah and great-grandson of Kohath, from the tribe of Levi (<ref="Exo.6.24; 1Ch.6.22">Exo.6.24; 1Ch.6.22</ref>).

column5: Levite ancestor of the prophet Samuel
column7: Assir was a Levite ancestor of Samuel the prophet (<ref="1Ch.6.23">1Ch.6.23, 37</ref>).

column5: A seaport in Mysia, visited by Paul.
column7: A sea-port town of Proconsular Asia, in the district of Mysia, on the north shore of the Gulf of Adramyttium. Paul came hither on foot along the Roman road from Troas ([[@44020013|Acts 20:13]], [[@44020014|Acts 20:14]]), a distance of 20 miles.

column5: A powerful ancient empire, often in conflict with Israel.
column7: The name derived from the city Asshur on the Tigris, the original capital of the country, was originally a colony from Babylonia, and was ruled by viceroys from that kingdom. It was a mountainous region lying to the north of Babylonia, extending along the Tigris as far as to the high mountain range of Armenia, the Gordiaean or Carduchian mountains. It was founded in B.C. 1700 under Bel-kap-kapu, and became an independent and a conquering power, and shook off the yoke of its Babylonian masters. It subdued the whole of Northern Asia.

column5: Believer in Rome greeted by Paul
column7: Asyncritus was a believer in Rome to whom Paul sent greetings (<ref="Rom.16.14">Rom.16.14</ref>).

column5: Threshing floor where Egyptians mourned Jacob
column7: Buckthorn, a place where Joseph and his brethren, when on their way from Egypt to Hebron with the remains of their father Jacob, made for seven days a “great and very sore lamentation.” On this account the Canaanites called it “Abel-mizraim” ([[@1050010|Gen. 50:10]], [[@1050011|Gen 50:11]]). It was probably near Hebron.

column5: Wife of Jerahmeel; mother of Onam
column7: Atarah was the wife of Jerahmeel and the mother of Onam, mentioned in the genealogy of Judah (<ref="1Ch.2.26">1Ch.2.26</ref>).

column5: Town in Gilead allotted to Gad
column7: A city east of Jordan, not far from Gilead ([[@4032003|Num. 32:3]]).

column5: A town on the border of Ephraim and Manasseh.
column7: A town on the border of Ephraim and Benjamin ([[@6016002|Josh. 16:2]], [[@6016007|Josh 16:7]]), called also Ataroth-adar (16:5).

column5: A town on the border of Ephraim and Benjamin.
column7: Ataroth-addar, a border town between the territories of Ephraim and Benjamin.

column5: Head of a family that returned from Babylonian exile
column7: Ater was the head of a family that returned to Jerusalem from Babylonian captivity (<ref="Ezr.2.16; Neh.7.21">Ezr.2.16; Neh.7.21</ref>).

column5: Head of a family of gatekeepers who returned from exile
column7: Ater was the head of a family of gatekeepers who returned to Jerusalem from Babylonian captivity (<ref="Ezr.2.42; Neh.7.45">Ezr.2.42; Neh.7.45</ref>).

column5: One of the signers of the covenant during Nehemiah's time
column7: Ater was one of the individuals who signed the covenant during the time of Nehemiah's reforms (<ref="Neh.10.17">Neh.10.17</ref>).

column5: A town that received spoils from David's victory.
column7: Athach, a town in Judah that received a share of the spoils from David's victory over the Amalekites.

column5: Descendant of Judah who resettled in Jerusalem
column7: Athaiah, a descendant of Judah, was one of the people who resettled in Jerusalem after the exile (<ref="Neh.11.4">Neh.11.4</ref>).

column5: Queen of Judah, daughter of Ahab and Jezebel
column7: The daughter of Ahab and Jezebel, and the wife of Jehoram, king of Judah ([[@12008018|2 Kings 8:18]]), who “walked in the ways of the house of Ahab” ([[@14021006|2 Chr. 21:6]]), called “daughter” of Omri ([[@12008026|2 Kings 8:26]]). On the death of her husband and of her son Ahaziah, she resolved to seat herself on the vacant throne. She slew all Ahaziah’s children except Joash, the youngest ([[@12011001|2 Kings 11:1]], [[@12011002|2 Kings 11:2]]).

column5: Descendant of Benjamin
column7: Athaliah was a descendant of Benjamin mentioned in the genealogy of Saul's family (<ref="1Ch.8.26">1Ch.8.26</ref>).

column5: Descendant of Elam who returned from Babylonian exile
column7: Athaliah, a descendant of Elam, was among those who returned to Jerusalem with Ezra (<ref="Ezr.8.7">Ezr.8.7</ref>).

column5: A place where the Canaanite king of Arad fought Israel.
column7: Atharim, a place near the Negev where the Canaanite king of Arad attacked the Israelites during their journey.

column5: A major city in Greece, visited by Paul.
column7: The capital of Attica, the most celebrated city of the ancient world, the seat of Greek literature and art during the golden period of Grecian history. Its inhabitants were fond of novelty ([[@44017021|Acts 17:21]]), and were remarkable for their zeal in the worship of the gods. It was a sarcastic saying of the Roman satirist that it was “easier to find a god at Athens than a man.” On his second missionary journey Paul visited this city ([[@44017015|Acts 17:15]]; comp. [[@52003001|1 Thess. 3:1]]), and delivered in the Areopagus his famous speech (17:22-31).

column5: One of those who agreed to put away foreign wives
column7: Athlai was one of the men who agreed to put away their foreign wives during Ezra's reforms (<ref="Ezr.10.28">Ezr.10.28</ref>).

This word does not occur in the Authorized Version of the New Testament except in [[@45005011|Rom. 5:11]], where in the Revised Version the word “reconciliation” is used. In the Old Testament it is of frequent occurrence. The meaning of the word is simply at-one-ment, i.e., the state of being at one or being reconciled, so that atonement is reconciliation. Thus it is used to denote the effect which flows from the death of Christ.

column5: Town associated with Joab from the tribe of Judah.
column7: Atroth-beth-joab was a town linked to Joab in Judah. (<ref="1Ch.2.54">1Ch.2.54</ref>)

column5: Town allotted to the tribe of Gad.
column7: Hidden, or hollow, a town east of Jordan ([[@4032035|Num. 32:35]]), built by the children of Gad.

column5: Grandson of Sheshan, descendant of Judah
column7: Attai was the grandson of Sheshan, a descendant of Judah (<ref="1Ch.2.35-36">1Ch.2.35-36</ref>).

column5: One of David's mighty men, a Gadite warrior
column7: Attai the son of Zabad was one of David's mighty men, a Gadite warrior who joined him at Ziklag (<ref="1Ch.12.11">1Ch.12.11</ref>).

column5: Son of King Rehoboam and Maacah
column7: Attai was a son of King Rehoboam of Judah and his wife Maacah (<ref="2Ch.11.20">2Ch.11.20</ref>).

column5: Seaport in Pamphylia visited by Paul and Barnabas.
column7: Attalia, a seaport in Pamphylia, was visited by Paul and Barnabas. (<ref="Act.14.25">Act.14.25</ref>)

column5: Roman emperor during the birth of Jesus
column7: The cognomen of the first Roman emperor, C. Julius Caesar Octavianus, during whose reign Christ was born ([[@42002001|Luke 2:1]]). His decree that “all the world should be taxed” was the divinely ordered occasion of Jesus’ being born, according to prophecy ([[@33005002|Micah 5:2]]), in Bethlehem. This name being simply a title meaning “majesty” or “venerable,” first given to him by the senate (B.C. 27), was borne by succeeding emperors.

column5: Plain near Damascus, prophesied to be destroyed.
column7: Aven Valley, a plain near Damascus, was prophesied to be destroyed. (<ref="Amo.1.5">Amo.1.5</ref>)

column5: Capital city of Edomite king Hadad.
column7: Avith was the capital city of Hadad, an early Edomite king.

column5: Ancient people who inhabited the Gaza area
column7: A people dwelling in Hazerim, or “the villages” or “encampments” on the south-west corner of the sea-coast ([[@5002023|Deut. 2:23]]). They were subdued and driven northward by the Caphtorim.

column5: Town allotted to the tribe of Benjamin.
column7: A people dwelling in Hazerim, or “the villages” or “encampments” on the south-west corner of the sea-coast ([[@5002023|Deut. 2:23]]). They were subdued and driven northward by the Caphtorim.

column5: Unidentified place near Jerusalem mentioned in Zechariah's prophecy.
column7: ([[@38014005|Zech. 14:5]]) should perhaps be rendered “very near” = “the way of escape shall be made easy.”

column5: Father of Shaphan the scribe during Josiah's reign
column7: Azaliah was the father of Shaphan the scribe, who served during the reign of King Josiah of Judah (<ref="2Ki.22.3; 2Ch.34.8">2Ki.22.3; 2Ch.34.8</ref>).

column5: One of the Levites who sealed the covenant
column6: hearing the Lord; the Lord's weapons
column7: Azaniah was one of the Levites who sealed the covenant during the time of Nehemiah (<ref="Neh.10.9">Neh.10.9</ref>).

column5: One of the Danite warriors who joined David at Ziklag
column7: Azarel was one of the Danite warriors who joined David at Ziklag (<ref="1Ch.12.6">1Ch.12.6</ref>).

column5: Leader of the half-tribe of Manasseh under David
column7: Azarel son of Jeroham was the leader of the half-tribe of Manasseh during David's reign (<ref="1Ch.27.22">1Ch.27.22</ref>).

column5: One of those who married foreign women during Ezra's time
column7: Azarel was among those who had married foreign women during the time of Ezra (<ref="Ezr.10.41">Ezr.10.41</ref>).

column5: Priest who participated in the dedication of Jerusalem's wall
column7: Azarel was a priest who participated in the dedication of Jerusalem's wall during Nehemiah's time (<ref="Neh.12.36">Neh.12.36</ref>).

column5: High priest during Solomon's reign, descendant of Zadok
column7: Son of Ahimaaz, who succeeded his grandfather Zadok as high priest ([[@13006009|1 Chr. 6:9]]; [[@11004002|1 Kings 4:2]]) in the days of Solomon.

column5: Son of Nathan, an official in Solomon's court
column7: Azariah, the son of Nathan, was an official in King Solomon's court (<ref="1Ki.4.5">1Ki.4.5</ref>).

column5: Son of Ethan, descendant of Judah
column7: Son of Ethan, of the tribe of Judah ([[@13002008|1 Chr. 2:8]]).

column5: Descendant of Jerahmeel, son of Hezron
column7: Azariah was a descendant of Jerahmeel, the son of Hezron, from the tribe of Judah (<ref="1Ch.2.38, 39">1Ch.2.38, 39</ref>).

column5: Descendant of Zadok, a priest before Solomon's reign
column7: Son of Ahimaaz, who succeeded his grandfather Zadok as high priest ([[@13006009|1 Chr. 6:9]]; [[@11004002|1 Kings 4:2]]) in the days of Solomon.

column5: Grandfather of Ezra, descended from High Priests
column7: Several other priests and Levites of this name are mentioned ([[@13006036|1 Chr. 6:36]]; [[@15007001|Ezra 7:1]]; [[@13009011|1 Chr. 9:11]]; [[@16003023|Neh. 3:23]], etc.).

column5: Prophet who encouraged King Asa to seek God
column7: The son of Oded, a remarkable prophet in the days of Asa ([[@14015001|2 Chr. 15:1]]).

column5: High priest who confronted King Uzziah
column7: High priest in the reign of Uzziah, king of Judah ([[@12014021|2 Kings 14:21]]; [[@14026017-14026020|2 Chr. 26:17-20]]).

column5: Leader who opposed the enslaving of captives
column7: Azariah, along with other leaders, opposed the enslaving of captives from Judah during the reign of King Ahaz (<ref="2Ch.28.12">2Ch.28.12</ref>).

column5: Chief priest during Hezekiah's reign
column7: High priest in the days of Hezekiah ([[@14031010-14031013|2 Chr. 31:10-13]]).

column5: Son of Maaseiah, repairer of Jerusalem's wall
column7: Several other priests and Levites of this name are mentioned ([[@13006036|1 Chr. 6:36]]; [[@15007001|Ezra 7:1]]; [[@13009011|1 Chr. 9:11]]; [[@16003023|Neh. 3:23]], etc.).

column5: Priest who participated in the dedication of Jerusalem's wall
column7: Azariah was a priest who participated in the dedication of Jerusalem's wall during Nehemiah's time (<ref="Neh.7.7; 10:2; 12:33">Neh.7.7; 10:2; 12:33</ref>).

column5: Levite who helped the people understand the Law
column7: Azariah was a Levite who helped the people understand the Law during the time of Ezra (<ref="Neh.8.7">Neh.8.7</ref>).

column5: One of Daniel's companions, survived the fiery furnace
Descendant of Reuben; father of Bela
column7: Azaz, a descendant of Reuben, was the father of Bela (<ref="1Ch.5.8">1Ch.5.8</ref>).

column5: Levite musician during David's reign
column7: One of the Levitical harpers in the temple ([[@13015021|1 Chr. 15:21]]).

column5: Leader of the half-tribe of Manasseh under David
column7: The father of Hoshea, who was made ruler over the Ephraimites ([[@13027020|1 Chr. 27:20]]).

column5: Levite during Hezekiah's reign, in charge of offerings
column7: One who had charge of the temple offerings ([[@14031013|2 Chr. 31:13]]).

column5: Father of Nehemiah, who repaired part of Jerusalem's wall
column7: Azbuk was the father of Nehemiah, who repaired a section of Jerusalem's wall near the tombs of David (<ref="Neh.3.16">Neh.3.16</ref>).

column5: Judean town, site of battles and sieges.
column7: Dug over, a town in the Shephelah or low hills of Judah ([[@6015035|Josh. 15:35]]), where the five confederated Amoritish kings were defeated by Joshua and their army destroyed by a hailstrom (10:10, 11).

column5: Descendant of Saul, had six sons
Ancestor of exiles who returned to Jerusalem
column6: a strong army; a gang of robbers
column7: Azgad was the ancestor of 1,222 (or 2,322) exiles who returned to Jerusalem (<ref="Ezr.2.12; 8:12; Neh.7.17">Ezr.2.12; 8:12; Neh.7.17</ref>).

column5: Leader who sealed the covenant during Nehemiah's time
column6: a strong army; a gang of robbers
column7: Azgad was one of the leaders who sealed the covenant during the time of Nehemiah (<ref="Neh.10.15">Neh.10.15</ref>).

column5: Descendant of Zattu, had married a foreign woman
column7: Aziza, a descendant of Zattu, was one of the men who had married foreign women during the time of Ezra (<ref="Ezr.10.27">Ezr.10.27</ref>).

column5: One of David's mighty men, a Barhumite
column7: One of David’s thirty warriors ([[@10023031|2 Sam. 23:31]]).

column5: Descendant of Saul, son of Jehoaddah
column7: Azmaveth, a descendant of Saul, son of Jehoaddah..

column5: Benjamite warrior who joined David at Ziklag
column7: Azmaveth, a Benjamite warrior, was one of the men who joined David at Ziklag when he was fleeing from Saul (<ref="1Ch.12.3">1Ch.12.3</ref>).

column5: Overseer of royal treasuries under King David
column7: An overseer over the royal treasury in the time of David and Solomon ([[@13027025|1 Chr. 27:25]]).

column5: Place on the southern border of Judah.
column6: bone of a bone; our strength
column7: Azmon was a place on the southern border of Judah.

column5: Border town of Naphtali near Mount Tabor.
column6: the ears of Tabor; the ears of purity or contrition
column7: Aznoth-tabor was a border town of Naphtali near Mount Tabor. (<ref="Joshua 19:34">Joshua 19:34</ref>)

column5: Ancestor of Jesus Christ in the genealogy of Matthew
column7: Azor was an ancestor of Jesus Christ, mentioned in the genealogy of Matthew (<ref="Matt 1:13, 14">Matt 1:13, 14</ref>).

column5: Head of a half-tribe of Manasseh in Gilead
column7: Azriel was a head of a father's house in the half-tribe of Manasseh in Gilead (<ref="1Ch.5.24">1Ch.5.24</ref>).

column5: Ruler of the tribe of Naphtali under David

column7: He has given a son, the father of the Babylonian king ([[@12020012|2 Kings 20:12]]; [[@23039001|Isa. 39:1]]) Merodach-baladan (q.v.).

column7: Heights, the forty-seventh station of the Israelites ([[@4021019|Num. 21:19]], [[@4021020|Num 21:20]]) in the territory of the Moabites.

column7: Heights of Baal, a place on the river Arnon, or in the plains through which it flows, east of Jordan ([[@6013017|Josh. 13:17]]; comp. [[@4021028|Num. 21:28]]).

column7: Barkos was the ancestor of a family of temple servants who returned from Babylonian captivity.

(Heb. kiyor), a “basin” for boiling in, a “pan” for cooking ([[@9002014|1 Sam. 2:14]]), a “fire-pan” or hearth ([[@38012006|Zech. 12:6]]), the sacred wash-bowl of the tabernacle and temple ([[@2030018|Ex. 30:18]], [[@2030028|Ex. 30:28]]; 31:9; 35:16; 38:8; 39:39; 40:7, 11, 30, etc.), a basin for the water used by the priests in their ablutions. column7: The eldest son of Benjamin ([[@4026038|Num. 26:38]]; “Belah,” [[@1046021|Gen. 46:21]]).

column7: Ben-hesed was one of Solomon's twelve officers over Israel.

column7: Beraiah was a Benjamite, a descendant of Shimei.

He was of the tribe of Judah, the son of Uri, and grandson of Hur (31:2).

column5: City where Judah defeated Canaanites
column7: The residence of Adoni-bezek, in the lot of Judah ([[@7001005|Judg. 1:5]]). It was in the mountains, not far from Jerusalem.

column5: Assembly point for Saul's army
column7: The place where Saul numbered the forces of Israel and Judah ([[@9011008|1 Sam. 11:8]]); somewhere in the centre of the country, near the Jordan valley.

column5: Levitical city of refuge in Reuben
column7: A city of the Reubenites; one of the three cities of refuge on the east of Jordan (Deut. 4: 43; [[@6020008|Josh. 20:8]]).

column5: Descendant of Asher through Helem
column7: Bezer was a descendant of Asher through Helem.

column5: Benjamite, father of the rebel Sheba
column7: Bichri, a Benjamite, was the father of Sheba, who led a rebellion against King David.

column5: Officer of Jehu who witnessed Ahab's judgment
column7: Bidkar, an officer of Jehu, witnessed the LORD's judgment against Ahab and his family.

column5: Eunuch in King Ahasuerus' court
column7: Garden, or gift of fortune, one of the seven eunuchs or chamberlains who had charge of the harem of Ahasuerus ([[@17001010|Esther 1:10]]).

column5: Persian official who plotted against King Ahasuerus
column7: One of the eunuchs who “kept the door” in the court of Ahasuerus. With Teresh he conspired against the king’s life.

column5: Leader who returned from Babylonian exile
column7: Bigvai was one of the leaders who returned to Jerusalem from Babylonian captivity.

column5: Ancestor of exiles who returned to Jerusalem
column7: Bigvai was an ancestor of over 2,000 individuals who returned to Jerusalem from Babylonian captivity.

column5: Judahite leader who sealed the covenant
column7: Bigvai, a leader of the people, sealed the covenant during Nehemiah's time.

column5: One of Job's three friends
column7: Son of contention, one of Job’s friends. He is called “the Shuhite,” probably as belonging to Shuah, a district in Arabia, in which Shuah, the sixth son of Abraham by Keturah, settled ([[@1025002|Gen. 25:2]]).

column5: Head of a priestly division in David's time
column7: The head of the fifteenth sacerdotal course for the temple service ([[@13024014|1 Chr. 24:14]]).

column5: Priest who returned from exile and sealed the covenant
column7: A priest who returned from Babylon with Zerubbabel ([[@16012005|Neh. 12:5]], [[@16012018|Neh. 12:18]]).

column5: Rachel's maidservant and mother of Dan and Naphtali
column6: Bilhan, who is old or confused
column7: Faltering; bashful, Rachel’s handmaid, whom she gave to Jacob ([[@1029029|Gen. 29:29]]). She was the mother of Dan and Naphtali ([[@1030003-1030008|Gen. 30:3-8]]). Reuben was cursed by his father for committing adultry with her (35:22; 49:4).

column5: Town in Simeon's territory
column6: Bilhan, who is old or confused
column7: Faltering; bashful, Rachel’s handmaid, whom she gave to Jacob ([[@1029029|Gen. 29:29]]). She was the mother of Dan and Naphtali ([[@1030003-1030008|Gen. 30:3-8]]). Reuben was cursed by his father for committing adultry with her (35:22; 49:4).

column5: Descendant of Esau and chief of Edom
column7: Bilhan, a descendant of Esau, was one of the chiefs of Edom.

column5: Leader who returned from Babylonian exile
column7: Son of the tongue; i.e., “eloquent”, a man of some note who returned from the Captivity with Zerubbabel ([[@15002002|Ezra 2:2]]; [[@16007007|Neh. 7:7]]).

column5: Son of Japhlet from the tribe of Asher
column7: Bimhal was a son of Japhlet, a descendant of Asher.

column5: Descendant of King Saul and Jonathan
column7: Binea was a descendant of King Saul and his son Jonathan.

column5: Levite who weighed the temple vessels after the exile
column7: Binnui, a Levite, was among those who weighed the temple vessels brought back from Babylon.

column5: Israelite who divorced his foreign wife during Ezra's reforms
column7: Binnui, one of the descendants of Pahath-moab, divorced his foreign wife during Ezra's reforms.

column5: Israelite who divorced his foreign wife during Ezra's reforms
column7: Binnui, one of the descendants of Bani, divorced his foreign wife during Ezra's reforms.

column5: Levite who repaired a section of Jerusalem's wall
column7: Binnui, son of Henadad, repaired a section of Jerusalem's wall near his house.

column5: King of Gomorrah during Abraham's time
column6: an evil; a son who beholds
column7: Son of wickedness, a king of Gomorrah whom Abraham succoured in the invasion of Chedorlaomer ([[@1014002|Gen. 14:2]]).

column5: A son or town of Malchiel
column7: Birzaith was a town or Malchiel, descendant of Asher through his son Beriah.

column5: Samaritan official who opposed the rebuilding of Jerusalem
column7: Bishlam was a Samaritan official who, along with others, wrote to King Artaxerxes to oppose the rebuilding of Jerusalem.

An overseer. In apostolic times, it is quite manifest that there was no difference as to order between bishops and elders or presbyters ([[@44020017-44020028|Acts 20:17-28]]; [[@60005001|1 Pet. 5:1]], [[@60005002|1 Pet. 5:2]]; [[@50001001|Phil. 1:1]]; 1 Tim. 3). The term bishop is never once used to denote a different office from that of elder or presbyter. These different names are simply titles of the same office, “bishop” designating the function, namely, that of oversight, and “presbyter” the dignity appertaining to the office.

column5: Daughter of Pharaoh who married Mered of Judah
column7: Bithiah, a daughter of Pharaoh, married Mered from the tribe of Judah.

column5: A ravine or region crossed by Abner's men
column7: Bithron, a ravine or region traversed by Abner and his men after a battle with Joab's forces.

column5: A region in Asia Minor
column7: A province in Asia Minor, to the south of the Euxine and Propontis. Christian congregations were here formed at an early time ([[@60001001|1 Pet. 1:1]]). Paul was prevented by the Spirit from entering this province ([[@44016007|Acts 16:7]]).

column5: A town in the Negev, allotted to Judah
column7: Biziothiah, a town in the Negev region, was allotted to the tribe of Judah.

column5: Eunuch in King Ahasuerus' court
column7: Biztha was one of the seven eunuchs who served King Ahasuerus.

column5: Herod's chamberlain who helped the people of Tyre and Sidon
column7: Chamberlain to king Herod Agrippa I. ([[@44012020|Acts 12:20]]).

column5: Kinsman-redeemer who married Ruth, ancestor of David and Jesus
column7: Boaz, a wealthy Bethlehemite, married Ruth and became an ancestor of King David and Jesus Christ.

column5: Son of Azel, a descendant of King Saul
column7: Bocheru was a son of Azel and a descendant of King Saul from the tribe of Benjamin.

column5: Reubenite after whom a boundary stone was named
column7: Bohan, son of Reuben, was the namesake of a boundary stone between the territories of Judah and Benjamin.

column5: A town in southern Judah
column7: Smoking furnace, one of the places where “David himself and his men were wont to haunt” ([[@9030030|1 Sam. 30:30]], [[@9030031|1 Sam. 30:31]]). It is probably identical with Ashan ([[@6015042|Josh. 15:42]]; [[@6019007|Josh 19:7]]), a Simeonite city in the Negeb, i.e., the south, belonging to Judah.

column5: A rocky crag near Michmash
column7: Bozez, one of the rocky crags that Jonathan and his armor-bearer crossed to attack the Philistine garrison.

column5: Town in Judah, birthplace of Josiah's mother
column7: Bozkath was a town in Judah and the birthplace of King Josiah's mother, Jedidah.

column5: Capital city of Edom
column7: The city of Jobab, one of the early Edomite kings ([[@1036033|Gen. 36:33]]). This place is mentioned by the prophets in later times ([[@23034006|Isa. 34:6]]; [[@24049013|Jer. 49:13]]; [[@30001012|Amos 1:12]]; [[@33002012|Micah 2:12]]). Its modern representative is el-Busseireh.

Among the Jews was generally made of wheat ([[@2029002|Ex. 29:2]]; [[@7006019|Judg. 6:19]]), though also sometimes of other grains ([[@1014018|Gen. 14:18]]; [[@7007013|Judg. 7:13]]). Parched grain was sometimes used for food without any other preparation ([[@8002014|Ruth 2:14]]). Bread was prepared by kneading in wooden bowls or “kneading troughs” ([[@1018006|Gen. 18:6]]; [[@2012034|Ex. 12:34]]; [[@24007018|Jer. 7:18]]). The dough was mixed with leaven and made into thin cakes, round or oval, and then baked.

column5: Section of Jerusalem's wall
column7: The Broad Wall was a section of Jerusalem's wall rebuilt during Nehemiah's time.

column5: Southwestern boundary of the Promised Land
column7: It is also applied to winter torrents ([[@18006015|Job 6:15]]; [[@4034005|Num. 34:5]]; [[@6015004|Josh. 15:4]], [[@6015047|Josh. 15:47]]), and to the torrent-bed or wady as well as to the torrent itself ([[@4013023|Num. 13:23]]; [[@11017003|1 Kings 17:3]]).

column5: Eastern boundary of Jeroboam II's kingdom
column7: The Brook of the Arabah was the eastern boundary of King Jeroboam II's kingdom.

column5: Boundary of Moab's territory
column7: The Brook of the Willows was a boundary of Moab's territory, possibly near the Wadi Zered.

column5: Son of Jogli, a prince of Dan
column7: Bukki, the son of Jogli, was a prince of the tribe of Dan chosen to help divide the Promised Land.

column5: High priest, son of Abishua and father of Uzzi
column7: Bukki, a high priest, was the son of Abishua and the father of Uzzi in the lineage of Aaron.

column5: Levite musician in David's time, son of Heman
column7: Bukkiah, a Levite and descendant of Heman, was a musician in the temple during David's reign.

column5: Son of Jerahmeel, descendant of Judah
column7: Bunah was a son of Jerahmeel and a descendant of Judah.

column5: Levite who led the people in confessing their sins
column7: Bunni, a Levite, was among those who led the people in confessing their sins during the time of Nehemiah.

column5: Israelite leader who sealed the covenant during Nehemiah's time
column7: Bunni was one of the leaders of the people who sealed the covenant during the time of Nehemiah.

column5: Levite who lived in Jerusalem during Nehemiah's time
column7: Bunni, a Levite, was a resident of Jerusalem during the time of Nehemiah.

Hebrew olah ; i.e., “ascending,” the whole being consumed by fire, and regarded as ascending to God while being consumed. Part of every offering was burnt in the sacred fire, but this was wholly burnt, a “whole burnt offering.” It was the most frequent form of sacrifice, and apparently the only one mentioned in the book of Genesis.

column5: Son of Nahor, Abraham's brother
column7: The second son of Nahor and Milcah, and brother of Huz ([[@1022021|Gen. 22:21]]).

column5: Descendant of Gad, son of Abdiel
column7: One of the chiefs of the tribe of Gad ([[@13005014|1 Chr. 5:14]]).

column5: Arabian tribe, possibly descendants of Nahor
column7: Buz was an Arabian tribe, possibly descended from Nahor, that was threatened with judgment.

column5: Father of Ezekiel the prophet
column7: The father of the prophet Ezekiel (1:3).

column5: Descendants of Buz, Nahor's son
column7: The Buzites were descendants of Buz, the son of Nahor, Abraham's brother.

column5: Town in Judah's lowlands
column7: Cabbon was a town in the lowlands of Judah.

column5: Border town of Asher
column7: A town on the eastern border of Asher ([[@6019027|Josh. 19:27]]), probably one of the towns given by Solomon to Hiram; the modern Kabul, some 8 miles east of Accho, on the very borders of Galilee.

column5: Name given to 20 cities by Hiram
column7: A district in the north-west of Galilee, near to Tyre, containing twenty cities given to Hiram by Solomon as a reward for various services rendered to him in building the temple ([[@11009013|1 Kings 9:13]]), and as payment of the six score talents of gold he had borrowed from him. Hiram gave the cities this name because he was not pleased with the gift, the name signifying “good for nothing.”

column5: Coastal city, center of Roman rule in Judea
column7: (Palestinae), a city on the shore of the Mediterranean, on the great road from Tyre to Egypt, about 70 miles northwest of Jerusalem, at the northern extremity of the plain of Sharon. It was built by Herod the Great (B.C. 10), who named it after Caesar Augustus, hence called Caesarea Sebaste (Gr. Sebastos = “Augustus”), on the site of an old town called “Strato’s Tower.” It was the capital of the Roman province of Judaea, the seat of the governors or procurators, and the headquarters of the Roman troops. It was the great Gentile city of Palestine, with a spacious artificial harbour.

column5: City where Peter confessed Jesus as Messiah
column7: Caesarea Philippi was the location where Peter acknowledged Jesus as the Messiah and Son of God.

column5: High priest during Jesus' ministry and trial
column7: The Jewish high priest (A.D. 27-36) at the beginning of our Lord’s public ministry, in the reign of Tiberius ([[@42003002|Luke 3:2]]), and also at the time of his condemnation and crucifixion ([[@40026003|Matt. 26:3]], [[@40026057|Matt 26:57]]; [[@43011049|John 11:49]]; [[@43018013|John 18:13]], [[@43018014|John 18:14]]). He held this office during the whole of Pilate’s administration. His wife was the daughter of Annas, who had formerly been high priest, and was probably the vicar or deputy (Heb. sagan) of Caiaphas.

column5: Adam and Eve's firstborn son, killed his brother Abel
column7: The first-born son of Adam and Eve (Gen. 4). He became a tiller of the ground, as his brother Abel followed the pursuits of pastoral life. He was “a sullen, self-willed, haughty, vindictive man; wanting the religious element in his character, and defiant even in his attitude towards God.” It came to pass “in process of time” (marg. “at the end of days”), i.e., probably on the Sabbath, that the two brothers presented their offerings to the Lord.

column5: Son of Arphaxad, ancestor of Jesus (Luke's genealogy)
column7: The son of Arphaxad ([[@42003036|Luke 3:36]]). He is nowhere named in the Old Testament.

column5: Ancient Assyrian city built by Nimrod
column7: One of the most ancient cities of Assyria. “Out of that land he [i.e., Nimrod] went forth into Assyria, and built Nineveh, Rehoboth-Ir, and Calah, and Resen” ([[@1010011|Gen. 10:11]], R.V.). Its site is now marked probably by the Nimrud ruins on the left bank of the Tigris. These cover an area of about 1,000 acres, and are second only in size and importance to the mass of ruins opposite Mosul.

column5: Wise man Solomon was compared to
column7: ([[@13002006|1 Chr. 2:6]]), sustenance, the same probably as Chalcol ([[@11004031|1 Kings 4:31]]), one of the four sages whom Solomon excelled in wisdom; for “he was wiser than all men.”

column5: Son of Zerah, grandson of Judah
column7: ([[@13002006|1 Chr. 2:6]]), sustenance, the same probably as Chalcol ([[@11004031|1 Kings 4:31]]), one of the four sages whom Solomon excelled in wisdom; for “he was wiser than all men.”

column5: Faithful spy, given Hebron as inheritance
column6: a dog; a crow; a basket
column7: The son of Jephunneh ([[@4013006|Num. 13:6]]; [[@4032012|Num 32:12]]; [[@6014006|Josh. 14:6]], [[@6014014|Josh. 14:14]]). He was one of those whom Moses sent to search the land in the second year after the Exodus. He was one of the family chiefs of the tribe of Judah. He and Joshua the son of Nun were the only two of the whole number who encouraged the people to go up and possess the land, and they alone were spared when a plague broke out in which the other ten spies perished (Num. 13; 14).

column5: Son of Hezron, descendant of Judah
column6: a dog; a crow; a basket
column7: One of the three sons of Hezron of the tribe of Judah. He is also called Chelubai ([[@13002009|1 Chr. 2:9]]).

column5: Place associated with Hezron's death
column7: Caleb Ephrathah was the place where Hezron, the son of Perez, died.

column5: Ancient Mesopotamian city, possibly Kullania or Kullanhu
column7: Fort, one of the four cities founded by Nimrod ([[@1010010|Gen. 10:10]]). It is the modern Niffer, a lofty mound of earth and rubbish situated in the marshes on the left, i.e., the east, bank of the Euphrates, but 30 miles distant from its present course, and about 60 miles south-south-east from Babylon. It is mentioned as one of the towns with which Tyre carried on trade. It was finally taken and probably destroyed by one of the Assyrian kings ([[@30006002|Amos 6:2]]).

The Arabian camel or dromedary, from the Greek dromos , “a runner” ([[@23060006|Isa. 60:6]]; [[@24002023|Jer. 2:23]]), has but one hump, and is a native of Western Asia or Africa. The camel was early used both for riding and as a beast of burden ([[@1024064|Gen. 24:64]]; [[@1037025|Gen 37:25]]), and in war ([[@9030017|1 Sam. 30:17]]; [[@23021007|Isa. 21:7]]). Mention is made of the camel among the cattle given by Pharaoh to Abraham ([[@1012016|Gen. 12:16]]). Its flesh was not to be eaten, as it was ranked among unclean animals ([[@3011004|Lev. 11:4]]; [[@5014007|Deut. 14:7]]).

column5: Son of Ham; father of Sidon and Heth
column6: merchant; trader; or that humbles and subdues
column7: The fourth son of Ham ([[@1010006|Gen. 10:6]]). His descendants were under a curse in consequence of the transgression of his father (9:22-27). His eldest son, Zidon, was the father of the Sidonians and Phoenicians.

column5: Ancient region; descendants of Ham; promised to Abraham's descendants
column6: merchant; trader; or that humbles and subdues
column7: The country which derived its name from the preceding. The name as first used by the Phoenicians denoted only the maritime plain on which Sidon was built. But in the time of Moses and Joshua it denoted the whole country to the west of the Jordan and the Dead Sea ([[@5011030|Deut. 11:30]]). In [[@6005012|Josh. 5:12]] the LXX. read, “land of the Phoenicians,” instead of “land of Canaan.”

column5: Shaul's mother, a Canaanite woman
column7: Shaul's mother was a Canaanite woman, according to the genealogies of Simeon.

column5: Town in Galilee; center of Jesus' ministry
column6: the field of repentance; city of comfort
column7: Nahum’s town, a Galilean city frequently mentioned in the history of our Lord. It is not mentioned in the Old Testament. After our Lord’s expulsion from Nazareth ([[@40004013-40004016|Matt. 4:13-16]]; [[@42004016-42004031|Luke 4:16-31]]), Capernaum became his “own city.” It was the scene of many acts and incidents of his life ([[@40008005|Matt. 8:5]], [[@40008014|Matt. 8:14]], [[@40008015|Matt. 8:15]]; 9:2-6, 10-17; 15:1-20; [[@41001032-41001034|Mark 1:32-34]], etc.).

column5: Island home of the Philistines; visited by Paul
column7: A chaplet, the original seat of the Philistines ([[@5002023|Deut. 2:23]]; [[@24047004|Jer. 47:4]]; [[@30009007|Amos 9:7]]). The name is found written in hieroglyphics in the temple of Kom Ombos in Upper Egypt. But the exact situation of Caphtor is unknown, though it is supposed to be Crete, since the Philistines seem to be meant by the “Cherethites” in [[@9030014|1 Sam. 30:14]] (see also [[@10008018|2 Sam. 8:18]]).

column5: Descendants of Mizraim who displaced the Avvim
column7: The Caphtorim, descendants of Mizraim, displaced the Avvim who lived in villages as far as Gaza.

column5: Region in Asia Minor; home to early Christian believers
column7: The easternmost and the largest province of Asia Minor. Christianity very early penetrated into this country ([[@60001001|1 Pet. 1:1]]).

column5: Ancient city; site of Babylonian victory over Egypt
column7: Fortress of Chemosh, a city on the west bank of the Euphrates ([[@24046002|Jer. 46:2]]; [[@14035020|2 Chr. 35:20]]), not, as was once supposed, the Circesium at the confluence of the Chebar and the Euphrates, but a city considerably higher up the river, and commanding the ordinary passage of the Euphrates; probably identical with Hierapolis. It was the capital of the kingdom of the northern Hittites. The Babylonian army, under Nebuchadnezzar, the son of Nabopolassar, here met and conquered the army of Pharaoh-necho, king of Egypt (B.C. 607).

column5: Eunuch in King Ahasuerus' court
column7: Carkas was one of the seven eunuchs who served King Ahasuerus.

column5: Town in Judah; home of Nabal and Abigail
column6: circumcised lamb; harvest; full of ears of corn
column7: A prominent headland of Central Palestine, consisting of several connected hills extending from the plain of Esdraelon to the sea, a distance of some 12 miles or more. At the east end, in its highest part, it is 1,728 feet high, and at the west end it forms a promontory to the bay of Acre about 600 feet above the sea. It lay within the tribe of Asher. It was here, at the east end of the ridge, at a place called el-Mukhrakah (i.e., the place of burning), that Elijah brought back the people to their allegiance to God, and slew the prophets of Baal (1 Kings 18).

column5: Mountain range; site of Elijah's confrontation with prophets of Baal
column7: Mount Carmel was a mountain range in northern Israel where the prophet Elijah confronted the prophets of Baal.

column5: Son of Reuben; father of the Carmites
column6: my vineyard; lamb of the waters
column7: The last named of the four sons of Reuben ([[@1046009|Gen. 46:9]]).

column5: Father of Achan, who stole devoted things
column6: my vineyard; lamb of the waters
column7: The son of Zimri, and the father of Achan ([[@6007001|Josh. 7:1]]), “the troubler of Israel.”

column5: Paul's friend in Troas
column7: Carpus was a friend of Paul in Troas, with whom Paul left his cloak, books, and parchments.

column5: Prince in King Ahasuerus' court
column7: Carshena was one of the seven princes of Persia and Media who had access to King Ahasuerus' presence.

column5: Descendants of Mizraim, ancestor of Philistines
column7: Fortified, a people descended from Mizraim ([[@1010014|Gen. 10:14]]; [[@13001012|1 Chr. 1:12]]).

column5: Island where Paul's ship sought shelter
column7: A small island off the southwest coast of Crete, passed by Paul on his voyage to Rome ([[@44027016|Acts 27:16]]). It is about 7 miles long and 3 broad.

column5: Port of Corinth; home of Phoebe
column7: Millet, the eastern harbour of Corinth, from which it was distant about 9 miles east, and the outlet for its trade with the Asiatic shores of the Mediterranean. When Paul returned from his second missionary journey to Syria, he sailed from this port ([[@44018018|Acts 18:18]]). In [[@45016001|Rom. 16:1]] he speaks as if there were at the time of his writing that epistle an organized church there. The western harbour of Corinth was Lechaeum, about a mile and a half from the city.

A Roman officer in command of a hundred men ([[@41015039|Mark 15:39]], [[@41015044|Mark 15:44]], [[@41015045|Mark 15:45]]). Cornelius, the first Gentile convert, was a centurion ([[@44010001|Acts 10:1]], [[@44010022|Acts 10:22]]).

column5: Ancient Mesopotamian empire; known for astrology and wisdom
column7: The southern portion of Babylonia, Lower Mesopotamia, lying chiefly on the right bank of the Euphrates, but commonly used of the whole of the Mesopotamian plain. The Hebrew name is Kasdim, which is usually rendered “Chaldeans” ([[@24050010|Jer. 50:10]]; [[@24051024|Jer 51:24]], [[@24051035|Jer 51:35]]). The country so named is a vast plain formed by the deposits of the Euphrates and the Tigris, extending to about 400 miles along the course of these rivers, and about 100 miles in average breadth.

A vehicle generally used for warlike purposes. Sometimes, though but rarely, it is spoken of as used for peaceful purposes. The first mention of the chariot is when Joseph, as a mark of distinction, was placed in Pharaoh’s second state chariot ([[@1041043|Gen. 41:43]]); and the next, when he went out in his own chariot to meet his father Jacob (46:29). Chariots formed part of the funeral procession of Jacob (50:9).

column5: River in Babylonia; location of Ezekiel's visions
column7: Length, a river in the “land of the Chaldeans” ([[@26001003|Ezek. 1:3]]), on the banks of which were located some of the Jews of the Captivity ([[@26001001|Ezek. 1:1]]; [[@26003015|Ezek 3:15]], [[@26003023|Ezek 3:23]]; [[@26010015|Ezek 10:15]], [[@26010020|Ezek 10:20]], [[@26010022|Ezek 10:22]]). It has been supposed to be identical with the river Habor, the Chaboras, or modern Khabour, which falls into the Euphrates at Circesium. To the banks of this river some of the Israelites were removed by the Assyrians ([[@12017006|2 Kings 17:6]]).

column5: King of Elam, led coalition against Sodom and Gomorrah
column7: (= Khudur-Lagamar of the inscriptions), king of Elam. Many centuries before the age of Abraham, Canaan and even the Sinaitic peninsula had been conquered by Babylonian kings, and in the time of Abraham himself Babylonia was ruled by a dynasty which claimed sovereignity over Syria and Palestine. The kings of the dynasty bore names which were not Babylonian, but at once South Arabic and Hebrew. The most famous king of the dynasty was Khammu-rabi, who united Babylonia under one rule, and made Babylon its capital.

column5: Israelite who married a foreign wife during Ezra's time
column7: Chelal was one of the Israelites who had married a foreign woman during the time of Ezra.

column5: Caleb's brother, son of Hezron
column7: Chelub, Caleb's brother and Hezron's son, was Mehir's father.

column5: Overseer of King David's farm workers
column7: Chelub the Ishmaelite was in charge of King David's farm workers.

column5: A man who married a foreign woman
column7: Cheluhi was among those who married foreign women during the Exile.

column5: False prophet who opposed Micaiah
column7: Zedekiah son of Chenaanah was a false prophet who opposed Micaiah.

column5: Son of Bilhan, descendant of Benjamin
column7: Chenaanah was a son of Bilhan and descendant of Benjamin.

column5: Levite who led the people in confession
column7: Chenani was a Levite who led the people in confession and worship.

column5: Levite leader of singing and administration under David
column6: preparation, or disposition, or strength, of the Lord
column7: Chenaniah was a Levite leader in charge of singing and administration during David's reign.

column5: Town in Benjamin's territory
column7: Chephar-ammoni was a town allotted to the tribe of Benjamin.

column5: Gibeonite town; later part of Benjamin and Judah
column7: Village, one of the four cities of the Gibeonitish Hivites with whom Joshua made a league (9:17). It belonged to Benjamin.

column5: Son of Dishon, descendant of Esau
column7: Cheran was a son of Dishon and a descendant of Esau.

column5: Member of Philistine tribe serving as royal guard
column7: The Cherethites were a Philistine tribe that served as royal guards for Israelite kings.

column5: Brook where Elijah hid during drought
column7: A cutting; separation; a gorge, a torrent-bed or winter-stream, a “brook,” in whose banks the prophet Elijah hid himself during the early part of the three years’ drought ([[@11017003|1 Kings 17:3]], [[@11017005|1 Kings 17:5]]). It has by some been identified as the Wady el-Kelt behind Jericho, which is formed by the junction of many streams flowing from the mountains west of Jericho. It is dry in summer. Travellers have described it as one of the wildest ravines of this wild region, and peculiarly fitted to afford a secure asylum to the persecuted.

column5: Babylonian location; home of some returning exiles
column7: Plural cherubim, the name of certain symbolical figures frequently mentioned in Scripture. They are first mentioned in connection with the expulsion of our first parents from Eden ([[@1003024|Gen. 3:24]]). There is no intimation given of their shape or form. They are next mentioned when Moses was commanded to provide furniture for the tabernacle ([[@2025017-2025020|Ex. 25:17-20]]; [[@2026001|Ex 26:1]], [[@2026031|Ex 26:31]]).
