column7: Esli was an ancestor of Jesus Christ, mentioned in His genealogy.

column5: Jewish queen of Persia; saved her people from genocide.
column7: The queen of Ahasuerus, and heroine of the book that bears her name. She was a Jewess named Hadas’sah (the myrtle), but when she entered the royal harem she received the name by which she henceforth became known ([[@17002007|Esther 2:7]]). It is a Syro-Arabian modification of the Persian word satarah, which means a star. She was the daughter of Abihail, a Benjamite.

column5: Cliff where Samson hid after defeating the Philistines
column7: A village of the tribe of Simeon ([[@13004032|1 Chr. 4:32]]). Into some cleft (“top,” A.V.,; R.V., “cleft”) of a rock here Samson retired after his slaughter of the Philistines ([[@7015008|Judg. 15:8]], [[@7015011|Judg. 15:11]]). It was a natural stronghold. It has been identified with Beit ’Atab, west of Bethlehem, near Zorah and Eshtaol.

column5: Villages associated with Simeon; home of Judahite clan
column7: A village of the tribe of Simeon ([[@13004032|1 Chr. 4:32]]). Into some cleft (“top,” A.V.,; R.V., “cleft”) of a rock here Samson retired after his slaughter of the Philistines ([[@7015008|Judg. 15:8]], [[@7015011|Judg. 15:11]]). It was a natural stronghold. It has been identified with Beit ’Atab, west of Bethlehem, near Zorah and Eshtaol.

column5: City fortified by Rehoboam in Judah
column7: A city of Judah, fortified by Rehoboam ([[@14011006|2 Chr. 11:6]]). It was near Bethlehem and Tekoah, and some distance apparently to the north of (1). It seems to have been in the district called Nephtoah (or Netophah), where were the sources of the water from which Solomon’s gardens and pleasure-grounds and pools, as well as Bethlehem and the temple, were supplied.

column5: Border town of Zebulun near Neah
column6: hour, or time, of a prince
column7: Eth-kazin, a border town of Zebulun located near Neah.

column5: Wilderness area where Israelites camped during the Exodus
column7: Perhaps another name for Khetam, or “fortress,” on the Shur or great wall of Egypt, which extended from the Mediterranean to the Gulf of Suez. Here the Israelites made their third encampment ([[@2013020|Ex. 13:20]]; [[@4033006|Num. 33:6]]). The camp was probably a little to the west of the modern town of Ismailia. Here the Israelites were commanded to change their route ([[@2014002|Ex. 14:2]]), and “turn” towards the south, and encamp before Pi-hahiroth.

column5: Wise man; Ezrahite; author of Psalm 89.
column6: strong; the gift of the island
column7: “The Ezrahite,” distinguished for his wisdom ([[@11004031|1 Kings 4:31]]). He is named as the author of the 89th Psalm.

column5: Son of Zerah; grandson of Judah.
column6: strong; the gift of the island
column7: Ethan was a son of Zerah and a grandson of Judah.

column5: King of Sidon; father of Jezebel.
column6: toward the idol, or with Baal
column7: Ethbaal was the king of Sidon and the father of Jezebel, who married King Ahab of Israel.

column5: City allotted to Judah and Simeon
column7: Ether, a city allotted to the tribes of Judah and Simeon in the Shephelah region.

column5: Son of Ashhur, the founder of Tekoa.
column7: Ethnan was a son of Ashhur (or 'Ashur'), the  father (ie founder) of Tekoa.

column5: Greeted by Paul in his letter to Timothy.
column7: Eubulus was a Christian who sent greetings to Timothy through Paul's letter.

column5: Mother of Timothy; a Jewish believer.
column7: Happily conquering, the mother of Timothy, a believing Jewess, but married to a Greek ([[@44016001|Acts 16:1]]). She trained her son from his childhood in the knowledge of the Scriptures ([[@55003015|2 Tim. 3:15]]).

column5: Christian woman in Philippi; urged by Paul to reconcile.
column7: A good journey, a female member of the church at Philippi. She was one who laboured much with Paul in the gospel. He exhorts her to be of one mind with Syntyche ([[@50004002|Phil. 4:2]]).

column5: Major river in ancient Near East; boundary of Promised Land
column7: Hebrew, Perath; Assyrian, Purat; Persian cuneiform, Ufratush, whence Greek Euphrates, meaning “sweet water.” The Assyrian name means “the stream,” or “the great stream.” It is generally called in the Bible simply “the river” ([[@2023031|Ex. 23:31]]), or “the great river” ([[@5001007|Deut. 1:7]]). The Euphrates is first mentioned in [[@1002014|Gen. 2:14]] as one of the rivers of Paradise.

column5: Young man in Troas; fell from window; restored by Paul.
column7: Fortunate, ([[@44020009-44020012|Acts 20:9-12]]), a young man of Troas who fell through drowsiness from the open window of the third floor of the house where Paul was preaching, and was “taken up dead.” The lattice-work of the window being open to admit the air, the lad fell out and down to the court below. Paul restored him to life again.

column5: First woman; wife of Adam; tempted by the serpent.
column7: Life; living, the name given by Adam to his wife ([[@1003020|Gen. 3:20]]; [[@1004001|Gen 4:1]]). The account of her creation is given in [[@1002021|Gen. 2:21]], [[@1002022|Gen. 2:22]]. The Creator, by declaring that it was not good for man to be alone, and by creating for him a suitable companion, gave sanction to monogamy. The commentator Matthew Henry says: “This companion was taken from his side to signify that she was to be dear unto him as his own flesh.

column5: Midianite king killed in battle against Israel.
column7: Evi was one of the Midianite kings killed by the Israelites during the time of Moses.

column5: King of Babylon; released Jehoiachin from prison.
column6: the fool of Merodach; the fool grinds bitterly
column7: Merodach’s man, the son and successor of Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon ([[@12025027|2 Kings 25:27]]; [[@24052031|Jer. 52:31]], [[@24052034|Jer. 52:34]]). He seems to have reigned but two years (B.C. 562-560). Influenced probably by Daniel, he showed kindness to Jehoiachin, who had been a prisoner in Babylon for thirty-seven years.

column5: Father of Naarai, one of David's mighty men.
column7: Ezbai was the father of Naarai, who was one of David's mighty men.

column5: Son of Gad; head of the Oznite clan.
column7: Hearing, one of the sons of Gad; also called Ezbon ([[@1046016|Gen. 46:16]]; [[@4026016|Num. 26:16]]).

column5: Son of Bela, grandson of Benjamin.
column7: Ezbon was a son of Bela and a grandson of Benjamin.

column5: Prophet during Babylonian exile; author of the Book of Ezekiel.
column7: One of the great prophets, the son of Buzi the priest ([[@26001003|Ezek. 1:3]]). He was one of the Jewish exiles who settled at Tel-Abib, on the banks of the Chebar, “in the land of the Chaldeans.” He was probably carried away captive with Jehoiachin (1:2; [[@12024014-12024016|2 Kings 24:14-16]]) about B.C. 597. His prophetic call came to him “in the fifth year of Jehoiachin’s captivity” (B.C. 594).

column5: Location where David and Jonathan planned to meet
column7: A separation, ([[@9020019|1 Sam. 20:19]]), a stone, or heap of stones, in the neighbourhood of Saul’s residence, the scene of the parting of David and Jonathan (42).

column5: City allotted to Judah and Simeon
column7: Ezem, a city allotted to the tribes of Judah and Simeon in the Negev region.

column5: Horite chief in Seir; son of Seir the Horite.
column7: One of the sons of Seir, the native princes, “dukes,” of Mount Hor ([[@1036021|Gen. 36:21]], [[@1036027|Gen. 36:27]]).

column5: Father or founder of Hushah, of Ephrathah.
column7: Ezer was the father or founder of Hushah and a son of Hur of Ephrathah.

column5: Son of Ephraim; killed by the men of Gath.
column7: Ezer was a son of Ephraim who was killed by the men of Gath while attempting to steal their livestock.

column5: Gadite warrior; joined David at Ziklag.
column7: Ezer was a Gadite warrior who joined David at Ziklag when he was fleeing from King Saul.

column5: Ruler of Mizpah; repaired a section of Jerusalem's wall.
column7: Ezer, the ruler of Mizpah, repaired another section of Jerusalem's wall near the armory.

column5: Levite; participated in the dedication of Jerusalem's wall.
column7: Ezer was a Levite who participated in the dedication of Jerusalem's wall during the time of Nehemiah.

column5: Israelite encampment; port city on Red Sea
column7: The giant’s backbone (so called from the head of a mountain which runs out into the sea), an ancient city and harbour at the north-east end of the Elanitic branch of the Red Sea, the Gulf of Akabah, near Elath or Eloth ([[@4033035|Num. 33:35]]; [[@5002008|Deut. 2:8]]). Here Solomon built ships, “Tarshish ships,” like those trading from Tyre to Tarshish and the west, which traded with Ophir ([[@11009026|1 Kings 9:26]]; [[@14008017|2 Chr. 8:17]]); and here also Jehoshaphat’s fleet was shipwrecked ([[@11022048|1 Kings 22:48]]; [[@14020036|2 Chr. 20:36]]).

column5: Adino the Eznite; one of David's mighty men.
column7: Adino the Eznite, also known as Josheb-Basshebeth, was one of David's mighty men who wielded his spear against eight hundred men.

column5: Priest; scribe; led a group of exiles back to Jerusalem.
column7: The “scribe” who led the second body of exiles that returned from Babylon to Jerusalem B.C. 459, and author of the book of Scripture which bears his name. He was the son, or perhaps grandson, of Seraiah ([[@12025018-12025021|2 Kings 25:18-21]]), and a lineal descendant of Phinehas, the son of Aaron ([[@15007001-15007005|Ezra 7:1-5]]). All we know of his personal history is contained in the last four chapters of his book, and in Neh. 8 and 12:26.

column5: Priest; returned from Babylon with Zerubbabel; participated in wall dedication.
column7: A priest among those that returned to Jerusalem under Zerubabel ([[@16012001|Neh. 12:1]]).

column5: Son of Chelub; mentioned in Judah's genealogy.
column7: Ezrah was a son of Chelub, mentioned in the genealogy of Judah.

column5: Overseer of David's agricultural workers.
column7: Help of Jehovah, the son of Chelub.

column5: Harbor on Crete; Paul's ship stopped during journey to Rome
column7: A harbour in the south of Crete, some 5 miles to the east of which was the town of Lasea ([[@44027008|Acts 27:8]]). Here the ship of Alexandria in which Paul and his companions sailed was detained a considerable time waiting for a favourable wind. Contrary to Paul’s advice, the master of the ship determined to prosecute the voyage, as the harbour was deemed incommodious for wintering in (9-12).

Faith is in general the persuasion of the mind that a certain statement is true ([[@50001027|Phil. 1:27]]; [[@53002013|2 Thess. 2:13]]). Its primary idea is trust. A thing is true, and therefore worthy of trust. It admits of many degrees up to full assurance of faith, in accordance with the evidence on which it rests.

column5: A close relative of John Mark.
column7: A reference to the grandfather or other close relative of John Mark.

column5: Father of Conaniah, a Levite in charge of offerings
column7: The father of Conaniah, a Levite who supervised the offerings during King Hezekiah's reign.

column5: The wife of Zechariah and mother of John the Baptist.
column7: Elizabeth was the wife of Zechariah, a priest, and the mother of John the Baptist.

column5: Father of Eunice - Grandfather of Timothy
column7: Eunice's father, unnamed in the Bible, was the maternal grandfather of Timothy.

column5: Father of Hilkiah, Jeremiah's cousin
column7: The father of Hilkiah, who was the cousin of the prophet Jeremiah.

column5: Father of Hodiah and Naham
column7: An unnamed man, the father Naham and his sister Hodiah

column5: The father of Mary, Martha and Lazarus of Bethany.
column7: The unnamed father of Mary, Martha and Lazarus, who lived in Bethany.

column5: Father of Mamre - Amorite, ally of Abraham
column7: Mamre's father, an Amorite, was an ally of Abraham during the battle against Chedorlaomer.

column5: Father of Nathan, one of David's mighty men
column7: The father of Nathan, one of King David's mighty men.

column5: Egyptian Pharaoh who gave his daughter to Hadad
column7: The father of Tahpenes, an Egyptian Pharaoh who gave his daughter in marriage to Hadad the Edomite.

column5: Father of Timothy - Greek man; husband of Eunice
column7: Timothy's father was a Greek man, and his mother was a believing Jewish woman named Eunice.

column5: Roman governor of Judea; heard Paul's case.
column7: Happy, the Roman procurator of Judea before whom Paul “reasoned” ([[@44024025|Acts 24:25]]). He appears to have expected a bribe from Paul, and therefore had several interviews with him. The “worthy deeds” referred to in 24:2 was his clearing the country of banditti and impostors. At the end of a two years’ term, Porcius Festus was appointed in the room of Felix (A.D. 60), who proceeded to Rome, and was there accused of cruelty and malversation of office by the Jews of Caesarea. The accusation was rendered nugatory by the influence of his brother Pallas with Nero.

column5: Roman governor of Judea; heard Paul's case; sent him to Rome.
column7: Porcius Festus succeeded Felix as the Roman governor of Judea and heard Paul's case, ultimately sending him to Rome for trial.

First mentioned in [[@1003007|Gen. 3:7]]. The fig-tree is mentioned ([[@5008008|Deut. 8:8]]) as one of the valuable products of Palestine. It was a sign of peace and prosperity ([[@11004025|1 Kings 4:25]]; [[@33004004|Micah 4:4]]; [[@38003010|Zech. 3:10]]). Figs were used medicinally ([[@12020007|2 Kings 20:7]]), and pressed together and formed into “cakes” as articles of diet ([[@9030012|1 Sam. 30:12]]; [[@24024002|Jer. 24:2]]).
That at the feast of Pentecost two loaves of leavened bread, made from the new flour, were to be waved in like manner ([[@3023015|Lev. 23:15]], [[@3023017|Lev. 23:17]]; [[@4028026|Num. 28:26]]).

column5: Gate in Jerusalem's wall; rebuilt by Hassenaah during Nehemiah's time
column7: The Fish Gate, a gate in Jerusalem's wall, was rebuilt by the sons of Hassenaah during Nehemiah's time and was a location of judgment and trade.

column5: Location of the battle between David's forces and Absalom's army
column7: The Forest of Ephraim, where the battle between David's forces and Absalom's army took place during Absalom's rebellion.

column5: Corinthian Christian; visited Paul in Ephesus.
column7: Fortunate, a disciple of Corinth who visited Paul at Ephesus, and returned with Stephanas and Achaicus, the bearers of the apostle’s first letter to the Corinthians ([[@46016017|1 Cor. 16:17]]).

column5: Marketplace on Appian Way; Christians met Paul on journey to Rome
column7: The Forum of Appius, a marketplace on the Appian Way, where Christians from Rome met Paul during his journey to the city as a prisoner.

column5: Gate in Jerusalem's wall; location of Levite singers during coronation
column7: The Foundation Gate, a gate in Jerusalem's wall, where a third of the Levite singers were positioned during the coronation of Joash.

column5: Gate in Jerusalem's wall; rebuilt by Shallun during Nehemiah's time
column7: The Fountain Gate, a gate in Jerusalem's wall, was rebuilt by Shallun during Nehemiah's time and was a location for processions and gatherings.

(Heb. lebonah; Gr. libanos, i.e., “white”), an odorous resin imported from Arabia ([[@23060006|Isa. 60:6]]; [[@24006020|Jer. 6:20]]), yet also growing in Palestine ([[@22004014|Cant. 4:14]]). It was one of the ingredients in the perfume of the sanctuary ([[@2030034|Ex. 30:34]]), and was used as an accompaniment of the meat-offering ([[@3002001|Lev. 2:1]], [[@3002016|Lev. 2:16]]; 6:15; 24:7).

column5: Son of Ebed; led a revolt against Abimelech.
column7: Loathing, the son of Ebed, in whom the Shechemites “placed their confidence” when they became discontented with Abimelech. He headed the revolution, and led out the men of Shechem against Abimelech; but was defeated, and fled to his own home ([[@7009026-7009046|Judg. 9:26-46]]).

column5: Mountain in Ephraim; burial place of Joshua
column7: A shaking, a hill, on the north side of which Joshua was buried ([[@6024030|Josh. 24:30]]; [[@7002009|Judg. 2:9]]), in the territory of Ephraim.

column5: Benjamite leader who settled in Jerusalem.
column7: Gabbai was a Benjamite leader who settled in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile.

column5: Raised stone platform in Jerusalem; location of Jesus' trial
column7: Gab Baitha, i.e., “the ridge of the house” = “the temple-mound,” on a part of which the fortress of Antonia was built. This “temple-mound” was covered with a tesselated “pavement” (Gr. lithostroton, i.e., “stone-paved”).

column5: Israelite tribe; descended from Gad, son of Jacob.
column7: Jacob’s seventh son, by Zilpah, Leah’s handmaid, and the brother of Asher ([[@1030011-1030013|Gen. 30:11-13]]; [[@1046016|Gen 46:16]], [[@1046018|Gen 46:18]]). In the Authorized Version of 30:11 the words, “A troop cometh: and she called,” etc., should rather be rendered, “In fortune [R.V., ‘Fortunate’]: and she called,” etc., or “Fortune cometh,” etc. The tribe of Gad during the march through the wilderness had their place with Simeon and Reuben on the south side of the tabernacle ([[@4002014|Num. 2:14]]).

column5: Prophet during the reigns of David and Solomon.
column7: A prophet who joined David in the “hold,” and at whose advice he quitted it for the forest of Hareth ([[@13029029|1 Chr. 29:29]]; [[@14029025|2 Chr. 29:25]]; [[@9022005|1 Sam. 22:5]]). Many years after we find mention made of him in connection with the punishment inflicted for numbering the people ([[@10024011-10024019|2 Sam. 24:11-19]]; [[@13021009-13021019|1 Chr. 21:9-19]]). He wrote a book called the “Acts of David” ([[@13029029|1 Chr. 29:29]]), and assisted in the arrangements for the musical services of the “house of God” ([[@14029025|2 Chr. 29:25]]).

column5: Son of Susi; representative of Manasseh among the spies.
column7: Fortunate, the representative of the tribe of Manasseh among the twelve “spies” sent by Moses to spy the land ([[@4013011|Num. 13:11]]).

column5: Son of Sodi; representative of Zebulun among the spies.
column6: goat of God; the Lord my happiness
column7: Fortune (i.e., sent) of God, the representative of the tribe of Zebulum among the twelve spies ([[@4013010|Num. 13:10]]).

column5: Father of Menahem, king of Israel.
column7: Gadi was the father of Menahem, who became king of Israel after assassinating Shallum.

column5: Son of Nahor and Reumah.
column7: Gaham was one of the sons born to Nahor, Abraham's brother, and his concubine Reumah.

column5: Ancestor of temple servants who returned from Babylonian exile.
column7: Lurking-place, one of the chief of the Nethinim, whose descendants returned to Jerusalem under Zerubbabel ([[@15002047|Ezra 2:47]]).

column5: Macedonian; Paul's traveling companion; caught in Ephesian riot.
column7: Gaius, a Macedonian and traveling companion of Paul, was seized along with Aristarchus during the riot in Ephesus.

column5: Derbean; accompanied Paul on his journey to Jerusalem.
column7: Gaius of Derbe accompanied Paul on his journey from Greece to Jerusalem, along with several others.

column5: Corinthian believer; host to Paul and the church.
column7: A Macedonian, Paul’s fellow-traveller, and his host at Corinth when he wrote his Epistle to the Romans (16:23). He with his household were baptized by Paul ([[@46001014|1 Cor. 1:14]]). During a heathen outbreak against Paul at Ephesus the mob seized Gaius and Aristarchus because they could not find Paul, and rushed with them into the theatre. Some have identified this Gaius with No.

column5: Recipient of John's third epistle; commended for his faithfulness.
column7: A Christain of Asia Minor to whom John addressed his third epistle ([[@64001001|3 John 1]]:1).

column5: Levite musician; descendant of Asaph; lived in Jerusalem.
column7: Galal, a Levite musician and descendant of Asaph, lived in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile.

column5: Levite musician; descendant of Jeduthun; lived in Jerusalem.
column7: Galal, a Levite musician and descendant of Jeduthun, lived in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile and assisted in the temple service.

column5: A region in Asia Minor, recipient of Paul's epistle.
column7: Has been called the “Gallia” of the East, Roman writers calling its inhabitants Galli. They were an intermixture of Gauls and Greeks, and hence were called Gallo-Graeci, and the country Gallo-Graecia. The Galatians were in their origin a part of that great Celtic migration which invaded Macedonia about B.C. 280. They were invited by the king of Bithynia to cross over into Asia Minor to assist him in his wars.

column5: Region in northern Israel; key location in Jesus' ministry
column7: Circuit. Solomon rewarded Hiram for certain services rendered him by the gift of an upland plain among the mountains of Naphtali. Hiram was dissatisfied with the gift, and called it “the land of Cabul” (q.v.). The Jews called it Galil.

column5: Town in Benjamin; home of Michal's husband Paltiel
column7: Heaps, ([[@9025044|1 Sam. 25:44]]; [[@23010030|Isa. 10:30]]). The native place of Phalti, to whom Michal was given by Saul.

column5: Roman proconsul of Achaia; refused to judge Paul.
column6: who sucks, or lives on milk
column7: The elder brother of Seneca the philosopher, who was tutor and for some time minister of the emperor Nero. He was “deputy”, i.e., proconsul, as in Revised Version, of Achaia, under the emperor Claudius, when Paul visited Corinth ([[@44018012|Acts 18:12]]). The word used here by Luke in describing the rank of Gallio shows his accuracy. Achaia was a senatorial province under Claudius, and the governor of such a province was called a “proconsul.”

column5: People group; defenders of the towers of Tyre
column7: ([[@26027011|Ezek. 27:11]]) brave warriors; R.V. marg., “valorous men;” others interpret this word as meaning “short-swordsmen,” or “daring ones”, the name of a class of men who were defenders of the towers of Tyre.

column5: Leader of the tribe of Manasseh during the Exodus.
column6: recompense of God; camel of God
column7: A chief of the tribe of Manasseh at the census at Sinai ([[@4001010|Num. 1:10]]; [[@4002020|Num 2:20]]; [[@4007054|Num 7:54]], [[@4007059|Num 7:59]]).

column5: Pharisee; teacher of the law; Paul's mentor.
column6: recompense of God; camel of God
column7: The son of rabbi Simeon, and grandson of the famous rabbi Hillel. He was a Pharisse, and therefore the opponent of the party of the Sadducees. He was noted for his learning, and was president of the Sanhedrim during the regins of Tiberius, Caligula, and Claudius, and died, it is said, about eighteen years before the destruction of Jerusalem. When the apostles were brought before the council, charged with preaching the resurrection of Jesus, as a zealous Pharisee Gamaliel councelled moderation and calmness.

column5: Head of a priestly division in David's time.
column7: Weaned the leader of one of the priestly courses ([[@13024017|1 Chr. 24:17]]).

column5: One of David's mighty warriors; an Ithrite.
column7: One of David’s warriors ([[@10023038|2 Sam. 23:38]]), an Ithrite.

column5: A hill near Jerusalem
column7: A hill near Jerusalem ([[@24031039|Jer. 31:39]]), probably the hill of lepers, and consequently a place outside the boundary of the city.

column5: Inhbibants around Keilah in Judah.
column6: men of Garmi, ie., bones, or, my cause
column7: The Garmite town of Keilah was founded by a son of Hodiah of Judah.

column5: Son of Eliphaz; grandson of Esau; Edomite chief.
column7: Gatam was a son of Eliphaz, grandson of Esau, and one of the chiefs of Edom.

column5: Philistine city; home of Goliath; refuge for David
column7: A wine-vat, one of the five royal cities of the Philistines ([[@6013003|Josh. 13:3]]) on which the ark brought calamity ([[@9005008|1 Sam. 5:8]], [[@9005009|1 Sam. 5:9]]; 6:17). It was famous also as being the birthplace or residence of Goliath ([[@9017004|1 Sam. 17:4]]). David fled from Saul to Achish, king of Gath ([[@9021010|1 Sam. 21:10]]; [[@9027002-9027004|1 Sam. 27:2-4]]; Ps. 56), and his connection with it will account for the words in [[@10001020|2 Sam. 1:20]]. It was afterwards conquered by David ([[@10008001|2 Sam. 8:1]]).

column5: Town in Zebulun; hometown of prophet Jonah
column7: Wine-press of the well, a town of Lower Galilee, about 5 miles from Nazareth; the birthplace of Jonah ([[@12014025|2 Kings 14:25]]); the same as Gittah-hepher ([[@6019013|Josh. 19:13]]). It has been identified with the modern el-Meshed, a village on the top of a rocky hill.

column5: Levitical city in Dan and Manasseh
Philistine city; Samson's exploits; Philip's ministry
column7: Called also Azzah, which is its Hebrew name ([[@5002023|Deut. 2:23]]; [[@11004024|1 Kings 4:24]]; [[@24025020|Jer. 25:20]]), strong, a city on the Mediterranean shore, remarkable for its early importance as the chief centre of a great commercial traffic with Egypt. It is one of the oldest cities of the world ([[@1010019|Gen. 10:19]]; [[@6015047|Josh. 15:47]]). Its earliest inhabitants were the Avims, who were conquered and displaced by the Caphtorims ([[@5002023|Deut. 2:23]]; [[@6013002|Josh. 13:2]], [[@6013003|Josh. 13:3]]), a Philistine tribe.

column5: Ancestor of temple servants who returned from Babylonian exile.
column7: Gazzam was an ancestor of a group of temple servants (Nethinim) who returned to Jerusalem from the Babylonian exile.

column5: Valley of craftsmen; inhabited by Benjamites after the exile
column7: Ge-harashim, the Valley of Craftsmen, was inhabited by some Benjamites after the return from the Babylonian exile.

column5: A Levitical city in Benjamin
column7: The hill, ([[@10005025|2 Sam. 5:25]] [[[@13014016|1 Chr. 14:16]], “Gibeon”]; [[@12023008|2 Kings 23:8]]; [[@16011031|Neh. 11:31]]), a Levitical city of Benjamin ([[@11015022|1 Kings 15:22]]; [[@9013016|1 Sam. 13:16]]; [[@9014005|1 Sam. 14:5]], wrongly “Gibeah” in the A.V.), on the north border of Judah near Gibeah ([[@23010029|Isa. 10:29]]; [[@6018024|Josh. 18:24]], [[@6018028|Josh. 18:28]]). “From Geba to Beersheba” expressed the whole extent of the kingdom of Judah, just as “from Dan to Beersheba” described the whole length of Palestine ([[@12023008|2 Kings 23:8]]).

column5: Phoenician city; skilled builders; allied against Israel
column7: A tract in the land of Edom south of the Dead Sea ([[@19083007|Ps. 83:7]]); now called Djebal.

column5: Son of Uri; one of Solomon's twelve district governors.
column7: A valiant man, ([[@11004019|1 Kings 4:19]]), one of Solomon’s purveyors, having jurisdiction over a part of Gilead, comprising all the kingdom of Sihon and part of the kingdom of Og (Deut. 2; 31).

column5: Town in Benjamin; mentioned in Isaiah's prophecy
column7: Cisterns, (rendered “pits,” [[@24014003|Jer. 14:3]]; “locusts,” [[@23033004|Isa. 33:4]]), a small place north of Jerusalem, whose inhabitants fled at the approach of the Assyrian army ([[@23010031|Isa. 10:31]]).

column5: Appointed governor of Judah by Babylonians; assassinated by Ishmael.
column7: The son of Ahikam, and grandson of Shaphan, secretary of king Josiah ([[@24026024|Jer. 26:24]]). After the destruction of Jerusalem (see ZEDEKIAH), Nebuchadnezzar left him to govern the country as tributary to him ([[@12025022|2 Kings 25:22]]; [[@24040005|Jer. 40:5]]; [[@24052016|Jer 52:16]]). Ishmael, however, at the head of a party of the royal family, “Jewish irreconcilables”, rose against him, and slew him and “all the Jews that were with him” ([[@24041002|Jer. 41:2]], [[@24041003|Jer. 41:3]]) at Mizpah about three months after the destruction of Jerusalem.

column5: Son of Jeduthun; a temple musician during David's reign.
column7: Gedaliah, a son of Jeduthun, was one of the temple musicians appointed by King David to prophesy with lyres, harps, and cymbals.

column5: Priest who married a foreign woman during the Exile.
column7: Gedaliah, a priest, was among those who had married foreign women during the Babylonian exile and pledged to put them away.

column5: Son of Pashhur; an official during Zedekiah's reign.
column7: One of the Jewish nobles who conspired against Jeremiah ([[@24038001|Jer. 38:1]]).

column5: Grandfather of the prophet Zephaniah.
column7: The grandfather of the prophet Zephaniah, and the father of Cushi ([[@36001001|Zeph. 1:1]]).

column5: Town in Judah; home of Baal-hanan and Jozabad
column7: The fortress; a fortified place, a town in the plain (shephelah) of Judah ([[@6015036|Josh. 15:36]]). This is a very common Canaanite and Phoenician name. It is the feminine form of Geder (12:13); the plural form is Gederoth (15:41).

column5: Town in Judah; captured by Philistines during Ahaz's reign
column7: Gederoth, a town in Judah, was captured by the Philistines during the reign of King Ahaz.

column5: Town in Judah; mentioned in list of allotted cities
column7: Gederothaim, a town in Judah, is mentioned in the list of cities allotted to the tribe of Judah.

column5: Town in Judah; home of Judahite clan members
column7: A town apparently in Benjamin ([[@13012007|1 Chr. 12:7]]), the same probably as Geder ([[@6012013|Josh. 12:13]]).

column5: Region where Simeonites sought pasture for their flocks
column7: [[@13004039|1 Chr. 4:39]], the Gederah of [[@6015036|Josh. 15:36]], or the well-known Gerar, as the LXX. read, where the patriarchs of old had sojourned and fed their flocks ([[@1020001|Gen. 20:1]], [[@1020014|Gen. 20:14]], [[@1020015|Gen. 20:15]]; 26:1, 6, 14).

column5: Son of Abiel, the founder of Gibeon.
column7: Gedor was a son of Abiel (or 'Jeiel'), the  father (ie re-founder) of Gibeon, and an ancestor of King Saul.

column5: Elisha's servant; punished with leprosy for greed and deceit.
column7: Valley of vision, Elisha’s trusted servant ([[@12004031|2 Kings 4:31]]; [[@12005025|2 Kings 5:25]]; [[@12008004|2 Kings 8:4]], [[@12008005|2 Kings 8:5]]). He appears in connection with the history of the Shunammite ([[@12004014|2 Kings 4:14]], [[@12004031|2 Kings 4:31]]) and of Naaman the Syrian. On this latter occasion he was guilty of duplicity and dishonesty of conduct, causing Elisha to denounce his crime with righteous sternness, and pass on him the terrible doom that the leprosy of Naaman would cleave to him and his for ever (5:20-27).

column5: Father of Ammiel, the spy from the tribe of Dan.
column7: Gemalli was the father of Ammiel, who represented the tribe of Dan as one of the twelve spies sent to explore Canaan.

column5: Son of Hilkiah; messenger sent by Zedekiah to Nebuchadnezzar.
column6: accomplishment or perfection of the Lord
column7: The son of Hilkiah, who accompanied Shaphan with the tribute-money from Zedekiah to Nebuchadnezzar, and was the bearer at the same time of a letter from Jeremiah to the Jewish captives at Babylon ([[@24029003|Jer. 29:3]], [[@24029004|Jer. 29:4]]).

column5: Son of Shaphan; official during Jehoiakim's reign; opposed burning scroll.
column6: accomplishment or perfection of the Lord
column7: The son of Shaphan, and one of the Levites of the temple in the time of Jehoiakim ([[@24036010|Jer. 36:10]]; [[@12022012|2 Kings 22:12]]). Baruch read aloud to the people from Gemariah’s chamber, and again in the hearing of Gemariah and other scribes, the prophecies of Jeremiah ([[@24036011-24036020|Jer. 36:11-20]]), which filled him with terror.

(Heb., usually in plural, goyim), meaning in general all nations except the Jews. In course of time, as the Jews began more and more to pride themselves on their peculiar privileges, it acquired unpleasant associations, and was used as a term of contempt.

column5: Descendant of Benjamin; ancestor of Ehud, a judge of Israel.
column7: The son of Bela and grandson of Benjamin ([[@13008003|1 Chr. 8:3]], [[@13008005|1 Chr. 8:5]], [[@13008007|1 Chr. 8:7]]).

column5: Benjamite; cursed David during Absalom's rebellion; later sought forgiveness.
column7: The father of Shimei, who so grossly abused David ([[@10016005|2 Sam. 16:5]]; [[@10019016|2 Sam. 19:16]], [[@10019018|2 Sam. 19:18]]).

column5: Son of Bela, grandson of Benjamin.
column7: The son of Bela and grandson of Benjamin ([[@13008003|1 Chr. 8:3]], [[@13008005|1 Chr. 8:5]], [[@13008007|1 Chr. 8:7]]).

column5: Son of Ehud, a Benjamite.
column7: The son of Bela and grandson of Benjamin ([[@13008003|1 Chr. 8:3]], [[@13008005|1 Chr. 8:5]], [[@13008007|1 Chr. 8:7]]).

column5: Philistine city; Abraham and Isaac's encounters with Abimelech
column7: A region; lodging-place, a very ancient town and district in the south border of Palestine, which was ruled over by a king named Abimelech ([[@1010019|Gen. 10:19]]; [[@1020001|Gen 20:1]], [[@1020002|Gen 20:2]]). Abraham sojourned here, and perhaps Isaac was born in this place. Both of these patriarchs were guilty of the sin of here denying their wives, and both of them entered into a treaty with the king before they departed to Beersheba (21:23-34; 26). It seems to have been a rich pastoral country ([[@14014012-14014018|2 Chr. 14:12-18]]).

column5: Region where Jesus healed a demon-possessed man
column7: Gerasa (or Gadara), a region southeast of the Sea of Galilee, was the location where Jesus healed a demon-possessed man.

column5: Mountain in Samaria; site of blessings and Jotham's parable
column7: Mount Gerizim, a mountain in Samaria, was designated as the site for pronouncing blessings and was the location of Jotham's parable to the men of Shechem.

column5: Son of Moses; father of Jonathan, a renegade priest.
column7: The elder of the two sons of Moses born to him in Midian ([[@2002022|Ex. 2:22]]; [[@2018003|Ex 18:3]]).

column5: Descendant of Phinehas; returned to Jerusalem with Ezra.
column7: A descendant of Phinehas who returned with Ezra from Babylon ([[@15008002|Ezra 8:2]]).

column5: Firstborn son of Levi; head of the Gershonite Levites.
column6: his banishment; the change of pilgrimage
column7: =Ger’shom expulsion, the eldest of Levi’s three sons ([[@1046011|Gen. 46:11]]; [[@2006016|Ex. 6:16]]). In the wilderness the sons of Gershon had charge of the fabrics of the tabernacle when it was moved from place to place, the curtains, veils, tent-hangings (Num. 3: 21-26).

column5: Lodging place near Bethlehem; refuge for Johanan's group
column7: Geruth Chimham, a lodging place near Bethlehem, served as a temporary refuge for Johanan and his group after the murder of Gedaliah.

column5: Son of Jahdai, a descendant of Caleb.
column7: Geshan was a son of Jahdai, a wife of Caleb, from the tribe of Judah.

column5: Arab opponent of Nehemiah; tried to hinder wall rebuilding.
column7: Or Gashmu, firmness, probably chief of the Arabs south of Palestine, one of the enemies of the Jews after the return from Babylon ([[@16002019|Neh. 2:19]]; [[@16006001|Neh 6:1]], [[@16006002|Neh 6:2]]).

column5: Aramean kingdom; Talmai's domain; refuge for Absalom
column6: Geshuri, sight of the valley; a walled valley
column7: Bridge, the name of a district or principality of Syria near Gilead, between Mount Hermon and the Lake of Tiberias ([[@10015008|2 Sam. 15:8]]; [[@13002023|1 Chr. 2:23]]). The Geshurites probably inhabited the rocky fastness of Argob, the modern Lejah, in the north-east corner of Bashan.

column5: Son of Aram; grandson of Shem; part of Table of Nations.
column6: the vale of trial or searching
column7: Gether was a son of Aram and a grandson of Shem, mentioned in the genealogies of the Table of Nations.

column5: Garden near Jerusalem; site of Jesus' prayer and arrest
column6: a very fat or plentiful vale
column7: Oil-press, the name of an olive-yard at the foot of the Mount of Olives, to which Jesus was wont to retire ([[@42022039|Luke 22:39]]) with his disciples, and which is specially memorable as being the scene of his agony ([[@41014032|Mark 14:32]]; [[@43018001|John 18:1]]; [[@42022044|Luke 22:44]]). The plot of ground pointed out as Gethsemane is now surrounded by a wall, and is laid out as a modern European flower-garden. It contains eight venerable olive-trees, the age of which cannot, however, be determined. The exact site of Gethsemane is still in question.

column5: Son of Machi; representative of Gad among the twelve spies.
column7: Geuel, the son of Machi, was the representative of the tribe of Gad among the twelve spies sent by Moses to explore Canaan.

column5: A Canaanite city, conquered by Joshua and later by David.
column7: A precipice, an ancient royal Canaanitish city ([[@6010033|Josh. 10:33]]; [[@6012012|Josh 12:12]]). It was allotted with its suburbs to the Kohathite Levites (21:21; [[@13006067|1 Chr. 6:67]]). It stood between the lower Beth-horon and the sea ([[@6016003|Josh. 16:3]]; [[@11009017|1 Kings 9:17]]). It was the last point to which David pursued the Philistines ([[@10005025|2 Sam. 5:25]]; [[@13014016|1 Chr. 14:16]]) after the battle of Baal-perazim.

column5: Location near Gibeon where Joab and Abishai pursued Abner.
column6: to guide; draw out; produce; a groan or sigh
column7: Giah was a place near Gibeon where Joab and Abishai pursued Abner after the battle at the pool of Gibeon.

column5: A Levitical city in the territory of Dan.
column7: A height, a city of the Philistines in the territory of Dan, given to the Kohathites ([[@6019044|Josh. 19:44]]; [[@6021023|Josh 21:23]]). Nadab the king of Israel, while besieging it, was slain under its walls by Baasha, one of his own officers ([[@11015027|1 Kings 15:27]]).

column5: With Machbenah, daughters or towns of Sheva.
column7: Gibea, with Machbenah, daughters or cities founded by Sheva.

column5: A town in the hill country of Judah.
column7: A hill or hill-town, “of Benjamin” ([[@9013015|1 Sam. 13:15]]), better known as “Gibeah of Saul” (11:4; [[@23010029|Isa. 10:29]]). It was here that the terrible outrage was committed on the Levite’s concubine which led to the almost utter extirpation of the tribe of Benjamin (Judg. 19; 20), only six hundred men surviving after a succession of disastrous battles. This was the birthplace of Saul, and continued to be his residence after he became king ([[@9010026|1 Sam. 10:26]]; [[@9011004|1 Sam. 11:4]]; [[@9015034|1 Sam. 15:34]]).

column5: A city of Benjamin, associated with Saul and atrocities.
column7: A hill or hill-town, “of Benjamin” ([[@9013015|1 Sam. 13:15]]), better known as “Gibeah of Saul” (11:4; [[@23010029|Isa. 10:29]]). It was here that the terrible outrage was committed on the Levite’s concubine which led to the almost utter extirpation of the tribe of Benjamin (Judg. 19; 20), only six hundred men surviving after a succession of disastrous battles. This was the birthplace of Saul, and continued to be his residence after he became king ([[@9010026|1 Sam. 10:26]]; [[@9011004|1 Sam. 11:4]]; [[@9015034|1 Sam. 15:34]]).

column5: A place with a garrison of Philistines, near Gibeah.
column7: Gibeath-elohim, meaning "Hill of God," was a place near Gibeah where a garrison of Philistines was located (<ref="1Sa.10.5">1Sa.10.5</ref>).

column5: Hivite city that tricked Joshua into a peace treaty.
column7: Hill-city, “one of the royal cities, greater than Ai, and all the men thereof were mighty” ([[@6010002|Josh. 10:2]]). Its inhabitants were Hivites (11:19). It lay within the territory of Benjamin, and became a priest-city (18:25; 21:17). Here the tabernacle was set up after the destruction of Nob, and here it remained many years till the temple was built by Solomon.

column5: Son of Heman; a temple musician during David's reign.
column7: Giddalti was one of the sons of Heman, appointed by King David as a temple musician to prophesy with lyres, harps, and cymbals.

column5: Ancestor of temple servants who returned from Babylonian exile.
column7: Giddel was an ancestor of a group of temple servants (Nethinim) who returned to Jerusalem from the Babylonian exile.

column5: Ancestor of Solomon's servants who returned from Babylonian exile.
column7: Giddel was an ancestor of a group of Solomon's servants who returned to Jerusalem from the Babylonian exile.

column5: Judge of Israel; defeated Midianites; tested and reassured by God.
column6: he that bruises or breaks; a destroyer
column7: Called also Jerubbaal ([[@7006029|Judg. 6:29]], [[@7006032|Judg. 6:32]]), was the first of the judges whose history is circumstantially narrated (Judg. 6-8). His calling is the commencement of the second period in the history of the judges. After the victory gained by Deborah and Barak over Jabin, Israel once more sank into idolatry, and the Midianites (q.v.) and Amalekites, with other “children of the east,” crossed the Jordan each year for seven successive years for the purpose of plundering and desolating the land.

column5: Leader of the tribe of Benjamin during the Exodus.
column6: he that bruises or breaks; a destroyer
column7: Gideoni, the son of Abidan, was the leader of the tribe of Benjamin during the Israelites' journey through the wilderness.

column5: A place near Gibeah, associated with the Benjamite War.
column7: Gidom was a place near Gibeah where the Benjamites were pursued and defeated during the Benjamite War (<ref="Judges 20:45">Judges 20:45</ref>).

column5: A river of Eden; a spring near Jerusalem.
column7: The only natural spring of water in or near Jerusalem is the “Fountain of the Virgin” (q.v.), which rises outside the city walls on the west bank of the Kidron valley. On the occasion of the approach of the Assyrian army under Sennacherib, Hezekiah, in order to prevent the besiegers from finding water, “stopped the upper water course of Gihon, and brought it straight down to the west side of the city of David” ([[@14032030|2 Chr. 32:30]]; [[@14033014|2 Chr. 33:14]]). This “fountain” or spring is therefore to be regarded as the “upper water course of Gihon.”

column5: Priest and musician during the dedication of Jerusalem's wall.
column7: Gilalai was a priest and musician who participated in the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem during Nehemiah's time.

column5: A mountain range where Saul and his sons died.
column7: Boiling spring, a mountain range, now Jebel Fukua’, memorable as the scene of Saul’s disastrous defeat by the Philistines. Here also his three sons were slain, and he himself died by his own hand ([[@9028004|1 Sam. 28:4]]; [[@9031001-9031008|1 Sam. 31:1-8]]; [[@10001006-10001021|2 Sam. 1:6-21]]; [[@10021012|2 Sam. 21:12]]; [[@13010001|1 Chr. 10:1]], [[@13010008|1 Chr. 10:8]]). It was a low barren range of mountains bounding the valley of Esdraelon (Jezreel) on the east, between it and the Jordan valley.

column5: A mountain range where Saul and his sons died.
column7: Mount Gilboa was the site where Saul and his sons were killed in battle against the Philistines (<ref="1Sa.31.1, 8; 2Sa.1.6; 1Ch.10.1, 8; Judges 7:3">1Sa.31.1, 8; 2Sa.1.6; 1Ch.10.1, 8; Judges 7:3</ref>).

column5: Mountainous region east of Jordan; tribal territory and personal name.
column6: the heap or mass of testimony
column7: Hill of testimony, ([[@1031021|Gen. 31:21]]), a mountainous region east of Jordan. From its mountainous character it is called “the mount of Gilead” ([[@1031025|Gen. 31:25]]). It is called also “the land of Gilead” ([[@4032001|Num. 32:1]]), and sometimes simply “Gilead” ([[@19060007|Ps. 60:7]]; [[@1037025|Gen. 37:25]]). It comprised the possessions of the tribes of Gad and Reuben and the south part of Manasseh ([[@5003013|Deut. 3:13]]; [[@4032040|Num. 32:40]]).

column5: Son of Machir; grandson of Manasseh; father of six sons.
column6: the heap or mass of testimony
column7: Hill of testimony, ([[@1031021|Gen. 31:21]]), a mountainous region east of Jordan. From its mountainous character it is called “the mount of Gilead” ([[@1031025|Gen. 31:25]]). It is called also “the land of Gilead” ([[@4032001|Num. 32:1]]), and sometimes simply “Gilead” ([[@19060007|Ps. 60:7]]; [[@1037025|Gen. 37:25]]). It comprised the possessions of the tribes of Gad and Reuben and the south part of Manasseh ([[@5003013|Deut. 3:13]]; [[@4032040|Num. 32:40]]).

column5: Father of Jephthah, a judge of Israel.
column6: the heap or mass of testimony
column7: Hill of testimony, ([[@1031021|Gen. 31:21]]), a mountainous region east of Jordan. From its mountainous character it is called “the mount of Gilead” ([[@1031025|Gen. 31:25]]). It is called also “the land of Gilead” ([[@4032001|Num. 32:1]]), and sometimes simply “Gilead” ([[@19060007|Ps. 60:7]]; [[@1037025|Gen. 37:25]]). It comprised the possessions of the tribes of Gad and Reuben and the south part of Manasseh ([[@5003013|Deut. 3:13]]; [[@4032040|Num. 32:40]]).

column5: Descendant of Manasseh; son of Michael; father of Jaroah.
column6: the heap or mass of testimony
column7: Hill of testimony, ([[@1031021|Gen. 31:21]]), a mountainous region east of Jordan. From its mountainous character it is called “the mount of Gilead” ([[@1031025|Gen. 31:25]]). It is called also “the land of Gilead” ([[@4032001|Num. 32:1]]), and sometimes simply “Gilead” ([[@19060007|Ps. 60:7]]; [[@1037025|Gen. 37:25]]). It comprised the possessions of the tribes of Gad and Reuben and the south part of Manasseh ([[@5003013|Deut. 3:13]]; [[@4032040|Num. 32:40]]).

column5: A significant site during Israel's early history in Canaan.
column7: From the solemn transaction of the reading of the law in the valley of Shechem between Ebal and Gerizim the Israelites moved forward to Gilgal, and there made a permanent camp ([[@6009006|Josh. 9:6]]; [[@6010006|Josh 10:6]]). It was “beside the oaks of Moreh,” near which Abraham erected his first altar ([[@1012006|Gen. 12:6]], [[@1012007|Gen. 12:7]]).

column5: A place associated with the prophets Elijah and Elisha.
column7: A place, probably in the hill country of Ephraim, where there was a school of the prophets ([[@12004038|2 Kings 4:38]]), and whence Elijah and Elisha, who resided here, “went down” to Bethel (2:1, 2). It is mentioned also in [[@5011030|Deut. 11:30]].

column5: A city in Judah; home of Ahithophel, David's counselor.
column6: he that rejoices; he that overturns
column7: Exile, a city in the south-west part of the hill-country of Judah ([[@6015051|Josh. 15:51]]). It was the native place or residence of the traitor Ahithophel “the Gilonite” ([[@6015051|Josh. 15:51]]; [[@10015012|2 Sam. 15:12]]), and where he committed suicide (17:23).

column5: A city in Judah captured by the Philistines.
column7: A place fertile in sycamores, a city in the plain of Judah, the villages of which were seized by the Philistines ([[@14028018|2 Chr. 28:18]]).

column5: Father of Tibni, who opposed Omri for kingship.
column7: Ginath was the father of Tibni, who contended with Omri for the throne of Israel.

column5: A priest who sealed the covenant during Nehemiah's time.
column7: Ginnethon, a priest, was among those who sealed the covenant during Nehemiah's reforms.

column5: A Canaanite people group living in the Promised Land.
column7: Dwelling in clayey soil, the descendants of the fifth son of Canaan ([[@1010016|Gen. 10:16]]), one of the original tribes inhabiting the land of Canaan before the time of the Israelites ([[@1015021|Gen. 15:21]]; [[@5007001|Deut. 7:1]]). They were a branch of the great family of the Hivites. Of their geographical position nothing is certainly known.

column5: A people group David raided while living among the Philistines.
column7: The Girzites were a people group David raided during his time living in Philistine territory.

column5: An overseer of the temple servants during Nehemiah's time.
column7: Gishpa was an overseer of the temple servants (Nethinim) during Nehemiah's time.

column5: Town where Beerothites fled; later inhabited by Benjamites.
column7: Two wine-presses, ([[@10004003|2 Sam. 4:3]]; [[@16011033|Neh. 11:33]]), a town probably in Benjamin to which the Beerothites fled.

column5: A people group mentioned in the Old Testament.
column7: A name given to Hashem, an inhabitant of Gizoh, a place somewhere in the mountains of Judah ([[@13011034|1 Chr. 11:34]]; [[@10023032|2 Sam. 23:32]], [[@10023034|2 Sam. 23:34]]).

column5: A place near Jerusalem, mentioned in a prophetic context.
column7: A lowing, a place near Jerusalem, mentioned only in [[@24031039|Jer. 31:39]].

column5: A descendant of Reuben, son of Joel.
column7: A Reubenite ([[@13005004|1 Chr. 5:4]]), the father of Shimei.

column5: A symbolic enemy of God's people in prophetic literature.
column7: The name of the leader of the hostile party described in Ezek. 38, 39, as coming from the “north country” and assailing the people of Israel to their own destruction. This prophecy has been regarded as fulfilled in the conflicts of the Maccabees with Antiochus, the invasion and overthrow of the Chaldeans, and the temporary successes and destined overthrow of the Turks. But “all these interpretations are unsatisfactory and inadequate. The vision respecting Gog and Magog in the Apocalypse ([[@66020008|Rev. 20:8]]) is in substance a reannouncement of this prophecy of Ezekiel.

column5: A king of Goyim who fought alongside Chedorlaomer.
column7: Tidal, king of Goiim (nations), was one of the kings who fought alongside Chedorlaomer in Genesis 14.

column5: A city of refuge in Bashan, allotted to Manasseh.
column7: Exile, a city of Bashan ([[@5004043|Deut. 4:43]]), one of the three cities of refuge east of Jordan, about 12 miles north-east of the Sea of Galilee ([[@6020008|Josh. 20:8]]). There are no further notices of it in Scripture.

The common name of the spot where Jesus was crucified. It is interpreted by the evangelists as meaning “the place of a skull” ([[@40027033|Matt. 27:33]]; [[@41015022|Mark 15:22]]; [[@43019017|John 19:17]]). This name represents in Greek letters the Aramaic word Gulgaltha, which is the Hebrew Gulgoleth ([[@4001002|Num. 1:2]]; [[@13023003|1 Chr. 23:3]], [[@13023024|1 Chr. 23:24]]; [[@12009035|2 Kings 9:35]]), meaning “a skull.” It is identical with the word Calvary (q.v.).

column5: The place where Jesus was crucified, meaning "Place of a Skull."
column6: a heap of skulls; something skull-shaped
column7: The common name of the spot where Jesus was crucified. It is interpreted by the evangelists as meaning “the place of a skull” ([[@40027033|Matt. 27:33]]; [[@41015022|Mark 15:22]]; [[@43019017|John 19:17]]). This name represents in Greek letters the Aramaic word Gulgaltha, which is the Hebrew Gulgoleth ([[@4001002|Num. 1:2]]; [[@13023003|1 Chr. 23:3]], [[@13023024|1 Chr. 23:24]]; [[@12009035|2 Kings 9:35]]), meaning “a skull.” It is identical with the word Calvary (q.v.).

column5: A Philistine giant defeated by David.
column7: In [[@10021019|2 Sam. 21:19]] there is another giant of the same name mentioned as slain by Elhanan. The staff of his apear “was like a weaver’s beam.”

column5: Son of Japheth; father of Ashkenaz, Riphath, and Togarmah.
column7: The eldest son of Japheth, and father of Ashkenaz, Riphath, and Togarmah ([[@1010002|Gen. 10:2]], [[@1010003|Gen. 10:3]]), whose descendants formed the principal branch of the population of South-eastern Europe. He is generally regarded as the ancestor of the Celtae and the Cimmerii, who in early times settled to the north of the Black Sea, and gave their name to the Crimea, the ancient Chersonesus Taurica.

column5: Hosea's wife, a promiscuous woman.
column7: Gomer, the daughter of Diblaim, was the wife of the prophet Hosea.

column5: Wicked city destroyed by God along with Sodom.
column7: Submersion, one of the five cities of the plain of Siddim (q.v.) which were destroyed by fire ([[@1010019|Gen. 10:19]]; [[@1013010|Gen 13:10]]; [[@1019024|Gen 19:24]], [[@1019028|Gen 19:28]]). These cities probably stood close together, and were near the northern extremity of what is now the Dead Sea. This city is always mentioned next after Sodom, both of which were types of impiety and wickedness ([[@1018020|Gen. 18:20]]; [[@45009029|Rom. 9:29]]). Their destruction is mentioned as an “ensample unto those that after should live ungodly” (2 Pet. 2:6; [[@65001001|Jude 1]]:4-7).

column5: A region in Egypt where the Israelites settled and prospered.
column7: A district in Egypt where Jacob and his family settled, and in which they remained till the Exodus ([[@1045010|Gen. 45:10]]; [[@1046028|Gen 46:28]], [[@1046029|Gen 46:29]], [[@1046031|Gen 46:31]], etc.). It is called “the land of Goshen” (47:27), and also simply “Goshen” (46:28), and “the land of Rameses” (47:11; [[@2012037|Ex. 12:37]]), for the towns Pithom and Rameses lay within its borders; also Zoan or Tanis ([[@19078012|Ps. 78:12]]). It lay on the east of the Nile, and apparently not far from the royal residence.

column5: A town and region in the hill country of Judah.
column7: Goshen was a town and region in the hill country of Judah, mentioned in the accounts of Joshua's conquests (<ref="Joshua 10:41; 11:16; 15:51">Joshua 10:41; 11:16; 15:51</ref>).

One of the most important facts recorded in Gen. 10 is the foundation of the earliest monarchy in Babylonia by Nimrod the grandson of Ham (6, 8, 10). The primitive Babylonian empire was thus Hamitic, and of a cognate race with the primitive inhabitants of Arabia and of Ethiopia.

column5: A relative of Paul in Rome.

column5: A district overseer under Solomon.

column5: Place on the northern border of Israel

column7: Hilkiah, a priest from Anathoth, was the father of the prophet Jeremiah.

column5: A Canaanite people group.
column7: One of the original tribes scattered over Palestine, from Hermon to Gibeon in the south. column5: A Benjamite descendant of Elpaal.

column5: A descendant of David through Jeconiah.
column7: An ancestor of the prophet Zephaniah (1:1).

column5: Place north of Damascus pursued by Abraham
column7: Hiding-place, a place to the north of Damascus, to which Abraham pursued Chedorlaomer and his confederates ([[@1014015|Gen. 14:15]]).

column5: A descendant of Asher.
column7: Hod was a descendant of Asher, mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Asher.

column7: Hodaviah was a descendant of Benjamin who resided in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile.

He took a lead in the affairs of the family, and “prevailed above his brethren” ([[@1043003-1043010|Gen. 43:3-10]]; [[@1044014|Gen 44:14]], [[@1044016-1044034|Gen 44:16-34]]; [[@1046028|Gen 46:28]]; [[@13005002|1 Chr. 5:2]]).

column5: Wife of Shaharaim, a Benjamite
column7: Hodesh was one of the wives of Shaharaim, a Benjamite, and the mother of several of his children.

column5: Wife of a Judahite named Ishbar.
column7: Hodiah was the wife of Ishbar, a descendant of Judah, and the mother two clans.

column7: One of the Levites who assisted Ezra in expounding the law ([[@16008007|Neh. 8:7]]; [[@16009005|Neh 9:5]]).

column7: Partridge, one of the daughters of Zelophehad the Gileadite, to whom portions were assigned by Moses ([[@4026033|Num. 26:33]]; [[@4027001|Num 27:1]]; [[@4036011|Num 36:11]]).

column7: Jehovah impels, the king of Hebron who joined the league against Gibeon.

column7: Holon, a city of Moab mentioned in Jeremiah's oracle against Moab.

column7: One of the two portions into which the tabernacle was divided ([[@2026031|Ex. 26:31]]; [[@2037017-2037025|Ex 37:17-25]]; [[@58009002|Heb. 9:2]]). column7: Pugilist or client, one of the two sons of Eli, the high priest ([[@9001003|1 Sam. 1:3]]; [[@9002034|1 Sam. 2:34]]), who, because he was “very old,” resigned to them the active duties of his office. By their scandalous conduct they brought down a curse on their father’s house (2:22, 12-27, 27-36; 3:11-14). For their wickedness they were called “sons of Belial,” i.e., worthless men (2:12). They both perished in the disastrous battle with the Philistines at Aphek (4:11).

column7: Hor-haggidgad (Gudgodah), an Israelite campsite between Bene-jaakan and Jotbathah.

column7: Horam, the king of Gezer, came to help Lachish but was defeated by Joshua and the Israelites.

column7: Consecrated, one of the fenced cities of Naphtali ([[@6019038|Josh. 19:38]]).

column7: Horesh, a wilderness area in Judah where David hid from Saul.

column7: The Horites were a people group who inhabited the region of Seir before the Edomites.

column7: Hori, the son of Shaphat, was one of the twelve spies sent by Moses to explore the land of Canaan.

column6: devoted or consecrated to God; utter destruction
column7: Banning; i.e., placing under a “ban,” or devoting to utter destruction. After the manifestation of God’s anger against the Israelites, on account of their rebellion and their murmurings when the spies returned to the camp at Kadesh, in the wilderness of Paran, with an evil report of the land, they quickly repented of their conduct, and presumed to go up “to the head of the mountain,” seeking to enter the Promised Land, but without the presence of the Lord, without the ark of the convenant, and without Moses.

column5: A Moabite city mentioned in prophecies of judgment
column7: Two caverns, a city of Moab to the south of the Arnon, built, apparently, upon an eminence, and a place of some importance ([[@23015005|Isa. 15:5]]; [[@24048003|Jer. 48:3]], [[@24048005|Jer. 48:5]], [[@24048034|Jer. 48:34]]).

column5: A people group opposed to Nehemiah's work.

column7: The designation of Sanballat ([[@16002010|Neh. 2:10]], [[@16002019|Neh. 2:19]]), a native of Horonaim, or of one of the two Beth-horons, the “upper” or the “nether,” mentioned in [[@6016003|Josh. 16:3]], [[@6016005|Josh. 16:5]].

column5: A gate in Jerusalem's wall near the temple
column7: The Horse Gate, a gate in Jerusalem's wall near the temple.

column7: A place on the border of the tribe of Asher ([[@6019029|Josh. 19:29]]), a little to the south of Zidon.

column5: Leader of the half-tribe of Ephraim.

column7: Circle, the second son of Aram ([[@1010023|Gen. 10:23]]), and grandson of Shem.

She resided in that part of Jerusalem called the Mishneh (A.V., “the college;” R.V., “the second quarter”), supposed by some to be the suburb between the inner and the outer wall, the second or lower city, Akra.

column5: A town in the hill country of Judah
column7: Humtah, a town in the hill country of Judah (<ref="Joshua 15:54">Joshua 15:54</ref>).

column5: A priest during David's reign.
column7: Huppah was a priest who was assigned the thirteenth division of priestly service during King David's reign.

column5: A descendant of Manasseh.
column7: Huppim is mentioned in the genealogy of Manasseh as a descendant of Ir or as a son of Machir.

column7: Mary's husband, unnamed in the Bible, was the father of John Mark.

column7: Matred's mother was Mezahab, the grandmother of Mehetabel, who was the wife of an Edomite king.

column7: Shimeath's husband, unnamed in the Bible, was the father of Jozachar, one of the assassins of King Joash.

column7: The unnamed husband of Zeruiah, who was the father of David's mighty men, Abishai and Joab.

Here they were persecuted by the Jews, and being driven from the city, they fled to Lystra. They afterwards returned to Iconium, and encouraged the church which had been founded there (14:21, 22).
