column7: Succeeded his father Jehoiakin (B.C. 599) when only eight years of age, and reigned for one hundred days ([[@14036009|2 Chr. 36:9]]). He is also called Jeconiah ([[@24024001|Jer. 24:1]]; [[@24027020|Jer 27:20]], etc.), and Coniah (22:24; 37:1). He was succeeded by his uncle, Mattaniah = Zedekiah (q.v.). He was the last direct heir to the Jewish crown.

column5: Father of one of David's warriors, Benaiah
column7: The father of Benaiah, who was one of David’s chief warriors ([[@10008018|2 Sam. 8:18]]; [[@10020023|2 Sam. 20:23]]).

column5: High priest who overthrew Athaliah and crowned Joash
column7: The high priest at the time of Athaliah’s usurpation of the throne of Judah. He married Jehosheba, or Jehoshabeath, the daughter of king Jehoram ([[@14022011|2 Chr. 22:11]]), and took an active part along with his wife in the preservation and training of Jehoash when Athaliah slew all the royal family of Judah. The plans he adopted in replacing Jehoash on the throne of his ancestors are described in [[@12011002|2 Kings 11:2]]; [[@12012002|2 Kings 12:2]]; [[@14022011|2 Chr. 22:11]]; [[@14023024|2 Chr. 23:24]].

column5: Counselor to King David after Ahithophel
column7: Jehoiada, the son of Benaiah, succeeded Ahithophel as King David's counselor.

column5: Overseer in the house of the Lord
column7: Jehoiada was appointed as an overseer in the house of the Lord during the time of Jeremiah.

column5: King of Judah, son of Josiah
column6: avenging, or establishing, or resurrection, of the Lord
column7: He whom Jehovah has set up, the second son of Josiah, and eighteenth king of Judah, which he ruled over for eleven years (B.C. 610-599). His original name was Eliakim (q.v.).

column5: Head of a priestly division during David's reign
column6: fighting, or multiplying, of the Lord
column7: Jehovah defends, a priest at Jerusalem, head of one of the sacerdotal courses ([[@13009010|1 Chr. 9:10]]; [[@13024007|1 Chr. 24:7]]).

column5: Levite sent by Jehoshaphat to teach the Law
column6: gift of the Lord; gift of a dove
column7: A Levite who taught the law to the people of Judah ([[@14017008|2 Chr. 17:8]]).

column5: Head of a priestly family during the high priesthood of Joiakim
column6: gift of the Lord; gift of a dove
column7: Jehonathan was the head of the priestly family of Shemaiah during the time of Joiakim, the son of Jeshua.

column5: Son of Jehoshaphat, king of Judah.
column7: The eldest son and successor of Jehoshaphat, king of Judah. He reigned eight years (B.C. 892-885) alone as king of Judah, having been previously for some years associated with his father ([[@14021005|2 Chr. 21:5]], [[@14021020|2 Chr. 21:20]]; [[@12008016|2 Kings 8:16]]). His wife was Athaliah, the daughter of Ahab and Jezebel. His daughter Jehosheba was married to the high priest Jehoiada.

column5: A Levite sent by Jehoshaphat to teach.
column7: A priest sent by Jehoshaphat to instructruct the people in Judah ([[@14017008|2 Chr. 17:8]]).

column5: Recorder for David and Solomon.
column7: Son of Ahilud, “recorder” or annalist under David and Solomon ([[@10008016|2 Sam. 8:16]]), a state officer of high rank, chancellor or vizier of the kingdom.

column5: Solomon's officer, son of Paruah.
column7: Solomon’s purveyor in Issachar ([[@11004017|1 Kings 4:17]]).

column5: Son of Asa, king of Judah.
column7: The son and successor of Asa, king of Judah. After fortifying his kingdom against Israel ([[@14017001|2 Chr. 17:1]], [[@14017002|2 Chr. 17:2]]), he set himself to cleanse the land of idolatry ([[@11022043|1 Kings 22:43]]). In the third year of his reign he sent out priests and Levites over the land to instruct the people in the law ([[@14017007-14017009|2 Chr. 17:7-9]]). He enjoyed a great measure of peace and prosperity, the blessing of God resting on the people “in their basket and their store.”

column5: Father of Jehu, king of Israel.
column7: The son of Nimshi, and father of Jehu, king of Israel ([[@12009002|2 Kings 9:2]], [[@12009014|2 Kings 9:14]]).

column5: Daughter of Jehoram, saved Joash from Athaliah's massacre.
column6: fullness, or oath, of the Lord
column7: Jehovah-swearing, the daughter of Jehoram, the king of Israel. She is called Jehoshabeath in [[@14022011|2 Chr. 22:11]].

column5: Son of Shomer, killed King Joash of Judah.
column6: the Lord's dowry; having a dowry
column7: The son of Shomer, one of the two conspirators who put king Jehoash to death in Millo in Jerusalem ([[@12012021|2 Kings 12:21]]).

column5: Son of Obed-edom, a gatekeeper for the ark.
column6: the Lord's dowry; having a dowry
column7: The son of Obed-edom ([[@13026004|1 Chr. 26:4]]), one of the Levite porters.

column5: Commander of 180,000 warriors under Jehoshaphat.
column6: the Lord's dowry; having a dowry
column7: Jehozabad was a commander who led 180,000 warriors under King Jehoshaphat of Judah.

column5: Father of Joshua the high priest during the exile.
column7: Jehovah-justified, the son of the high priest Seraiah at the time of the Babylonian exile ([[@13006014|1 Chr. 6:14]], [[@13006015|1 Chr. 6:15]]). He was carried into captivity by Nebuchadnezzar, and probably died in Babylon.

column5: Son of Hanani, prophet during the reign of Baasha and Jehoshaphat.
column7: The son of Hanani, a prophet of Judah ([[@11016001|1 Kings 16:1]], [[@11016007|1 Kings 16:7]]; [[@14019002|2 Chr. 19:2]]; [[@14020034|2 Chr. 20:34]]), who pronounced the sentence of God against Baasha, the king of Israel.

column5: Son of Jehoshaphat, king of Israel, destroyed Ahab's dynasty.
column7: King of Israel, the son of Jehoshaphat ([[@12009002|2 Kings 9:2]]), and grandson of Nimshi. The story of his exaltation to the throne is deeply interesting. During the progress of a war against the Syrians, who were becoming more and more troublesome to Israel, in a battle at Ramoth-gilead Jehoram, the king of Israel, had been wounded; and leaving his army there, had returned to Jezreel, whither his ally, Ahaziah, king of Judah, had also gone on a visit of sympathy with him ([[@12008028|2 Kings 8:28]], [[@12008029|2 Kings 8:29]]).

column5: Son of Joshibiah, a descendant of Simeon.
column7: Jehu, the son of Joshibiah, was a descendant of Simeon mentioned in the genealogy recorded in 1 Chronicles.

column5: A Benjamite warrior who joined David at Ziklag.
column7: One of the Benjamite slingers that joined David at Ziklag ([[@13012003|1 Chr. 12:3]]).

column5: A descendant of Asher.
column7: Jehubbah was a descendant of Asher mentioned in the genealogy recorded in 1 Chronicles.

column5: An official during Zedekiah's reign, opposed Jeremiah.
column7: Able, the son of Shelemiah. He is also called Jucal ([[@24038001|Jer. 38:1]]). He was one of the two persons whom Zedekiah sent to request the prophet Jeremiah to pray for the kingdom ([[@24037003|Jer. 37:3]]) during the time of its final siege by Nebuchadnezzar.

column5: A town allotted to Dan
column7: Jehud, a town allotted to the tribe of Dan (<ref="Joshua 19:45">Joshua 19:45</ref>).

column5: An official who read Jeremiah's scroll to Jehoiakim.
column7: Jehudi was an official during King Jehoiakim's reign who read Jeremiah's scroll to the king, who then burned it piece by piece.

column5: Wife of Mered; mother of Jered, Heber, and Jekuthiel.
column7: Jehudijah (or the Judahite) was the wife of Mered and the mother of Jered, Heber, and Jekuthiel, as recorded in the genealogy of Judah.

column5: A Levite who helped cleanse the temple under Hezekiah.
column7: One of the Levites of the family of Heman who assisted Hezekiah in his work of reformation ([[@14029014|2 Chr. 29:14]]).

column5: Head of a Reubenite family.
column7: Jeiel was the head of a family in the tribe of Reuben, as recorded in the genealogy in 1 Chronicles.

column5: One of David's mighty men from Mahavite.
column6: God hath taken away; God heaping up
column7: Jeiel the Mahavite was listed among David's mighty men in 1 Chronicles.

column5: A Levite musician and gatekeeper during David's reign.
column7: Jeiel (or Jehiah) was a Levite who served as a musician and gatekeeper during the time of David, particularly in the transportation of the ark to Jerusalem.

column5: Grandfather of Jahaziel, a Levite during Jehoshaphat's reign.
column7: Jeiel was the grandfather of Jahaziel, a Levite who prophesied during the reign of King Jehoshaphat of Judah.

column5: A scribe in King Uzziah's army.
column6: God hath taken away; God heaping up
column7: Jeiel was the scribe who recorded the number of soldiers in King Uzziah's army.

column5: A Levite who contributed to Josiah's Passover celebration.
column7: One of the chief Levites, who made an offering for the restoration of the Passover by Josiah ([[@14035009|2 Chr. 35:9]]).

column5: A descendant of Nebo who married a foreign wife.
column7: Jeiel, a descendant of Nebo, was among those who married foreign women during the time of Ezra and agreed to send them away.

column5: A town in Judah inhabited after the Babylonian exile
column7: Jekabzeel, a town in Judah inhabited by the people of Judah after the Babylonian exile (<ref="Nehemiah 11:25">Nehemiah 11:25</ref>).

column5: A Levite, son of Hebron.
column7: Jekameam was a Levite, the son of Hebron, mentioned in the genealogies of the Levites in 1 Chronicles.

column5: Descendant of Jeconiah, a descendant of David.
column6: establishing, or revenging, of the Lord
column7: Jekamiah was a descendant of Jeconiah and a descendant of David, as recorded in the genealogy in 1 Chronicles.

column5: Son of Mered, founder of Zanoah.
column6: hope, or congregation, of the Lord
column7: Jekuthiel was the son of Mered and the  father (ie founder) of Zanoah, as recorded in the genealogy of Judah in 1 Chronicles.

column5: One of Job's daughters born after his restoration.
column7: Dove, the eldest of Job’s three daughters born after his time of trial ([[@18042014|Job 42:14]]).

column5: Son of Simeon, also known as Nemuel.
column7: One of Simeon’s five sons ([[@13004024|1 Chr. 4:24]]), called also Jemuel ([[@1046010|Gen. 46:10]]).

column5: A judge of Israel, known for his tragic vow.
column7: Whom God sets free, or the breaker through, a “mighty man of valour” who delivered Israel from the oppression of the Ammonites ([[@7011001-7011033|Judg. 11:1-33]]), and judged Israel six years (12:7). He has been described as “a wild, daring, Gilead mountaineer, a sort of warrior Elijah.” After forty-five years of comparative quiet Israel again apostatized, and in “process of time the children of Ammon made war against Israel” (11:5).

column5: The Kenizzite, father of Caleb the spy.
column7: The father of Caleb, who was Joshua’s companion in exploring Canaan ([[@4013006|Num. 13:6]]), a Kenezite ([[@6014014|Josh. 14:14]]).

column5: A descendant of Asher.
column7: One of the descendants of Asher ([[@13007038|1 Chr. 7:38]]).

column5: A son of Joktan, descendant of Shem.
column7: Jerah was one of the sons of Joktan, a descendant of Shem, as recorded in the Table of Nations in Genesis and 1 Chronicles.

column5: Son of Hezron, a descendant of Judah.
column6: the mercy, or the beloved, of God

column5: A Levite of the Merari clan.
column6: the mercy, or the beloved, of God
column7: Jerahmeel was a Levite of the family of Merari, as recorded in the genealogy in 1 Chronicles.

column5: Son of Hammelech, sent to arrest Jeremiah.
column6: the mercy, or the beloved, of God
column7: Jerahmeel, the son of Hammelech, was one of the officers sent by King Jehoiakim to arrest Jeremiah and Baruch.

column5: Son of Mered, founder of Gedor.
column7: Jered was the son of Mered and the  father (ie founder) of Gedor, as recorded in the genealogy of Judah in 1 Chronicles.

column5: A descendant of Hashum who married a foreign wife.
column7: Jeremai, a descendant of Hashum, was among those who married foreign women during the time of Ezra and agreed to send them away.

column5: Father-in-law of Jehoahaz and Zedekiah
column7: The father of Hamutal ([[@12023031|2 Kings 23:31]]), the wife of Josiah.

column5: A leader of the half-tribe of Manasseh.
column7: One of the chiefs of the tribe of Manasseh on the east of Jordan ([[@13005024|1 Chr. 5:24]]).

column5: A Gadite warrior who joined David at Ziklag.
column7: A Benjamite slinger who joined David at Ziklag ([[@13012004|1 Chr. 12:4]]).

column5: A Gadite warrior who joined David at Ziklag.
column7: A Gadite who joined David in the wilderness ([[@13012010|1 Chr. 12:10]]).

column5: A Gadite warrior who joined David at Ziklag.
column7: Jeremiah was one of the Gadite warriors who joined David at Ziklag when he was fleeing from King Saul.

column5: Son of Hilkiah, the prophet during Judah's final days.
column7: One of the “greater prophets” of the Old Testament, son of Hilkiah (q.v.), a priest of Anathoth ([[@24001001|Jer. 1:1]]; [[@24032006|Jer 32:6]]). He was called to the prophetical office when still young (1:6), in the thirteenth year of Josiah (B.C. 628). He left his native place, and went to reside in Jerusalem, where he greatly assisted Josiah in his work of reformation ([[@12023001-12023025|2 Kings 23:1-25]]). The death of this pious king was bewailed by the prophet as a national calamity ([[@14035025|2 Chr. 35:25]]).

column5: A priest who returned from the Babylonian exile.
column7: Jeremiah was one of the priests who returned to Jerusalem from the Babylonian exile, as recorded in Nehemiah.

column5: Son of Habazziniah, a Rechabite.
column7: Jeremiah, the son of Habazziniah, was a Rechabite who was tested by the prophet Jeremiah for his obedience to his ancestor's commands.

column5: Son of Becher, a Benjamite.
column7: Jeremoth was a son of Becher and a member of the tribe of Benjamin, as mentioned in the genealogy in 1 Chronicles.

column5: Son of Beriah, a Benjamite leader in Jerusalem.
column7: Jeremoth, the son of Beriah, was a leader of the Benjamites living in Jerusalem, as recorded in the genealogy in 1 Chronicles.

column5: A descendant of Elam who married a foreign wife.
column7: Jeremoth, a descendant of Elam, was among those who married foreign women during the time of Ezra and agreed to send them away.

column5: A descendant of Zattu who married a foreign wife.
column7: Jeremoth, a descendant of Zattu, was among those who married foreign women during the time of Ezra and agreed to send them away.

column5: A descendant of Bani who married a foreign wife.
column7: Jeremoth, a descendant of Bani, was among those who married foreign women during the time of Ezra and agreed to send them away.

column5: A Levite, the firstborn son of Hebron.
column6: fear, or throwing down, of the Lord
column7: Jeriah was a Levite, the firstborn son of Hebron, and an ancestor of the Hebronites who served in the tabernacle during David's reign.

column5: One of David's mighty men.
column7: Jeribai was listed among David's mighty men, a group of skilled warriors who fought alongside him.

column5: An ancient city in Canaan, famously conquered by Israel
column6: his moon; his month; his sweet smell
column7: Place of fragrance, a fenced city in the midst of a vast grove of palm trees, in the plain of Jordan, over against the place where that river was crossed by the Israelites ([[@6003016|Josh. 3:16]]). Its site was near the ‘Ain es-Sultan, Elisha’s Fountain ([[@12002019-12002022|2 Kings 2:19-22]]), about 5 miles west of Jordan. It was the most important city in the Jordan valley ([[@4022001|Num. 22:1]]; [[@4034015|Num 34:15]]), and the strongest fortress in all the land of Canaan. It was the key to Western Palestine.

column5: A son of Tola, from the tribe of Issachar.
column7: Jeriel was one of the sons of Tola and a leader in the tribe of Issachar, as mentioned in the genealogy in 1 Chronicles.

column5: A Levite leader during David's reign.
column6: fear, or throwing down, of the Lord
column7: Jerijah was a Levite leader from the family of Hebron who served during the reign of King David.

column5: Son of Bela, from the tribe of Benjamin.
column6: he that fears or rejects death
column7: Jerimoth was a son of Bela and a leader in the tribe of Benjamin, as mentioned in the genealogy in 1 Chronicles.

column5: One of David's warriors from the tribe of Benjamin.
column6: he that fears or rejects death
column7: A Benjamite slinger who joined David at Ziklag ([[@13012005|1 Chr. 12:5]]).

column5: A Levite, son of Mushi, from the Merari clan.
column6: he that fears or rejects death
column7: Jerimoth was a Levite, the son of Mushi, from the clan of Merari, as recorded in the genealogies in 1 Chronicles.

column5: A Levite, son of Heman the singer.
column6: he that fears or rejects death
column7: A Levitical musician under Heman his father ([[@13025004|1 Chr. 25:4]]).

column5: Son of Azriel, a leader from the tribe of Naphtali.
column6: he that fears or rejects death
column7: Jerimoth, the son of Azriel, was a leader from the tribe of Naphtali during the reign of King David.

column5: Son of David and Abihail.
column6: he that fears or rejects death
column7: Jerimoth was a son of King David and Abihail, the daughter of Eliab, David's brother.

column5: A Levite overseer during Hezekiah's temple restoration.
column6: he that fears or rejects death
column7: A Levite, one of the overseers of the temple offerings ([[@14031013|2 Chr. 31:13]]) in the reign of Hezekiah.

column5: Wife of Caleb; mother of unnamed children.
column7: Jerioth was one of the wives of Caleb, and she bore him some unnamed children, as mentioned in the genealogy of Judah in 1 Chronicles.

column5: First king of the northern kingdom of Israel.
column7: The son of Nebat ([[@11011026-11011039|1 Kings 11:26-39]]), “an Ephrathite,” the first king of the ten tribes, over whom he reigned twenty-two years (B.C. 976-945). He was the son of a widow of Zereda, and while still young was promoted by Solomon to be chief superintendent of the “burnden”, i.e., of the bands of forced labourers.

column5: King of Israel, son of Jehoash.
column7: Jeroboam II., the son and successor of Jehoash, and the fourteenth king of Israel, over which he ruled for forty-one years, B.C. 825-784 ([[@12014023|2 Kings 14:23]]). He followed the example of the first Jeroboam in keeping up the worship of the golden calves ([[@12014024|2 Kings 14:24]]). His reign was contemporary with those of Amaziah ([[@12014023|2 Kings 14:23]]) and Uzziah (15:1), kings of Judah. He was victorious over the Syrians (13:4; 14:26, 27), and extended Israel to its former limits, from “the entering of Hamath to the sea of the plain” (14:25; [[@30006014|Amos 6:14]]).

column5: An Ephraimite, father of Elkanah and grandfather of Samuel.
column7: Father of Elkanah, and grandfather of the prophet Samuel ([[@9001001|1 Sam. 1:1]]).

column5: A Benjamite, son of Jeshaiah.
column7: Jeroham was a Benjamite, the son of Jeshaiah, mentioned in the genealogy of Benjamin in 1 Chronicles.

column5: A Benjamite, father of Ibneiah.
column7: Jeroham was a Benjamite, the father of Ibneiah, mentioned in the genealogy of Benjamin in 1 Chronicles.

column5: A priest, father of Adaiah.
column7: [[@13009012|1 Chr. 9:12]]; a priest, perhaps the same as in [[@16011012|Neh. 11:12]].

column5: A Benjamite warrior who joined David at Ziklag.
column7: Jeroham was a Benjamite warrior who joined David at Ziklag when he was fleeing from King Saul.

column5: A leader from the tribe of Dan.
column7: The father of Azareel, the “captain” of the tribe of Dan ([[@13027022|1 Chr. 27:22]]).

column5: Father of Azariah, who supported Jehoiada's coup.
column7: [[@14023001|2 Chr. 23:1]]; one whose son assisted in placing Joash on the throne.

column5: A wilderness where Jehoshaphat defeated his enemies
column7: Founded by God, a “desert” on the ascent from the valley of the Dead Sea towards Jerusalem. It lay beyond the wilderness of Tekoa, in the direction of Engedi ([[@14020016|2 Chr. 20:16]], [[@14020020|2 Chr. 20:20]]).

column5: The capital of Israel, a holy city for three religions
column7: Called also Salem, Ariel, Jebus, the “city of God,” the “holy city;” by the modern Arabs el-Khuds, meaning “the holy;” once “the city of Judah” ([[@14025028|2 Chr. 25:28]]). This name is in the original in the dual form, and means “possession of peace,” or “foundation of peace.” The dual form probably refers to the two mountains on which it was built, viz., Zion and Moriah; or, as some suppose, to the two parts of the city, the “upper” and the “lower city.”

column5: Wives David took in Jerusalem
column7: The unnamed wives David took in Jerusalem, who bore him more sons and daughters.

column5: Mother of King Jotham of Judah.
column7: Possession, or possessed; i.e., “by a husband”, the wife of Uzziah, and mother of king Jotham ([[@12015033|2 Kings 15:33]]).

column5: A descendant of Shecaniah from the line of David.
column6: health, or salvation, of the Lord
column7: One of the three sons of Hananiah ([[@13003021|1 Chr. 3:21]]).

column5: A Levite, son of Jeduthun the musician.
column7: Jeshaiah was a Levite, the son of Jeduthun, and a musician appointed by King David to serve in the tabernacle choir.

column5: A descendant of Elam who returned with Ezra.
column7: Jeshaiah, a descendant of Elam, was among those who returned to Jerusalem with Ezra.

column5: A Levite who accompanied Ezra to Jerusalem.
column7: Jeshaiah was a Levite who accompanied Ezra on his journey from Babylon to Jerusalem.

column5: A descendant of Benjamin who lived in Jerusalem.
column6: health, or salvation, of the Lord
column7: Jeshaiah, a descendant of Benjamin, was among those who settled in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile.

column5: A town captured by Abijah from Jeroboam
column7: A city of the kingdom of Israel ([[@14013019|2 Chr. 13:19]]).

column5: Head of the fourteenth priestly division.
column6: sitting, or captivity, of the father
column7: Seat of his father, the head of the fourteenth division of priests ([[@13024013|1 Chr. 24:13]]).

column5: A son of Caleb and Azubah.
column7: Uprightness, the first of the three sons of Caleb by Azubah ([[@13002018|1 Chr. 2:18]]).

column5: A wilderness near Ziph, where David hid from Saul
column7: The waste, probably some high waste land to the south of the Dead Sea ([[@4021020|Num. 21:20]]; [[@4023028|Num 23:28]]; [[@9023019|1 Sam. 23:19]], [[@9023024|1 Sam. 23:24]]); or rather not a proper name at all, but simply “the waste” or “wilderness,” the district on which the plateau of Ziph (q.v.) looks down.

column5: An ancestor of Gadite leaders.
column7: Jeshishai was an ancestor of the Gadite leaders who lived in Bashan, as mentioned in the genealogy of Gad in 1 Chronicles.

column5: A leader from the tribe of Simeon.
column7: Jeshohaiah was a leader from the tribe of Simeon during the time of King Hezekiah.

column5: Head of a priestly family that returned from exile.
column7: Head of the ninth priestly order ([[@15002036|Ezra 2:36]]); called also Jeshuah ([[@13024011|1 Chr. 24:11]]).

column5: A Levite during King Hezekiah's reign.
column7: A Levite appointed by Hezekiah to distribute offerings in the priestly cities ([[@14031015|2 Chr. 31:15]]).

column5: Leader of a group that returned from Babylonian exile.
column7: Jeshua was the leader of a group of Israelites who returned to Jerusalem from the Babylonian exile.

column5: A prominent Levite leader during the post-exilic period.
column7: Jeshua was a prominent Levite leader who played a significant role in the restoration of Jerusalem and the temple after the Babylonian exile.

column5: A priest who received the temple treasures.
column7: Jeshua was a priest who received the temple treasures brought back from Babylon during the return from exile.

column5: Son of Jozadak, who helped rebuild Jerusalem's wall.
column7: Jeshua, the son of Jozadak, was a high priest who helped rebuild a section of Jerusalem's wall during the time of Nehemiah.

column5: A town in Judah inhabited after the Babylonian exile
column7: Jeshua, a town in Judah inhabited by the people of Judah after the Babylonian exile (<ref="Nehemiah 11:26">Nehemiah 11:26</ref>).

column5: A Levite leader during Nehemiah's time.
column7: Jeshua was a Levite leader who served during the time of Nehemiah and participated in the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem.

column5: A leader from the tribe of Simeon.
column7: Jesimiel was a leader from the tribe of Simeon during the reign of King Hezekiah.

column5: Father of King David.
column7: Firm, or a gift, a son of Obed, the son of Boaz and Ruth ([[@8004017|Ruth 4:17]], [[@8004022|Ruth 4:22]]; [[@40001005|Matt. 1:5]], [[@40001006|Matt. 1:6]]; [[@42003032|Luke 3:32]]). He was the father of eight sons, the youngest of whom was David ([[@9017012|1 Sam. 17:12]]). The phrase “stem of Jesse” is used for the family of David ([[@23011001|Isa. 11:1]]), and “root of Jesse” for the Messiah ([[@23011010|Isa. 11:10]]; [[@66005005|Rev. 5:5]]).

column5: The Son of God and Savior of the world.
column7: A Jewish Christian surnamed Justus ([[@51004011|Col. 4:11]]). Je’sus, the proper, as Christ is the official, name of our Lord. To distinguish him from others so called, he is spoken of as “Jesus of Nazareth” ([[@43018007|John 18:7]]), and “Jesus the son of Joseph” ([[@43006042|John 6:42]]). This is the Greek form of the Hebrew name Joshua, which was originally Hoshea ([[@4013008|Num. 13:8]], [[@4013016|Num. 13:16]]), but changed by Moses into Jehoshua ([[@4013016|Num. 13:16]]; [[@13007027|1 Chr. 7:27]]), or Joshua.

column5: Gideon's firstborn son who refused to kill captives.
column7: The oldest of Gideon’s seventy sons ([[@7008020|Judg. 8:20]]).

column5: An Ishmaelite, father of Amasa.
column7: The father of Amasa, David’s general ([[@11002005|1 Kings 2:5]], [[@11002032|1 Kings 2:32]]); called Ithra ([[@10017025|2 Sam. 17:25]]).

column5: Son of Ezrah; brother of Mered, Epher and Jalon
column7: Jether, mentioned in the genealogy of Judah.

column5: A chief of Edom
column7: A peg, or a prince, one of the Edomitish kings of Mount Seir ([[@1036040|Gen. 36:40]]).

column5: Moses' father-in-law, priest of Midian
column7: His excellence, or gain, a prince or priest of Midian, who succeeded his father Reuel. Moses spent forty years after his exile from the Egyptian court as keeper of Jethro’s flocks. While the Israelites were encamped at Sinai, and soon after their victory over Amalek, Jethro came to meet Moses, bringing with him Zipporah and her two sons. They met at the “mount of God,” and “Moses told him all that the Lord had done unto Pharaoh” ([[@2018008|Ex. 18:8]]).

column5: Son of Ishmael
column7: An enclosure, one of the twelve sons of Ishmael ([[@1025015|Gen. 25:15]]).

column5: A descendant of Ishmael and a region in Syria
column7: An enclosure, one of the twelve sons of Ishmael ([[@1025015|Gen. 25:15]]).

column5: A descendant of Zerah
column6: God hath taken away; God heaping up
column7: Snatched away by God, a descendant of Zerah ([[@13009006|1 Chr. 9:6]]).

column5: A Levite who helped cleanse the temple
column6: God hath taken away; God heaping up
column7: Snatched away by God, a descendant of Zerah ([[@13009006|1 Chr. 9:6]]).

column5: A descendant of Adonikam who returned from exile
column6: God hath taken away; God heaping up
column7: Snatched away by God, a descendant of Zerah ([[@13009006|1 Chr. 9:6]]).

column5: Son of Esau and Oholibamah
column7: The oldest of Esau’s three sons by Aholibamah ([[@1036005|Gen. 36:5]], [[@1036014|Gen. 36:14]], [[@1036018|Gen. 36:18]]).

column5: A descendant of Bilhan from the tribe of Benjamin
column7: A son of Bilhan, grandson of Benjamin ([[@13007010|1 Chr. 7:10]]).

column5: A descendant of Eleasah from the tribe of Benjamin
column7: Jeush, a Benjamite, was a son of Eleasah (or 'Eshek').

column5: A Levite, son of Shimei or Shubael
column7: A Levite, one of the sons of Shimei ([[@13023010|1 Chr. 23:10]], [[@13023011|1 Chr. 23:11]]).

column5: Son of King Rehoboam and Mahalath
column7: One of the three sons of Rehoboam ([[@14011019|2 Chr. 11:19]]).

column5: A descendant of Shaharaim from the tribe of Benjamin
column7: Jeuz was a Benjamite, born to Shaharaim in the country of Moab.

column5: A leader of the Judean forces
column6: nourishment, or weapons, of the Lord
column7: Jezaniah, also known as Azariah, was a leader of the Judean forces after the fall of Jerusalem.

column5: Queen of Israel; wife of King Ahab
column7: Chaste, the daughter of Ethbaal, the king of the Zidonians, and the wife of Ahab, the king of Israel ([[@11016031|1 Kings 16:31]]). This was the “first time that a king of Israel had allied himself by marriage with a heathen princess; and the alliance was in this case of a peculiarly disastrous kind. Jezebel has stamped her name on history as the representative of all that is designing, crafty, malicious, revengeful, and cruel. She is the first great instigator of persecution against the saints of God.

column5: Son of Naphtali, founder of the Jezerite clan
column7: Jezer, a son of Naphtali, was the ancestor of the Jezerite clan.

column5: A Benjamite warrior who joined David at Ziklag
column7: Assembled by God, a son of Azmaveth.

column5: A leader of the singers at the wall dedication
column6: the Lord arises; brightness of the Lord
column7: Jezrahiah was one of the leaders of the singers during the dedication of Jerusalem's wall.

column5: A town in Judah, home of David's wife Ahinoam
column7: A town in Judah ([[@6015056|Josh. 15:56]]), to the south-east of Hebron.

column5: A city in Issachar, associated with Ahab and Jezebel
column7: A town of Issachar ([[@6019018|Josh. 19:18]]), where the kings of Israel often resided ([[@11018045|1 Kings 18:45]]; [[@11021001|1 Kings 21:1]]; [[@12009030|2 Kings 9:30]]). Here Elijah met Ahab, Jehu, and Bidkar; and here Jehu executed his dreadful commission against the house of Ahab ([[@12009014-12009037|2 Kings 9:14-37]]; [[@12010001-12010011|2 Kings 10:1-11]]).

column5: A son of Saul's son Jonathan, also called Merib-baal
column7: Jezreel, a son of Jonathan, who was also known as Merib-baal (<ref="2Sa.4.4">2Sa.4.4</ref>).

column5: A son of Hur in the genealogy of Judah
column7: Jezreel was a son of Hur, mentioned in the genealogy of Judah.

column5: A fertile valley in northern Israel, site of many battles
column7: The Jezreel Valley, a strategically important and fertile valley in northern Israel, was the site of several significant battles in the Bible.

column5: Son of Nahor and Milcah
column7: Jidlaph, a son of Nahor and Milcah, was Abraham's nephew.

column5: Son of Zeruiah, commander of David's army
column7: One of the three sons of Zeruiah, David’s sister, and “captain of the host” during the whole of David’s reign ([[@10002013|2 Sam. 2:13]]; [[@10010007|2 Sam. 10:7]]; [[@10011001|2 Sam. 11:1]]; [[@11011015|1 Kings 11:15]]). His father’s name is nowhere mentioned, although his sepulchre at Bethlehem is mentioned ([[@10002032|2 Sam. 2:32]]). His two brothers were Abishai and Asahel, the swift of foot, who was killed by Abner ([[@10002013-10002032|2 Sam. 2:13-32]]), whom Joab afterwards treacherously murdered (3:22-27).

column5: Son of Seraiah, founder of Ge-harashim
column7: Joab, the son of Seraiah, was the  father (ie founder) of Ge-harashim.

column5: Ancestor of a family that returned from Babylonian exile
column7: Joab was the ancestor of a family that returned to Judah from Babylonian exile.

column5: A descendant of Pahath-Moab who returned with Ezra
column7: Joab, a descendant of Pahath-Moab, was among those who returned to Jerusalem with Ezra.

column5: Son of Asaph, King Hezekiah's secretary
column7: The son of Asaph, and “recorder” (q.v.) or chronicler to King Hezekiah ([[@12018018|2 Kings 18:18]], [[@12018026|2 Kings 18:26]], [[@12018037|2 Kings 18:37]]).

column5: A Gershonite Levite, son of Zimmah
column7: A Levite of the family of Gershom ([[@13006021|1 Chr. 6:21]]), probably the same as Ethan (42).

column5: A son of Obed-edom, a gatekeeper of the temple
column7: One of the sons of Obed-edom ([[@13026004|1 Chr. 26:4]]), a Korhite porter.

column5: Son of Joahaz, King Josiah's secretary
column7: Son of Joahaz, and “recorder” (q.v.) or keeper of the state archives under King Josiah ([[@14034008|2 Chr. 34:8]]).

column5: Father of Joah, King Josiah's secretary
column7: ([[@14034008|2 Chr. 34:8]]), a contracted form of Jehoahaz (q.v.).

column5: An ancestor of Jesus Christ
column6: grace or gift of the Lord
column7: The grandson of Zerubbabel, in the lineage of Christ ([[@42003027|Luke 3:27]]); the same as Hananiah ([[@13003019|1 Chr. 3:19]]).

column5: A follower of Jesus who supported His ministry
column6: grace or gift of the Lord
column7: The wife of Chuza, the steward of Herod Antipas, tetrarch of Galilee ([[@42008003|Luke 8:3]]).

column5: The father of Gideon, a judge of Israel
column7: A contracted form of Jehoash, the father of Gideon ([[@7006011|Judg. 6:11]], [[@7006029|Judg. 6:29]]; 8:13, 29, 32).

column5: Son of King Ahab of Israel
column7: Joash, the son of King Ahab, was imprisoned by his father for a prophecy against him.

column5: King of Judah, son of Ahaziah
column7: Joash (Jehoash), son of Ahaziah, became king of Judah at age seven and reigned for forty years.

column5: King of Israel, son of Jehoahaz
column7: Joash (Jehoash), son of Jehoahaz, reigned as king of Israel for sixteen years.

column5: A descendant of Shelah in the tribe of Judah
column7: Joash was a descendant of Shelah, mentioned in the genealogy of Judah.

column5: A descendant of Benjamin through Becher
column7: Joash was a descendant of Benjamin through Becher, mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe.

column5: A Benjaminite warrior who joined David at Ziklag
column7: One of the Benjamite archers who joined David at Ziklag ([[@13012003|1 Chr. 12:3]]).

column5: An official in charge of David's olive and sycamore trees
column7: One who had charge of the royal stores of oil under David and Solomon ([[@13027028|1 Chr. 27:28]]).

column5: A righteous man who endured great suffering
column7: Persecuted, an Arabian patriarch who resided in the land of Uz (q.v.). While living in the midst of great prosperity, he was suddenly overwhelmed by a series of sore trials that fell upon him. Amid all his sufferings he maintained his integrity. Once more God visited him with the rich tokens of his goodness and even greater prosperity than he had enjoyed before.

column5: A son of Joktan, descendant of Shem
column7: One of the sons of Joktan, and founder of an Arabian tribe ([[@1010029|Gen. 10:29]]).

column5: A king of Edom, son of Zerah of Bozrah
column7: Jobab, the son of Zerah of Bozrah, was an early king of Edom who reigned before Israel had a king.

column5: King of Madon, who joined forces against Joshua
column7: A Canaanitish king ([[@6011001|Josh. 11:1]]) who joined the confederacy against Joshua.

column5: A son of Shaharaim and Hodesh
column7: Jobab was one of the sons born to Shaharaim and his wife Hodesh in the genealogy of Benjamin.

column5: A son of Elpaal, descendant of Benjamin
column7: Jobab, a descendant of Benjamin, was one of the sons of Elpaal.

column5: Mother of Moses, Aaron, and Miriam
column7: Jehovah is her glory, the wife of Amram, and the mother of Miriam, Aaron, and Moses ([[@4026059|Num. 26:59]]).

column5: An ancestor of Jesus Christ
column7: Joda is listed as an ancestor of Jesus in the genealogy recorded by Luke.

column5: A Benjaminite who resettled in Jerusalem
column7: Joed, a Benjaminite, was among those who resettled in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile.

column5: Samuel's firstborn son who judged Israel
column7: The oldest of Samuel’s two sons appointed by him as judges in Beersheba ([[@9008002|1 Sam. 8:2]]).

column5: A Simeonite mentioned in the genealogy of Judah
column7: Joel is listed in the genealogy of Judah as a descendant of Simeon.

column5: A descendant of Reuben
column7: Joel is mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Reuben as a descendant of Shemaiah.

column5: Father of Shema living in Reubenite lands
column7: Joel, a father of Shema who lived in Reuben and also neighbouring Gad.

column5: A Gadite chief in Bashan
column7: Joel was a chief of the Gadites who lived in the territory of Bashan.

column5: A son of Izrahiah from the tribe of Issachar
column7: Joel was one of the five sons of Izrahiah, a descendant of Issachar, known for their bravery.

column5: The brother of Nathan, one of David's mighty men
column7: One of David’s famous warriors ([[@13011038|1 Chr. 11:38]]).

column5: A Gershomite Levite during the reign of David
column7: A Levite of the family of Gershom ([[@13015007|1 Chr. 15:7]], [[@13015011|1 Chr. 15:11]]).

column5: A Gershonite Levite during David's organization of the Levites
column7: Joel, a descendant of Ladan from the Gershonite clan, was a Levite during David's time.

column5: A ruler of the half-tribe of Manasseh in Gilead
column7: Joel was appointed as the ruler over the half-tribe of Manasseh in Gilead during David's reign.

column5: A Kohathite Levite during Hezekiah's temple restoration
column7: Joel, a Levite of the Kohathite clan, participated in the purification of the temple during King Hezekiah's reign.

column5: An Israelite who married a foreign woman during the Exile
column7: Joel was among the Israelites who had married foreign women and pledged to put them away during Ezra's reforms.

column5: A Benjaminite leader in Jerusalem after the Exile
column7: Joel, the son of Zichri, was a Benjaminite leader in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile.

column5: A prophet of Judah and the author of the Book of Joel
column7: Joel, the son of Pethuel, was a prophet of Judah who delivered a message of judgment and hope.

column5: A Benjaminite warrior who joined David at Ziklag
column6: lifting up; profiting; taking away slander
column7: A Benjamite who joined David at Ziklag ([[@13012007|1 Chr. 12:7]]).

column5: A Benjaminite warrior who joined David at Ziklag
column7: Jehovah is his help, one of the Korhites who became part of David’s body-guard ([[@13012006|1 Chr. 12:6]]).

column5: A town in Gilead, fortified by the Gadites
column7: Jogbehah, a town in Gilead fortified by the Gadites (<ref="Numbers 32:35">Numbers 32:35</ref>), was located near the route Gideon took when pursuing the Midianites (<ref="Judges 8:11">Judges 8:11</ref>).

column5: A leader from the tribe of Dan
column7: Jogli, the son of Bukki, was a leader from the tribe of Dan appointed to help divide the Promised Land.

column5: A Benjaminite, son of Beriah
column7: Joha was a son of Beriah and a member of the tribe of Benjamin.

column5: One of David's mighty warriors from the Tizite clan
column7: Joha the Tizite was one of David's mighty warriors, known for his bravery and military skill.

column5: A Judean military leader after the fall of Jerusalem
column7: Son of Careah, one of the Jewish chiefs who rallied round Gedaliah, whom Nebuchadnezzar had made governor in Jerusalem ([[@12025023|2 Kings 25:23]]; [[@24040008|Jer. 40:8]]). He warned Gedaliah of the plans of Ishmael against him, a warning which was unheeded ([[@24040013|Jer. 40:13]], [[@24040016|Jer 40:16]]). He afterwards pursued the murderer of the governor, and rescued the captives (41:8, 13, 15, 16). He and his associates subsequently fled to Tahpanhes in Egypt (43:2, 4, 5), taking Jeremiah with them.

column5: A descendant of David through the line of Jehoiachin
column7: Johanan is listed in the genealogy of David as a descendant of King Jehoiachin.

column5: A Levite in the lineage of Elkanah
column7: Johanan was a Priest in the lineage of Elkanah, the father of Samuel.

column5: A Benjaminite warrior who joined David at Ziklag
column7: Johanan, a Benjaminite warrior, was among the mighty men who joined David at Ziklag.

column5: A Gadite warrior who joined David at Ziklag
column7: One of the Gadite heroes who joined David in the desert of Judah ([[@13012012|1 Chr. 12:12]]).

column5: An Ephraimite leader during the reign of Ahaz
column7: Johanan, the son of Jehohanan, was one of the leaders of Ephraim who opposed the bringing of Judean captives to Samaria.

column5: A leader who returned to Jerusalem with Ezra
column7: Johanan, the son of Hakkatan, was one of the leaders who returned to Jerusalem with Ezra.

column5: A high priest during the Persian period
column7: Johanan served as a high priest during the Persian period, as recorded in the genealogies of the priests and Levites.

column5: The Baptist, a prophet who prepared the way for Jesus
column6: the grace or mercy of the Lord
column7: John the Baptist was a prophet who preached repentance and baptized many, including Jesus, preparing the way for the Messiah.

column5: Apostle and son of Zebedee
column6: the grace or mercy of the Lord
column7: THE APOSTLE, brother of James the “Greater” ([[@40004021|Matt. 4:21]]; [[@40010002|Matt 10:2]]; [[@41001019|Mark 1:19]]; [[@41003017|Mark 3:17]]; [[@41010035|Mark 10:35]]). He was one, probably the younger, of the sons of Zebedee ([[@40004021|Matt. 4:21]]) and Salome ([[@40027056|Matt. 27:56]]; comp. [[@41015040|Mark 15:40]]), and was born at Bethsaida. His father was apparently a man of some wealth (comp. [[@41001020|Mark 1:20]]; [[@42005003|Luke 5:3]]; [[@43019027|John 19:27]]). He was doubtless trained in all that constituted the ordinary education of Jewish youth.

column5: The father of Simon Peter
column6: the grace or mercy of the Lord
column7: John, also known as Jonah, was the father of Simon Peter, one of Jesus' closest disciples.

column5: A member of the high priest's family
column6: the grace or mercy of the Lord
column7: One who, with Annas and Caiaphas, sat in judgment on the apostles Peter and John ([[@44004006|Acts 4:6]]).

column5: Son of Paseah, who repaired the Old Gate
column7: Joiada, the son of Paseah, repaired the Old Gate during the rebuilding of Jerusalem's walls under Nehemiah.

column5: A high priest, son of Eliashib
column7: Joiada served as a high priest during the Persian period, succeeding his father Eliashib.

column5: A high priest, son of Jeshua
column7: (whom Jehovah has set up) = Jehoiakim, a high priest, the son and successor of Jeshua ([[@16012010|Neh. 12:10]], [[@16012012|Neh. 12:12]], [[@16012026|Neh. 12:26]]).

column5: A priestly family that returned from Babylonian exile
column6: chiding, or multiplying, of the Lord
column7: The founder of one of the courses of the priests ([[@16011010|Neh. 11:10]]).

column5: A man of understanding sent by Ezra
column6: chiding, or multiplying, of the Lord
column7: [[@15008016|Ezra 8:16]], a “man of understanding” whom Ezra sent to “bring ministers for the house of God.”

column5: A descendant of Judah who settled in Jerusalem
column6: chiding, or multiplying, of the Lord
column7: Joiarib, a descendant of Judah through Perez, settled in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile.

column5: A town in the hill country of Judah
column6: crookedness, or burning, of the people
column7: A city in the mountains of Judah ([[@6015056|Josh. 15:56]]).

column5: A descendant of Judah through Shelah
column6: that made the sun stand still
column7: Whom Jehovah has set up, one of the descendants of Shelah ([[@13004022|1 Chr. 4:22]]).

column5: A Canaanite city, later a Levitical city in Zebulun
column6: possessing, or building up, of the people
column7: Gathered by the people, ([[@6019011|Josh. 19:11]]; [[@6021034|Josh 21:34]]), a city “of Carmel” (12:22), i.e., on Carmel, allotted with its suburbs to the Merarite Levites.

column5: A son of Abraham and Keturah
column7: Snarer, the second son of Abraham and Keturah ([[@1025002|Gen. 25:2]], [[@1025003|Gen. 25:3]]; [[@13001032|1 Chr. 1:32]]).

column5: Son of Eber and ancestor of Arabian tribes
column7: Little, the second of the two sons of Eber ([[@1010025|Gen. 10:25]]; [[@13001019|1 Chr. 1:19]]). There is an Arab tradition that Joktan (Arab.

column5: A town in the Shephelah region of Judah
column7: Joktheel, a town in the Shephelah (lowland) region of Judah (<ref="Joshua 15:38">Joshua 15:38</ref>).

column5: Nephew of David, friend and advisor to Amnon
column7: Jonadab, also known as Jonathan, was the son of David's brother Shimeah and a friend and advisor to Amnon, David's eldest son.

column5: Son of Rechab, who promoted Rechabite lifestyle
column7: The son of Rechab, and founder of the Rechabites (q.v.), [[@12010015|2 Kings 10:15]]; [[@24035006|Jer. 35:6]], [[@24035010|Jer. 35:10]].

column5: Prophet swallowed by fish, preached to Nineveh
column6: or Jonas, a dove; he that oppresses; destroyer
column7: A dove, the son of Amittai of Gath-hepher. He was a prophet of Israel, and predicted the restoration of the ancient boundaries ([[@12014025-12014027|2 Kings 14:25-27]]) of the kingdom. He exercised his ministry very early in the reign of Jeroboam II., and thus was contemporary with Hosea and Amos; or possibly he preceded them, and consequently may have been the very oldest of all the prophets whose writings we possess. His personal history is mainly to be gathered from the book which bears his name.

column5: An ancestor of Jesus
column6: a dove; multiplying of the people
column7: Jonam, son of Eliakim, was an ancestor of Jesus Christ.

column5: A Levite who served as a priest for Dan
column7: A Levite descended from Gershom ([[@7018030|Judg. 18:30]]). His history is recorded in 17:7-13 and 18:30. The Rabbins changed this name into Manasseh “to screen the memory of the great lawgiver from the stain of having so unworthy an apostate among his near descendants.”

column5: Eldest son of King Saul and friend of David
column7: The eldest son of king Saul, and the bosom friend of David. He is first mentioned when he was about thirty years of age, some time after his father’s accession to the throne ([[@9013002|1 Sam. 13:2]]). Like his father, he was a man of great strength and activity ([[@10001023|2 Sam. 1:23]]), and excelled in archery and slinging ([[@13012002|1 Chr. 12:2]];[[@10001022|2 Sam. 1:22]]). The affection that evidently subsisted between him and his father was interrupted by the growth of Saul’s insanity.

column5: Son of Abiathar the priest during David's reign
column7: Son of the high priest Abiathar, and one who adhered to David at the time of Absalom’s rebellion ([[@10015027|2 Sam. 15:27]], [[@10015036|2 Sam. 15:36]]).

column5: Son of Shammah the Hararite, one of David's mighty men
column7: Jonathan, the son of Shammah the Hararite, was one of David's mighty men, known for his military prowess.

column5: Son of Jada, descendant of Judah
column7: One of the descendants of Judah, Jonathan was the son of Jada.

column5: One of King David's officials
column7: Jonathan, the son of Uzziah, was one of King David's officials in charge of the royal treasuries.

column5: Descendant of Adaiah who returned from exile
column7: Jonathan, of the descendants of Adaiah, was among those who returned to Jerusalem from Babylonian exile.

column5: Opposed divorcing foreigners, with Jahzeiah and Meshullam
column7: Jonathan, along with Jahzeiah and Meshullam, opposed Ezra's demand to put away foreign wives.

column5: Head of priestly family of Malluchi
column7: Jonathan was the head of the priestly family of Malluchi during the high priesthood of Joiakim.

column5: Priest who participated in dedication of Jerusalem's wall
column7: Jonathan, a priest, was among those who blew trumpets at the dedication of Jerusalem's wall.

column5: Scribe with a house used as prison
column7: Jonathan was a scribe who had a house in Jerusalem that was used as a prison.

column5: Son of Kareah, came to Gedaliah at Mizpah
column7: Jonathan son of Kareah was one of the army officers who came to Gedaliah at Mizpah after the fall of Jerusalem.

column5: An ancient seaport, the main port for Jerusalem
column7: Beauty, a town in the portion of Dan ([[@6019046|Josh. 19:46]]; A.V., “Japho”), on a sandy promontory between Caesarea and Gaza, and at a distance of 30 miles north-west from Jerusalem. It is one of the oldest towns in Asia. It was and still is the chief sea-port of Judea. It was never wrested from the Phoenicians.

column5: Ancestor of exiles who returned to Jerusalem
column6: Jorai, showing; casting forth; a cauldron
column7: The descendants of Jorah (or Hariph) were among the exiles who returned to Jerusalem from Babylon.

column5: A chief of the half-tribe of Manasseh
column7: Jorai was a clan chief of the half-tribe of Manasseh during the reign of King Jotham of Judah.

column5: Son of King Toi, brought gifts to David
column7: Joram (or Hadoram), son of King Toi of Hamath, brought gifts to King David after David's defeat of Hadadezer.

column5: King of N. Israel, son of Ahab
column7: Joram (or Jehoram), the son of Ahab, was king of Northern Israel for twelve years.

column5: A Levite during the reign of King David
column7: Joram was a Levite who served during the reign of King David.

column5: A river and region, significant in Israel's history
column7: The Jabbok or Wady Zerka, formerly the northern boundary of Ammon. It enters the Jordan about 20 miles north of Jericho. The first historical notice of the Jordan is in the account of the separation of Abraham and Lot ([[@1013010|Gen. 13:10]]). “Lot beheld the plain of Jordan as the garden of the Lord.”

column5: An ancestor of Jesus Christ
column7: Jorim is listed as one of the ancestors of Jesus Christ in the genealogy recorded by Luke.

column5: A son or town founded by Raham
column7: Jorkeam was a descendant of Caleb or a town founded by Raham in the tribe of Judah.

column5: An ancestor of Jesus Christ
column7: The son of Judah, and father of Semei ([[@42003026|Luke 3:26]]).

column5: Son of Jacob, ruler in Egypt
column7: The elder of the two sons of Jacob by Rachel ([[@1030023|Gen. 30:23]], [[@1030024|Gen. 30:24]]), who, on the occasion of his birth, said, “God hath taken away [Heb. ‘asaph] my reproach.” “The Lord shall add [Heb. yoseph] to me another son” ([[@1030024|Gen. 30:24]]). He was a child of probably six years of age when his father returned from Haran to Canaan and took up his residence in the old patriarchal town of Hebron.

column5: Representative of Issachar among the spies
column7: Joseph son of Igal represented the tribe of Issachar among the twelve spies sent to Canaan.

column5: Son of Asaph, a musician in David's time
column7: One of the sons of Asaph, head of the first division of sacred musicians ([[@13025002|1 Chr. 25:2]], [[@13025009|1 Chr. 25:9]]).

column5: An Israelite who married a foreign woman
column7: Joseph was among the Israelites who had married foreign women during the time of Ezra.

column5: Head of the priestly family of Shebaniah
column7: Joseph was the head of the priestly family of Shebaniah during the high priesthood of Joiakim.

column5: Husband of Mary and earthly father of Jesus
column7: The foster-father of our Lord ([[@40001016|Matt. 1:16]]; [[@42003023|Luke 3:23]]). He lived at Nazareth in Galilee ([[@42002004|Luke 2:4]]). He is called a “just man.” He was by trade a carpenter ([[@40013055|Matt. 13:55]]). He is last mentioned in connection with the journey to Jerusalem, when Jesus was twelve years old. It is probable that he died before Jesus entered on his public ministry.

column5: Of Arimathea, buried Jesus in his own tomb
column7: A native of Arimathea, probably the Ramah of the Old Testament ([[@9001019|1 Sam. 1:19]]), a man of wealth, and a member of the Sanhedrim ([[@40027057|Matt. 27:57]]; [[@42023050|Luke 23:50]]), an “honourable counsellor, who waited for the kingdom of God.” As soon as he heard the tidings of Christ’s death, he “went in boldly” (lit. “having summoned courage, he went”) “unto Pilate, and craved the body of Jesus.”

column5: An ancestor of Jesus Christ
column7: Joseph, the son of Mattathias, is listed as an ancestor of Jesus Christ in Luke's genealogy.

column5: An ancestor of Jesus Christ
column7: Joseph, the son of Jonam, is listed as an ancestor of Jesus Christ in Luke's genealogy.

column5: Candidate to replace Judas as apostle
column7: Surnamed Barsabas ([[@44001023|Acts 1:23]]); also called Justus.

column5: Brother of Jesus and son of Mary
column7: The foster-father of our Lord ([[@40001016|Matt. 1:16]]; [[@42003023|Luke 3:23]]). He lived at Nazareth in Galilee ([[@42002004|Luke 2:4]]). He is called a “just man.” He was by trade a carpenter ([[@40013055|Matt. 13:55]]). He is last mentioned in connection with the journey to Jerusalem, when Jesus was twelve years old. It is probable that he died before Jesus entered on his public ministry.

column5: Brother of James "the Less" and son of the "other" Mary
column7: Joses (or Joseph) was brother of James "the Less" who was an apostle.

column5: A Simeonite leader during Hezekiah's reign
column7: Joshah was one of the leaders from the tribe of Simeon during the reign of King Hezekiah.

column5: One of David's mighty warriors from Mithan
column7: Joshaphat the Mithnite was listed among David's mighty warriors.

column5: A priest who blew trumpets before the ark
column7: One of the priests who accompanied the removal of the ark to Jerusalem ([[@13015024|1 Chr. 15:24]]).

column5: One of David's mighty warriors from Eliahba's sons
column6: the seat, alteration, or captivity of the Lord
column7: Joshaviah, a son of Elnaam, was listed among David's mighty warriors.

column5: A son of Heman, a musician in David's time
column7: Joshbekashah, one of Heman's sons, was a musician appointed by King David to lead worship.

column5: A Simeonite leader during Hezekiah's reign
column6: the seat, or captivity of the Lord
column7: Joshibiah was one of the leaders from the tribe of Simeon during the reign of King Hezekiah.

column5: Moses' assistant who led Israel into Canaan
column7: Jehovah is his help, or Jehovah the Saviour. The son of Nun, of the tribe of Ephraim, the successor of Moses as the leader of Israel. He is called Jehoshua in [[@4013016|Num. 13:16]] (A.V.), and Jesus in [[@44007045|Acts 7:45]] and [[@58004008|Heb. 4:8]] (R.V., Joshua). He was born in Egypt, and was probably of the age of Caleb, with whom he is generally associated.

column5: King of Judah known for his religious reforms
column6: the Lord burns; the fire of the Lord
column7: Healed by Jehovah, or Jehovah will support. The son of Amon, and his successor on the throne of Judah ([[@12022001|2 Kings 22:1]]; [[@14034001|2 Chr. 34:1]]). His history is contained in 2 Kings 22, 23. He stands foremost among all the kings of the line of David for unswerving loyalty to Jehovah (23:25).

column5: One who provided silver and gold for a crown

column5: Father of Shelomith, a returning exile
column6: increase of the Lord; the Lord's finishing
column7: Josiphiah was the father of Shelomith, who was among the exiles who returned with Ezra to Jerusalem.

column5: The hometown of Amon's mother, Meshullemeth
column7: Jotbah, the hometown of Meshullemeth; mother of King Amon of Judah (<ref="2Ki.21.19">2Ki.21.19</ref>).

column5: A place where the Israelites camped during their wilderness journey
column7: Jotbathah, a place where the Israelites camped during their wilderness journey, known for its streams of water (<ref="Numbers 33:33-34; Deu.10.7">Numbers 33:33-34; Deu.10.7</ref>).

column5: Youngest son of Gideon who escaped Abimelech's massacre
column7: The youngest of Gideon’s seventy sons. He escaped when the rest were put to death by the order of Abimelech ([[@7009005|Judg. 9:5]]). When “the citizens of Shechem and the whole house of Millo” were gathered together “by the plain of the pillar” (i.e., the stone set up by Joshua, 24:26; comp. [[@1035004|Gen. 35:4]]) “that was in Shechem, to make Abimelech king,” from one of the heights of Mount Gerizim he protested against their doing so in the earliest parable, that of the bramble-king. His words then spoken were prophetic.

column5: King of Judah and son of Uzziah
column7: The son and successor of Uzziah on the throne of Judah. As during his last years Uzziah was excluded from public life on account of his leprosy, his son, then twenty-five years of age, administered for seven years the affairs of the kingdom in his father’s stead ([[@14026021|2 Chr. 26:21]], [[@14026023|2 Chr. 26:23]]; 27:1). After his father’s death he became sole monarch, and reigned for sixteen years (B.C. 759-743). He ruled in the fear of God, and his reign was prosperous.

column5: A son of Jahdai, a Calebite
column7: Jotham was a son of Jahdai, who was a wife of Caleb.

column5: A Benjamite warrior who joined David at Ziklag
column7: One of the Benjamite archers who joined David at Ziklag ([[@13012004|1 Chr. 12:4]]).

column5: A Levite appointed as an overseer during Hezekiah's reign
column7: Jozabad, a Levite, was one of the overseers appointed by King Hezekiah to distribute the contributions to the priests and Levites.

column5: A Levite who contributed to the Passover celebration
column7: Jozabad, along with other Levitical leaders, generously provided animals for the Passover offerings during King Josiah's reign.

column5: A priest who weighed the silver and gold offerings
column7: Jozabad, along with Noadiah, was a priest appointed to weigh the silver, gold, and vessels brought as offerings to the temple.

column5: A priest who married a foreign woman
column7: Jozabad was one of the priests who had married foreign women during the time of Ezra and agreed to put them away.

column5: A Levite who married a foreign woman
column7: Jozabad was one of the Levites who had married foreign women during the time of Ezra and agreed to put them away.

column5: A Levite who helped explain the Law to the people
column7: Jozabad was one of the Levites who helped the people understand the Law as Ezra read it aloud.

column5: A Levite leader in charge of outside work
column7: Jozabad, one of the leaders of the Levites, was in charge of the outside work of the house of God.

column5: One of the servants who killed King Joash
column7: Jozacar (or Zabad), along with Jehozabad, was one of the servants who conspired against and killed King Joash of Judah.

column5: A priest whose descendants married foreign women
column7: Among the descendants of Jozadak, some priests were found to have married foreign women during the time of Ezra.

column5: Father of musicians who play the lyre and pipe
column7: Jubilee, music, Lamech’s second son by Adah, of the line of Cain.

A joyful shout or clangour of trumpets, the name of the great semi-centennial festival of the Hebrews. It lasted for a year. During this year the land was to be fallow, and the Israelites were only permitted to gather the spontaneous produce of the fields ([[@3025011|Lev. 25:11]], [[@3025012|Lev. 25:12]]). All landed property during that year reverted to its original owner (13-34; 27:16-24), and all who were slaves were set free (25:39-54), and all debts were remitted.

column5: Israelite tribe, kingdom, and province
column6: the praise of the Lord; confession
column7: Praise, the fourth son of Jacob by Leah. The name originated in Leah’s words of praise to the Lord on account of his birth: “Now will I praise [Heb. odeh] Jehovah, and she called his name Yehudah” ([[@1029035|Gen. 29:35]]). It was Judah that interposed in behalf of Joseph, so that his life was spared ([[@1037026|Gen. 37:26]], [[@1037027|Gen. 37:27]]). He took a lead in the affairs of the family, and “prevailed above his brethren” ([[@1043003-1043010|Gen. 43:3-10]]; [[@1044014|Gen 44:14]], [[@1044016-1044034|Gen 44:16-34]]; [[@1046028|Gen 46:28]]; [[@13005002|1 Chr. 5:2]]).
