column5: One of the twelve apostles of Jesus
column7: Judas, also known as Lebbaeus or Thaddaeus, was one of the twelve apostles chosen by Jesus Christ.

column5: The apostle who betrayed Jesus
column7: Son of Simon ([[@43006071|John 6:71]]; [[@43013002|John 13:2]], [[@43013026|John 13:26]]), surnamed Iscariot, i.e., a man of Kerioth ([[@6015025|Josh. 15:25]]). His name is uniformly the last in the list of the apostles, as given in the synoptic (i.e., the first three) Gospels. The evil of his nature probably gradually unfolded itself till “Satan entered into him” ([[@43013027|John 13:27]]), and he betrayed our Lord (18:3).

column5: The Galilean, a Jewish rebel leader
column7: Judas the Galilean led a revolt against the Roman census during the time of Quirinius, governor of Syria.

column5: A Christian living on Straight Street in Damascus
column7: A Jew of Damascus ([[@44009011|Acts 9:11]]), to whose house Ananias was sent.

column5: A prophet and leader in the Jerusalem church
column7: A Christian teacher, surnamed Barsabas. He was sent from Jerusalem to Antioch along with Paul and Barnabas with the decision of the council ([[@44015022|Acts 15:22]], [[@44015027|Acts 15:27]], [[@44015032|Acts 15:32]]).

column5: A brother of Jesus and author of the epistle
column7: = Judas. Among the apostles there were two who bore this name, (1) Judas ([[@65001001|Jude 1]]:1; [[@40013055|Matt. 13:55]]; [[@43014022|John 14:22]]; [[@44001013|Acts 1:13]]), called also Lebbaeus or Thaddaeus ([[@40010003|Matt. 10:3]]; [[@41003018|Mark 3:18]]); and (2) Judas Iscariot ([[@40010004|Matt. 10:4]]; [[@41003019|Mark 3:19]]). He who is called “the brother of James” ([[@42006016|Luke 6:16]]), may be the same with the Judas surnamed Lebbaeus.

column5: The southern region of Israel, centered around Jerusalem
column7: After the Captivity this name was applied to the whole of the country west of the Jordan ([[@37001001|Hag. 1:1]], [[@37001014|Hag. 1:14]]; 2:2). But under the Romans, in the time of Christ, it denoted the southernmost of the three divisions of Palestine ([[@40002001|Matt. 2:1]], [[@40002005|Matt. 2:5]]; 3:1; 4:25), although it was also sometimes used for Palestine generally ([[@44028021|Acts 28:21]]). The province of Judea, as distinguished from Galilee and Samaria, included the territories of the tribes of Judah, Benjamin, Dan, Simeon, and part of Ephraim.

column5: A Hittite woman who married Esau
column6: the praise of the Lord; confession
column7: Jewess, the daughter of Beeri the Hittite, and one of Esau’s wives ([[@1026034|Gen. 26:34]]), elsewhere called Aholibamah (36:2-14).

column5: A Christian woman greeted by Paul in Romans
column7: A Christian woman at Rome to whom Paul sent his salutations ([[@45016015|Rom. 16:15]]), supposed to be the wife of Philologus.

column5: A centurion of the Augustan Cohort
column7: The centurion of the Augustan cohort, or the emperor’s body-guard, in whose charge Paul was sent prisoner to Rome ([[@44027001|Acts 27:1]], [[@44027003|Acts 27:3]], [[@44027043|Acts 27:43]]).

column5: A prominent apostle and relative of Paul
column7: ([[@45016007|Rom. 16:7]]), a Christian at Rome to whom Paul sends salutations along with Andronicus.

column5: A descendant of King Jehoiachin
column7: Jushab-hesed was one of the sons of Zerubbabel, a descendant of King Jehoiachin of Judah.

A forensic term, opposed to condemnation. As regards its nature, it is the judicial act of God, by which he pardons all the sins of those who believe in Christ, and accounts, accepts, and treats them as righteous in the eye of the law, i.e., as conformed to all its demands. In addition to the pardon (q.v.) of sin, justification declares that all the claims of the law are satisfied in respect of the justified. It is the act of a judge and not of a sovereign.

column5: Titius Justus, a Gentile believer who hosted Paul in Corinth
column7: A Jewish proselyte at Corinth, in whose house, next door to the synagogue, Paul held meetings and preached after he left the synagogue ([[@44018007|Acts 18:7]]).

column5: Jesus Justus, a Jewish believer who supported Paul
column7: A Jewish Christian, called Jesus, Paul’s only fellow-labourer at Rome, where he wrote his Epistle to the Colossians ([[@51004011|Col. 4:11]]).

column5: A town in the hill country of Judah, a Levitical city
column7: Extended, a Levitical city in the mountains or hill-country of Judah ([[@6015055|Josh. 15:55]]; [[@6021016|Josh 21:16]]). Its modern name is Yutta, a place about 5 1/2 miles south of Hebron. It is supposed to have been the residence of Zacharias and Elisabeth, and the birthplace of John the Baptist, and on this account is annually visited by thousands of pilgrims belonging to the Greek Church ([[@42001039|Luke 1:39]]).

column5: A town in the Negev, home of Benaiah
column7: Gathering of God, a city in the extreme south of Judah, near to Idumaea ([[@6015021|Josh. 15:21]]), the birthplace of Benaiah, one of David’s chief warriors ([[@10023020|2 Sam. 23:20]]; [[@13011022|1 Chr. 11:22]]).

column5: An important oasis in the Wilderness of Zin
column7: Holy, or Kadesh-Barnea, sacred desert of wandering, a place on the south-eastern border of Palestine, about 165 miles from Horeb. It lay in the “wilderness” or “desert of Zin” ([[@1014007|Gen. 14:7]]; [[@4013003-4013026|Num. 13:3-26]]; [[@4014029-4014033|Num 14:29-33]]; [[@4020001|Num 20:1]]; [[@4027014|Num 27:14]]), on the border of Edom (20:16). From this place, in compliance with the desire of the people, Moses sent forth “twelve spies” to spy the land.

column5: A Levite who returned from Babylonian exile
column6: God of antiquity; God of rising
column7: Before God; i.e., his servant, one of the Levites who returned with Zerubbabel from the Captivity ([[@16009004|Neh. 9:4]]; [[@16010009|Neh 10:9]]; [[@16012008|Neh 12:8]]).

column5: A Canaanite people group
column7: Orientals, the name of a Canaanitish tribe which inhabited the north-eastern part of Palestine in the time of Abraham ([[@1015019|Gen. 15:19]]).

column5: A town in the hill country of Judah
column7: A town of the Kenites, a branch of the Midianites ([[@6015057|Josh. 15:57]]), on the east edge of the mountain above Engedi; probably the “nest in a rock” mentioned by Balaam ([[@4024021|Num. 24:21]]).

column5: A priest during the time of Joiakim
column6: light; resting by fire; my voice
column7: Kallai was a priest who served during the time of Joiakim, the son of Jeshua, after the Babylonian exile.

column5: The burial place of Jair, a judge of Israel
column7: Full of stalks, a place ([[@7010005|Judg. 10:5]]) where Jair was buried. It has usually been supposed to have been a city of Gilead, on the east of Jordan.

column5: A brook marking the border between Ephraim and Manasseh
column7: A stream forming the boundary between Ephraim and Manasseh, from the Mediterranean eastward to Tappuah ([[@6016008|Josh. 16:8]]). It has been identified with the sedgy streams that constitute the Wady Talaik, which enters the sea between Joppa and Caesarea.

column5: Town in Asher's territory; village where Jesus performed miracles
column7: A town in the north of Asher ([[@6019028|Josh. 19:28]]). It has been identified with ‘Ain-Kana, a village on the brow of a valley some 7 miles south-east of Tyre. About a mile north of this place are many colossal ruins strown about. And in the side of a neighbouring ravine are figures of men, women, and children cut in the face of the rock.

column5: Father of Johanan and Jonathan
column7: Bald, the father of Johanan and Jonathan, who for a time were loyal to Gedaliah, the Babylonian governor of Jerusalem ([[@24040008|Jer. 40:8]], [[@24040013|Jer 40:13]], [[@24040015|Jer 40:15]], [[@24040016|Jer 40:16]]).

column5: A place on the southern border of Judah
column7: Karka, a location along the southern border of the tribe of Judah (<ref="Joshua 15:3">Joshua 15:3</ref>).

column5: A place where Gideon defeated Zebah and Zalmunna
column7: Foundation, a place in the open desert wastes on the east of Jordan ([[@7008010|Judg. 8:10]]), not far beyond Succoth and Penuel, to the south.

column5: A Levitical city in the territory of Naphtali
column7: Double city, a town of Naphali, assigned to the Gershonite Levites, and one of the cities of refuge ([[@6021032|Josh. 21:32]]).

column5: A son of Ishmael and a nomadic tribe
column7: Dark-skinned, the second son of Ishmael ([[@1025013|Gen. 25:13]]). It is the name for the nomadic tribes of Arabs, the Bedouins generally ([[@23021016|Isa. 21:16]]; [[@23042011|Isa 42:11]]; [[@23060007|Isa 60:7]]; [[@24002010|Jer. 2:10]]; [[@26027021|Ezek. 27:21]]), who dwelt in the north-west of Arabia. They lived in black hair-tents ([[@22001005|Cant. 1:5]]). To “dwell in the tents of Kedar” was to be cut off from the worship of the true God ([[@19120005|Ps. 120:5]]).

column5: A son of Ishmael; Nodab, a Hagrite tribe
column7: Eastward, the last-named of the sons of Ishmael ([[@1025015|Gen. 25:15]]).

column5: A town in Moab, later a Levitical city in Reuben
column7: Beginnings; easternmost, a city of Reuben, assigned to the Levites of the family of Merari ([[@6013018|Josh. 13:18]]).

column5: A Canaanite city, later a Levitical city of refuge in Naphtali
column7: A “fenced city” of Naphtali, one of the cities of refuge ([[@6019037|Josh. 19:37]]; [[@7004006|Judg. 4:6]]). It was assigned to the Gershonite Levites ([[@6021032|Josh. 21:32]]). It was originally a Canaanite royal city ([[@6012022|Josh. 12:22]]), and was the residence of Barak ([[@7004006|Judg. 4:6]]); and here he and Deborah assembled the tribes of Zebulun and Naphtali before the commencement of the conflict with Sisera in the plain of Esdraelon, “for Jehovah among the mighty” (9, 10). In the reign of Pekah it was taken by Tiglath-Pileser ([[@12015029|2 Kings 15:29]]).

column5: A place where the Israelites camped during their wilderness journey
column7: Assembly, one of the stations of the Israelites in the desert ([[@4033022|Num. 33:22]], [[@4033023|Num. 33:23]]).

column5: A town in the Shephelah of Judah, rescued by David
column7: Citadel, a city in the lowlands of Judah ([[@6015044|Josh. 15:44]]). David rescued it from the attack of the Philistines ([[@9023001-9023008|1 Sam. 23:1-8]]); but the inhabitants proving unfaithful to him, in that they sought to deliver him up to Saul (13), he and his men “departed from Keilah, and went whithersoever they could go.” They fled to the hill Hareth, about 3 miles to the east, and thence through Hebron to Ziph (q.v.). “And David was in the wilderness of Ziph, in a wood” ([[@9023015|1 Sam. 23:15]]). Here Jonathan sought him out, “and strengthened his hand in God.”

column5: A Levite who married a foreign woman
column6: voice of the Lord; gathering together
column7: Dwarf, a Levite who assisted Ezra in expounding the law to the people ([[@16008007|Neh. 8:7]]; [[@16010010|Neh 10:10]]).

column5: A Levite who taught the Law and sealed the covenant
column7: Dwarf, a Levite who assisted Ezra in expounding the law to the people ([[@16008007|Neh. 8:7]]; [[@16010010|Neh 10:10]]).

column5: A son of Nahor and Milcah
column6: God hath raised up, or established him
column7: Kemuel was a son of Nahor and Milcah and the father of Aram.

column5: A leader from the tribe of Ephraim
column6: God hath raised up, or established him
column7: Son of Shiphtan, appointed on behalf of the tribe of Ephraim to partition the land of Canaan ([[@4034024|Num. 34:24]]).

column5: A Levite leader during David's reign
column6: God hath raised up, or established him
column7: Kemuel, the son of Hebron, was the leader of the Levites during the reign of King David.

column5: Son of Enosh, descendant of Seth
column7: The fourth antediluvian patriarch, the eldest son of Enos. He was 70 years old at the birth of his eldest son Mahalaleel, after which he lived 840 years ([[@1005009-1005014|Gen. 5:9-14]]), and was 910 years old when he died.

column5: A city in Gilead, captured by Nobah and renamed
column7: Possession, a city of Gilead. It was captured by Nobah, who called it by his own name ([[@4032042|Num. 32:42]]).

column5: An Edomite clan descended from Esau
column7: One of the sons of Eliphaz, the son of Esau.

column5: Father of Othniel, a judge of Israel
column7: Caleb’s younger brother, and father of Othniel ([[@6015017|Josh. 15:17]]), whose family was of importance in Israel down to the time of David ([[@13027015|1 Chr. 27:15]]).

column5: A descendant of Caleb
column7: Kenaz was a descendant of Caleb, mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah.

column5: A nomadic tribe friendly to the Israelites
column7: The Kenites were a nomadic tribe who lived in the region of Canaan and were generally friendly to the Israelites, often providing them with assistance and support.

column5: A Canaanite tribe in the Promised Land
column7: The name of a tribe referred to in the covenant God made with Abraham ([[@1015019|Gen. 15:19]]).

column5: Job's third daughter born after his restoration
column6: the horn or child of beauty
column7: Horn of the face-paint = cosmetic-box, the name of Job’s third daughter ([[@18042014|Job. 42:14]]), born after prosperity had returned to him.

column5: A town in the Negev region of Judah
column7: Kerioth-hezron, also known as Hazor, was a town in the Negev region of Judah (<ref="Joshua 15:25">Joshua 15:25</ref>).

column5: A family of temple servants who returned from exile
column7: Keros was the name of a family of temple servants (Nethinim) who returned to Jerusalem from Babylonian exile.

column5: Abraham's concubine after Sarah's death
column6: that makes the incense to fume
column7: Incense, the wife of Abraham, whom he married probably after Sarah’s death ([[@1025001-1025006|Gen. 25:1-6]]), by whom he had six sons, whom he sent away into the east country. Her nationality is unknown. She is styled “Abraham’s concubine” ([[@13001032|1 Chr. 1:32]]).

column5: Job's second daughter born after his restoration
column7: Cassia, the name of Job’s second daughter (42:14), born after prosperity had returned to him.

column5: A place where the Israelites complained and were punished
column7: The graves of the longing or of lust, one of the stations of the Israelites in the wilderness. It was probably in the Wady Murrah, and has been identified with the Erweis el-Ebeirig, where the remains of an ancient encampment have been found, about 30 miles north-east of Sinai, and exactly a day’s journey from ‘Ain Hudherah. “Here began the troubles of the journey.

column5: A Levitical city in the territory of Ephraim
column7: Two heaps, a city of Ephraim, assigned to the Kohathite Levites, and appointed as a city of refuge (Josh. 21: 22).

column5: A valley east of Jerusalem, site of significant events
column7: = Kedron = Cedron, turbid, the winter torrent which flows through the Valley of Jehoshaphat, on the eastern side of Jerusalem, between the city and the Mount of Olives. This valley is known in Scripture only by the name “the brook Kidron.” David crossed this brook bare-foot and weeping, when fleeing from Absalom ([[@10015023|2 Sam. 15:23]], [[@10015030|2 Sam. 15:30]]), and it was frequently crossed by our Lord in his journeyings to and fro ([[@43018001|John 18:1]]).

column5: A town in the Negev region of Judah
column7: An elegy, a city in the extreme south of Judah ([[@6015022|Josh. 15:22]]).

column5: An ancient trade route through Edom and Moab
column7: The King's Highway, an ancient trade route through Edom and Moab, was the path the Israelites sought to use during their journey to Canaan (<ref="Numbers 20:17; 21:22">Numbers 20:17; 21:22</ref>).

column5: A valley near Salem (Jerusalem), site of significant events
column7: The King's Valley, located near Salem (Jerusalem), was the site where Melchizedek met Abraham and where Absalom erected a pillar for himself (<ref="Genesis 14:17; 2Sa.18.18">Genesis 14:17; 2Sa.18.18</ref>).

column5: A Moabite city, later destroyed by the Babylonians
column7: A wall or fortress, a place to which Tiglath-pileser carried the Syrians captive after he had taken the city of Damascus ([[@12016009|2 Kings 16:9]]; [[@30001005|Amos 1:5]]; [[@30009007|Amos 9:7]]). Isaiah (22:6), who also was contemporary with these events, mentions it along with Elam.

column5: A city or region in Mesopotamia, possibly Elam
column7: A wall or fortress, a place to which Tiglath-pileser carried the Syrians captive after he had taken the city of Damascus ([[@12016009|2 Kings 16:9]]; [[@30001005|Amos 1:5]]; [[@30009007|Amos 9:7]]). Isaiah (22:6), who also was contemporary with these events, mentions it along with Elam.

column5: A place Balak took Balaam
column7: City of streets, [[@4022039|Num. 22:39]], a Moabite city, which some identify with Kirjathaim. Balak here received and entertained Balaam, whom he had invited from Pethor, among the “mountains of the east,” beyond the Euphrates, to lay his ban upon the Israelites, whose progress he had no hope otherwise of arresting.

column5: A city where the ark resided
column6: her idol; she that is governed or subdued; a spouse
column7: A city on the northern border of the tribe of Judah ([[@6015010|Josh. 15:10]]), called also Kirjath-jearim, q.v. (15:9; [[@13013006|1 Chr. 13:6]]), now Kuriet-el-Enab, or as some think, ‘Erma.

column5: A Moabite city, later allotted to Reuben
A Levitical city in Reuben
column6: the two cities; callings; or meetings
column7: Kiriathaim, a Levitical city in the territory of Reuben (<ref="1Ch.6.76">1Ch.6.76</ref>).

column5: Father of Saul, the first king of Israel
column7: A Benjamite, the son of Abiel, and father of king Saul ([[@9009001|1 Sam. 9:1]], [[@9009003|1 Sam. 9:3]]; [[@9010011|1 Sam. 10:11]], [[@9010021|1 Sam. 10:21]]; [[@9014051|1 Sam. 14:51]]; [[@10021014|2 Sam. 21:14]]). All that is recorded of him is that he sent his son Saul in search of his asses that had strayed, and that he was buried in Zelah.

column5: A Levite from the Merari clan
column7: A Levite of the family of Merari ([[@13023021|1 Chr. 23:21]]; [[@13024029|1 Chr. 24:29]]).

column5: A Levite who helped purify the temple
column7: A Levite in the time of Hezekiah ([[@14029012|2 Chr. 29:12]]).

column5: An ancestor of Mordecai
column7: The great-grandfather of Mordecai ([[@17002005|Esther 2:5]]).

column5: A Levite and father of Jeduthun (or 'Ethan')
column7: Kishi, also known as Kushaiah, was a Levite from the clan of Merari and the father of Jeduthun (or 'Ethan'), a prominent musician in King David's court.

column5: A Levitical city in Issachar
column7: Hardness, a city of Issachar assigned to the Gershonite Levites ([[@6019020|Josh. 19:20]]), the same as Kishon (21:28).

column5: A river in northern Israel
column7: Winding, a winter torrent of Central Palestine, which rises about the roots of Tabor and Gilboa, and passing in a northerly direction through the plains of Esdraelon and Acre, falls into the Mediterranean at the north-eastern corner of the bay of Acre, at the foot of Carmel. It is the drain by which the waters of the plain of Esdraelon and of the mountains that surround it find their way to the sea. It bears the modern name of Nahr el-Mokattah, i.e., “the river of slaughter” (comp. [[@11018040|1 Kings 18:40]]).

column5: A city in Zebulun not conquered
column7: Knotty, a city of Zebulun ([[@7001030|Judg. 1:30]]), called also Kattath ([[@6019015|Josh. 19:15]]); supposed to be “Cana of Galilee.”

column5: Descendants of Javan, son of Japheth
column7: Kittim, a descendant of Japheth, son of Noah.

column5: A people group mentioned by Ezekiel
column6: hope; a congregation; a line; a rule
column7: He-camel, occurs only in [[@26023023|Ezek. 23:23]], some province or place in the Babylonian empire, used in this passage along with Shoa (q.v.).

column5: Son of Levi; Levite clan ancestor
column7: Assembly, the second son of Levi, and father of Amram ([[@1046011|Gen. 46:11]]).

column5: Benjamite of Jerusalem
column7: Kolaiah, a Benjamite who lived in Jerusalem.

column5: False prophet in Babylon
column7: Kolaiah, a false prophet among the exiles in Babylon.

column5: Son of Esau
column7: The third son of Esau, by Aholibamah ([[@1036014|Gen. 36:14]]; [[@13001035|1 Chr. 1:35]]).

column5: Edomite chief, descendant of Eliphaz
column7: Korah, an Edomite chief, descendant of Eliphaz, son of Esau.

column5: Levite rebel leader; his descendants became temple servants
column7: A Levite, the son of Izhar, the brother of Amram, the father of Moses and Aaron ([[@2006021|Ex. 6:21]]). The institution of the Aaronic priesthood and the Levitical service at Sinai was a great religious revolution. The old priesthood of the heads of families passed away. This gave rise to murmurings and discontent, while the Israelites were encamped at Kadesh for the first time, which came to a head in a rebellion against Moses and Aaron, headed by Korah, Dathan, and Abiram.

column5: Son of Hebron, descendant of Caleb
column7: Korah, son of Hebron, from the tribe of Judah.

column5: Levite gatekeeper
column7: A Levite and temple-warder of the Korahites, the son of Asaph.

column5: Levite in charge of freewill offerings
column7: A Levitical porter at the east gate of the temple ([[@14031014|2 Chr. 31:14]]).

column5: Son of Ashhur, a Judahite
column7: A descendant of Judah. [[@13004008|1 Chr. 4:8]], “Coz;” R.V., “Hakkoz.”

column5: Son of Shelah, a Judahite
column6: to assemble together; to testify; passing over
column7: Laadah, a son of Shelah and descendant of Judah.

column5: Brother of Rebekah; father of Leah and Rachel
column7: Laban, the brother of Rebekah and father of Jacob's wives, Leah and Rachel.

column5: A place Moses spoke to Israel
column7: A city in the Arabian desert in the route of the Israelites ([[@5001001|Deut. 1:1]]), probably identical with Libnah ([[@4033020|Num. 33:20]]).

column5: A fortified city in Judah
column6: who walks, or exists, of himself
column7: Impregnable, a royal Canaanitish city in the Shephelah, or maritime plain of Palestine ([[@6010003|Josh. 10:3]], [[@6010005|Josh. 10:5]]; 12:11). It was taken and destroyed by the Israelites ([[@6010031-6010033|Josh. 10:31-33]]). It afterwards became, under Rehoboam, one of the strongest fortresses of Judah ([[@14010009|2 Chr. 10:9]]). It was assaulted and probably taken by Sennacherib ([[@12018014|2 Kings 18:14]], [[@12018017|2 Kings 18:17]]; 19:8; [[@23036002|Isa. 36:2]]).

column5: Descendant of Ephraim
column7: Ladan, a descendant of Ephraim.

column5: Father of Eliasaph, a Gershonite Levite
column7: Lael, the father of Eliasaph, a leader of the Gershonite Levites.

column5: Son of Jahath, a Judahite
column7: Lahad, a descendant of Judah through Jahath.

column5: A city in the lowlands of Judah
column7: Lahmam, a city in the lowlands of Judah (<ref="Joshua 15:40">Joshua 15:40</ref>).

column5: Brother of Goliath the Gittite
column7: Lahmi, the brother of Goliath, was killed by Elhanan the Bethlehemite.

column5: Father of Michal's husband Palti (or 'Paltiel')
column7: Laish, the father of Palti (or 'Paltiel'), to whom Saul gave his daughter Michal in marriage.

column5: A place near Anathoth and Gallim
column7: Laishah, a place near Anathoth and Gallim, mentioned in a prophecy of Isaiah (<ref="Isaiah 10:30">Isaiah 10:30</ref>).

column5: A border town of Naphtali
column7: Lakkum, a border town of the tribe of Naphtali (<ref="Joshua 19:33">Joshua 19:33</ref>).

column5: Descendant of Cain; first polygamist mentioned in the Bible
column7: The fifth in descent from Cain. He was the first to violate the primeval ordinance of marriage ([[@1004018-1004024|Gen. 4:18-24]]). His address to his two wives, Adah and Zillah (4:23, 24), is the only extant example of antediluvian poetry. It has been called “Lamech’s sword-song.”

column5: Father of Noah; lived 777 years
column7: The seventh in descent from Seth, being the only son of Methuselah.

column5: A city in Asia Minor
column7: The city of this name mentioned in Scripture lay on the confines of Phrygia and Lydia, about 40 miles east of Ephesus ([[@66003014|Rev. 3:14]]), on the banks of the Lycus. It was originally called Diospolis and then Rhoas, but afterwards Laodicea, from Laodice, the wife of Antiochus II., king of Syria, who rebuilt it. It was one of the most important and flourishing cities of Asia Minor. At a very early period it became one of the chief seats of Christianity ([[@51002001|Col. 2:1]]; [[@51004015|Col 4:15]]; [[@66001011|Rev. 1:11]], etc.).

column5: Husband of Deborah the prophetess and judge
column7: Torches. Deborah is called “the wife of Lapidoth” ([[@7004004|Judg. 4:4]]).

column5: A city near Fair Havens, Crete
column7: Lasea, a city near Fair Havens on the island of Crete (<ref="Act.27.8">Act.27.8</ref>).

column5: A place marking Canaanite territory; a stop in Israel's journey
column7: Fissure, a place apparently east of the Dead Sea ([[@1010019|Gen. 10:19]]).

column5: A Canaanite city conquered by Joshua
column7: Lasharon, a Canaanite city whose king was defeated by Joshua (<ref="Joshua 12:18">Joshua 12:18</ref>).

column5: Poor man in Jesus' parable of the rich man
column7: Lazarus, a poor man in Jesus' parable of the rich man and Lazarus (<ref="Luk.16.20-25">Luk.16.20-25</ref>).

column5: Brother of Mary and Martha; raised from the dead
column7: The brother of Mary and Martha of Bethany. He was raised from the dead after he had lain four days in the tomb ([[@43011001-43011044|John 11:1-44]]).

column5: Wife of Jacob; mother of six sons and Dinah
column7: Weary, the eldest daughter of Laban, and sister of Rachel ([[@1029016|Gen. 29:16]]). Jacob took her to wife through a deceit of her father ([[@1029023|Gen. 29:23]]). She was “tender-eyed” (17). She bore to Jacob six sons (32-35), also one daughter, Dinah (30:21).

Heb. hamets, properly “ferment.” In [[@4006003|Num. 6:3]], “vinegar of wine” is more correctly “fermented wine.” In [[@2013007|Ex. 13:7]], the proper rendering would be, “Unfermented things [Heb. matstsoth] shall be consumed during the seven days; and there shall not be seen with thee fermented things [hamets], and there shall not be seen with thee leavened mass [seor] in all thy borders.” The chemical definition of ferment or yeast is “a substance in a state of putrefaction, the atoms of which are in a continual motion.”

column5: Ancestor of temple servants who returned from Babylonian exile
column7: Lebanah or Lebana, whose descendants were among the temple servants who returned from the Babylonian exile.

column5: A mountainous region known for its cedar trees
column7: White, “the white mountain of Syria,” is the loftiest and most celebrated mountain range in Syria. It is a branch running southward from the Caucasus, and at its lower end forking into two parallel ranges, the eastern or Anti-Lebanon, and the western or Lebanon proper. They enclose a long valley ([[@6011017|Josh. 11:17]]) of from 5 to 8 miles in width, called by Roman writers Coele-Syria, now called el-Buka’a, “the valley,” a prolongation of the valley of the Jordan.

column5: A mountain range marking the northern border of Israel
column7: Mount Lebanon, a mountain range marking the northern border of the Promised Land (<ref="Judges 3:3">Judges 3:3</ref>).

column5: A valley in the Promised Land conquered by Joshua
column7: The Valley of Lebanon, a valley in the Promised Land conquered by Joshua (<ref="Joshua 11:17; 12:7">Joshua 11:17; 12:7</ref>).

column5: A town in the Negev of Judah
column7: Lebaoth, a town in the Negev region of Judah (<ref="Joshua 15:32">Joshua 15:32</ref>).

column5: A place near Shiloh in Ephraim
column7: Frankincense, a town near Shiloh, on the north side of Bethel ([[@7021019|Judg. 21:19]]).

column5: Son of Er, a Judahite
column7: Lecah, a descendant of Judah through Er.
A regiment of the Roman army, the number of men composing which differed at different times.

column5: Son of Mizraim; progenitor of a people group
column7: Lehabim, a son of Mizraim and progenitor of a people group.

column5: A place where Samson fought the Philistines
column7: A jawbone, a place in the tribe of Judah where Samson achieved a victory over the Philistines ([[@7015009|Judg. 15:9]], [[@7015014|Judg. 15:14]], [[@7015016|Judg. 15:16]]), slaying a thousand of them with the jawbone of an ass. The words in 15:19, “a hollow place that was in the jaw” (A.V.), should be, as in Revised Version, “the hollow place that is in Lehi.”

column5: King mentioned in Proverbs; his mother taught him wisdom
column7: Dedicated to God, a king whom his mother instructed ([[@20031001-20031009|Prov. 31:1-9]]).

(Heb. tsara’ath, a “smiting,” a “stroke,” because the disease was regarded as a direct providential infliction). This name is from the Greek lepra, by which the Greek physicians designated the disease from its scaliness.

column5: Son of Dedan, descendant of Abraham and Keturah
column7: Letushim, a son of Dedan and descendant of Abraham and Keturah.

column5: Son of Dedan, descendant of Abraham and Keturah
column7: Peoples; nations, the last mentioned of the three sons of Dedan, and head of an Arabian tribe ([[@1025003|Gen. 25:3]]).

column5: Son of Jacob; progenitor of the Levites
column7: The third son of Jacob by Leah. The origin of the name is found in Leah’s words ([[@1029034|Gen. 29:34]]), “This time will my husband be joined [Heb. yillaveh] unto me.” He is mentioned as taking a prominent part in avenging his sister Dinah ([[@1034025-1034031|Gen. 34:25-31]]).

column5: Son of Melchi, an ancestor of Jesus
column7: Levi, son of Melchi, an ancestor of Jesus mentioned in Luke's genealogy (<ref="Luk.3.24">Luk.3.24</ref>).

column5: Son of Simeon, an ancestor of Jesus
column7: The father of Matthat, and son of Simeon, of the ancestors of Christ ([[@42003029|Luke 3:29]]).

A descendant of the tribe of Levi ([[@2006025|Ex. 6:25]]; [[@3025032|Lev. 25:32]]; [[@4035002|Num. 35:2]]; [[@6021003|Josh. 21:3]], [[@6021041|Josh. 21:41]]). This name is, however, generally used as the title of that portion of the tribe which was set apart for the subordinate offices of the sanctuary service ([[@11008004|1 Kings 8:4]]; [[@15002070|Ezra 2:70]]), as assistants to the priests. When the Israelites left Egypt, the ancient manner of worship was still observed by them, the eldest son of each house inheriting the priest’s office.

column5: A place where Israel camped in the wilderness
column7: One of the stations of the Israelites in the wilderness ([[@4033020|Num. 33:20]], [[@4033021|Num. 33:21]]).

column5: A Canaanite city conquered by Joshua; a Levitical city
column7: One of the royal cities of the Canaanites taken by Joshua ([[@6010029-6010032|Josh. 10:29-32]]; [[@6012015|Josh 12:15]]). It became one of the Levitical towns in the tribe of Judah (21:13), and was strongly fortified. Sennacherib laid siege to it ([[@12019008|2 Kings 19:8]]; [[@23037008|Isa. 37:8]]). It was the native place of Hamutal, the queen of Josiah ([[@12023031|2 Kings 23:31]]).

column5: Son of Gershon; grandson of Levi
column7: White, one of the two sons of Gershon, the son of Levi ([[@2006017|Ex. 6:17]]; [[@4003018|Num. 3:18]], [[@4003021|Num. 3:21]]).

column5: Grandson of Merari; grandson of Levi
column7: White, one of the two sons of Gershon, the son of Levi ([[@2006017|Ex. 6:17]]; [[@4003018|Num. 3:18]], [[@4003021|Num. 3:21]]).

column5: A country in North Africa
column6: the heart of the sea; fat
column7: The country of the Ludim ([[@1010013|Gen. 10:13]]), Northern Africa, a large tract lying along the Mediterranean, to the west of Egypt ([[@44002010|Acts 2:10]]).

column5: Son of Shemida, a Manassite
column7: Likhi, a son of Shemida and descendant of Manasseh.

column5: Christian in Rome; greeted by Paul
column7: Linus, a Christian in Rome to whom Paul sent greetings.

column5: Symbolic name of Hosea's son; represents God's rejection of Israel
column7: Not my people, a symbolical name given by God’s command to Hosea’s second son in token of Jehovah’s rejection of his people ([[@28001009|Hos. 1:9]], [[@28001010|Hos. 1:10]]), his treatment of them as a foreign people.

column5: A town in Gilead; home of Mephibosheth
column7: No pasture, ([[@10017027|2 Sam. 17:27]]), a town in Gilead not far from Mahanaim, north of the Jabbok (9:4, 5).

column5: Symbolic name of Hosea's daughter; represents God's withdrawal of mercy
column6: not having obtained mercy; not pitied
column7: Not pitied, the name of the prophet Hosea’s first daughter, a type of Jehovah’s temporary rejection of his people ([[@28001006|Hos. 1:6]]; [[@28002023|Hos 2:23]]).

column5: A city in Benjamin; home of Aeneas healed by Peter
column7: A town in the tribe of Ephraim, mentioned only in the New Testament ([[@44009032|Acts 9:32]], [[@44009035|Acts 9:35]], [[@44009038|Acts 9:38]]) as the scene of Peter’s miracle in healing the paralytic AEneas. It lay about 9 miles east of Joppa, on the road from the sea-port to Jerusalem. In the Old Testament ([[@13008012|1 Chr. 8:12]]) it is called Lod. It was burned by the Romans, but was afterwards rebuilt, and was known by the name of Diospolis.

column5: Grandmother of Timothy; commended for her faith
column7: The maternal grandmother of Timothy.
To commemorate the death of Christ: “This do in remembrance of me.”

column5: Abraham's nephew; rescued from Sodom's destruction
column6: Lotan, wrapt up; hidden; covered; myrrh; rosin
column7: (Heb. goral, a “pebble”), a small stone used in casting lots ([[@4033054|Num. 33:54]]; [[@32001007|Jonah 1:7]]). The lot was always resorted to by the Hebrews with strictest reference to the interposition of God, and as a method of ascertaining the divine will ([[@20016033|Prov. 16:33]]), and in serious cases of doubt ([[@17003007|Esther 3:7]]).

column5: Son of Seir the Horite; chief of Edom
column7: Coverer, one of the sons of Seir, the Horite ([[@1036020|Gen. 36:20]], [[@1036029|Gen. 36:29]]).

(Heb. goral, a “pebble”), a small stone used in casting lots ([[@4033054|Num. 33:54]]; [[@32001007|Jonah 1:7]]). The lot was always resorted to by the Hebrews with strictest reference to the interposition of God, and as a method of ascertaining the divine will ([[@20016033|Prov. 16:33]]), and in serious cases of doubt ([[@17003007|Esther 3:7]]).

column5: Prophet and teacher in the church at Antioch.
column7: Of Cyrene, a Christian teacher at Antioch ([[@44013001|Acts 13:1]]), and Paul’s kinsman ([[@45016021|Rom. 16:21]]).

column5: Son of Shem; progenitor of the Lydians
column7: One of the Hamitic tribes descended from Mizraim ([[@1010013|Gen. 10:13]]), a people of Africa ([[@26027010|Ezek. 27:10]]; [[@26030005|Ezek 30:5]]), on the west of Egypt.

column5: Son of Mizraim; progenitor of a people group
A place in Moab
column7: Made of boards, a Moabitish place between Zoar and Horonaim ([[@23015005|Isa. 15:5]]; [[@24048005|Jer. 48:5]]).

column5: Physician; companion of Paul; author of Luke and Acts
column7: The evangelist, was a Gentile. The date and circumstances of his conversion are unknown. According to his own statement ([[@42001002|Luke 1:2]]), he was not an “eye-witness and minister of the word from the beginning.” It is probable that he was a physician in Troas, and was there converted by Paul, to whom he attached himself.

column5: A Canaanite city; a man built another city named Luz
column7: A place in the land of the Hittites, founded ([[@7001026|Judg. 1:26]]) by “a man who came forth out of the city of Luz.”

column5: A region in Asia Minor; Paul and Barnabas preached there
column7: An inland province of Asia Minor, on the west of Cappadocia and the south of Galatia. It was a Roman province, and its chief towns were Iconium, Lystra, and Derbe. The “speech of Lycaonia” ([[@44014011|Acts 14:11]]) was probably the ancient Assyrian language, or perhaps, as others think, a corrupt Greek intermingled with Syriac words.

column5: A region on the southwest coast of Asia Minor
column7: A wolf, a province in the south-west of Asia Minor, opposite the island of Rhodes. It forms part of the region now called Tekeh. It was a province of the Roman empire when visited by Paul ([[@44021001|Acts 21:1]]; [[@44027005|Acts 27:5]]).

column5: Seller of purple goods; converted by Paul in Philippi
column7: A woman of Thyatira, a “seller of purple,” who dwelt in Philippi ([[@44016014|Acts 16:14]], [[@44016015|Acts 16:15]]). She was not a Jewess but a proselyte. The Lord opened her heart as she heard the gospel from the lips of Paul (16:13). She thus became the first in Europe who embraced Christianity.

column5: Tetrarch of Abilene during John the Baptist's ministry
column7: Tetrarch of Abilene ([[@42003001|Luke 3:1]]), on the eastern slope of Anti-Lebanon, near the city of Damascus.

column5: Roman commander who rescued Paul from a Jewish mob
column7: Claudius Lysias, a Greek who, having obtained by purchase the privilege of Roman citizenship, took the name of Claudius ([[@44021031-44021040|Acts 21:31-40]]; [[@44022028|Acts 22:28]]; [[@44023026|Acts 23:26]]).

column5: A city in Lycaonia; Paul and Barnabas preached there
column7: A town of Lycaonia, in Asia Minor, in a wild district and among a rude population. Here Paul preached the gospel after he had been driven by persecution from Iconium ([[@44014002-44014007|Acts 14:2-7]]).

column5: Concubine of Nahor, Abraham's brother
column7: Maacah, a concubine of Nahor, was the mother of Nahor's son Tebah.

column5: A region near Geshur
column7: Maacah (Maacath), a region near Geshur (<ref="Deu.3.14; Joshua 12:5">Deu.3.14; Joshua 12:5</ref>).

column5: Daughter of Talmai; wife of David; mother of Absalom
column7: A daughter of Talmai, king of the old native population of Geshur.

column5: Daughter of Abishalom; wife of Rehoboam; mother of Abijah
column7: The daughter of Abishalom (called Absalom, [[@14011020-14011022|2 Chr. 11:20-22]]), the third wife of Rehoboam, and mother of Abijam ([[@11015002|1 Kings 15:2]]). She is called “Michaiah the daughter of Uriel,” who was the husband of Absalom’s daughter Tamar ([[@14013002|2 Chr. 13:2]]).

column5: Caleb's concubine; mother of Sheber and Tirhanah
column7: Maacah, Caleb's concubine, was the mother of Sheber and Tirhanah.

column5: Sister of Huppim and Shuppim; mother of Peresh and Sheresh
column7: Maacah, the sister of Huppim and Shuppim, was the wife of Machir and mother of Peresh and Sheresh.

column5: Grandmother of Saul
column7: Maacah, the mother of Kish, the father of Saul.

column5: Father of Hanan, one of David's mighty men

column7: Maaseiah, a Levite, was among those who assisted Ezra in reading the Law to the people.

column7: Maaseiah, a descendant of Benjamin, lived in Jerusalem after the exile.

column7: Maaseiah was an ancestor of Jaazaniah, who was associated with the Rechabites during the reign of Jehoiakim.

column7: In New Testament times, was a Roman province lying north of Greece. It was governed by a propraetor with the title of proconsul. Paul was summoned by the vision of the “man of Macedonia” to preach the gospel there ([[@44016009|Acts 16:9]]). Frequent allusion is made to this event (18:5; 19:21; [[@45015026|Rom. 15:26]]; [[@47001016|2 Cor. 1:16]]; [[@47011009|2 Cor. 11:9]]; [[@50004015|Phil. 4:15]]).

column7: Clad with a mantle, or bond of the Lord, one of the Gadite heroes who joined David in the wilderness ([[@13012013|1 Chr. 12:13]]).

column7: Manasseh’s oldest son ([[@6017001|Josh. 17:1]]), or probably his only son (see [[@13007014|1 Chr. 7:14]], [[@13007015|1 Chr. 7:15]]; comp. [[@4026029-4026033|Num. 26:29-33]]; [[@6013031|Josh. 13:31]]). His descendants are referred to under the name of Machirites, being the offspring of Gilead ([[@4026029|Num. 26:29]]). column7: A descendant of the preceding, residing at Lo-debar, where he maintained Jonathan’s son Mephibosheth till he was taken under the care of David ([[@10009004|2 Sam. 9:4]]), and where he afterwards gave shelter to David himself when he was a fugitive (17:27).

column5: One of those who married foreign women
column7: Machnadebai was among those who had married foreign women during the time of Ezra.

column5: A cave near Hebron; burial place of patriarchs
column7: Portion; double cave, the cave which Abraham bought, together with the field in which it stood, from Ephron the Hittite, for a family burying-place (Gen. 23). It is one of those Bible localities about the identification of which there can be no doubt. It was on the slope of a hill on the east of Hebron, “before Mamre.” Here were laid the bodies of Abraham and Sarah, Isaac and Rebekah, Jacob and Leah ([[@1023019|Gen. 23:19]]; [[@1025009|Gen 25:9]]; [[@1049031|Gen 49:31]]; [[@1050013|Gen 50:13]]).

column5: Son of Japheth; progenitor of the Medes
column7: Middle land, the third “son” of Japheth ([[@1010002|Gen. 10:2]]), the name by which the Medes are known on the Assyrian monuments.

column5: A town in the Negev of Judah
column6: measure of a gift; preparation of a garment
column7: Dunghill, the modern el-Minyay, 15 miles south-south-west of Gaza ([[@6015031|Josh. 15:31]]; [[@13002049|1 Chr. 2:49]]), in the south of Judah. The Pal.

column5: Descendant of Caleb, son of Hezron
column6: measure of a gift; preparation of a garment
column7: Dunghill, the modern el-Minyay, 15 miles south-south-west of Gaza ([[@6015031|Josh. 15:31]]; [[@13002049|1 Chr. 2:49]]), in the south of Judah. The Pal.

column5: A place in Moab threatened with destruction
column7: Ibid., a Moabite town threatened with the sword of the Babylonians ([[@24048002|Jer. 48:2]]).

column7: Ibid., a town in Benjamin, not far from Jerusalem, towards the north ([[@23010031|Isa. 10:31]]). The same Hebrew word occurs in [[@23025010|Isa. 25:10]], where it is rendered “dunghill.”

column5: A Canaanite city conquered by Joshua
column6: a chiding; a garment; his measure
column7: Strife, a Canaanitish city in the north of Palestine ([[@6011001|Josh. 11:1]]; [[@6012019|Josh 12:19]]), whose king was slain by Joshua; perhaps the ruin Madin, near Hattin, some 5 miles west of Tiberias.

column5: A place on the Sea of Galilee; home of Mary Magdalene
column7: A place on the west of the Sea of Galilee, mentioned only in [[@41008010|Mark 8:10]]. In the parallel passage it is said that Christ came “into the borders of Magdala” ([[@40015039|Matt. 15:39]]). It is plain, then, that Dalmanutha was near Magdala, which was probably the Greek name of one of the many Migdols (i.e., watch-towers) on the western side of the lake of Gennesaret.

column5: A place whose people returned from Babylonian exile
column7: Magbish, a place whose people are listed among those who returned to Judah from Babylonian exile (<ref="Ezra 2:30">Ezra 2:30</ref>).

column5: Edomite chief descended from Esau
column6: declaring God; chosen fruit of God
column7: Magdiel was an Edomite chief, a descendant of Esau, the son of Isaac.

column5: Son of Japheth; progenitor of a people group
column7: Region of Gog, the second of the “sons” of Japheth ([[@1010002|Gen. 10:2]]; [[@13001005|1 Chr. 1:5]]). In Ezekiel (38:2; 39:6) it is the name of a nation, probably some Scythian or Tartar tribe descended from Japheth. They are described as skilled horsemen, and expert in the use of the bow. The Latin father Jerome says that this word denotes “Scythian nations, fierce and innumerable, who live beyond the Caucasus and the Lake Maeotis, and near the Caspian Sea, and spread out even onward to India.”

column5: A nation that will attack Israel in the future
column7: Region of Gog, the second of the “sons” of Japheth ([[@1010002|Gen. 10:2]]; [[@13001005|1 Chr. 1:5]]). In Ezekiel (38:2; 39:6) it is the name of a nation, probably some Scythian or Tartar tribe descended from Japheth. They are described as skilled horsemen, and expert in the use of the bow. The Latin father Jerome says that this word denotes “Scythian nations, fierce and innumerable, who live beyond the Caucasus and the Lake Maeotis, and near the Caspian Sea, and spread out even onward to India.”

column5: One who sealed the covenant during Nehemiah's time
column7: Magpiash was among those who sealed the covenant during the time of Nehemiah.

column5: Descendant of Seth; ancestor of Noah
column7: The son of Cainan, of the line of Seth ([[@1005012-1005017|Gen. 5:12-17]]); called Maleleel ([[@42003037|Luke 3:37]]).

column5: Descendant of Perez; lived in Jerusalem after the exile
column7: Mahalalel, a descendant of Perez, lived in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile.

column5: Esau's wife, daughter of Ishmael
column6: perfumed; confusion of death; in desolation
column7: The daughter of Ishmael, and third wife of Esau ([[@1028009|Gen. 28:9]]); called also Bashemath ([[@1036003|Gen. 36:3]]).

column5: Rehoboam's wife, granddaughter of David
column7: The daughter of Jerimoth, who was one of David’s sons.

column5: A place east of the Jordan; David's refuge
column7: Two camps, a place near the Jabbok, beyond Jordan, where Jacob was met by the “angels of God,” and where he divided his retinue into “two hosts” on his return from Padan-aram ([[@1032002|Gen. 32:2]]). This name was afterwards given to the town which was built at that place. It was the southern boundary of Bashan ([[@6013026|Josh. 13:26]], [[@6013030|Josh. 13:30]]), and became a city of the Levites (21:38). Here Saul’s son Ishbosheth reigned ([[@10002008|2 Sam. 2:8]], [[@10002012|2 Sam. 2:12]]), while David reigned at Hebron.

column5: A place between Zorah and Eshtaol; Samson's birthplace
column7: [[@7018012|Judg. 18:12]] = “camp of Dan” 13:25 (R.V., “Mahaneh-dan”), a place behind (i.e., west of) Kirjath-jearim, where the six hundred Danites from Zorah and Eshtaol encamped on their way to capture the city of Laish, which they rebuilt and called “Dan, after the name of their father” (18:11-31).

column5: One of David's mighty warriors from Netophah
column6: hasting; a hill; from a hill
column7: Maharai the Netophathite was one of David's mighty warriors and served as a commander in his army.

column5: Levite who helped purify the temple under Hezekiah
column7: Another Kohathite Levite, of the time of Hezekiah ([[@14029012|2 Chr. 29:12]]).

column5: Levite who assisted in distributing tithes during Hezekiah's reign.
column7: Mahath, a Levite, helped distribute tithes in Hezekiah's time.

column5: Some of David's mighty men, possibly from Mahavim.
column7: The Mahavites were represented among David's mighty men.

column6: seeing a sign; seeing a letter
column7: Visions, a Kohathite Levite, chief of the twenty-third course of musicians ([[@13025004|1 Chr. 25:4]], [[@13025030|1 Chr. 25:30]]).

column5: Symbolic name given to Isaiah's son, meaning "swift is booty, speedy is prey."
column6: making speed to the spoil; he hastens to the prey
column7: Plunder speedeth; spoil hasteth, ([[@23008001-23008003|Isa. 8:1-3]]; comp. [[@36001014|Zeph. 1:14]]), a name Isaiah was commanded first to write in large characters on a tablet, and afterwards to give as a symbolical name to a son that was to be born to him ([[@23008001|Isa. 8:1]], [[@23008003|Isa. 8:3]]), as denoting the sudden attack on Damascus and Syria by the Assyrian army.

column5: Daughter of Zelophehad, who received an inheritance among her brothers.
column7: Disease, one of the five daughters of Zelophehad ([[@4027001-4027011|Num. 27:1-11]]) who had their father’s inheritance, the law of inheritance having been altered in their favour.

column7: Disease, one of the five daughters of Zelophehad ([[@4027001-4027011|Num. 27:1-11]]) who had their father’s inheritance, the law of inheritance having been altered in their favour.

column7: Mahli, a son of Merari and grandson of Levi, was an ancestor of the Mahlites.

column7: Mahli, a son of Mushi and grandson of Merari, was a Levite during the time of David.

column7: Sickly, the elder of Elimelech the Bethlehemite’s two sons by Naomi.

column7: Dance, the father of four sons ([[@11004031|1 Kings 4:31]]) who were inferior in wisdom only to Solomon.

column7: The father of the false prophet Zedekiah ([[@24029021|Jer. 29:21]]).

column7: Makaz, a place in one of the twelve administrative districts established by Solomon (<ref="1Ki.4.9">1Ki.4.9</ref>).

column5: A place where the Israelites camped in the wilderness
column7: Assemblies, a station of the Israelites in the desert ([[@4033025|Num. 33:25]], [[@4033026|Num 33:26]]).

column5: A Canaanite city conquered by Joshua
column7: Herdsman’s place, one of the royal cities of the Canaanites ([[@6012016|Josh. 12:16]]), near which was a cave where the five kings who had confederated against Israel sought refuge (10:10-29). They were put to death by Joshua, who afterwards suspended their bodies upon five trees. It has been identified with the modern village called Sumeil, standing on a low hill about 7 miles to the north-west of Eleutheropolis (Beit Jibrin), where are ancient remains and a great cave.

column5: Prophet who wrote the book bearing his name.
column7: Messenger or angel, the last of the minor prophets, and the writer of the last book of the Old Testament canon ([[@39004004|Mal. 4:4]], [[@39004005|Mal 4:5]], [[@39004006|Mal 4:6]]). Nothing is known of him beyond what is contained in his book of prophecies. Some have supposed that the name is simply a title descriptive of his character as a messenger of Jehovah, and not a proper name. There is reason, however, to conclude that Malachi was the ordinary name of the prophet.

column5: Son of Shaharaim, a Benjamite.
column7: ([[@10012030|2 Sam. 12:30]], Heb., R.V., “their king;” [[@24049001|Jer. 49:1]], [[@24049003|Jer. 49:3]], R.V.; [[@36001005|Zeph. 1:5]]), the national idol of the Ammonites. When Rabbah was taken by David, the crown of this idol was among the spoils. The weight is said to have been “a talent of gold” (above 100 lbs.). The expression probably denotes its value rather than its weight.

column5: Son of King Saul, killed in battle against the Philistines.
column7: King of help, one of the four sons of Saul ([[@13008033|1 Chr. 8:33]]).

column7: Malchiel, son of Beriah and grandson of Asher, was the ancestor of the Malchielites.

column6: Malchijah, the Lord my king, or my counselor
column7: Malchijah, a son of Ethni, was a Gershonite Levite.

column6: Malchijah, the Lord my king, or my counselor
column7: A priest, the father of Pashur ([[@13009012|1 Chr. 9:12]]; [[@24038001|Jer. 38:1]]).

column7: Malchijah was the head of the fifth priestly division during David's reign.

column7: Malchijah, a descendant of Harim, divorced his foreign wife during Ezra's reforms.

column5: Son of Harim, helped repair the wall of Jerusalem.
column7: Malchijah, son of Harim, repaired a section of Jerusalem's wall.

column5: Son of Rechab, repaired the Dung Gate in Jerusalem.
column6: Malchijah, the Lord my king, or my counselor
column7: Malchijah, son of Rechab, repaired the Dung Gate during Nehemiah's wall restoration.

column5: Goldsmith who helped repair the wall of Jerusalem.
column6: Malchijah, the Lord my king, or my counselor
column7: Malchijah, a goldsmith, repaired a section of Jerusalem's wall near the Levites.

column5: Priest who stood beside Ezra during the reading of the Law.
column6: Malchijah, the Lord my king, or my counselor
column7: A priest who stood by Ezra when he “read in the book of the law of God” ([[@16008004|Neh. 8:4]]).

column7: Malchijah, a priest, was among those who sealed the covenant during Nehemiah's time.

column7: Reigning, the personal servant or slave of the high priest Caiaphas. He is mentioned only by John. Peter cut off his right ear in the garden of Gethsemane ([[@43018010|John 18:10]]). But our Lord cured it with a touch ([[@40026051|Matt. 26:51]]; [[@41014047|Mark 14:47]]; [[@42022051|Luke 22:51]]).

column5: Son of Heman, a musician in David's court.
column7: My fulness, a Kohathite Levite, one of the sons of Heman the Levite ([[@13025004|1 Chr. 25:4]]), and chief of the nineteenth division of the temple musicians (26).

column5: Son of Hashabiah, a Merarite Levite.
column7: A Levite of the family of Merari ([[@13006044|1 Chr. 6:44]]).

column7: Malluch, a descendant of Harim, divorced his foreign wife during Ezra's reforms.

column5: One who sealed the covenant with Nehemiah.
column7: Malluch was among those who sealed the covenant during Nehemiah's time.

column5: An island where Paul was shipwrecked
column7: ([[@44027028|Acts 27:28]]), an island in the Mediterranean, the modern Malta. Here the ship in which Paul was being conveyed a prisoner to Rome was wrecked. The bay in which it was wrecked now bears the name of “St. Paul’s Bay”, “a certain creek with a shore.” It is about 2 miles deep and 1 broad, and the whole physical condition of the scene answers the description of the shipwreck given in Acts 28.

A Chaldee or Syriac word meaning “wealth” or “riches” ([[@42016009-42016011|Luke 16:9-11]]); also, by personification, the god of riches ([[@40006024|Matt. 6:24]]; [[@42016009-42016011|Luke 16:9-11]]).

column7: An Amoritish chief in alliance with Abraham ([[@1014013|Gen. 14:13]], [[@1014024|Gen. 14:24]]).

column5: Amorite, ally of Abraham.
column7: An Amoritish chief in alliance with Abraham ([[@1014013|Gen. 14:13]], [[@1014024|Gen. 14:24]]).

column7: Consoler, a Christian teacher at Antioch.

column7: Manahath was a son of Shobal, a Horite.

column7: Manahath (Nohah), a place where some Benjamites lived after returning from the Babylonian exile (<ref="1Ch.8.6">1Ch.8.6</ref>).

column5: Firstborn son of Joseph, blessed by Jacob.
column7: The elder of the two sons of Joseph. He and his brother Ephraim were afterwards adopted by Jacob as his own sons (48:1). There is an account of his marriage to a Syrian ([[@13007014|1 Chr. 7:14]]); and the only thing afterwards recorded of him is, that his grandchildren were “brought up upon Joseph’s knees” ([[@1050023|Gen. 50:23]]; R.V., “born upon Joseph’s knees”) i.e., were from their birth adopted by Joseph as his own children. The tribe of Manasseh was associated with that of Ephraim and Benjamin during the wanderings in the wilderness.

column5: King of Judah, son of Hezekiah.
column7: The only son and successor of Hezekiah on the throne of Judah. He was twelve years old when he began to reign ([[@12021001|2 Kings 21:1]]), and he reigned fifty-five years (B.C. 698-643). Though he reigned so long, yet comparatively little is known of this king. His reign was a continuation of that of Ahaz, both in religion and national polity.

column5: Descendant of Pahath-moab, who divorced his foreign wife.
column7: Manasseh, a descendant of Pahath-moab, divorced his foreign wife during Ezra's reforms.

column5: Descendant of Hashum, who divorced his foreign wife.
column7: Manasseh, a descendant of Hashum, divorced his foreign wife during Ezra's reforms.

Heb. man-hu, “What is that?” the name given by the Israelites to the food miraculously supplied to them during their wanderings in the wilderness ([[@2016015-2016035|Ex. 16:15-35]]). The name is commonly taken as derived from man , an expression of surprise, “What is it?” but more probably it is derived from manan , meaning “to allot,” and hence denoting an “allotment” or a “gift.” This “gift” from God is described as “a small round thing,” like the “hoar-frost on the ground,” and “like coriander seed,” “of the colour of bdellium,” and in taste “like wafers made with honey.”

column5: Father of Samson, from the tribe of Dan.
column7: Rest, a Danite, the father of Samson ([[@7013001-7013022|Judg. 13:1-22]], and 14:2-4).

Heb. ‘addereth, a large over-garment. This word is used of Elijah’s mantle ([[@11019013|1 Kings 19:13]], [[@11019019|1 Kings 19:19]]; [[@12002008|2 Kings 2:8]], [[@12002013|2 Kings 2:13]], etc.), which was probably a sheepskin. It appears to have been his only garment, a strip of skin or leather binding it to his loins. ’Addereth twice occurs with the epithet “hairy” ([[@1025025|Gen. 25:25]]; [[@38013004|Zech. 13:4]], R.V.).

column5: Father of Achish, king of Gath.
column7: Compressed, the father of Achish, king of Gath ([[@9027002|1 Sam. 27:2]]).
