column7: Habitation, a town in the tribe of Judah, about 7 miles south of Hebron, which gave its name to the wilderness, the district round the conical hill on which the town stood. Here David hid from Saul, and here Nabal had his possessions and his home ([[@9023024|1 Sam. 23:24]], [[@9023025|1 Sam. 23:25]]; [[@9025002|1 Sam. 25:2]]). “Only some small foundations of hewn stone, a square enclosure, and several cisterns are now to be seen at Maon. Are they the remains of Nabal’s great establishment?”

column5: A place with bitter water on the Exodus route
column7: Bitterness, a fountain at the sixth station of the Israelites ([[@2015023|Ex. 15:23]], [[@2015024|Ex. 15:24]]; [[@4033008|Num. 33:8]]) whose waters were so bitter that they could not drink them.

column5: A place on the border of Zebulun
column6: sleep; a sacrifice of myrrh; ascension
column7: Trembling, a place on the southern boundary of Zebulun ([[@6019011|Josh. 19:11]]).

column5: A town in Judah; fortified by Rehoboam
column7: Possession, a city in the plain of Judah ([[@43015044|John. 15:44]]). Here Asa defeated Zerah the Ethiopian ([[@14014009|2 Chr. 14:9]], [[@14014010|2 Chr. 14:10]]).

column5: Son of Mesha, re-founder of Hebron.
column7: Possession, a city in the plain of Judah ([[@43015044|John. 15:44]]). Here Asa defeated Zerah the Ethiopian ([[@14014009|2 Chr. 14:9]], [[@14014010|2 Chr. 14:10]]).

column5: Son or town of Laadah in Judah.
column7: Possession, a city in the plain of Judah ([[@43015044|John. 15:44]]). Here Asa defeated Zerah the Ethiopian ([[@14014009|2 Chr. 14:9]], [[@14014010|2 Chr. 14:10]]).

column5: Cousin of Barnabas, companion of Paul, author of Gospel.
column7: The evangelist; “John whose surname was Mark” ([[@44012012|Acts 12:12]], [[@44012025|Acts 12:25]]). Mark (Marcus, [[@51004010|Col. 4:10]], etc.) was his Roman name, which gradually came to supersede his Jewish name John. He is called John in [[@44013005|Acts 13:5]], [[@44013013|Acts 13:13]], and Mark in 15:39, [[@55004011|2 Tim. 4:11]], etc. He was the son of Mary, a woman apparently of some means and influence, and was probably born in Jerusalem, where his mother resided ([[@44012012|Acts 12:12]]). Of his father we know nothing.

column5: A town in Judah
column7: Bitterness; i.e., “perfect grief”, a place not far from Jerusalem; mentioned in connection with the invasion of the Assyrian army ([[@33001012|Micah 1:12]]).

column5: One of the seven princes of Persia and Media.
column7: Marsena was one of the seven princes of Persia and Media who advised King Ahasuerus.

column5: Sister of Mary and Lazarus, hosted Jesus.
column7: Bitterness, the sister of Lazarus and Mary, and probably the eldest of the family, who all resided at Bethany ([[@42010038|Luke 10:38]], [[@42010040|Luke 10:40]], [[@42010041|Luke 10:41]]; [[@43011001-43011039|John 11:1-39]]).

column5: Mother of Jesus; wife of Joseph.
column7: The wife of Joseph, the mother of Jesus, called the “Virgin Mary,” though never so designated in Scripture ([[@40002011|Matt. 2:11]]; [[@44001014|Acts 1:14]]). Little is known of her personal history. Her genealogy is given in Luke 3. She was of the tribe of Judah and the lineage of David ([[@19132011|Ps. 132:11]]; [[@42001032|Luke 1:32]]).

column5: Sister of Martha and Lazarus, sat at Jesus' feet.
column7: Mary the sister of Lazarus is brought to our notice in connection with the visits of our Lord to Bethany. She is contrasted with her sister Martha, who was “cumbered about many things” while Jesus was their guest, while Mary had chosen “the good part.” Her character also appears in connection with the death of her brother ([[@43011020|John 11:20]], [[@43011031|John 11:31]], [[@43011033|John 11:33]]).

column5: Mother of John Mark; hosted prayer meeting.
column7: Mary the mother of John Mark was one of the earliest of our Lord’s disciples. She was the sister of Barnabas ([[@51004010|Col. 4:10]]), and joined with him in disposing of their land and giving the proceeds of the sale into the treasury of the Church ([[@44004037|Acts 4:37]]; [[@44012012|Acts 12:12]]).

column5: A woman who worked hard for the church in Rome.
column7: A Christian at Rome who treated Paul with special kindness ([[@45016006|Rom. 16:6]]).

column5: Follower of Jesus, first witness of His resurrection.
column7: Mary Magdalene, i.e., Mary of Magdala, a town on the western shore of the Lake of Tiberias. She is for the first time noticed in [[@42008003|Luke 8:3]] as one of the women who “ministered to Christ of their substance.” Their motive was that of gratitude for deliverances he had wrought for them. Out of Mary were cast seven demons.

column5: Son of Aram, grandson of Shem.
column7: (= Meshech [[@13001017|1 Chr. 1:17]]), one of the four sons of Aram, and the name of a tribe descended from him ([[@1010023|Gen. 10:23]]) inhabiting some part probably of Mesopotamia.

column5: The royal city of Samlah, an Edomite king
column7: Vineyard of noble vines, a place in Idumea, the native place of Samlah, one of the Edomitish kings ([[@1036036|Gen. 36:36]]; [[@13001047|1 Chr. 1:47]]).

column5: Son of Ishmael, grandson of Abraham.
column7: A lifting up, gift, one of the sons of Ishmael, the founder of an Arabian tribe ([[@1025014|Gen. 25:14]]); a nomad tribe inhabiting the Arabian desert toward Babylonia.

column5: A place where the Israelites tested God
column7: Trial, temptation, a name given to the place where the Israelites, by their murmuring for want of water, provoked Jehovah to anger against them.

column5: Mother of Mehetabel, wife of Hadar, king of Edom.
column7: Matred was the mother of Mehetabel, who was the wife of Hadar, king of Edom.

column5: Saul's ancestral clan from the tribe of Benjamin.
column7: The Matrite (or Matri) clan was Saul's ancestral clan from the tribe of Benjamin.

column5: Priest of Baal, killed during Jehoiada's reforms.
column7: A priest of Baal, slain before his altar during the reformation under Jehoiada ([[@12011018|2 Kings 11:18]]).

column5: Father of Shephatiah, an opponent of Jeremiah.
column7: Mattan was the father of Shephatiah, one of the officials who opposed the prophet Jeremiah.

column5: A place where the Israelites camped during their wilderness journey
column7: A gift, a station of the Israelites ([[@4021018|Num. 21:18]], [[@4021019|Num. 21:19]]) between the desert and the borders of Moab, in the Wady Waleh.

column5: Levite singer and gatekeeper during the time of Nehemiah.
column6: gift, or hope, of the Lord
column7: Mattaniah, a Levite singer and gatekeeper, served during the time of Nehemiah.

column5: Son of Heman, a musician in David's court.
column6: gift, or hope, of the Lord
column7: A Levite, son of Heman, the chief of the ninth class of temple singers ([[@13025004|1 Chr. 25:4]], [[@13025016|1 Chr. 25:16]]).

column5: Levite, grandfather of Jahaziel, who prophesied during Jehoshaphat's reign.
column6: gift, or hope, of the Lord
column7: Mattaniah, a Levite, was the grandfather of Jahaziel, who prophesied during King Jehoshaphat's reign.

column5: Levite who helped cleanse the temple during Hezekiah's reign.
column6: gift, or hope, of the Lord
column7: A Levite who assisted in purifying the temple at the reformation under Hezekiah ([[@14029013|2 Chr. 29:13]]).

column5: Descendant of Zattu, who divorced his foreign wife.
column6: gift, or hope, of the Lord
column7: Mattaniah, a descendant of Zattu, divorced his foreign wife during Ezra's reforms.

column5: Descendant of Elam, who divorced his foreign wife.
column6: gift, or hope, of the Lord
column7: Mattaniah, a descendant of Elam, divorced his foreign wife during Ezra's reforms.

column5: Descendant of Pahath-moab, who divorced his foreign wife.
column6: gift, or hope, of the Lord
column7: Mattaniah, a descendant of Pahath-moab, divorced his foreign wife during Ezra's reforms.

column5: Descendant of Bani, who divorced his foreign wife.
column6: gift, or hope, of the Lord
column7: Mattaniah, a descendant of Bani, divorced his foreign wife during Ezra's reforms.

column5: Levite singer, descendant of Asaph, during Nehemiah's time.
column6: gift, or hope, of the Lord
column7: Mattaniah, a Levite singer and descendant of Asaph, served during Nehemiah's time.

column5: Levite appointed as a treasurer during Nehemiah's time.
column6: gift, or hope, of the Lord
column7: Mattaniah, a Levite, was appointed as a treasurer during Nehemiah's time.

column5: An ancestor of Jesus Christ.
column7: Mattatha was an ancestor of Jesus Christ, mentioned in His genealogy.

column5: An ancestor of Jesus Christ.
column7: The son of Amos, in the genealogy of our Lord ([[@42003025|Luke 3:25]]).

column5: An ancestor of Jesus Christ.
column7: The son of Semei, in the same genealogy ([[@42003026|Luke 3:26]]).

column5: Descendant of Hashum, who divorced his foreign wife.
column7: Mattattah, a descendant of Hashum, divorced his foreign wife during Ezra's reforms.

column5: Descendant of Hashum, who divorced his foreign wife.
column7: Mattenai, a descendant of Hashum, divorced his foreign wife during Ezra's reforms.

column5: Descendant of Bani, who divorced his foreign wife.
column7: Mattenai, a descendant of Bani, divorced his foreign wife during Ezra's reforms.

column5: Priest during the time of Joiakim.
column7: Mattenai was a priest who served during the time of Joiakim.

column5: An ancestor of Jesus Christ.
column7: The son of Levi, and father of Heli ([[@42003024|Luke 3:24]]).

column5: An ancestor of Jesus Christ.
column7: Matthat was an ancestor of Jesus Christ, mentioned in His genealogy.

column5: Apostle, tax collector, author of the Gospel of Matthew.
column7: Gift of God, a common Jewish name after the Exile. He was the son of Alphaeus, and was a publican or tax-gatherer at Capernaum. On one occasion Jesus, coming up from the side of the lake, passed the custom-house where Matthew was seated, and said to him, “Follow me.” Matthew arose and followed him, and became his disciple ([[@40009009|Matt. 9:9]]). Formerly the name by which he was known was Levi ([[@41002014|Mark 2:14]]; [[@42005027|Luke 5:27]]); he now changed it, possibly in grateful memory of his call, to Matthew.

column5: Apostle chosen to replace Judas Iscariot.
column7: Matthias was chosen by lot to replace Judas Iscariot as one of the twelve apostles.

column5: Levite in charge of baking bread in the temple.
column7: The eldest son of Shallum, of the family of Korah ([[@13009031|1 Chr. 9:31]]).

column5: Levite musician during the time of David.
column7: Mattithiah, a Levite, served as a musician during the time of King David.

column5: Descendant of Nebo, who divorced his foreign wife.
column7: Mattithiah, a descendant of Nebo, divorced his foreign wife during Ezra's reforms.

column5: Levite who assisted Ezra in reading the Law.
column7: One who stood by Ezra while reading the law ([[@16008004|Neh. 8:4]]).

column5: A place in the territory of Dan
column7: Waters of yellowness, or clear waters, a river in the tribe of Dan ([[@6019046|Josh. 19:46]]).

(Heb. minhah), originally a gift of any kind. This Hebrew word came latterly to denote an “unbloody” sacrifice, as opposed to a “bloody” sacrifice. A “drink-offering” generally accompanied it. The law regarding it is given in Lev. 2, and 6:14-23. It was a recognition of the sovereignty of God and of his bounty in giving all earthly blessings ([[@13029010-13029014|1 Chr. 29:10-14]]; [[@5026005-5026011|Deut. 26:5-11]]).

column5: A place near Sidon
column7: A cave, a place in the northern boundary of Palestine ([[@6013004|Josh. 13:4]]).

column5: Clan or inhabitants of an unknown place called Mecherah.
column7: The Mecherathites were a clan or inhabitants of an unknown place called Mecherah.

column5: A town inhabited by the people of Judah after the exile
column6: a foot of a pillar; provision
column7: A base or foundation, a town in the south of Judah ([[@16011028|Neh. 11:28]]), near Ziklag.

column5: Eldad's companion who prophesied in the Israelite camp.
column6: he that measures; water of love
column7: Love, one of the elders nominated to assist Moses in the government of the people.

column5: Son of Abraham and Keturah.
column7: Contention, the third son of Abraham by Keturah ([[@1025002|Gen. 25:2]]).

column5: A Moabite city captured by the Israelites
column6: waters of grief; waters springing up
column7: Waters of quiet, an ancient Moabite town ([[@4021030|Num. 21:30]]). It was assigned to the tribe of Reuben ([[@6013016|Josh. 13:16]]). Here was fought the great battle in which Joab defeated the Ammonites and their allies ([[@13019007-13019015|1 Chr. 19:7-15]]; comp. [[@10010006-10010014|2 Sam. 10:6-14]]). In the time of Isaiah (15:2) the Moabites regained possession of it from the Ammonites.

column5: An ancient kingdom; part of the Persian Empire
column7: Heb. Madai, which is rendered in the Authorized Version (1) “Madai,” [[@1010002|Gen. 10:2]]; (2) “Medes,” [[@12017006|2 Kings 17:6]]; [[@12018011|2 Kings 18:11]]; (3) “Media,” [[@17001003|Esther 1:3]]; [[@17010002|Esther 10:2]]; [[@23021002|Isa. 21:2]]; [[@27008020|Dan. 8:20]]; (4) “Mede,” only in [[@27011001|Dan. 11:1]]. We first hear of this people in the Assyrian cuneiform records, under the name of Amada, about B.C. 840. They appear to have been a branch of the Aryans, who came from the east bank of the Indus, and were probably the predominant race for a while in the Mesopotamian valley.

column5: A strategic city in the Jezreel Valley
column6: his precious fruit; declaring a message
column7: Place of troops, originally one of the royal cities of the Canaanites ([[@6012021|Josh. 12:21]]), belonged to the tribe of Manasseh ([[@7001027|Judg. 1:27]]), but does not seem to have been fully occupied by the Israelites till the time of Solomon ([[@11004012|1 Kings 4:12]]; [[@11009015|1 Kings 9:15]]). The valley or plain of Megiddo was part of the plain of Esdraelon, the great battle-field of Palestine. It was here Barak gained a notable victory over Jabin, the king of Hazor, whose general, Sisera, led on the hostile army.

column5: Wife of Hadar, king of Edom.
column7: Wife of Hadad, one of the kings of Edom ([[@1036039|Gen. 36:39]]).

column5: Ancestor of Shemaiah, who opposed Nehemiah.
column7: Wife of Hadad, one of the kings of Edom ([[@1036039|Gen. 36:39]]).

column5: Ancestor of temple servants who returned from Babylonian exile.
column7: Mehida was an ancestor of temple servants (Nethinim) who returned to Jerusalem from Babylonian captivity.

column5: Son of Chelub.
column7: Mehir was the son of Chelub.

column5: People from Abel-meholah, including Adriel and Barzillai.
column7: The Meholathites were people from Abel-meholah, including Adriel, who married Saul's daughter Merab, and Barzillai, whose son married Saul's daughter Michal.

column5: One of King Ahasuerus' seven eunuchs.
column7: Faithful, one of the eunchs whom Ahasuerus (Xerxes) commanded to bring in Vashti ([[@17001010|Esther 1:10]]).

column5: Gibeonite who helped repair Jerusalem's wall under Nehemiah.
column7: Melatiah the Gibeonite helped repair a section of Jerusalem's wall during Nehemiah's rebuilding project.

column5: An ancestor of Jesus in Luke's genealogy.
column7: Melchi, mentioned in Luke's genealogy of Jesus.

column5: An ancestor of Jesus in Luke's genealogy.
column7: The son of Addi, and father of Neri ([[@42003028|Luke 3:28]]).

column5: King of Salem and priest of God Most High.
column7: King of righteousness, the king of Salem (q.v.). All we know of him is recorded in [[@1014018-1014020|Gen. 14:18-20]]. He is subsequently mentioned only once in the Old Testament, in [[@19110004|Ps. 110:4]]. The typical significance of his history is set forth in detail in the Epistle to the Hebrews, ch. 7.

column5: An ancestor of Jesus in Luke's genealogy.
column7: Fulness, the son of Menan and father of Eliakim, in the genealogy of our Lord ([[@42003031|Luke 3:31]]).

column5: A descendant of King Saul.
column7: King, the second of Micah’s four sons ([[@13008035|1 Chr. 8:35]]), and thus grandson of Mephibosheth.

column5: Babylonian official in charge of Daniel and his friends.
column6: circumcision of a narrow place, or of a bond
column7: Probably a Persian word meaning master of wine, i.e., chief butler; the title of an officer at the Babylonian court ([[@27001011|Dan. 1:11]], [[@27001016|Dan 1:16]]) who had charge of the diet of the Hebrew youths.

column5: An important city in ancient Egypt
column7: Only in [[@28009006|Hos. 9:6]], Hebrew Moph. In [[@23019013|Isa. 19:13]]; [[@24002016|Jer. 2:16]]; [[@24046014|Jer 46:14]], [[@24046019|Jer 46:19]]; [[@26030013|Ezek. 30:13]], [[@26030016|Ezek. 30:16]], it is mentioned under the name Noph. It was the capital of Lower, i.e., of Northern Egypt. From certain remains found half buried in the sand, the site of this ancient city has been discovered near the modern village of Minyet Rahinch, or Mitraheny, about 16 miles above the ancient head of the Delta, and 9 miles south of Cairo, on the west bank of the Nile.

column5: One of the seven princes of Persia and Media.
column7: Dignified, one of the royal counsellors at the court of Ahasuerus, by whose suggestion Vashti was divorced ([[@17001014|Esther 1:14]], [[@17001016|Esther 1:16]], [[@17001021|Esther 1:21]]).

column5: King of Israel who reigned for ten years.
column6: comforter; who conducts them; preparation of heat
column7: Conforting, the son of Gadi, and successor of Shallum, king of Israel, whom he slew. After a reign of about ten years (B.C. 771-760) he died, leaving the throne to his son Pekahiah. His reign was one of cruelty and oppression ([[@12015014-12015022|2 Kings 15:14-22]]).

column5: An ancestor of Jesus in Luke's genealogy.
column7: Menna, mentioned in Luke's genealogy of Jesus.

column5: A clan descended from Caleb.
column7: Menuhoth, a clan descended from Caleb, mentioned in the genealogy of Judah.

column5: Son of Othniel and father of Ophrah.
column7: Meonothai, son of Othniel, mentioned in the genealogy of Judah.

column5: A Levitical city in Reuben, later Moabite
column7: Splendour, a Levitical city ([[@6021037|Josh. 21:37]]) of the tribe of Reuben (13:18).

column5: Son of Jonathan and grandson of King Saul.
column6: out of my mouth proceeds reproach
column7: The son of Jonathan, and grandson of Saul ([[@10004004|2 Sam. 4:4]]). He was but five years old when his father and grandfather fell on Mount Gilboa. The child’s nurse hearing of this calamity, fled with him from Gibeah, the royal residence, and stumbling in her haste, the child was thrown to the ground and maimed in both his feet, and ever after was unable to walk (19:26).

column5: Son of Saul and Rizpah, given to the Gibeonites.
column6: out of my mouth proceeds reproach
column7: The name of Saul’s son by the concubine Rizpah (q.v.), the daughter of Aiah.

column5: Eldest daughter of King Saul.
column7: Increase, the eldest of Saul’s two daughters ([[@9014049|1 Sam. 14:49]]). She was betrothed to David after his victory over Goliath, but does not seem to have entered heartily into this arrangement (18:2, 17, 19). She was at length, however, married to Adriel of Abel-Meholah, a town in the Jordan valley, about 10 miles south of Bethshean, with whom the house of Saul maintained alliance.

column5: A priest during the high priesthood of Joiakim.
column7: Resistance, a chief priest, a contemporary of the high priest Joiakim ([[@16012012|Neh. 12:12]]).

column5: A priest in the lineage of Eleazar.
column7: Father of Amariah, a high priest of the line of Eleazar ([[@13006006|1 Chr. 6:6]], [[@13006007|1 Chr. 6:7]], [[@13006052|1 Chr. 6:52]]).

column5: The third son of Levi and founder of the Merarites.
column7: Sad; bitter, the youngest son of Levi, born before the descent of Jacob into Egypt, and one of the seventy who accompanied him thither ([[@1046011|Gen. 46:11]]; [[@2006016|Ex. 6:16]]). He became the head of one of the great divisions of the Levites ([[@2006019|Ex. 6:19]]).

(Heb. kapporeth, a “covering;” LXX. and N.T., hilasterion; Vulg., propitiatorium), the covering or lid of the ark of the covenant (q.v.). It was of acacia wood, overlaid with gold, or perhaps rather a plate of solid gold, 2 1/2 cubits long and 1 1/2 broad ([[@2025017|Ex. 25:17]]; [[@2030006|Ex 30:6]]; [[@2031007|Ex 31:7]]). It is compared to the throne of grace ([[@58009005|Heb. 9:5]]; [[@49002006|Eph. 2:6]]). The holy of holies is called the “place of the mercy-seat” ([[@13028011|1 Chr. 28:11]]: [[@3016002|Lev. 16:2]]).

column5: Son of Ezrah from the tribe of Judah.
column7: Rebellion, one of the sons of Ezra, of the tribe of Judah ([[@13004017|1 Chr. 4:17]]).

column5: A priest who returned from the Babylonian exile.
column7: Exaltations, heights, a priest who returned from Babylon with Zerubbabel ([[@16012003|Neh. 12:3]]), to whom were sent the sacred vessels ([[@15008033|Ezra 8:33]]) belonging to the temple.

column5: An Israelite who married a foreign woman.
column7: Exaltations, heights, a priest who returned from Babylon with Zerubbabel ([[@16012003|Neh. 12:3]]), to whom were sent the sacred vessels ([[@15008033|Ezra 8:33]]) belonging to the temple.

column5: One of the seven princes of Persia and Media.
column7: Meres, one of the seven princes of Persia and Media who advised King Ahasuerus.

column5: A place where the Israelites quarreled with Moses
column7: Another fountain having a similar origin in the desert of Zin, near to Kadesh ([[@4027014|Num. 27:14]]). The two places are mentioned together in [[@5033008|Deut. 33:8]]. Some think the one place is called by the two names ([[@19081007|Ps. 81:7]]). In smiting the rock at this place Moses showed the same impatience as the people ([[@4020010-4020012|Num. 20:10-12]]).

column5: A place where Moses disobeyed God
column7: Another fountain having a similar origin in the desert of Zin, near to Kadesh ([[@4027014|Num. 27:14]]). The two places are mentioned together in [[@5033008|Deut. 33:8]]. Some think the one place is called by the two names ([[@19081007|Ps. 81:7]]). In smiting the rock at this place Moses showed the same impatience as the people ([[@4020010-4020012|Num. 20:10-12]]).

column5: King of Babylon who sent envoys to Hezekiah.
column7: Merodach has given a son, ([[@23039001|Isa. 39:1]]), “the hereditary chief of the Chaldeans, a small tribe at that time settled in the marshes at the mouth of the Euphrates, but in consequence of his conquest of Babylon afterwards, they became the dominant caste in Babylonia itself.” One bearing this name sent ambassadors to Hezekiah (B.C. 721). He is also called Berodach-baladan ([[@12020012|2 Kings 20:12]]; [[@14020031|2 Chr. 20:31]]).

column5: A place where Joshua defeated Jabin's coalition
column7: Height, a lake in Northern Palestine through which the Jordan flows. It was the scene of the third and last great victory gained by Joshua over the Canaanites ([[@6011005-6011007|Josh. 11:5-7]]). It is not again mentioned in Scripture. Its modern name is Bakrat el-Huleh.

column5: A term used to describe two individuals in the Bible
column7: A name given to Jehdeiah, the herdsman of the royal asses in the time of David and Solomon ([[@13027030|1 Chr. 27:30]]), probably as one being a native of some unknown town called Meronoth.

column5: A place cursed for not helping against Sisera
column7: A plain in the north of Palestine, the inhabitants of which were severely condemned because they came not to help Barak against Sisera ([[@7005023|Judg. 5:23]]: comp. 21:8-10; [[@9011007|1 Sam. 11:7]]).

column5: A place marking the Joktanite territory
column7: A plain in that part of the boundaries of Arabia inhabited by the descendants of Joktan ([[@1010030|Gen. 10:30]]).

column5: King of Moab who rebelled against Israel.
column7: Heb. id, a king of Moab, the son of Chemosh-Gad, a man of great wealth in flocks and herds ([[@12003004|2 Kings 3:4]]). After the death of Ahab at Ramoth-Gilead, Mesha shook off the yoke of Israel; but on the ascension of Jehoram to the throne of Israel, that king sought the help of Jehoshaphat in an attempt to reduce the Moabites again to their former condition. The united armies of the two kings came unexpectedly on the army of the Moabites, and gained over them an easy victory.

column5: Son of Caleb and founder of Ziph.
column7: Heb. meysh’a, “deliverance,” the eldest son of Caleb ([[@13002042|1 Chr. 2:42]]), and brother of Jerahmeel.

column5: A descendant of Benjamin born in Moab.
column7: Mesha, a descendant of Benjamin, was born to Shaharaim in the country of Moab.

column5: Son of Japheth and grandson of Noah.
column7: Drawing out, the sixth son of Japheth ([[@1010002|Gen. 10:2]]), the founder of a tribe ([[@13001005|1 Chr. 1:5]]; [[@26027013|Ezek. 27:13]]; [[@26038002|Ezek 38:2]], [[@26038003|Ezek 38:3]]). They were in all probability the Moschi, a people inhabiting the Moschian Mountains, between the Black and the Caspian Seas. In [[@19120005|Ps. 120:5]] the name occurs as simply a synonym for foreigners or barbarians.

column5: A nation, descendant of Japheth; associated with Tubal
column7: Drawing out, the sixth son of Japheth ([[@1010002|Gen. 10:2]]), the founder of a tribe ([[@13001005|1 Chr. 1:5]]; [[@26027013|Ezek. 27:13]]; [[@26038002|Ezek 38:2]], [[@26038003|Ezek 38:3]]). They were in all probability the Moschi, a people inhabiting the Moschian Mountains, between the Black and the Caspian Seas. In [[@19120005|Ps. 120:5]] the name occurs as simply a synonym for foreigners or barbarians.

column5: Two nations mentioned together; defeated by Babylon
column7: Drawing out, the sixth son of Japheth ([[@1010002|Gen. 10:2]]), the founder of a tribe ([[@13001005|1 Chr. 1:5]]; [[@26027013|Ezek. 27:13]]; [[@26038002|Ezek 38:2]], [[@26038003|Ezek 38:3]]). They were in all probability the Moschi, a people inhabiting the Moschian Mountains, between the Black and the Caspian Seas. In [[@19120005|Ps. 120:5]] the name occurs as simply a synonym for foreigners or barbarians.

column5: A Levite gatekeeper in the time of David.
column6: peace, or perfection, of the Lord
column7: Friendship of Jehovah, a Levite of the family of the Korhites, called also Shelemiah ([[@13009021|1 Chr. 9:21]]; [[@13026001|1 Chr. 26:1]], [[@13026002|1 Chr. 26:2]], [[@13026009|1 Chr. 26:9]], [[@13026014|1 Chr. 26:14]]).

column5: One who helped repair the wall of Jerusalem.
column7: Meshezabel, son of Berechiah, helped repair the wall of Jerusalem during Nehemiah's time.

column5: A leader who sealed the covenant with Nehemiah.
column7: Meshezabel, one of the leaders who sealed the covenant with Nehemiah.

column5: A representative of the people to the Persian king.
column7: Meshezabel, from the descendants of Judah, was the people's representative to the Persian king.

column5: A priest who settled in Jerusalem after the exile.

In the Plains of Moab, opposite Jericho ([[@4022001|Num. 22:1]]; [[@4026063|Num 26:63]]; [[@6013032|Josh. 13:32]]), the children of Israel had their last encampment before they entered the land of Canaan.

column7: The plains of Moab, located east of the Jordan River and opposite Jericho, were where the Israelites camped before entering the Promised Land (<ref="Num.22.1; 26:3, 63; 31:12; 33:48-50; 35:1; 36:13; Deut 34:1, 8; Josh 13:32">Num.22.1; 26:3, 63; 31:12; 33:48-50; 35:1; 36:13; Deut 34:1, 8; Josh 13:32</ref>).

column5: Town in the Negev, allotted to Judah and Simeon
column7: Birth, a city in the south of Judah which fell to Simeon ([[@6015021-6015026|Josh. 15:21-26]]; [[@6019002|Josh 19:2]]).

column5: Son of Abisur, of the tribe of Judah.
column7: Molid was the son of Abisur and Abihail, mentioned in the genealogy of Judah.

column5: A leader who returned from Babylonian exile.
column7: The son of Jair, of the tribe of Benjamin. It has been alleged that he was carried into captivity with Jeconiah, and hence that he must have been at least one hundred and twenty-nine years old in the twelfth year of Ahasuerus (Xerxes). But the words of Esther do not necessarily lead to this conclusion. It was probably Kish of whom it is said (ver. 6) that he “had been carried away with the captivity.”

column5: Esther's cousin, a Jewish leader in the Persian court.
column7: The son of Jair, of the tribe of Benjamin. It has been alleged that he was carried into captivity with Jeconiah, and hence that he must have been at least one hundred and twenty-nine years old in the twelfth year of Ahasuerus (Xerxes). But the words of Esther do not necessarily lead to this conclusion. It was probably Kish of whom it is said (ver. 6) that he “had been carried away with the captivity.”

column5: Place near Shechem; also a hill near Gilgal
column7: A Canaanite probably who inhabited the district south of Shechem, between Mounts Ebal and Gerizim, and gave his name to the “plain” there ([[@1012006|Gen. 12:6]]).

column5: Place near Shechem; hill where Gideon camped
column7: A Canaanite probably who inhabited the district south of Shechem, between Mounts Ebal and Gerizim, and gave his name to the “plain” there ([[@1012006|Gen. 12:6]]).

column5: Hometown of the prophet Micah in Judah
column7: Possession of the wine-press, the birthplace of the prophet Micah (1:14), who is called the “Morasthite” ([[@24026018|Jer. 26:18]]).

column5: Site of Solomon's temple in Jerusalem
column7: Mount Moriah was the site where Solomon built the temple in Jerusalem.

column5: A district or valley in or near Jerusalem
column7: (Heb. homer), cement of lime and sand ([[@1011003|Gen. 11:3]]; [[@2001014|Ex. 1:14]]); also potter’s clay ([[@23041025|Isa. 41:25]]; [[@34003014|Nah. 3:14]]). Also Heb. ‘aphar, usually rendered “dust,” clay or mud used for cement in building ([[@3014042|Lev. 14:42]], [[@3014045|Lev. 14:45]]). Mortar for pulverizing ([[@20027022|Prov. 27:22]]) grain or other substances by means of a pestle instead of a mill. Mortars were used in the wilderness for pounding the manna ([[@4011008|Num. 11:8]]).

column5: A place where the Israelites camped during their wilderness wanderings
column7: A bond, one of the stations of the Israelites in the wilderness ([[@5010006|Deut. 10:6]]), at the foot of Mount Hor. (Comp. [[@4033037|Num. 33:37]], [[@4033038|Num. 33:38]]).

column5: A place where the Israelites camped during their wilderness wanderings
column7: Bonds, one of the stations in the wilderness ([[@4033030|Num. 33:30]], [[@4033031|Num. 33:31]]), probably the same as Mosera.

column5: Prophet who led Israel out of Egypt
column7: Drawn (or Egypt. mesu, “son;” hence Rameses, royal son). On the invitation of Pharaoh ([[@1045017-1045025|Gen. 45:17-25]]), Jacob and his sons went down into Egypt. This immigration took place probably about 350 years before the birth of Moses. Some centuries before Joseph, Egypt had been conquered by a pastoral Semitic race from Asia, the Hyksos, who brought into cruel subjection the native Egyptians, who were an African race.

column5: The innermost room of the tabernacle and temple
column7: The Most Holy Place was the innermost room of the tabernacle and temple, where the Ark of the Covenant was kept.

column5: Mother-in-law of Peter, healed by Jesus
column7: Peter's unnamed mother-in-law, whom Jesus healed of a fever.

column5: Son of Caleb by his concubine Ephah
column7: Moza was a son of Caleb, the renowned spy, by his concubine Ephah.

column5: Son of Zimri, descendant of King Saul
A town in the territory of Benjamin
column7: An issuing of water, a city of Benjamin ([[@6018026|Josh. 18:26]]).

column5: A son of Benjamin.
column7: Muppim, also known as Shephupham, Shephuphan, or Shuphamite, was a son of Benjamin mentioned in the genealogies of Genesis, Numbers, and 1 Chronicles.

column5: A Levite, son of Merari, and head of a clan.
column6: he that touches, that withdraws or takes away
column7: Receding, the second of the two sons of Merari ([[@2006019|Ex. 6:19]]; [[@4003020|Num. 3:20]]).

A plant of the genus sinapis, a pod-bearing, shrub-like plant, growing wild, and also cultivated in gardens. The little round seeds were an emblem of any small insignificant object. It is not mentioned in the Old Testament; and in each of the three instances of its occurrence in the New Testament ([[@40013031|Matt. 13:31]], [[@40013032|Matt 13:32]]; [[@41004031|Mark 4:31]], [[@41004032|Mark 4:32]]; [[@42013018|Luke 13:18]], [[@42013019|Luke 13:19]]) it is spoken of only with reference to the smallness of its seed. The common mustard of Palestine is the Sinapis nigra.

column5: A gate in Jerusalem mentioned in Nehemiah's time
column7: The Muster Gate, also known as the Miphkad Gate, was one of the gates of Jerusalem mentioned in Nehemiah's time.

column5: A city in Lycia where Paul's ship stopped
column7: One of the chief towns of Lycia, in Asia Minor, about 2 1/2 miles from the coast ([[@44027005|Acts 27:5]]).

First mentioned as a principal ingredient in the holy anointing oil ([[@2030023|Ex. 30:23]]). It formed part of the gifts brought by the wise men from the east, who came to worship the infant Jesus ([[@40002011|Matt. 2:11]]). It was used in embalming ([[@43019039|John 19:39]]), also as a perfume ([[@17002012|Esther 2:12]]; [[@19045008|Ps. 45:8]]; [[@20007017|Prov. 7:17]]). It was a custom of the Jews to give those who were condemned to death by crucifixion “wine mingled with myrrh” to produce insensibility.

column5: A region in northwest Asia Minor visited by Paul
column7: A province in the north-west of Asia Minor.

column5: Son of Caleb, from the tribe of Judah.
column7: Pleasantness, one of the three sons of Caleb, the son of Jephunneh ([[@13004015|1 Chr. 4:15]]).

column5: Daughter of Lamech and Zillah, sister of Tubal-cain.
column7: Naamah was the daughter of Lamech and Zillah, and the sister of Tubal-cain, mentioned in the genealogy of Cain.

column5: A town in the Judean lowlands
column7: A city in the plain of Judah ([[@6015041|Josh. 15:41]]), supposed by some to be identified with Na’aneh, some 5 miles south-east of Makkedah.

column5: An Ammonite; mother of King Rehoboam of Judah.
column7: The daughter of the king of Ammon, one of the wives of Solomon, the only one who appears to have borne him a son, viz., Rehoboam ([[@11014021|1 Kings 14:21]], [[@11014031|1 Kings 14:31]]).

column5: A son of Benjamin.
column7: Pleasantness, a Syrian, the commander of the armies of Benhadad II. in the time of Joram, king of Israel. He was afflicted with leprosy; and when the little Hebrew slave-girl that waited on his wife told her of a prophet in Samaria who could cure her master, he obtained a letter from Benhadad and proceeded with it to Joram. The king of Israel suspected in this some evil design against him, and rent his clothes. Elisha the prophet hearing of this, sent for Naaman, and the strange interview which took place is recorded in 2 Kings 5.

column5: Grandson of Benjamin, head of the Naamite clan.
column7: Pleasantness, a Syrian, the commander of the armies of Benhadad II. in the time of Joram, king of Israel. He was afflicted with leprosy; and when the little Hebrew slave-girl that waited on his wife told her of a prophet in Samaria who could cure her master, he obtained a letter from Benhadad and proceeded with it to Joram. The king of Israel suspected in this some evil design against him, and rent his clothes. Elisha the prophet hearing of this, sent for Naaman, and the strange interview which took place is recorded in 2 Kings 5.

column5: Aramean commander healed of leprosy by Elisha.
column7: Pleasantness, a Syrian, the commander of the armies of Benhadad II. in the time of Joram, king of Israel. He was afflicted with leprosy; and when the little Hebrew slave-girl that waited on his wife told her of a prophet in Samaria who could cure her master, he obtained a letter from Benhadad and proceeded with it to Joram. The king of Israel suspected in this some evil design against him, and rent his clothes. Elisha the prophet hearing of this, sent for Naaman, and the strange interview which took place is recorded in 2 Kings 5.

column5: A descendant of Benjamin, son of Ehud.
column7: Pleasantness, a Syrian, the commander of the armies of Benhadad II. in the time of Joram, king of Israel. He was afflicted with leprosy; and when the little Hebrew slave-girl that waited on his wife told her of a prophet in Samaria who could cure her master, he obtained a letter from Benhadad and proceeded with it to Joram. The king of Israel suspected in this some evil design against him, and rent his clothes. Elisha the prophet hearing of this, sent for Naaman, and the strange interview which took place is recorded in 2 Kings 5.

column5: The people group of Zophar, Job's friend.
column7: The designation of Zophar, one of Job’s three friends ([[@18002011|Job 2:11]]; [[@18011001|Job 11:1]]), so called from some place in Arabia, called Naamah probably.

column5: Wife of Ashhur, the founder of Tekoa.
column7: A girl, the second of Ashur’s two wives, of the tribe of Judah ([[@13004005|1 Chr. 4:5]], [[@13004006|1 Chr. 4:6]]).

column5: One of David's mighty warriors, son of Ezbai.
column7: Youthful, a military chief in David’s army ([[@13011037|1 Chr. 11:37]]), called also Paarai ([[@10023035|2 Sam. 23:35]]).

column5: A border town between Ephraim and Benjamin
column7: Boyish, juvenile, a town in Ephraim between Bethel and Jericho ([[@13007028|1 Chr. 7:28]]).

column5: Wealthy Carmelite; husband of Abigail. He was known for foolishness.
column7: Foolish, a descendant of Caleb who dwelt at Maon (1 Sam. 25), the modern Main, 7 miles south-east of Hebron. He was “very great, and he had 3,000 sheep and 1,000 goats...but the man was churlish and evil in his doings.” During his wanderings David came into that district, and hearing that Nabal was about to shear his sheep, he sent ten of his young men to ask “whatsoever cometh unto thy hand for thy servants.” Nabal insultingly resented the demand, saying, “Who is David, and who is the son of Jesse?”

column5: Jezreelite vineyard owner, unjustly killed by Ahab and Jezebel.
column7: Fruits, “the Jezreelite,” was the owner of a portion of ground on the eastern slope of the hill of Jezreel ([[@12009025|2 Kings 9:25]], [[@12009026|2 Kings 9:26]]). This small “plat of ground” seems to have been all he possessed. It was a vineyard, and lay “hard by the palace of Ahab” ([[@11021001|1 Kings 21:1]], [[@11021002|1 Kings 21:2]]), who greatly coveted it. Naboth, however, refused on any terms to part with it to the king. He had inherited it from his fathers, and no Israelite could lawfully sell his property ([[@3025023|Lev. 25:23]]).

column5: Threshing floor where Uzzah touched the ark.
column7: Dart, the name of the threshing-floor at which the death of Uzzah took place ([[@13013009|1 Chr. 13:9]]). In the parallel passage in Samuel ([[@10006006|2 Sam. 6:6]]) it is called “Nachon’s threshing-floor.”

column5: Son of Aaron, consumed by fire for offering incense.
column7: The eldest of Aaron’s four sons ([[@2006023|Ex. 6:23]]; [[@4003002|Num. 3:2]]). He with his brothers and their father were consecrated as priests of Jehovah ([[@2028001|Ex. 28:1]]).

column5: King of Israel, son of Jeroboam I, reigned briefly.
column7: The son and successor of Jeroboam, the king of Israel ([[@11014020|1 Kings 14:20]]). While engaged with all Israel in laying siege to Gibbethon, a town of southern Dan ([[@6019044|Josh. 19:44]]), a conspiracy broke out in his army, and he was slain by Baasha ([[@11015025-11015028|1 Kings 15:25-28]]), after a reign of two years (B.C. 955-953).

column5: Son of Shammai, from the tribe of Judah.
column7: One of the sons of Shammai in the tribe of Judah ([[@13002028|1 Chr. 2:28]], [[@13002030|1 Chr. 2:30]]).

column5: Son of Abiel, from the tribe of Benjamin.
column7: Nadab was a son of Abiel, mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin.

column5: An ancestor of Jesus Christ.
column7: Illuminating, one of the ancestors of Christ in the maternal line ([[@42003025|Luke 3:25]]).

column5: A Levitical city in Zebulun
column7: Pasture, a city in Zebulun on the border of Issachar ([[@6019015|Josh. 19:15]]), the same as Nahalol ([[@7001030|Judg. 1:30]]). It was given to the Levites.

column5: Brother of Hodiah who married Ishbar.
column7: Naham, the brother of Hodiah whose son founded Keilah the Garmite city.

column5: One who returned from Babylonian exile with Zerubbabel.
column7: Nahamani was among those who returned to Jerusalem from Babylonian captivity with Zerubbabel.

column5: One of David's mighty men, Joab's armor-bearer.
column7: Snorer, a Berothite, one of David’s heroes, and armour-bearer of Joab ([[@13011039|1 Chr. 11:39]]).

column5: Ammonite king who besieged Jabesh Gilead.
column7: Nahash, the king of the Ammonites, besieged Jabesh Gilead and threatened to gouge out the right eyes of its inhabitants.

column5: Ammonite king, father of Hanun, showed kindness to David.
column7: Another king of the Ammonites of the same name is mentioned, who showed kindness to David during his wanderings ([[@10010002|2 Sam. 10:2]]). On his death David sent an embassy of sympathy to Hanun, his son and successor, at Rabbah Ammon, his capital. The grievous insult which was put upon these ambassadors led to a war against the Ammonites, who, with their allies the Syrians, were completely routed in a battle fought at “the entering in of the gate,” probably of Medeba ([[@10010006-10010014|2 Sam. 10:6-14]]).

column5: Mother of Abigail and Zeruiah, David's sisters.
column7: The father of Amasa, who was commander-in-chief of Abasolom’s army ([[@10017025|2 Sam. 17:25]]).

column5: King of the Ammonites, provided supplies to David.
column7: Nahash, the king of the Ammonites, provided supplies to David and his men during their time in Mahanaim.

column5: A descendant of Esau, a chief of Edom.
column7: One of the four sons of Reuel, the son of Esau ([[@1036013|Gen. 36:13]], [[@1036017|Gen 36:17]]).

column5: A Levite during the reign of King Hezekiah.
column7: A Levite, one of the overseers of the sacred offerings of the temple ([[@14031013|2 Chr. 31:13]]).

column5: The spy from the tribe of Naphtali.
column7: Hidden, one of the twelve spies sent out to explore the land of Canaan ([[@4013014|Num. 13:14]]).

column5: Son of Serug; father of Terah, Abraham's father.
column7: The father of Terah, who was the father of Abraham ([[@1011022-1011025|Gen. 11:22-25]]; [[@42003034|Luke 3:34]]).

column5: Son of Terah, Abraham's brother; father of Bethuel.
column7: A son of Terah, and elder brother of Abraham ([[@1011026|Gen. 11:26]], [[@1011027|Gen 11:27]]; [[@6024002|Josh. 24:2]], R.V.). He married Milcah, the daughter of his brother Haran, and remained in the land of his nativity on the east of the river Euphrates at Haran ([[@1011027-1011032|Gen. 11:27-32]]). A correspondence was maintained between the family of Abraham in Canaan and the relatives in the old ancestral home at Haran till the time of Jacob. When Jacob fled from Haran all intercourse between the two branches of the family came to an end ([[@1031055|Gen. 31:55]]).

column5: Son of Amminadab, leader of Judah, ancestor of David.
column7: Sorcerer, the son of Aminadab, and prince of the children of Judah at the time of the first numbering of the tribes in the wilderness ([[@2006023|Ex. 6:23]]). His sister Elisheba was the wife of Aaron. He died in the wilderness ([[@4026064|Num. 26:64]], [[@4026065|Num. 26:65]]).

column5: Old Testament prophet, author of the Book of Nahum.
column7: Consolation, the seventh of the so-called minor prophets, an Elkoshite. All we know of him is recorded in the book of his prophecies. He was probably a native of Galilee, and after the deportation of the ten tribes took up his residence in Jerusalem.

column5: An ancestor of Jesus Christ.
column7: Consolation, the seventh of the so-called minor prophets, an Elkoshite. All we know of him is recorded in the book of his prophecies. He was probably a native of Galilee, and after the deportation of the ten tribes took up his residence in Jerusalem.

column5: A town in Galilee where Jesus raised a widow's son
column7: (from Heb. nain, “green pastures,” “lovely”), the name of a town near the gate of which Jesus raised to life a widow’s son ([[@42007011-42007017|Luke 7:11-17]]). It is identified with the village called Nein, standing on the north-western slope of Jebel ed-Duhy (=the “hill Moreh” = “Little hermon”), about 4 miles from Tabor and 25 southwest of Capernaum. At the foot of the slope on which it stands is the great plain of Esdraelon.

column5: A place near Ramah where David fled from Saul
column7: Dwellings, the name given to the prophetical college established by Samuel near Ramah. It consisted of a cluster of separate dwellings, and hence its name. David took refuge here when he fled from Saul ([[@9019018|1 Sam. 19:18]], [[@9019019|1 Sam. 19:19]], [[@9019022|1 Sam. 19:22]], [[@9019023|1 Sam. 19:23]]), and here he passed a few weeks in peace (comp. Ps. 11).

column5: Israelite woman, mother-in-law of Ruth.
column7: The lovable; my delight, the wife of Elimelech, and mother of Mahlon and Chilion, and mother-in-law of Ruth (1:2, 20, 21; 2:1). Elimelech and his wife left the district of Bethlehem-Judah, and found a new home in the uplands of Moab. In course of time he died, as also his two sons Mahlon and Chilion, who had married women of Moab, and three widows were left mourning the loss of their husbands. Naomi longs to return now to her own land, to Bethlehem.

column5: A region in Issachar with Manassite towns
column7: Naphath was a region in Issachar that contained towns belonging to the tribe of Manasseh.

column5: Son of Ishmael, defeated by Reubenites, Gadites, and Manassites.
column6: the soul; he that rests, refreshes himself, or respires
column7: Refresher, one of the sons of Ishmael ([[@1025015|Gen. 25:15]]; [[@13001031|1 Chr. 1:31]]).

column5: Son of Jacob, founder of the tribe of Naphtali.
column7: My wrestling, the fifth son of Jacob. His mother was Bilhah, Rachel’s handmaid ([[@1030008|Gen. 30:8]]). When Jacob went down into Egypt, Naphtali had four sons ([[@1046024|Gen. 46:24]]).

column5: Descendants of Mizraim, son of Ham
column7: A Hamitic tribe descended from Mizraim ([[@1010013|Gen. 10:13]]). Others identify this word with Napata, the name of the city and territory on the southern frontier of Mizraim, the modern Meroe, at the great bend of the Nile at Soudan. This city was the royal residence, it is said, of Queen Candace ([[@44008027|Acts 8:27]]).

column5: Christian in Rome with a household
column7: Daffodil, a Roman whom Paul salutes ([[@45016011|Rom. 16:11]]). He is supposed to have been the private secretary of the emperor Claudius.

(Heb. nerd), a much-valued perfume ([[@22001012|Cant. 1:12]]; [[@22004013|Cant 4:13]], [[@22004014|Cant 4:14]]). It was “very precious”, i.e., very costly ([[@41014003|Mark 14:3]]; [[@43012003|John 12:3]], [[@43012005|John 12:5]]). It is the root of an Indian plant, the Nardostachys jatamansi, of the family of Valeriance, growing on the Himalaya mountains. It is distinguished by its having many hairy spikes shooting out from one root.

column5: Son of David and Bathsheba, ancestor of Jesus.
column7: A son of David, by Bathsheba ([[@10005014|2 Sam. 5:14]]), whose name appears in the genealogy of Mary, the mother of our Lord ([[@42003031|Luke 3:31]]).

column5: Prophet during the reigns of David and Solomon.
column7: A prophet in the reigns of David and Solomon ([[@14009029|2 Chr. 9:29]]). He is first spoken of in connection with the arrangements David made for the building of the temple ([[@10007002|2 Sam. 7:2]], [[@10007003|2 Sam. 7:3]], [[@10007017|2 Sam. 7:17]]), and next appears as the reprover of David on account of his sin with Bathsheba (12:1-14). He was charged with the education of Solomon (12:25), at whose inauguration to the throne he took a prominent part ([[@11001008|1 Kings 1:8]], [[@11001010|1 Kings 1:10]], [[@11001011|1 Kings 1:11]], [[@11001022|1 Kings 1:22]]-45).

column5: One of David's mighty men, brother of Joel.
column7: Nathan, the brother of Joel, was one of David's mighty men.

column5: A leader summoned by Ezra to help teach the Law.
column7: Nathan, along with other leaders, was summoned by Ezra to assist in teaching the Law to the people.

column5: An Israelite who married a foreign woman during the Exile.
column7: Nathan is listed among the Israelites who had married foreign women during the Exile and pledged to put them away.

column5: A court official during King Josiah's reign.
column6: the gift of the king, or of counsel
column7: Nathan-melech was a court official who had living quarters near the entrance of the temple during King Josiah's reign.

column5: Disciple of Jesus, from Cana in Galilee.
column7: Given or gift of God, one of our Lord’s disciples, “of Cana in Galilee” ([[@43021002|John 21:2]]). He was “an Israelite indeed, in whom was no guile” (1:47, 48). His name occurs only in the Gospel of John, who in his list of the disciples never mentions Bartholomew, with whom he has consequently been identified.

column5: The hometown of Jesus in Galilee
column7: Separated, generally supposed to be the Greek form of the Hebrew netser , a “shoot” or “sprout.” Some, however, think that the name of the city must be connected with the name of the hill behind it, from which one of the finest prospects in Palestine is obtained, and accordingly they derive it from the Hebrew notserah , i.e., one guarding or watching, thus designating the hill which overlooks and thus guards an extensive region. This city is not mentioned in the Old Testament.

(Heb. form Nazirite), the name of such Israelites as took on them the vow prescribed in [[@4006002-4006021|Num. 6:2-21]]. The word denotes generally one who is separated from others and consecrated to God. Although there is no mention of any Nazarite before Samson, yet it is evident that they existed before the time of Moses. The vow of a Nazarite involved these three things, (1) abstinence from wine and strong drink, (2) refraining from cutting the hair off the head during the whole period of the continuance of the vow, and (3) the avoidance of contact with the dead.

column5: A border town of Zebulun and Asher
column7: Shaking, or settlement, or descent, a town on the east side of Zebulun, not far from Rimmon ([[@6019013|Josh. 19:13]]).

column5: A port city in Macedonia visited by Paul
column7: New city, a town in Thrace at which Paul first landed in Europe ([[@44016011|Acts 16:11]]). It was the sea-port of the inland town of Philippi, which was distant about 10 miles. From this port Paul embarked on his last journey to Jerusalem ([[@44020006|Acts 20:6]]).

column5: Descendant of David, son of Shemaiah.
column7: Neariah, a descendant of King David, was the son of Shemaiah and had three sons: Elioenai, Hizkiah, and Azrikam.

column5: A Simeonite leader who defeated the Amalekites.
column7: Neariah, along with other Simeonite leaders, defeated the remaining Amalekites during the reign of King Hezekiah.

column5: A leader who sealed the covenant with Nehemiah.
column7: Nebai was one of the leaders who sealed the covenant with Nehemiah to follow God's law.

column5: Firstborn son of Ishmael; father of a tribe.
column7: Ishmael’s eldest son ([[@1025013|Gen. 25:13]]), and the prince of an Israelitish tribe (16).

column5: A town in Benjamin inhabited by Benjamites after the exile
column7: Wickedness in secret, ([[@16011034|Neh. 11:34]]), probably the village of Beit Nebala, about 4 miles north of Lydda.

column5: Father of Jeroboam, the first king of Israel.
column7: Sight; aspect, the father of Jeroboam, the king of Israel ([[@11011026|1 Kings 11:26]], etc.).

column5: A city and mountain in Moab
column7: A town on the east of Jordan which was taken possession of and rebuilt by the tribe of Reuben ([[@4032003|Num. 32:3]], [[@4032038|Num. 32:38]]; [[@13005008|1 Chr. 5:8]]).

column5: A town in Judah, possibly named after a person
column7: The “children of Nebo” ([[@15002029|Ezra 2:29]]; [[@16007033|Neh. 7:33]]) were of those who returned from Babylon.

column5: The mountain where Moses viewed the Promised Land
column7: Regions beyond; i.e., on the east of Jordan, a mountain, or rather a mountain-chain, over against Jericho, to the east and south-east of the Dead Sea, in the land of Moab. From “the top of Pisgah”, i.e., Mount Nebo (q.v.), one of its summits, Moses surveyed the Promised Land ([[@5003027|Deut. 3:27]]; [[@5032049|Deut 32:49]]), and there he died (34:1, 5).

column5: Babylonian official at Jerusalem's fall
column7: Nebu-sar-sekim was a high official in Nebuchadnezzar's army when Jerusalem fell.

column5: Emperor of Babylon who conquered Judah
column6: Nebuchadrezzar, tears and groans of judgment
column7: In the Babylonian orthography Nabu-kudur-uzur, which means “Nebo, protect the crown!” or the “frontiers.” In an inscription he styles himself “Nebo’s favourite.” He was the son and successor of Nabopolassar, who delivered Babylon from its dependence on Assyria and laid Nineveh in ruins. He was the greatest and most powerful of all the Babylonian kings.

column5: Babylonian official during the fall of Jerusalem.
column7: Adorer of Nebo, or Nebo saves me, the “Rabsaris,” or chief chamberlain, of the court of Babylon.

column5: Babylonian captain of the guard during Jerusalem's fall.
column7: “the captain of the guard,” in rank next to the king, who appears prominent in directing affairs at the capture of Jerusalem ([[@12025008-12025020|2 Kings 25:8-20]]; [[@24039011|Jer. 39:11]]; [[@24040002-24040005|Jer 40:2-5]]). He showed kindness toward Jeremiah, as commanded by Nebuchadnezzar (40:1).

column5: Egyptian Pharaoh during the reigns of Josiah and Jehoiakim.
column7: The Pharaoh by whom Josiah was defeated and slain at Megiddo ([[@14035020-14035024|2 Chr. 35:20-24]]; [[@12023029|2 Kings 23:29]], [[@12023030|2 Kings 23:30]]).

column5: Descendant of King Jeconiah of Judah
column6: prince or vow of the Lord
column7: Moved of Jehovah, one of the sons of Jeconiah ([[@13003018|1 Chr. 3:18]]).

column5: The southern region of Israel, a semi-arid area
column7: The Negeb, meaning "south," refers to the semi-arid region in the southern part of Israel.

column5: Hometown of the false prophet Shemaiah
column7: The name given to a false prophet Shemaiah, who went with the captives to Babylon ([[@24029024|Jer. 29:24]], [[@24029031|Jer. 29:31]], [[@24029032|Jer. 29:32]]). The origin of the name is unknown.

column5: A leader who returned from Babylon to Jerusalem.
column7: Nehemiah was among the leaders who returned with Zerubbabel from Babylonian exile to Jerusalem.

column5: Governor of Judah, rebuilt Jerusalem's walls.
column7: The son of Hachaliah ([[@16001001|Neh. 1:1]]), and probably of the tribe of Judah. His family must have belonged to Jerusalem ([[@16002003|Neh. 2:3]]). He was one of the “Jews of the dispersion,” and in his youth was appointed to the important office of royal cup-bearer at the palace of Shushan. The king, Artaxerxes Longimanus, seems to have been on terms of friendly familiarity with his attendant.

column5: Son of Azbuk, repaired a section of Jerusalem's wall.
column7: Nehemiah, the son of Azbuk, was a leader who repaired a section of Jerusalem's wall near the tombs of David during the rebuilding process led by Nehemiah the governor.

column5: Mother of King Jehoiachin of Judah.
column7: Copper, the daughter of Elnathan of Jerusalem, and the wife of Jehoiakin ([[@12024008|2 Kings 24:8]]), king of Judah.

column5: A family of temple servants who returned from exile.
column7: The descendants of Nekoda were among the temple servants who returned to Jerusalem from Babylonian captivity.

column5: Family excluded from the priesthood after the Exile.
column7: The descendants of Nekoda were among those who could not prove their priestly lineage after returning from the Babylonian exile.

column5: Son of Eliab, from the tribe of Reuben.
column7: A Reubenite, a son of Eliab, and brother of Dathan and Abiram ([[@4026009|Num. 26:9]]).

column5: Son of Izhar, from the tribe of Levi.
column7: Nepheg was a son of Izhar and a member of the Levite clan of Kohath.

column5: Son of King David, born in Jerusalem.
column7: Nepheg was one of the sons of King David, born to him in Jerusalem.

column5: Mysterious giants mentioned in the pre-flood and post-flood eras.
column7: ([[@1006004|Gen. 6:4]]; [[@4013033|Num. 13:33]], R.V.), giants, the Hebrew word left untranslated by the Revisers, the name of one of the Canaanitish tribes.

column5: A spring on the border of Judah and Benjamin
column7: Opened, a fountain and a stream issuing from it on the border between Judah and Benjamin ([[@6015008|Josh. 15:8]], [[@6015009|Josh. 15:9]]; 18:15). It has been identified with ‘Ain Lifta, a spring about 2 1/2 miles north-west of Jerusalem.

column5: Family of temple servants who returned from exile.
column7: The Nephushesim (or Nephisim) were a family of temple servants who returned to Jerusalem from Babylonian captivity.

column5: Father of Abner, King Saul's commander.
column7: Light, the father of Kish ([[@13008033|1 Chr. 8:33]]). [[@9014051|1 Sam. 14:51]] should be read, “Kish, the father of Saul, and Ner, the father of Abner, were the sons of Abiel.”

column5: A Christian in Rome greeted by Paul.
column7: A Christian at Rome to whom Paul sent his salutation ([[@45016015|Rom. 16:15]]).

column5: Babylonian official at Jerusalem's fall
column7: One of the “princes of the king of Babylon who accompanied him in his last expedition against Jerusalem” ([[@24039003|Jer. 39:3]], [[@24039013|Jer. 39:13]]).

column5: Ancestor of Jesus
column7: Neri was an ancestor of Jesus, mentioned in Luke's genealogy.

column5: Father of Baruch
column7: Neriah was the father of Baruch, Jeremiah's scribe.

column5: Roman emperor
column6: a name applied to those who are cut out of the womb
column7: Occurs only in the superscription (which is probably spurious, and is altogether omitted in the R.V.) to the Second Epistle to Timothy. He became emperor of Rome when he was about seventeen years of age (A.D. 54), and soon began to exhibit the character of a cruel tyrant and heathen debauchee. In May A.D. 64, a terrible conflagration broke out in Rome, which raged for six days and seven nights, and totally destroyed a great part of the city. The guilt of this fire was attached to him at the time, and the general verdict of history accuses him of the crime.

column5: A place associated with potters in Judah
column7: Netaim was a place in Judah where potters lived and worked.

column5: Leader of Issachar
column7: The son of Zuar, chief of the tribe of Issachar at the Exodus ([[@4001008|Num. 1:8]]; [[@4002005|Num 2:5]]).

column5: Brother of David
column7: Nethanel was a son of Jesse and brother of King David.

column5: Priest who blew trumpets
column7: A priest who blew the trumpet before the ark when it was brought up to Jerusalem ([[@13015024|1 Chr. 15:24]]).

column5: Scribe during David's reign
column7: Nethanel was a scribe who helped divide the priests into their divisions during David's reign.

column5: Son of Obed-Edom
column7: A temple porter, of the family of the Korhites ([[@13026004|1 Chr. 26:4]]).

column5: Levite sent to teach
column7: One of the “princes” appointed by Jehoshaphat to teach the law through the cities of Judah ([[@14017007|2 Chr. 17:7]]).

column5: Levite leader under Josiah
column7: A chief Levite in the time of Josiah ([[@14035009|2 Chr. 35:9]]).

column5: Priest during Ezra's time
column7: Nethanel was a priest who had married a foreign woman during the Exile.

column5: Priest during Nehemiah's time
column7: Nethanel was a priest in Jerusalem during the time of Nehemiah.

column5: Musician in dedication parade
column7: A priest’s son who bore a trumpet at the dedication of the walls of Jerusalem ([[@16012036|Neh. 12:36]]).

column5: Father of Ishmael
column7: Nethaniah was the father of Ishmael, the assassin of Gedaliah the governor.

column5: Musician in David's time, descended from Asaph
column7: One of Asaph’s sons, appointed by David to minister in the temple ([[@13025002|1 Chr. 25:2]], [[@13025012|1 Chr. 25:12]]).

column5: Levite sent to teach
column7: A Levite sent by Jehoshaphat to teach the law ([[@14017008|2 Chr. 17:8]]).

column5: Official under Jehoiakim
column7: Nethaniah was the father of Jehudi, an official in King Jehoiakim's court.

column5: A town in Judah, home to several notable individuals
column7: Distillation; dropping, a town in Judah, in the neighbourhood, probably, of Bethlehem ([[@16007026|Neh. 7:26]]; [[@13002054|1 Chr. 2:54]]). Two of David’s guards were Netophathites ([[@13027013|1 Chr. 27:13]], [[@13027015|1 Chr. 27:15]]).

column5: A gate in Jerusalem during Jeremiah's time
column7: The New Gate was a gate in Jerusalem during the time of the prophet Jeremiah.

column5: Ancestor of temple servants
column7: Neziah was the ancestor of a family of temple servants who returned from the Babylonian exile.

column5: A town in the Judean lowlands
column7: A town in the “plain” of Judah.

column5: A town in the Judean wilderness
column7: Fertile; light soil, a city somewhere “in the wilderness” of Judah ([[@6015062|Josh. 15:62]]), probably near Engedi.

column5: One of seven deacons
column7: Conqueror, one of the seven deacons appointed in the apostolic Church ([[@44006001-44006006|Acts 6:1-6]]).

column5: Pharisee who visited Jesus
column7: The people is victor, a Pharisee and a member of the Sanhedrin. He is first noticed as visiting Jesus by night ([[@43003001-43003021|John 3:1-21]]) for the purpose of learning more of his doctrines, which our Lord then unfolded to him, giving prominence to the necessity of being “born again.” He is next met with in the Sanhedrin (7:50-52), where he protested against the course they were taking in plotting against Christ. Once more he is mentioned as taking part in the preparation for the anointing and burial of the body of Christ ([[@43019039|John 19:39]]).

column5: Proselyte chosen as deacon
column7: The victory of the people, a proselyte of Antioch, one of the seven deacons ([[@44006005|Acts 6:5]]).

column5: A city in Epirus where Paul planned to winter
column7: City of victory, where Paul intended to winter ([[@56003012|Titus 3:12]]). There were several cities of this name. The one here referred to was most probably that in Epirus, which was built by Augustus Caesar to commemorate his victory at the battle of Actium (B.C. 31). It is the modern Paleoprevesa, i.e., “Old Prevesa.”

column5: The major river of Egypt, mentioned in various contexts
column7: Dark; blue, not found in Scripture, but frequently referred to in the Old Testament under the name of Sihor, i.e., “the black stream” ([[@23023003|Isa. 23:3]]; [[@24002018|Jer. 2:18]]) or simply “the river” ([[@1041001|Gen. 41:1]]; [[@2001022|Ex. 1:22]], etc.) and the “flood of Egypt” ([[@30008008|Amos 8:8]]). It consists of two rivers, the White Nile, which takes its rise in the Victoria Nyanza, and the Blue Nile, which rises in the Abyssinian Mountains.

column5: A place in Moab known for its waters
column7: Nimrim was a place in Moab known for its waters, which are mentioned in the context of God's judgment on Moab.

column5: Mighty hunter, built cities
column6: rebellion (but probably an unknown Assyrian word)
column7: Firm, a descendant of Cush, the son of Ham. He was the first who claimed to be a “mighty one in the earth.” Babel was the beginning of his kingdom, which he gradually enlarged ([[@1010008-1010010|Gen. 10:8-10]]).

column5: Grandfather of Jehu
column7: Nimshi was the grandfather of Jehu, the king of Israel who overthrew the dynasty of Ahab.

column5: The capital of Assyria, known for its wickedness and repentance
column7: First mentioned in [[@1010011|Gen. 10:11]], which is rendered in the Revised Version, “He [i.e., Nimrod] went forth into Assyria and builded Nineveh.” It is not again noticed till the days of Jonah, when it is described ([[@32003003|Jonah 3:3]]; [[@32004011|Jonah 4:11]]) as a great and populous city, the flourishing capital of the Assyrian empire ([[@12019036|2 Kings 19:36]]; [[@23037037|Isa. 37:37]]). The book of the prophet Nahum is almost exclusively taken up with prophetic denunciations against this city.

column5: Levite in charge of treasuries
column6: witness, or ornament, of the Lord
column7: A Levite who returned from Babylon ([[@15008033|Ezra 8:33]]).

column5: False prophetess opposed Nehemiah
column6: witness, or ornament, of the Lord
column7: A false prophetess who assisted Tobiah and Sanballat against the Jews ([[@16006014|Neh. 6:14]]).

column5: Righteous man, built ark, survived flood
column7: Rest, (Heb. Noah) the grandson of Methuselah ([[@1005025-1005029|Gen. 5:25-29]]), who was for two hundred and fifty years contemporary with Adam, and the son of Lamech, who was about fifty years old at the time of Adam’s death. This patriarch is rightly regarded as the connecting link between the old and the new world. He is the second great progenitor of the human family.

column5: Daughter of Zelophehad
column7: Rest, (Heb. Noah) the grandson of Methuselah ([[@1005025-1005029|Gen. 5:25-29]]), who was for two hundred and fifty years contemporary with Adam, and the son of Lamech, who was about fifty years old at the time of Adam’s death. This patriarch is rightly regarded as the connecting link between the old and the new world. He is the second great progenitor of the human family.

column5: A city of priests near Jerusalem
column7: High place, a city of the priests, first mentioned in the history of David’s wanderings ([[@9021001|1 Sam. 21:1]]). Here the tabernacle was then standing, and here Ahimelech the priest resided. (See AHIMELECH.) From [[@23010028-23010032|Isa. 10:28-32]] it seems to have been near Jerusalem. It has been identified by some with el-Isawiyeh, one mile and a half to the north-east of Jerusalem.

column5: The land where Cain settled after killing Abel
column7: Exile; wandering; unrest, a name given to the country to which Cain fled ([[@1004016|Gen. 4:16]]).

column5: Son of David
column7: Splendour, one of David’s sons, born at Jerusalem ([[@13003007|1 Chr. 3:7]]).

column5: Father of Joshua
column7: Beyond the fact that he was the father of Joshua nothing more is known of him ([[@2033011|Ex. 33:11]]).

column5: Hosted a church in her house
column7: Nympha was a woman who hosted a church in her house in Laodicea.

column5: Ahab's palace administrator, protected prophets
column7: Obadiah was a palace administrator under King Ahab who feared the Lord and protected a hundred prophets during Jezebel's persecution.

column5: Descendant of David
column7: Obadiah was a descendant of King David, mentioned in the genealogy of David's descendants.

column5: Son of Azel
column7: A chief of the tribe of Issachar ([[@13007003|1 Chr. 7:3]]).

column5: Son of Izrahiah
column7: Obadiah was one of the five sons of Izrahiah, a descendant of Issachar.

column5: Gatekeeper, descendant of Jeduthun
column7: Obadiah, also known as Abda, was a gatekeeper and descendant of Jeduthun who served in the temple.

column5: Gadite warrior who joined David
column7: A Gadite who joined David at Ziklag ([[@13012009|1 Chr. 12:9]]).

column5: Ruler over Zebulun in David's time
column7: A prince of Zebulun in the time of David ([[@13027019|1 Chr. 27:19]]).

column5: Levite sent to teach in Judah
column7: One of the princes sent by Jehoshaphat to instruct the people in the law ([[@14017007|2 Chr. 17:7]]).

column5: Levite overseer of temple repairs
column7: A Levite who superintended the repairs of the temple under Josiah ([[@14034012|2 Chr. 34:12]]).

column5: Returnee from Babylon
column7: One who accompanied Ezra on the return from Babylon ([[@15008009|Ezra 8:9]]).

column5: Signatory to Nehemiah's covenant
column7: Obadiah was one of the leaders who signed the covenant of faithfulness during Nehemiah's time.

column5: Prophet who prophesied against Edom
column7: Obadiah was a prophet who delivered a message of judgment against the nation of Edom.

column5: Son of Joktan
column7: Stripped, the eight son of Joktan ([[@1010028|Gen. 10:28]]); called also Ebal ([[@13001022|1 Chr. 1:22]]).

column5: Son of Boaz and Ruth
column7: A son of Boaz and Ruth ([[@8004021|Ruth 4:21]], [[@8004022|Ruth 4:22]]), and the grandfather of David ([[@40001005|Matt. 1:5]]).

column5: Descendant of Judah
column7: Obed was a descendant of Judah through the line of Jerahmeel.

column5: Ishmaelite warrior in David's army
column7: Obed was an Ishmaelite warrior who fought in David's army.

column5: Gatekeeper, son of Shemaiah
column7: Obed was a gatekeeper in the temple, the son of Shemaiah.

column5: Father of Azariah
column7: Obed was the father of Azariah, one of the captains who supported Joash in overthrowing Athaliah.

column5: Gittite who housed the Ark
column7: “The Gittite” (probably so called because he was a native of Gath-rimmon), a Levite of the family of the Korhites ([[@13026001|1 Chr. 26:1]], [[@13026004|1 Chr. 26:4]]-8), to whom was specially intrusted the custody of the ark ([[@13015018|1 Chr. 15:18]]). When David was bringing up the ark “from the house of Abinadab, that was in Gibeah” (probably some hill or eminence near Kirjath-jearim), and had reached Nachon’s threshing-floor, he became afraid because of the “breach upon Uzzah,” and carried it aside into the house of Obededom ([[@10006001-10006012|2 Sam. 6:1-12]]).

column5: Overseer of David's camels
column6: that weeps; who deserves to be bewailed
column7: A keeper of camels, an Ishmaelite who was “over the camels” in the time of David ([[@13027030|1 Chr. 27:30]]).

column5: A place where the Israelites camped during the Exodus
column7: Bottles, an encampment of the Israelites during the wanderings in the wilderness ([[@4033043|Num. 33:43]]), the first after the setting up of the brazen serpent.

column5: Father of Pagiel
column7: Ochran was the father of Pagiel, a leader from the tribe of Asher during the Exodus.

column5: Prophet, father of Azariah
column6: to sustain, hold or lift up
column7: Oded was a prophet and the father of Azariah, who prophesied during the reign of King Asa of Judah.

column5: Prophet who confronted victorious Israelite army
column6: to sustain, hold or lift up
column7: A prophet in the time of Ahaz and Pekah ([[@14028009-14028015|2 Chr. 28:9-15]]).

column5: King of Bashan, defeated by Israel
column6: a cake; bread baked in ashes
column7: Gigantic, the king of Bashan, who was defeated by Moses in a pitched battle at Edrei, and was slain along with his sons ([[@5001004|Deut. 1:4]]), and whose kingdom was given to the tribes of Reuben and Gad and half the tribe of Manasseh ([[@4021032-4021035|Num. 21:32-35]]; [[@5003001-5003013|Deut. 3:1-13]]). His bedstead (or rather sarcophagus) was of iron (or ironstone), 9 cubits in length and 4 cubits in breadth. His overthrow was afterwards celebrated in song ([[@19135011|Ps. 135:11]]; [[@19136020|Ps 136:20]]).

column5: Son of Simeon
column7: United, or power, the third son of Simeon ([[@1046010|Gen. 46:10]]).

column5: Descendant of Judah
column7: A house; tent, the fourth son of Zerubbabel ([[@13003020|1 Chr. 3:20]]).

column5: Symbolic name for Samaria
column7: She has her own tent, a name used by Ezekiel (23:4, 5, 36, 44) as a symbol of the idolatry of the kingdom of Israel. This kingdom is described as a lewdwoman, an adulteress, given up to the abominations and idolatries of the Egyptians and Assyrians. Because of her crimes, she was carried away captive, and ceased to be a kingdom.

column5: Skilled craftsman for the tabernacle
column7: Tent of the father, an artist of the tribe of Dan, appointed to the work of preparing materials for the tabernacle ([[@2031006|Ex. 31:6]]; [[@2035034|Ex 35:34]]; [[@2036001|Ex 36:1]], [[@2036002|Ex 36:2]]; [[@2038023|Ex 38:23]]).

column5: Symbolic name for Jerusalem
column6: my tent, or my tabernacle, in her
column7: My tent is in her, the name of an imaginary harlot, applied symbolically to Jerusalem, because she had abandoned the worship of the true God and given herself up to the idolatries of foreign nations.

column5: Wife of Esau
column7: Tent of the height, the name given to Judith, the daughter of Beeri = Anah ([[@1026034|Gen. 26:34]]; [[@1036002|Gen 36:2]]), when she became the wife of Esau. A district among the mountains of Edom, probably near Mount Hor, was called after her name, or it may be that she received her name from the district.

The fruit of the olive-tree. This tree yielded oil which was highly valued. The best oil was from olives that were plucked before being fully ripe, and then beaten or squeezed ([[@5024020|Deut. 24:20]]; [[@23017006|Isa. 17:6]]; [[@23024013|Isa 24:13]]). It was called “beaten,” or “fresh oil” ([[@2027020|Ex. 27:20]]).

column5: A mountain ridge east of Jerusalem
column7: The Mount of Olives is a mountain ridge east of Jerusalem, known as the site of many significant events in the Bible, particularly in the life of Jesus.

column5: Believer greeted by Paul
column7: A Roman Christian whom Paul salutes ([[@45016015|Rom. 16:15]]).

column5: Son of Eliphaz, grandson of Esau
column7: Eloquent, the son of Eliphaz, who was Esau’s eldest son ([[@1036011-1036015|Gen. 36:11-15]]).
A handful, one-tenth of an ephah=half a gallon dry measure ([[@2016022|Ex. 16:22]], [[@2016032|Ex 16:32]], [[@2016033|Ex 16:33]], [[@2016036|Ex 16:36]])=“tenth deal.”

column5: King of Israel; father of Ahab
column7: Servant of Jehovah. When Elah was murdered by Zimri at Tirzah ([[@11016015-11016027|1 Kings 16:15-27]]), Omri, his captain, was made king (B.C. 931). For four years there was continued opposition to his reign, Tibni, another claimant to the throne, leading the opposing party; but at the close of that period all his rivals were defeated, and he became king of Israel, “Tibni died and Omri reigned” (B.C. 927). By his vigour and power he gained great eminence and consolidated the kingdom.

column5: Descendant of Benjamin
column7: Servant of Jehovah. When Elah was murdered by Zimri at Tirzah ([[@11016015-11016027|1 Kings 16:15-27]]), Omri, his captain, was made king (B.C. 931). For four years there was continued opposition to his reign, Tibni, another claimant to the throne, leading the opposing party; but at the close of that period all his rivals were defeated, and he became king of Israel, “Tibni died and Omri reigned” (B.C. 927). By his vigour and power he gained great eminence and consolidated the kingdom.

column5: Descendant of Judah in Jerusalem
column7: Servant of Jehovah. When Elah was murdered by Zimri at Tirzah ([[@11016015-11016027|1 Kings 16:15-27]]), Omri, his captain, was made king (B.C. 931). For four years there was continued opposition to his reign, Tibni, another claimant to the throne, leading the opposing party; but at the close of that period all his rivals were defeated, and he became king of Israel, “Tibni died and Omri reigned” (B.C. 927). By his vigour and power he gained great eminence and consolidated the kingdom.

column5: Chief of the tribe of Issachar
column7: Servant of Jehovah. When Elah was murdered by Zimri at Tirzah ([[@11016015-11016027|1 Kings 16:15-27]]), Omri, his captain, was made king (B.C. 931). For four years there was continued opposition to his reign, Tibni, another claimant to the throne, leading the opposing party; but at the close of that period all his rivals were defeated, and he became king of Israel, “Tibni died and Omri reigned” (B.C. 927). By his vigour and power he gained great eminence and consolidated the kingdom.

column5: An ancient Egyptian city, mentioned in relation to Joseph
column7: Light; the sun, ([[@1041045|Gen. 41:45]], [[@1041050|Gen. 41:50]]), the great seat of sun-worship, called also Bethshemesh ([[@24043013|Jer. 43:13]]) and Aven ([[@26030017|Ezek. 30:17]]), stood on the east bank of the Nile, a few miles north of Memphis, and near Cairo, in the north-east. The Vulgate and the LXX. Versions have “Heliopolis” (“city of the sun”) instead of On in Genesis and of Aven in Ezekiel.

column5: Reubenite involved in Korah's rebellion
column7: Light; the sun, ([[@1041045|Gen. 41:45]], [[@1041050|Gen. 41:50]]), the great seat of sun-worship, called also Bethshemesh ([[@24043013|Jer. 43:13]]) and Aven ([[@26030017|Ezek. 30:17]]), stood on the east bank of the Nile, a few miles north of Memphis, and near Cairo, in the north-east. The Vulgate and the LXX. Versions have “Heliopolis” (“city of the sun”) instead of On in Genesis and of Aven in Ezekiel.

column5: Descendant of Seir the Horite
column7: Onam was a descendant of Seir the Horite, mentioned in the genealogies of Edom.

column5: Descendant of Judah, son of Jerahmeel
column7: Onam was a descendant of Judah, the son of Jerahmeel, and had two sons, Shammai and Jada.

column5: Son of Judah
Runaway slave, convert of Paul
column7: Useful, a slave who, after robbing his master Philemon (q.v.) at Colosse, fled to Rome, where he was converted by the apostle Paul, who sent him back to his master with the epistle which bears his name. In it he beseeches Philemon to receive his slave as a “faithful and beloved brother.” Paul offers to pay to Philemon anything his slave had taken, and to bear the wrong he had done him. He was accompanied on his return by Tychicus, the bearer of the Epistle to the Colossians ([[@57001001|Philemon 1]]:16, 18).

column5: Friend and supporter of Paul
column7: Bringing profit, an Ephesian Christian who showed great kindness to Paul at Rome.

column5: A town in Benjamin, near Lod
column6: grief or strength or iniquity of him
column7: A town of Benjamin, in the “plain of Ono” ([[@13008012|1 Chr. 8:12]]; [[@15002033|Ezra 2:33]]); now Kefr ‘Ana, 5 miles north of Lydda, and about 30 miles north-west of Jerusalem. Not succeeding in their attempts to deter Nehemiah from rebuilding the walls of Jerusalem, Sanballat and Tobiah resorted to strategem, and pretending to wish a conference with him, they invited him to meet them at Ono. Four times they made the request, and every time Nehemiah refused to come.

column5: A fortified area in Jerusalem
column6: a tower; darkness; small white cloud
column7: Hill; mound, the long, narrow, rounded promontory on the southern slope of the temple hill, between the Tyropoeon and the Kedron valley ([[@14027003|2 Chr. 27:3]]; [[@14033014|2 Chr. 33:14]]; [[@16003026|Neh. 3:26]], [[@16003027|Neh. 3:27]]). It was surrounded by a separate wall, and was occupied by the Nethinim after the Captivity. This wall has been discovered by the engineers of the Palestine Exploration Fund at the south-eastern angle of the temple area. It is 4 feet below the present surface.

column5: Son of Joktan
column7: Ophir was a son of Joktan, a descendant of Shem, mentioned in the Table of Nations.

column5: A region known for its gold
column7: Some region famous for its gold ([[@11009028|1 Kings 9:28]]; [[@11010011|1 Kings 10:11]]; [[@11022048|1 Kings 22:48]]; [[@18022024|Job 22:24]]; [[@18028016|Job 28:16]]; [[@23013012|Isa. 13:12]]). In the LXX. this word is rendered “Sophir,” and “Sofir” is the Coptic name for India, which is the rendering of the Arabic version, as also of the Vulgate. Josephus has identified it with the Golden Chersonese, i.e., the Malay peninsula. It is now generally identified with Abhira, at the mouth of the Indus.

column5: A town in Benjamin
column7: Ophni was a town allotted to the tribe of Benjamin during the division of the Promised Land.

column5: A town in Benjamin and a place in Manasseh
column7: A city of Benjamin ([[@6018023|Josh. 18:23]]); probably identical with Ephron ([[@14013019|2 Chr. 13:19]]) and Ephraim ([[@43011054|John 11:54]]).

column5: Gideon's hometown in Manasseh; a town in Issachar
