column5: A place near the Jordan River associated with Israel's crossing
column7: When the Hebrews crossed the Jordan, as soon as the feet of the priests were dipped in the water, the flow of the stream was arrested. The point of arrest was the “city of Adam beside Zaretan,” probably near Succoth, at the mouth of the Jabbok, some 30 miles up the river from where the people were encamped. There the water “stood and rose upon an heap.”

column5: Ancestor of returning exiles
column7: Id., one whose descendants returned from the Captivity with Zerubbabel ([[@15002008|Ezra 2:8]]; [[@16007013|Neh. 7:13]]); probably the same as Zatthu.

column5: Israelite leader who sealed Nehemiah's covenant
column7: Id., one whose descendants returned from the Captivity with Zerubbabel ([[@15002008|Ezra 2:8]]; [[@16007013|Neh. 7:13]]); probably the same as Zatthu.

column5: Son of Jonathan, descendant of Jerahmeel
column7: Zaza was a son of Jonathan and a descendant of Jerahmeel from the tribe of Judah.

A sect of Jews which originated with Judas the Gaulonite ([[@44005037|Acts 5:37]]). They refused to pay tribute to the Romans, on the ground that this was a violation of the principle that God was the only king of Israel. They rebelled against the Romans, but were soon scattered, and became a lawless band of mere brigands.

column5: Son of Beriah, a Benjamite
column6: portion of the Lord; the Lord is my portion
column7: Zebadiah was a greandson of Elpaal and a member of the tribe of Benjamin.

column5: Son of Elpaal, a Benjamite
column6: portion of the Lord; the Lord is my portion
column7: Zebadiah was a son of Elpaal and a member of the tribe of Benjamin.

column5: Gadite warrior who joined David
column6: portion of the Lord; the Lord is my portion
column7: Zebadiah was a Gadite warrior who joined David's forces at Ziklag.

column5: Son of Meshelemiah, a Korahite gatekeeper
column6: portion of the Lord; the Lord is my portion
column7: A Korhite porter of the Lord’s house ([[@13026002|1 Chr. 26:2]]).

column5: Son of Asahel, commander of David's army
column6: portion of the Lord; the Lord is my portion
column7: A son of Asahel, Joab’s brother ([[@13027007|1 Chr. 27:7]]).

column5: Levite sent by Jehoshaphat to teach the Law
column6: portion of the Lord; the Lord is my portion
column7: A Levite who took part as one of the teachers in the system of national education instituted by Jehoshaphat ([[@14017007|2 Chr. 17:7]], [[@14017008|2 Chr. 17:8]]).

column5: Chief priest in matters of the Lord
column6: portion of the Lord; the Lord is my portion
column7: Zebadiah, son of Ishmael, was appointed as the leader in all matters concerning the king during Jehoshaphat's reign.

column5: Leader of returning exiles with Shecaniah
column6: portion of the Lord; the Lord is my portion
column7: Zebadiah, son of Michael, led a group of 80 men who returned to Jerusalem with Ezra after the Babylonian exile.

column5: Priest who married a foreign woman
column6: portion of the Lord; the Lord is my portion
column7: Zebadiah, one of the priests, was among those who had married foreign women during the time of Ezra.

column5: Midianite king defeated by Gideon
column7: Man-killer, or sacrifice, one of the two kings who led the vast host of the Midianites who invaded the land of Israel, and over whom Gideon gained a great and decisive victory (Judg. 8). Zebah and Zalmunna had succeeded in escaping across the Jordan with a remnant of the Midianite host, but were overtaken at Karkor, probably in the Hauran, and routed by Gideon.

column5: Father of the apostles James and John
column7: A Galilean fisherman, the husband of Salome (q.v.), and the father of James and John, two of our Lord’s disciples ([[@40004021|Matt. 4:21]]; [[@40027056|Matt 27:56]]; [[@41015040|Mark 15:40]]).

column5: Mother of King Jehoiakim of Judah
column7: Given, the wife of Josiah and mother of Jehoiakim ([[@12023036|2 Kings 23:36]]).

column5: Israelite who married a foreign woman
column7: Zebina was one of the Israelites who had married foreign women during the time of Ezra.

column5: One of the cities of the plain destroyed with Sodom
column7: One of the “five cities of the plain” of Sodom, generally coupled with Admah ([[@1010019|Gen. 10:19]]; [[@1014002|Gen 14:2]]; [[@5029023|Deut. 29:23]]; [[@28011008|Hos. 11:8]]). It had a king of its own (Shemeber), and was therefore a place of some importance.

column5: A town resettled by the people of Judah after the exile
column7: A place mentioned only in [[@16011034|Neh. 11:34]], inhabited by the Benjamites after the Captivity.

column5: A valley mentioned in connection with Saul's military campaigns
column7: The Valley of Zeboim, a location mentioned in the context of Saul's military campaigns against the Philistines (<ref="1Sam. 13:18">1Sam. 13:18</ref>).

column5: Governor of Shechem under Abimelech
column7: Habitation, the governor of Shechem under Abimelech ([[@7009028|Judg. 9:28]], [[@7009030|Judg 9:30]], [[@7009036|Judg 9:36]]). He informed his master of the intention of the people of Shechem to transfer their allegiance to the Hivite tribe of Hamor.

column5: Israelite tribe, son of Jacob and Leah
column7: Dwelling, the sixth and youngest son of Jacob and Leah ([[@1030020|Gen. 30:20]]). Little is known of his personal history.

column5: Last king of the northern kingdom of Israel
column7: Zechariah, son of Jeroboam II, was the last king of the northern kingdom of Israel, reigning for only six months before being assassinated.

column5: Mentioned in the genealogy of King Hezekiah
column7: The father of Abijah, who was the mother of Hezekiah ([[@14029001|2 Chr. 29:1]]).

column5: Reubenite chief during the reign of Jotham
column7: One of the chiefs of the tribe of Reuben ([[@13005007|1 Chr. 5:7]]).

column5: Levite gatekeeper and musician during David's reign
column7: One of the porters of the tabernacle ([[@13009021|1 Chr. 9:21]]).

column5: Son of Isshiah, a Levite
column7: Zechariah, son of Isshiah, was a Levite mentioned in the genealogical records of the Levites during the reign of David.

column5: Son of Hosah, a Merarite
column7: Zechariah was the fourth son of Hosah, a Merarite.

column5: Leader of the half-tribe of Manasseh
column7: Zechariah, son of Obadiah, was the leader of the half-tribe of Manasseh in Gilead during the reign of David.

column5: Levite sent by Jehoshaphat to teach the Law
column7: One who assisted in teaching the law to the people in the time of Jehoshaphat ([[@14017007|2 Chr. 17:7]]).

column5: Levite who prophesied during Jehoshaphat's reign
column7: Zechariah, a Levite who prophesied during Jehoshaphat's reign.

column5: Son of Jehoshaphat, king of Judah
column7: Zechariah, one of the sons of Jehoshaphat, king of Judah.

column5: Priest murdered in the temple court
column7: The son or grandson of Jehoiada, the high priest in the times of Ahaziah and Joash. After the death of Jehoiada he boldly condemned both the king and the people for their rebellion against God ([[@14024020|2 Chr. 24:20]]), which so stirred up their resentment against him that at the king’s commandment they stoned him with stones, and he died “in the court of the house of the Lord” (24:21). Christ alludes to this deed of murder in [[@40023035|Matt. 23:35]], [[@42011051|Luke 11:51]].

column5: Prophet who instructed King Uzziah
column7: A prophet, who had “understanding in the seeing of God,” in the time of Uzziah, who was much indebted to him for his wise counsel ([[@14026005|2 Chr. 26:5]]).

column5: Levite during Hezekiah's temple cleansing
column7: Zechariah, a Levite of the sons of Asaph, helped cleanse the temple during Hezekiah's reign.

column5: Levite who helped repair the temple under Josiah
column7: Zechariah, a Levite who helped repair the temple during Josiah's reign.

column5: Leader who contributed to Josiah's Passover
column7: One of the “rulers of the house of God” ([[@14035008|2 Chr. 35:8]]).

column5: Post-exilic prophet who wrote the book of Zechariah
column7: A prophet of Judah, the eleventh of the twelve minor prophets. Like Ezekiel, he was of priestly extraction. He describes himself (1:1) as “the son of Berechiah.” In [[@15005001|Ezra 5:1]] and 6:14 he is called “the son of Iddo,” who was properly his grandfather.

column5: Descendant of Parosh who returned with Ezra
column7: Zechariah, a descendant of Parosh, who returned to Jerusalem with Ezra.

column5: Descendant of Bebai who returned with Ezra
column7: Zechariah, a descendant of Bebai, who returned to Jerusalem with Ezra.

column5: Levite sent by Ezra to find ministers
column7: A chief of the people in the time of Ezra, who consulted him about the return from captivity ([[@15008016|Ezra 8:16]]); probably the same as mentioned in [[@16008004|Neh. 8:4]]

column5: Israelite who married a foreign woman
column7: Zechariah, an Israelite who married a foreign woman during the exile.

column5: Levite who assisted Ezra in reading the Law
column7: A chief of the people in the time of Ezra, who consulted him about the return from captivity ([[@15008016|Ezra 8:16]]); probably the same as mentioned in [[@16008004|Neh. 8:4]]

column5: Descendant of Perez who lived in Jerusalem
column7: Zechariah, a descendant of Perez, who lived in Jerusalem after the exile.

column5: Descendant of Shelah who lived in Jerusalem
column7: Zechariah, a descendant of Shelah, who settled in Jerusalem after the exile.

column5: Priest who lived in Jerusalem after the exile
column7: Zechariah, a priest who lived in Jerusalem after the exile, was the son of Pashhur (or 'Pashur').

column5: Head of the priestly family of Iddo
column7: Zechariah was the head of the priestly family of Iddo during the high priesthood of Joiakim.

column5: Priest who played a trumpet in the procession
column7: Zechariah, son of Jonathan, was a priest who played a trumpet in the procession at Jerusalem's wall dedication.

column5: Priest who participated in the wall dedication
column7: Zechariah, a priest who participated in the dedication of Jerusalem's wall.

column5: Witness to Isaiah's prophecy about Maher-Shalal-Hash-Baz
column7: Zechariah, son of Jeberechiah, was a faithful witness to Isaiah's prophecy about his son Maher-Shalal-Hash-Baz.

column5: Priest, father of John the Baptist
column7: Zechariah, a priest of the division of Abijah, was the father of John the Baptist and husband of Elizabeth.

column5: Son of Abiel, founder of Gibeon
column7: Memorial, a son of Jehiel ([[@13008031|1 Chr. 8:31]]; [[@13009035|1 Chr. 9:35]]); called Zechariah (9:37).

column5: A place on the northern border of the Promised Land
column7: Side; sloping place, a town in the north of Palestine, near Hamath ([[@4034008|Num. 34:8]]; [[@26047015|Ezek. 47:15]]).

column5: False prophet who opposed Micaiah
column6: the Lord is my justice; the justice of the Lord
column7: The son of Chenaanah, a false prophet in the days of Ahab ([[@11022011|1 Kings 22:11]], [[@11022024|1 Kings 22:24]]; [[@14018010|2 Chr. 18:10]], [[@14018023|2 Chr. 18:23]]).

column5: Last king of Judah before the Babylonian exile
column6: the Lord is my justice; the justice of the Lord
column7: The last king of Judah. He was the third son of Josiah, and his mother’s name was Hamutal, the daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah, and hence he was the brother of Jehoahaz ([[@12023031|2 Kings 23:31]]; [[@12024017|2 Kings 24:17]], [[@12024018|2 Kings 24:18]]). His original name was Mattaniah; but when Nebuchadnezzar placed him on the throne as the successor to Jehoiachin he changed his name to Zedekiah. The prophet Jeremiah was his counsellor, yet “he did evil in the sight of the Lord” ([[@12024019|2 Kings 24:19]], [[@12024020|2 Kings 24:20]]; [[@24052002|Jer. 52:2]], [[@24052003|Jer. 52:3]]).

column5: Son of Jeconiah, king of Judah
column6: the Lord is my justice; the justice of the Lord
column7: Zedekiah, a son of Jeconiah (also known as Jehoiachin), king of Judah.

column5: Priest who sealed the covenant with Nehemiah
column6: the Lord is my justice; the justice of the Lord
column7: Zedekiah, a priest who sealed the covenant with Nehemiah after the exile.

column5: False prophet in Babylon during the exile
column6: the Lord is my justice; the justice of the Lord
column7: Zedekiah, a false prophet among the exiles in Babylon, was denounced by Jeremiah for his lies and immorality.

column5: Official during the reign of King Jehoiakim
column6: the Lord is my justice; the justice of the Lord
column7: The son of Hananiah, a prince of Judah in the days of Jehoiakim ([[@24036012|Jer. 36:12]]).

column5: Midianite prince defeated by Gideon
column7: The wolf, one of the two leaders of the great Midianite host which invaded Israel and was utterly routed by Gideon.

column5: A city in Benjamin where Saul's family was buried
column7: Zela was a city in Benjamin where Saul and his family were buried .

column5: Ammonite, one of David's mighty men
column6: the shadow or noise of him that licks or laps
column7: Cleft, an Ammonite; one of David’s valiant men ([[@10023037|2 Sam. 23:37]]).

column5: Israelite whose daughters received his inheritance
column6: the shade or tingling of fear
column7: First-born, of the tribe of Manasseh, and of the family of Gilead; died in the wilderness. Having left no sons, his daughters, concerned lest their father’s name should be “done away from among his family,” made an appeal to Moses, who, by divine direction, appointed it as “a statute of judgment” in Israel that daughters should inherit their father’s portion when no sons were left ([[@4027001-4027011|Num. 27:1-11]]).

column5: A place near Rachel's tomb in Benjamin
column7: Zelzah was a place near Rachel's tomb in Benjamin that Samuel referenced when giving directions to Saul .

column5: A town in Benjamin; also a hill in Ephraim
column7: A town of Benjamin ([[@6018022|Josh. 18:22]]); now the ruin, rather two ruins, es-Sumrah, 4 miles north of Jericho.

column5: Canaanite people group
column7: The designation of one of the Phoenician tribes ([[@1010018|Gen. 10:18]]) who inhabited the town of Sumra, at the western base of the Lebanon range.

column5: Son of Becher, a Benjamite
column7: Vine-dresser, a Benjamite; one of the sons of Becher ([[@13007008|1 Chr. 7:8]]).

column5: A town in the Judean lowlands
column7: Zenan was a town in the lowlands of Judah .

column5: Christian lawyer whom Paul commended
column7: A disciple called “the lawyer,” whom Paul wished Titus to bring with him ([[@56003013|Titus 3:13]]).

column5: Priest during the reign of Zedekiah
column7: The son of Maaseiah, the “second priest” in the reign of Zedekiah, often mentioned in Jeremiah as having been sent from the king to inquire ([[@24021001|Jer. 21:1]]) regarding the coming woes which he had denounced, and to entreat the prophet’s intercession that the judgment threatened might be averted ([[@24029025|Jer. 29:25]], [[@24029026|Jer. 29:26]], [[@24029029|Jer. 29:29]]; 37:3; 52:24).

column5: Prophet, son of Cushi, descendant of Hezekiah
column7: Zephaniah, the prophet who wrote the book bearing his name, was the son of Cushi and descendant of Hezekiah.

column5: One of the men in Zechariah's prophecy
column7: The father of Josiah, the priest who dwelt in Jerusalem when Darius issued the decree that the temple should be rebuilt ([[@38006010|Zech. 6:10]]).

column5: A valley where Asa defeated the Cushite army
column7: The Valley of Zephathah is where King Asa of Judah defeated Zerah the Cushite's large army .

column5: Son of Eliphaz, grandson of Esau
column6: Zephon, that sees and observes; that expects or covers
column7: Zepho, a son of Eliphaz and grandson of Esau, was a chief of Edom.

column5: A fortified city in Naphtali
column7: Zer was a fortified city in the territory of Naphtali .

column5: Son of Reuel, grandson of Esau
column7: Zerah, a son of Reuel and grandson of Esau, was a chief of Edom.

column5: King of Edom
column7: Zerah, from Bozrah, was a king of Edom before Israel had a king.

column5: Son of Judah, twin of Perez
column7: A son of Tamar ([[@1038030|Gen. 38:30]]); called also Zara ([[@40001003|Matt. 1:3]]).

column5: Son of Simeon; ancestor of the Zerahites
column7: Zerah (or Zohar), a son of Simeon, was the ancestor of the Zerahite clan.

column5: Levite of the Gershonite clan
column7: Zerah, a Levite of the Gershonite clan, was the son of Iddo.

column5: Ethiopian commander who invaded Judah
column7: An “Ethiopian,” probably Osorkon II., the successor of Shishak on the throne of Egypt. With an enormous army, the largest we read of in Scripture, he invaded the kingdom of Judah in the days of Asa ([[@14014009-14014015|2 Chr. 14:9-15]]). He reached Zephathah, and there encountered the army of Asa. This is the only instance “in all the annals of Judah of a victorious encounter in the field with a first-class heathen power in full force.”

column5: Priest, ancestor of Ezra
column6: the Lord rising; brightness of the Lord
column7: Zerahiah (or Ahitub), a priest, was an ancestor of Ezra the scribe.

column5: Descendant of Pahath-Moab who returned with Ezra
column6: the Lord rising; brightness of the Lord
column7: Zerahiah, a descendant of Pahath-Moab, led 200 men in the return to Jerusalem with Ezra.

column5: A brook marking the end of Israel's wilderness wanderings
column7: =Zared, luxuriance; willow bush, a brook or valley communicating with the Dead Sea near its southern extremity ([[@4021012|Num. 21:12]]; [[@5002014|Deut. 2:14]]). It is called the “brook of the willows” ([[@23015007|Isa. 15:7]]) and the “river of the wilderness” ([[@30006014|Amos 6:14]]).

column5: The hometown of Jeroboam, first king of Israel
column7: The fortress, a city on the north of Mount Ephraim; the birthplace of Jeroboam ([[@11011026|1 Kings 11:26]]).

column5: Wife of Haman, enemy of the Jews
column7: Star of Venus, the wife of Haman, whom she instigated to prepare a gallows for Mordecai ([[@17005010|Esther 5:10]]).

column5: Son of Ashhur, founder of Tekoa
column7: Zereth, a son of Ashhur (or 'Ashur') and Helah, was a Judahite.

column5: A city in Reuben's territory by the Dead Sea
column7: The splendour of the dawn, a city “in the mount of the valley” ([[@6013019|Josh. 13:19]]). It is identified with the ruins of Zara, near the mouth of the Wady Zerka Main, on the eastern shore of the Dead Sea, some 3 miles south of the Callirrhoe. Of this town but little remains.

column5: Son of Jeduthun, a temple musician
column7: Zeri (or Izri), a son of Jeduthun, was a temple musician during the reign of David.

column5: Ancestor of King Saul
column6: root; that straitens or binds; that keeps tight
column7: Zeror, a Benjamite, was an ancestor of King Saul.

column5: Mother of Jeroboam, first king of Israel
column7: Stricken, mother of Jeroboam, the first king of the ten tribes ([[@11011026|1 Kings 11:26]]).

column5: Leader of the first Jewish exiles from Babylon
column6: a stranger at Babylon; dispersion of confusion
column7: The seed of Babylon, the son of Salathiel or Shealtiel ([[@37001001|Hag. 1:1]]; Zorobabel, [[@40001012|Matt. 1:12]]); called also the son of Pedaiah ([[@13003017-13003019|1 Chr. 3:17-19]]), i.e., according to a frequent usage of the word “son;” the grandson or the nephew of Salathiel. He is also known by the Persian name of Sheshbazzar ([[@15001008|Ezra 1:8]], [[@15001011|Ezra 1:11]]).

column5: Ancestor of Jesus
column6: a stranger at Babylon; dispersion of confusion
column7: The seed of Babylon, the son of Salathiel or Shealtiel ([[@37001001|Hag. 1:1]]; Zorobabel, [[@40001012|Matt. 1:12]]); called also the son of Pedaiah ([[@13003017-13003019|1 Chr. 3:17-19]]), i.e., according to a frequent usage of the word “son;” the grandson or the nephew of Salathiel. He is also known by the Persian name of Sheshbazzar ([[@15001008|Ezra 1:8]], [[@15001011|Ezra 1:11]]).

column5: Sister of David; mother of Joab, Abishai, and Asahel
column6: pain or tribulation of the Lord
column7: Stricken of the Lord, David’s sister, and the mother of Abishai, Joab, and Asahel ([[@13002016|1 Chr. 2:16]]), who were the three leading heroes of David’s army, and being his nephews, they were admitted to the closest companionship with him.

column5: Son of Laadan, a Gershonite Levite
column7: Zetham, a son of Laadan, was a Gershonite Levite during the time of David.

column5: Son of Bilhan, a Benjamite
column7: Zethan was a son of Bilhan and a descendant of Benjamin.

column5: One of the seven eunuchs of King Ahasuerus
column7: Zethar was one of the seven eunuchs who served King Ahasuerus of Persia.

column5: Gadite clan leader during the reign of Jotham
column7: Zia was a Gadite clan leader during the reigns of Jotham, king of Judah, and Jeroboam, king of Israel.

column5: Servant of Saul's household, later served David
column7: Post; statue, “a servant of the house of Saul” ([[@10009002|2 Sam. 9:2]]), who informed David that Mephibosheth, a son of Jonathan, was alive.

column5: Hivite grandfather of Esau's wife Oholibamah
column7: Zibeon, the Hivite grandfather of Esau's wife Oholibamah.

column5: Son of Shaharaim, a Benjamite
column7: Zibia was a son of Shaharaim, a Benjamite, born to his wife Hodesh in the country of Moab.

column5: Mother of King Joash (or 'Jehoash') of Judah from Beersheba
column7: Zibiah, from Beersheba, was the mother of King Joash (or 'Jehoash') of Judah.

column5: Son of Izhar, a Levite
column6: that remembers; that is a man
column7: Zichri was a son of Izhar and grandson of Kohath, of the tribe of Levi.

column5: Son of Shimei, a Benjamite
column6: that remembers; that is a man
column7: Zichri was a son of Shimei, a Benjamite, and a descendant of Shaharaim.

column5: Son of Jeroham, a Benjamite
column6: that remembers; that is a man
column7: Zichri was a son of Jeroham, a Benjamite, and a descendant of Shaharaim.

column5: Son of Jeroham, a Benjamite
column6: that remembers; that is a man
column7: Zichri was another son of Jeroham, a Benjamite, and a descendant of Shaharaim.

column5: Levite, descendant of Asaph, temple singer
column6: that remembers; that is a man
column7: Zichri (or Zabdi), a Levite descendant of Asaph, was a temple singer during the time of Nehemiah.

column5: Levite, descendant of Moses, treasurer
column6: that remembers; that is a man
column7: Zichri, a Levite descendant of Moses, was a treasurer in the temple during the time of David.

column5: Leader of the tribe of Reuben
column6: that remembers; that is a man
column7: Zichri was the leader of the tribe of Reuben during the reign of King David.

column5: Commander of 200,000 soldiers under Jehoshaphat
column6: that remembers; that is a man
column7: Zichri was a commander of 200,000 soldiers who volunteered to serve King Jehoshaphat of Judah.

column5: Father of Elishaphat, a supporter of Jehoiada
column6: that remembers; that is a man
column7: Zichri was the father of Elishaphat, one of the commanders who supported Jehoiada the priest in overthrowing Athaliah.

column5: Ephraimite warrior who killed Maaseiah, Ahaziah, and Elkanah
column6: that remembers; that is a man
column7: Zichri, a mighty warrior from Ephraim, killed Maaseiah the king's son, Ahaziah the governor, and Elkanah the second to the king during the reign of Ahaz.

column5: Son of Joab, a leader in Jerusalem
column6: that remembers; that is a man
column7: Zichri, the son of Joab, was a leader in Jerusalem during the time of Nehemiah.

column5: Head of the priestly family of Abijah
column6: that remembers; that is a man
column7: Zichri was the head of the priestly family of Abijah during the time of Joiakim the high priest.

column5: A fortified city in Naphtali
column7: Sides, a town of Naphtali ([[@6019035|Josh. 19:35]]), has been identified with Kefr-Hattin, the “village of the Hittites,” about 5 miles west of Tiberias.

column5: Family of temple servants who returned from exile
column7: The name of a family of Nethinim ([[@15002043|Ezra 2:43]]; [[@16007046|Neh. 7:46]]).

column5: Family of temple servants living on the Ophel
column7: The temple servants, including the family of Ziha, lived on Ophel in Jerusalem during the time of Nehemiah.

column5: A city given to David; originally Judah's, then Simeon's
column7: A town in the Negeb, or south country of Judah ([[@6015031|Josh. 15:31]]), in the possession of the Philistines when David fled to Gath from Ziph with all his followers. Achish, the king, assigned him Ziklag as his place of residence. There he dwelt for over a year and four months. From this time it pertained to the kings of Judah ([[@9027006|1 Sam. 27:6]]).

column5: Wife of Lamech; mother of Tubal-Cain and Naamah
column6: shadow; the tingling of the ear
column7: Shadow, one of the wives of Lamech, of the line of Cain, and mother of Tubal-cain ([[@1004019|Gen. 4:19]], [[@1004022|Gen. 4:22]]).

column5: Son of Shimei, a Benjamite
column7: Zillethai was a son of Shimei and a descendant of Benjamin.

column5: Manassite leader who joined David at Ziklag
column7: One of the captains of the tribe of Manasseh who joined David at Ziklag ([[@13012020|1 Chr. 12:20]]).

column5: Leah's maidservant; mother of Gad and Asher
column7: Drooping, Leah’s handmaid, and the mother of Gad and Asher ([[@1030009-1030013|Gen. 30:9-13]]).

column5: Levite, son of Shimei, descendant of Gershon
column7: Zimmah, a Levite and descendant of Gershon, was the son of Shimei.

column5: Levite, son of Asaph, during Hezekiah's reign
column7: Zimmah, a Levite and son of Asaph, participated in the purification of the temple during King Hezekiah's reign.

column5: Son of Abraham and Keturah
column7: Vine-dressers; celebrated, one of the sons of Abraham by Keturah ([[@1025002|Gen. 25:2]]).

column5: Simeonite prince, killed in the Baal-Peor incident
column7: Zimri, a prince of the Simeonites, was one of the Israelites killed in the incident involving the worship of Baal-Peor.

column5: King of Israel, reigned seven days
column7: Zimri, a commander of half of Israel's chariots, became king after assassinating Elah, but his reign lasted only seven days.

column5: A nation mentioned in Jeremiah's prophecy against nations
column7: Zimri was a nation mentioned in Jeremiah's prophecy of God's judgment against various nations .

column5: A desert and wilderness region south of Judah
column7: A low palm-tree, the south-eastern corner of the desert et-Tih, the wilderness of Paran, between the Gulf of Akabah and the head of the Wady Guraiyeh ([[@4013021|Num. 13:21]]).

column5: A town in the hill country of Judah
column7: Littleness, a city in the mountains of Judah ([[@6015054|Josh. 15:54]]); the modern Si’air, 4 1/2 miles north-north-east of Hebron.

column5: A town in the Negev of Judah
column7: A city in the south of Judah ([[@6015024|Josh. 15:24]]), probably at the pass of Sufah.

column5: A town in Judah where David hid from Saul
column7: A city in the mountains of Judah ([[@6015055|Josh. 15:55]]), identified with the uninhabited ruins of Tell ez-Zif, about 5 miles south-east of Hebron.

column5: Son of Jehallelel, a Judahite
column7: Ziph, a descendant of Judah, was one of the sons of Jehallelel.

column5: Son of Jehallelel, a Judahite
column7: Ziphah, a descendant of Judah, was one of the sons of Jehallelel.

column5: Son of Gad, progenitor of the Zephonites
column7: Ziphion (or Zephon), a son of Gad, was the ancestor of the Zephonite clan.

column5: A place on the northern border of the Promised Land
column7: Sweet odour, a city on the northern border of Palestine ([[@4034009|Num. 34:9]]), south-east of Hamath.

column5: Father of Balak, king of Moab
column7: A little bird, the father of Balak, king of Moab ([[@4022002|Num. 22:2]], [[@4022004|Num. 22:4]]).

column5: Wife of Moses, daughter of Jethro
column7: A female bird. Reuel’s daughter, who became the wife of Moses ([[@2002021|Ex. 2:21]]).

column5: A pass where Jehoshaphat defeated Moab and Ammon
column6: flower; branch; a lock of hair
column7: Projecting; a flower, a cleft or pass, probably that near En-gedi, which leads up from the Dead Sea ([[@14020016|2 Chr. 20:16]]) in the direction of Tekoa; now Tell Hasasah.

column5: Son of Shiphi, a Simeonite
column7: Ziza, a descendant of Simeon, was the son of Shiphi.

column5: Son of King Rehoboam and Maacah
column7: Ziza was one of the sons born to King Rehoboam of Judah and his wife Maacah, the granddaughter of Absalom.

column5: Gershonite Levite, son of Shimei
column7: Zizah (or Zina), a Gershonite Levite, was the second son of Shimei.

column5: An ancient Egyptian city, probably Tanis
column7: (Old Egypt. Sant= “stronghold,” the modern San). A city on the Tanitic branch of the Nile, called by the Greeks Tanis. It was built seven years after Hebron in Palestine ([[@4013022|Num. 13:22]]).

column5: A city near Sodom, spared from destruction
column7: Small, a town on the east or south-east of the Dead Sea, to which Lot and his daughters fled from Sodom ([[@1019022|Gen. 19:22]], [[@1019023|Gen. 19:23]]). It was originally called Bela (14:2, 8). It is referred to by the prophets Isaiah (15:5) and Jeremiah (48:34).

column5: An Aramean kingdom, enemy of Israel during David's reign
column7: =Aram-Zobah, (Ps. 60, title), a Syrian province or kingdom to the south of Coele-Syria, and extending from the eastern slopes of Lebanon north and east toward the Euphrates.

column5: Son of Koz, a Judahite
column7: Zobebah was one of the sons of Koz, a descendant of Judah.

column5: Father of Ephron the Hittite
column7: The father of Ephron the Hittite ([[@1023008|Gen. 23:8]]).

column5: Son of Ishi, a Judahite
column7: Snatching (?), one of the sons of Ishi ([[@13004020|1 Chr. 4:20]]).

column5: Son of Hotham, an Asherite
column7: Spreading out, a son of Helem ([[@13007035|1 Chr. 7:35]]), a chief of Asher.

column5: One of Job's three friends, the Naamathite
column7: Chirping, one of Job’s friends who came to condole with him in his distress ([[@18002011|Job 2:11]]. The LXX. render here “king of the Mineans” = Ma’in, Maonites, [[@7010012|Judg. 10:12]], in Southern Arabia).

column5: A place in Moab where Balaam blessed Israel
column7: The field of Zophim was a place on the top of Pisgah in Moab where Balaam blessed Israel .

column5: A town in the Shephelah, home of Samson
column7: Place of wasps, a town in the low country of Judah, afterwards given to Dan ([[@6019041|Josh. 19:41]]; [[@7018002|Judg. 18:2]]), probably the same as Zoreah ([[@6015033|Josh. 15:33]]). This was Samson’s birthplace ([[@7013002|Judg. 13:2]], [[@7013025|Judg 13:25]]), and near it he found a grave (16:31). It was situated on the crest of a hill overlooking the valley of Sorek, and was fortified by Rehoboam ([[@14011010|2 Chr. 11:10]]). It has been identified with Sur’ah, in the Wady Surar, 8 miles west of Jerusalem.

column5: Judahite clan descended from Shobal
column7: The Zorathites were a Judahite clan descended from Shobal.

column5: Father of Nethanel, leader of Issachar
column7: Zuar was the father of Nethanel, a leader of the tribe of Issachar during the wilderness wanderings.

column5: Levite ancestor of Samuel the prophet
column6: that beholds, observes, watches; roof; covering
column7: Honeycomb, a Kohathite Levite, ancestor of Elkanah and Samuel ([[@9001001|1 Sam. 1:1]]); called also Zophai ([[@13006026|1 Chr. 6:26]]).

column5: A land where Saul searched for his father's donkeys
column6: that beholds, observes, watches; roof; covering
column7: Honeycomb, a Kohathite Levite, ancestor of Elkanah and Samuel ([[@9001001|1 Sam. 1:1]]); called also Zophai ([[@13006026|1 Chr. 6:26]]).

column5: Midianite leader killed by Phinehas
column7: Zur was a Midianite leader whose daughter was involved with an Israelite, resulting in a plague on Israel.

column5: Midianite king defeated by Israel
column7: One of the five Midianite kings whom the Israelites defeated and put to death ([[@4031008|Num. 31:8]]).

column5: Son of Abiel, a Benjamite
column7: Zur was a son of Abiel and a descendant of Benjamin.

column5: Leader of the Merarite Levites
column7: Rock of God, chief of the family of the Merarites ([[@4003035|Num. 3:35]]) at the time of the Exodus.

column5: Father of Shelumiel, leader of Simeon
column6: the Almighty is my rock and strength
column7: Rock of the Almighty, the father of Shelumiel, who was chief of the tribe of Simeon when Israel was encamped at Sinai ([[@4001006|Num. 1:6]]; [[@4002012|Num 2:12]]).

column5: Ancient people defeated by Chedorlaomer
column7: The Zuzim were an ancient people defeated by Chedorlaomer and his allies during Abraham's time.
